title: Klint Kubiak: Brock Bowers was "very close" to playing on Sunday
summary: The Raiders are 2-0 and may be getting a boost to their offense next week.
full_text: The Raiders are 2-0 and may be getting a boost to their offense next week. Tight end Brock Bowers may be back for Week 3 after undergoing a recent knee procedure. In his postgame press conference following Sunday's victory over the Chargers, head coach Klint Kubiak said Bowers was " close — very close " to playing in Week 2. Bowers went through an on-field, pregame workout before Sunday's game, with Kubiak saying that the tight end "looked great." Last season, Bowers caught 64 passes for 680 yards with seven touchdowns in 12 games. Through two games this year, Michael Mayer has started at tight end and caught nine passes for 55 yards.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Lions S Avonte Maddox out for season with foot injury
summary: Lions safety Avonte Maddox was forced out of last Sunday's loss to the Bills with a foot injury and he won't be back on the field anytime soon.
full_text: ' Lions safety Avonte Maddox was forced out of last Sunday's loss to the Bills with a foot injury and he won't be back on the field anytime soon. Head coach Dan Campbell said at a Monday press conference that Maddox will have surgery to repair the injury and that he will miss the rest of the season as a result. Maddox played 14 games for the Lions and was a backup in most of those contests. He started the first two games this season with Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph sidelined by injuries of their own. All of those missing pieces have the Lions looking for outside help in the secondary as they move toward a Week 3 game against the Jets.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Caleb Williams did not suffer major hamstring injury, not ruled out for Week 3
summary: Though Williams' injury initially looked bad, he may not miss the Week 3 contest against the Eagles on Monday night.
full_text: There's more positive news on the injury front for Bears quarterback Caleb Williams. According to Tom Pelissero of Netflix, Williams did not suffer a major injury to his hamstring during Sunday’s loss to the Vikings. Furthermore, the team is not ruling him out for the Week 3 matchup against the Eagles next Monday night. Williams suffered his hamstring injury as he was trying to run toward the end zone deep in opponent territory on Sunday afternoon. With rainy conditions throughout the afternoon, the grass at Soldier Field was wet. Williams was helped off the field and then carted to the locker room, but head coach Ben Johnson said he was in “good spirits” after the game. Johnson also noted his relief that Williams hadn’t suffered a knee injury. PFT reported on Sunday that the initial belief was that Williams suffered a Grade 1 hamstring strain. The quarterback completed 15-of-26 passes for 138 yards with an interception before departing the contest. He also rushed 42 yards on five carries. In two games so far this season, Williams has completed 65.5 percent of his throws for 407 yards with two touchdowns and one pick. He’s rushed for 107 yards with two TDs.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Lions bring in veteran defensive backs for workouts Monday
summary: Only the Colts have given up more points and yards than the Lions so far this season, so it's not surprising to hear that Detroit is looking for some outside defensive help.
full_text: Only the Colts have given up more points and yards than the Lions so far this season, so it's not surprising to hear that Detroit is looking for some outside defensive help. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that the team will have several veteran defensive backs in for workouts on Monday. Jordan Fuller, Jalen Mills, and Mike Edwards are among the players set to participate. Mills played in three games for the Lions last season. Edwards saw time with the Chiefs while Fuller appeared in six games for the Falcons. The Lions have safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph on the physically unable to perform list, which means they won't be able to return until Week 5 at the earliest. They lost another safety to injury when Avonte Maddox got hurt last Thursday and cornerback Rock Ya-Sin was also banged up during their loss to the Bills.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Vrabel didn't want his Sunday ruined by questions about Drake Maye's struggles
summary: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye finished second in the MVP voting in 2025.
full_text: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye finished second in the MVP voting in 2025. This year, he's second from the bottom in passer rating among the quarterbacks who have played two games. The Week 1 game was bad, with three ill-advised fourth-quarter interceptions. The Week 2 performance wasn't much better, featuring a head-scratching interception after a long completion to receiver Romeo Doubs. Maye finished with 14 completions in 22 attempts for 208 yards and one interception. After the game, Ben Volin of the Boston Globe asked Vrabel about his concern level with the offense, and whether he's worried Maye is pressing. "No, just trying to win the game, Ben," Vrabel said. " You’re not gonna ruin my Sunday , but I'll come back to you tomorrow. Thanks, bud." Greg Bedard of Boston Sports Journal tried to ask a related question. Vrabel cut him off. "You, neither," Vrabel said. "You're not gonna ruin it, either." On one hand, Vrabel should be happy. With road trips coming up to Jacksonville and Buffalo, the Patriots desperately needed a win. Still, his reaction shows that, yes, there is something to be worried about with the offense generally, and with Maye specifically.
author: Mike Florio

title: Vikings are now the betting favorites to win the NFC North
summary: Heading into the season, the Vikings were a distant fourth in the betting odds to win the NFC North.
full_text: Heading into the season, the Vikings were a distant fourth in the betting odds to win the NFC North. A lot can change in two weeks. The Vikings are now 2-0, with both wins coming against division opponents, a game ahead of the Lions, Packers and Bears, and the new betting favorites to win the division. The Vikings' odds are +194 to win what looks to be the NFL's most competitive division. The Lions are next at +205, followed by the Packers at +285. Last year's NFC North winners, the Bears, not have the longest odds, at +500, amid concerns that Caleb Williams could miss extended time with a hamstring injury. Uncertainty at quarterback in Minnesota is an issue, but the Vikings have found a way to win two weeks in a row with Carson Wentz replacing the injured Kyler Murray. The Vikings' defense looks ferocious, and the Vikings look like a playoff team. Something few thought they'd be just a couple weeks ago.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Fox audio issues had some viewers watching one game, hearing Vikings-Bears
summary: The second Sunday of the 2026 regular season gave new meaning to the second-game experience.
full_text: The second Sunday of the 2026 regular season gave new meaning to the second-game experience. As noted by Megan Armstrong of Awful Announcing , multiple viewers of the Packers-Jets and Falcons-Panthers games on Fox complained that the sound was replaced with audio from Bears-Vikings . Armstrong's story includes multiple tweets, including visual/audio evidence. A PFT reader emailed the same concern. "My husband and I were watching the Packers/Jets game on FOX today," the reader said. "Twice, we lost the audio for our game and were listening to the Vikings/Bears game. The first time only lasted about a minute but the second time was at least 5-6 minutes. So we're watching the Pack and listening to the Vikes." In nearly 25 years of doing this, audio from one game making its way into another game is a first. And hopefully it's the last time something like that will happen.
author: Mike Florio

title: Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy see the issues with the Pittsburgh offense
summary: When he's complaining about Anthony Fauci, ESPN, and/or Shailene Woodley, Aaron Rodgers is not subtle.
full_text: When he's complaining about Anthony Fauci, ESPN, and/or Shailene Woodley, Aaron Rodgers is not subtle. When he has concerns about his football team, his criticisms are harder to pinpoint. But they're still there. After Sunday's loss to the Patriots, Rodgers dropped a hint or two regarding coach Mike McCarthy's offense. And Rodgers did it in a way that will give him plausible deniability if someone else spots it and points it out. "In a game like today where there wasn't a lot of flow to it, we need to be better," Rodgers told reporters after the 20-6 loss. "And that starts with me at like making sure Mike knows what's working, what's not working, our coaches know, and — so we can call stuff that we feel like has a better chance." In other words, some of the "stuff" McCarthy was calling didn't have a very good chance. When asked later about things that are "working" and "not working," Rodgers said, "The plays were fine." But he then suggested that perhaps the offense was overloaded with plays. "If there's too much stuff in the plan, we've got to cut it back," Rodgers said. "I'm always liking to push the envelope, and if I see guys doing it the right way in practice, then I feel good about it, but we've got to transfer the practice to the game obviously and the details gotta come with it." The hidden criticisms aren't off-base; McCarthy himself made similar comments about the size of the game plan. "We've got to look at the volume," he told reporters after the game. "That's Marty Schottenheimer, that was his thing. It was a great lesson for a young coach to learn, and here I am some old bastard that didn't do it this week. If it's not clean, you cut the volume down, and we're not clean on offense. "So the volume is getting cut down. That's the first starting point, and that's my fault. I felt it earlier in the week. We've got a quarterback that could play at any volume of game plan, but at the end of the day, it's a team game. We've got to give Aaron better platforms to throw off of and have the opportunities because I don't want to dink and dunk and play all day and play keep-away football." McCarthy's remarks on the volume of the game plan came after he attributed the offensive struggles to things he had observed during the week. "Felt it in practice frankly, coming off of last week," McCarthy said. "As I stated, I felt we were real herky-jerky trying to get in the run and pass. . . . The run game was a little bit herky-jerky. . . . But the reality of it is the detail is not there, and that's on coaching. It starts with me. I'm calling the offense. I have to get the detail better. . . . I felt it on Wednesday and Thursday. I'm a veteran coach. I know better. I didn't do a good job." McCarthy was asked to clarify his comment about "feeling it" during the week. "Just volume," McCarthy said. "We've done this a long time. You know when the volume is up, and you know when you're pushing the envelope too. It's also the first year of the staff and players working together. So you want to push your players, but end of the day, you've got to do it to win a game." Rodgers has faith McCarthy will make the fixes that need to be made. "I've seen Mike for 14 years. So, Mike is going to take accountability, sometimes when it's not his fault, doesn't need to do that," Rodgers said. "But Mike loves the guys, and he wants us to have some urgency and to bounce back with this, and I know we will." They need to. The offense has engineered one touchdown drive in two full games, and it covered only 31 yards. The Steelers easily could have lost to the Falcons in Week 1, and the Falcons looked horrible in Week 2. In six days, the 2-0 Bengals come to Pittsburgh. And while the Steelers tend to find a way to win certain key games, it becomes a much taller task if the offense isn't delivering. At some point, Rodgers himself has to deliver. He's completing fewer than 60 percent of his passes (his career average is 65.1), he's averaging only 5.2 yards per attempt (down from 6.7 in 2025), and his passer rating is a very sluggish 72.1. Rodgers has never had a full-season rating below 90.5, and that happened during his 5-12 final year with the Jets.
author: Mike Florio

title: Troy Aikman thought he'd have a new deal with ESPN by now
summary: On Monday night, Joe Buck and Troy Aikman will call the Giants-Rams game.
full_text: On Monday night, Joe Buck and Troy Aikman will call the Giants-Rams game. Buck has a new contract. Aikman does not. And Aikman is surprised that his new deal is not yet done. Via Jon Lewis of SportsMediaWatch.com, Aikman recently addressed the situation in an appearance on the Sports Media Podcast with Richard Deitsch . “ I thought something would be done prior to the start of this season,” Aikman told Deitsch. “I’ve never gone into the last year of a contract ever since I signed with the Dallas Cowboys. And so I thought that it would be done. It’s not. When it might get done, if it gets done, is anyone’s guess. And it’s really not something that I’m putting a lot of energy into.” Buck and Aikman have worked together since 2002. They jumped from Fox to ESPN in 2022. They signed five-year deals. Buck now has a five-year extension; Aikman does not. Aikman said that he hasn't spoken with ESPN executives regarding what Buck's deal means to Aikman's. “How much of that is my decision, I guess is yet to be determined,” Aikman said. “Would I like to continue working with Joe Buck moving down the road? 100 percent." Perhaps ESPN will decide to pair Buck with someone else, like Pat McAfee. (I'm kidding, I think.) However it goes, Aikman realizes that the broader mission of ESPN pilfering Buck and Aikman from Fox has been accomplished. “I came over in 2022 in large part to kind of help mend the relationship with ESPN and the NFL,” Aikman said. “I feel like the reason that I was brought over, I fulfilled whatever obligations they were expecting from me. So much so that . . . the league now owns 10 percent of the network. So I would say the fence has been mended." The only question left is whether the bridge with Aikman will eventually be burned.
author: Mike Florio

title: Shane Steichen on 9 straight losses: We're right there, have to find a way to win at the end
summary: After the conclusion of the 2025 season in January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon made it clear that General Manager Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen had to put a better product on the field in 2026.
full_text: After the conclusion of the 2025 season in January, Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon made it clear that General Manager Chris Ballard and head coach Shane Steichen had to put a better product on the field in 2026. “We have been very clear with Chris and Shane that giving them another opportunity means that the sense of urgency for them to deliver and perform has never been higher ,” Irsay-Gordon said at her press conference after announcing that Ballard and Steichen would both return. But with Sunday’s overtime loss to Kansas City, Indianapolis has now lost nine consecutive games dating back to Week 12 of last season. The team finished 8-9 after starting 8-2 and has now dropped the first two this season. A lot has happened along the way — including starting quarterback Daniel Jones going down with a torn Achilles. But in a results-oriented business, Indianapolis has not been good enough. At the end of his postgame press conference on Sunday night, Steichen was asked what he tells the team after nine consecutive losses. “I tell them to keep your freaking heads up, dude,” Steichen said. “It is a long season ahead of us. We are battling like crazy. That’s the message. We have to continue to grow and learn. There is a lot of football left. Like I said last week, we are right there. We have to find a way to win at the end. That was one of those games. “It is a freaking hard-ass league, and you have got to find a way to win these tight games.” The Colts will be back at home next weekend to face a division rival, the 0-2 Texans.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Report: Saints LT Kelvin Banks believed to have a high-ankle sprain
summary: The Saints came back to beat the Ravens in Baltimore on Sunday, but it looks like their attempt to build on that win will come without their starting left tackle.
full_text: The Saints came back to beat the Ravens in Baltimore on Sunday, but it looks like their attempt to build on that win will come without their starting left tackle. Kelvin Banks was carted off during the 24-17 win and Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Banks is believed to have a high-ankle sprain. Banks is set to have an MRI to evaluate the extent of the injury. High-ankle sprains often keep players out for weeks, so a stint on injured reserve could be in the cards for the 2025 first-round pick. Asim Richards replaced Banks after he hurt his ankle on Sunday and is in line to take over as the starter for any future absences.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears had second biggest scoring dip ever from Week 1 to Week 2
summary: In Week 1, the Bears came within one point of scoring 60.
full_text: In Week 1, the Bears came within one point of scoring 60. In Week 2, they came within three points of scoring none. The dip from 59 points to start the season to only a field goal in the second game is, per NBC Sports research, the second biggest turnaround from Week 1 to Week 2 in NFL history. In 1973, the Falcons opened the season with a 62-7 win over the Saints. The following week, they lost to the Rams, 31-0. That year, Falcons quarterback Dick Shiner went from completing 13 of 15 passes for 227 yards and three touchdowns to completing two of nine for 17 yards and an interception. (The Falcons finished the year 9-5 but missed the playoffs.) On Sunday, the weather — and the Minnesota defense — had something to do with the reduction in production. Still, it won't be easy to get closer to 59 than three if quarterback Caleb Williams misses time with the hamstring injury he suffered in the fourth quarter.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dallas Turner beat TE Colston Loveland for decisive sack
summary: Vikings defensive end Dallas Turner has blossomed into one of the best pass rushers in the NFL.
full_text: Vikings defensive end Dallas Turner has blossomed into one of the best pass rushers in the NFL. He had two sacks on Sunday at Chicago, to go with the sack he had last week against the Packers. The last sack came on the last play of the day, slamming the door on a potential game-winning touchdown from backup quarterback Tyson Bagent. On the play, Turner bull rushed Bears tight end Colston Loveland , riding Loveland all the way to Bagent. After the game, I asked Turner by phone why the Bears thought they could slow him down with a tight end. He said the attack crafted by defensive coordinator Brian Flores dictates the approach, by creating the kind of chaos that forces the offense into unfavorable matchups. Turner said that, on several plays during the final drive, a tight end was trying to block him. The effort was just the latest example of Turner's arrival as an elite pass rusher. He said that his recent success is a "progressive thing," based on the time he has spent in the Flores defense, and not the result of any specific moment where the light went on. He turned the lights out for the Bears on Sunday, propelling the Vikings to 2-0 with an unlikely 9-3 win in Chicago — Minnesota's seventh straight win at Soldier Field.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kirk Cousins throws three TDs, Raiders start 2-0 with 26-14 victory over Chargers
summary: Klint Kubiak is the first Raiders coach to start his tenure 2-0 since Bill Callahan in 2002.
full_text: You like that? Raiders fans all over might be chanting Kirk Cousins' unofficial slogan for at least the next week after the quarterback threw for three more touchdowns, powering Las Vegas to a 26-14 victory to begin the season 2-0. The Raiders had not started the season with two consecutive wins since 2021. Las Vegas played solid defense against Los Angeles, picking up some timely takeaways. Omarion Hampton had another game-changing fumble, coughing the ball up on a fourth-quarter run up the middle with the Chargers down by three. The Raiders scored a couple of plays later with Cousins’ third touchdown pass, going up by 10 with 2:59 on the clock. After Justin Herbert’s second interception of the game, Joe Alt closed what was a particularly bad day with a holding penalty in the end zone for a safety to close out the scoring. Alt had previously been flagged for three false start penalties, despite the Chargers playing at home. Herbert finished the contest 15-of-27 for 192 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. He also had three of the Chargers’ six fumbles on the day, though the team did not lose possession on any of them. Hampton had 94 yards on 23 carries with a touchdown. But on the other side, Cousins was 19-of-29 for 253 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. Tre Tucker was his top target, catching five passes for 119 yards. Two of Tucker’s catches went for at least 40 yards, including a long touchdown in the first quarter to open the scoring. Cousins is now just the second quarterback in franchise history to have at least three touchdown passes in each of the club’s first two games, joining Ken Stabler from 1976. Kubiak has become the fourth coach in franchise history to win each of his first two games, joining Al Davis, John Madden, and Bill Callahan. At 2-0, the Raiders will again be on the road in Week 3 as they play the Saints in New Orleans. The schedule doesn’t get easier for the 0-2 Chargers, as they’ll be on the road to face the Bills in Week 3.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Saints rally for 24-17 upset of Ravens
summary: The Saints fell behind the Lions 21-0 in the season opener but rallied to force overtime.
full_text: The Saints fell behind the Lions 21-0 in the season opener but rallied to force overtime. They lost on a failed 2-point conversion. They trailed the Ravens 14-3 in the first half and 17-9 in the second. They did not lose. Tyler Shough directed the Saints to a 24-17 comeback win over the Ravens. The Saints outscored the Ravens 14-0 in the fourth quarter as Shough threw a 21-yard touchdown pass to Chris Olave and ran for a 1-yard touchdown on fourth down with 1:28 remaining. The Saints outgained the Ravens 137 to 43 in the fourth quarter, with Baltimore getting only two first downs. In four possessions in the second half, the Ravens got no closer to the end zone than the Saints 31. Shough's touchdown run was reviewed and upheld on replay. Two downs earlier, replay upheld officials' on-field ruling that tight end Juwan Johnson came up just short of the goal line on a diving attempt after a reception from Shough. The Saints still had to hold off the Ravens, and Lamar Jackson got Baltimore to the New Orleans 37 with 20 seconds left. Saints safety Julian Blackmon intercepted Jackson on a desperation throw toward Rashod Bateman at the 7. Shough went 27-of-34 for 252 yards and a touchdown and ran for 23 yards and a touchdown on nine carries. The Saints rushed for only 65 yards on 27 carries. They were 8-of-15 on third down and 2-of-2 on fourth. The Ravens, who had 228 yards at halftime, finished with 312 yards. Jackson was 21-of-31 for 235 yards with a touchdown and an interception, and he ran for 34 yards on four carries. Derrick Henry ran for 68 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries, and Bateman caught seven passes for 88 yards and a touchdown.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bengals stymie Texans 20-6 as Houston drops first two games again
summary: The Bengals defense is not the same defense as last season.
full_text: The Bengals defense is not the same defense as last season. The Texans were 0-for-4 in the red zone, with their only points coming on two field goals, and the Bengals won 20-6. Cincinnati ran its record to 2-0 in 2026, only the third time in its history that it has started 2-0. Houston lost its first two games for a second consecutive season. The Texans rallied from an 0-3 start last season to make the playoffs. The Bengals sacked C.J. Stroud four times, with Cedric Johnson getting two and Jonathan Allen and Shemar Stewart each getting one. The Texans were 5-of-17 on third down and 0-for-4 on fourth down, and they gained only 60 yards on 18 carries as prize offseason acquisition David Montgomery ran for 10 yards on six carries. Stroud led the Texans in rushing 29 yards on three carries. Stroud threw a career-high 55 passes, completing 30 for 353 yards without his three top receivers. Nico Collins was inactive; Jayden Higgins is on season-ending injured reserve; and Tank Dell is still working his way back from his 2024 leg injury. The Bengals had only 267 yards and punted eight times, and Joe Burrow was sacked five times. But Burrow, who was limited in two practices last week with a back injury, threw touchdown passes of 32 and 18 yards to Ja'Marr Chase. Chase, who had only two catches for 12 yards in the season opener, caught seven passes for 75 yards. Tee Higgins made five receptions for 95 yards. Chase Brown ran 20 times for 80 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Aaron Glenn: No regrets about how we handled end of regulation against Packers
summary: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's late-game decision-making came under fire in Sunday's overtime loss to the Packers, but he doesn't feel any differently about his choices after a night to sleep on it.
full_text: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's late-game decision-making came under fire in Sunday's overtime loss to the Packers, but he doesn't feel any differently about his choices after a night to sleep on it. After the 20-17 loss, Glenn said he never considered calling a timeout when the Packers faced a fourth down near midfield with about a minute left in regulation. The Packers wound up running the clock down and taking a delay of game penalty before trying a Hail Mary on the final snap of the game. On Sunday, Glenn said he didn't want the team's offense to be backed up after a punt and reiterated that on a Monday video conference while expressing no doubt about the course of action he chose for the team. "Between me and our game management guys, our analytical guys, we talk through those situations quite a bit," Glenn said. "That situation actually came up in a number of our conversations. When we have the punter at the logo, we don't want to put ourselves in a situation where we get our guys in a backed up situation. I know we talk about getting our offense going in that situation, but the thing is they had two timeouts also. If you put yourself in a backed up situation and things don't go as planned, I think you’re giving the other team an opportunity to go out there and make a play. I just felt like that was the right decision to do at that point and we actually wanted to play for overtime when it came to that.” Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said on Sunday that he was "really confused" by how Glenn handled the situation, which could be translated to being really thankful that Glenn allowed the Packers to control how the final minute of regulation played out.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Glenn on Jets taking the ball in OT: I wanted to control the clock
summary: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn faced questions about a number of his decisions after Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers.
full_text: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn faced questions about a number of his decisions after Sunday's 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers. Glenn chose not to use his final timeouts before the end of regulation, which was questioned by many because the Jets had a chance to get the ball back and end the contest without needing to go into extra time. After the game went into overtime, Glenn made another decision that came up for further inspection. The Jets won the toss and opted to receive the kickoff. Quarterback Geno Smith was sacked on the first two plays and the Jets never got the ball back after punting because the Packers drove for a game-winning field goal. After the game, Glenn said he was hoping to leave the Packers with as little time on offense as possible. "Usually, if you can get yourself in a situation like that and you can really control the clock, you can control exactly how they're going to play offense once you go and score," Glenn said, via a transcript from the team. "So, we control the clock, we go run it down; say we run it seven minutes, which we’ve done before, we've run a number of time off the clock, it only gives them so much time to try to rebuttal. We didn’t do a good job in that situation. And plus, to me, once you get the ball and you go down and score, you put the pressure on the other team that has to go ahead and score. But that didn’t happen for us the way I planned." Having Smith drop back to pass is a curious way to control the clock, although the Jets had struggled to find momentum running the ball all afternoon. They had held the Packers' offense in check, however, and Green Bay ended the afternoon with 199 total yards, but Glenn went with his offense and that turned out to be the wrong choice.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos rally for 20-13 win over Jaguars
summary: The Broncos wiped out a 10-point deficit on their way to their first win.
full_text: The Broncos offense took a big step forward in the final quarter of Sunday's home game against the Broncos. After being limited to 16 points through the first seven quarters of the season, the Broncos found themselves down 13-3 to the Jaguars in the fourth quarter. They responded with a pair of touchdown drives in the fourth quarter to take a 20-13 lead over the Jaguars and then put together an impressive four-minute offense to run out the clock on their first win of the season. Quarterback Bo Nix converted one third down with a 29-yard strike to wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and rookie running back Jonah Coleman picked up another one with a 12-yard run that forced the Jaguars to use their final timeout. Coleman was pressed into duty with RJ Harvey inactive and J.K. Dobbins leaving with a hamstring injury, and the fourth-round pick came through with one more big run to allow the Broncos to run out the clock. Coleman also scored the go-ahead touchdown run with 7:21 left to play. It was his first NFL score and he finished the day with 10 carries for 39 yards. That score came after Jaguars kicker Cam Little missed a 54-yard field goal and the first Broncos touchdown came after cornerback Riley Moss picked off Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence. Waddle had two catches on that touchdown drive and finished the day with eight catches for 138 yards. That's the impact Denver was looking for when they traded for Waddle this offseason and it helped get Bo Nix on track after a bad interception in the end zone to kill a first half scoring chance. Nix finished 22-of-31 for 288 yards and a touchdown to tight end Nate Adkins. Neither team scored in the first quarter, but the Jaguars got a touchdown to open the second quarter and took a 10-3 lead into halftime. They extended it to 13-3, but the interception and missed field goal opened the door for the Broncos. Denver's defense forced a punt after Coleman's touchdown put them ahead and the offense was able to slam the door. That's a good development for offensive coordinator Davis Mills and the Broncos will now turn their attention to a Sunday night game against the Rams. The Jaguars will try to stop the bleeding at home against the Patriots.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ja'Marr Chase scores second TD of day
summary: Ja'Marr Chase scored his second touchdown of the day, on an 18-yard pass from Joe Burrow.
full_text: Ja'Marr Chase scored his second touchdown of the day, on an 18-yard pass from Joe Burrow. The Bengals lead 17-3 with 3:03 remaining in the third quarter. Chase, who had only two catches for 12 yards in the season opener, has six receptions for 70 yards. His first touchdown covered 32 yards as he made a poster catch around Texans cornerback Derek Stingley. Chase caught two passes for 26 yards in Week 1 of 2025 before14 receptions for 165 yards and a touchdown the following week against the Jaguars. Burrow, who was limited in two of the three practices last week with a back injury, is 17-of-25 for 179 yards and two touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Todd Monken: "'Browns are gonna Browns' — f—k that"
summary: When NBC analyst Mike Tomlin quoted JuJu Smith-Schuster and said, “Browns is the Browns” after the team’s embarrassing 34-10 loss to open the season, Cleveland head coach Todd Monken said he didn’t see it that way.
full_text: When NBC analyst Mike Tomlin quoted JuJu Smith-Schuster and said, “Browns is the Browns” after the team’s embarrassing 34-10 loss to open the season, Cleveland head coach Todd Monken said he didn’t see it that way. He was a little more emphatic after the club’s 23-19 victory over the Buccaneers on Sunday. “Browns are gonna Browns — fuck that, OK? ” Monken said. “The guys took that to heart.” That was Monken’s walk-off message in his press conference and the end to an answer about how his team was able to stay warm and motivated during the long weather delay. Monken also noted — before the expletive — that practice earlier in the week got chippy. “We had a couple of scuffles Wednesday — which is good,” Monken said. “It’s awesome, because guys didn’t like it. They were a little pissed off, right? You ought to be a little pissed off. Played awful. It wasn’t the standard.” The Browns played a lot better on Sunday. We’ll see if Monken can talk that same talk after next week’s matchup against the Panthers.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Dan Quinn: Commanders are bummed for Jayden Daniels, will rally around Marcus Mariota
summary: Daniels suffered a dislocation to his left (non-throwing) elbow.
full_text: The Commanders don't yet know how serious Jayden Daniels' elbow injury is, but the tone of coach Dan Quinn's post-game comments suggested that Daniels will be out for a while. Quinn talked about the importance of supporting both Daniels and backup quarterback Marcus Mariota, who finished today's game against the Cowboys and will apparently be starting for the Commanders next week. "He did injure his left elbow, it was a dislocation. X-rays showed no fracture. He'll travel back home with the team. More imaging tomorrow," Quinn said after the game. "Man, are we bummed for him. I thought he was really playing his ass off. And we will rally so hard around Marcus until Jayden is back." It's the second year in a row that Daniels has dislocated his non-throwing elbow. Last year, Daniels missed four weeks with the injury, returned for one game, re-aggravated the elbow in that game, and then missed the final four weeks of the season. How much time Daniels misses now remains to be seen, but Quinn summed Daniels' injury up by saying, "It sucks."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Eagles need last-minute comeback to beat Titans 24-20
summary: It wasn't easy, but the Eagles pulled out a win in Tennessee.
full_text: The Eagles were expected to beat the Titans easily today in Tennessee. Philadelphia won, but it wasn't easy. The Titans were competitive throughout the game and took a 20-17 lead with two minutes to go, but the Eagles came back with a nine-play, 65-yard drive that ended with Jalen Hurts hitting Darius Cooper in the end zone for the game-winning touchdown in a 24-20 victory. The Eagles got next to nothing from Saquon Barkley, who was injured on Philadelphia's first offensive snap, missed the rest of the first half, and was limited in the second half. Barkley finished with four carries for nine yards and one catch for 11 yards. Titans quarterback Cam Ward showed promise, completing 13 of 20 passes for 183 yards and also running for two touchdowns. The game ended, however, with Ward setting up to throw a Hail Mary and getting nowhere close. The Eagles are 2-0, but neither win has been particularly impressive. The Titans are 0-2, but they have to feel like today's game showed progress.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Patriots shut down Steelers' offense, win 20-3
summary: Aaron Rodgers could do nothing today in New England.
full_text: The Steelers' offense was putrid today against the Patriots, with Aaron Rodgers able to do nothing in a 20-3 loss. It was an ugly performance by Pittsburgh that will raise serious questions about whether Rodgers, in what he says is his final NFL season, is going to be able to lead them to anything better than mediocrity. Today, the Steelers were sub-mediocre. Rodgers managed just 187 yards on 23-of-39 passing, with no touchdowns and one interception, and he also lost a fumble that New England's Elijah Ponder picked up and returned for a touchdown. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye wasn't great either, completing 14 of 22 passes for 208 yards, with no touchdown and one interception. But the Patriots got 76 rushing yards from TreVeyon Henderson and 43 rushing yards from Rhamondre Stevenson, and that was enough to control the game on a day when the Steelers' offense kept punting. The Patriots and Steelers are both 1-1 through two weeks, but the Patriots have to feel a lot better about where they are going. The Steelers look like they're going nowhere.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Shane Steichen defends decisions to kick off, kick field goal in overtime
summary: The Colts lost 33-30 in overtime after giving the Chiefs the ball first, then settling for a field goal on their own possession.
full_text: Colts coach Shane Steichen chose to kick in Sunday night's overtime loss to the Chiefs. Questioned about those decisions after the game, Steichen defended his process even though his team lost the game. Steichen's two choices came when the Colts won the coin toss and chose to kick off to start overtime, and then when the Colts settled for a game-tying field goal rather than trying to score a game-winning touchdown at the end of their only overtime possession. On the choice to kick off after winning the toss, Steichen said he didn't want to score first because it would be too easy for Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes to move the ball down the field if the Chiefs knew they were going to go for it on every fourth down. "If we go first with it, Mahomes gets four downs going the other way, so we wanted to play defense there and know we had four downs," Steichen said. "It can go either way in those situations, but we decided to kick off there, and we had a chance at the end. Didn't finish it." On the Chiefs' opening possession, they kicked a field goal. That meant on the Colts' possession, a touchdown would win the game, while a field goal would tie it and give the ball back to the Chiefs. The Colts marched down the field and faced a fourth-and-8 at the Chiefs' 15-yard line, and Steichen initially kept his offense on the field, appearing ready to go for the win. But after seeing how the Chiefs' defense lined up, Steichen told his offense to take a delay of game penalty and settled for a field goal. "It was fourth-and-8, had a play called, had to love the look to run it there, and if not, we took the delay of game there and kicked the field goal there to tie it," Steichen said. That tied the game 30-30, and Mahomes proceeded to move the Chiefs into field goal range, where Harrison Butker's kick gave Kansas City the 33-30 win. Steichen thinks he made the right choices, even if he doesn't like the result.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Key overtime ruling in Colts-Chiefs ignored the "clear and obvious" standard
summary: Chiefs should have won the game after LaQuon Treadwell's fumble.
full_text: The NFL centralized replay review in order to ensure that a consistent standard will apply when a second look is being taken at rulings on the field. And the consistent standard is, or should be, that the available evidence makes it "clear and obvious" that the officials got it wrong in real time. Sometimes, that standard applies. Sometimes, it doesn't. When it comes to the play that gave the Colts a chance to beat the Chiefs in overtime, it didn't. It wasn't clear and obvious that the officials made a mistake when ruling that Colts receiver Laquon Treadwell had caught the ball, landed on a knee/leg without being touched, and fumbled. The key question was whether Treadwell was down by contact. Which required a frame-by-frame review as to whether he had been touched by Chiefs cornerback L'Jarius Sneed after Treadwell satisfied the multi-step process of making the catch. It was not clear and obvious that Sneed had touched Treadwell after Treadwell had completed the act of catching the ball. The fact that nearly three minutes passed from the announcement by referee Craig Wrolstad of the ruling on the field and the issuance of the final verdict shows that it was not clear and obvious. The standard often has been summed up like this — the ruling on the field should be overturned by replay only if 50 drunks in a bar would have agreed that a mistake had been made. Here's what is clear and obvious: Whoever made the decision in New York re-officiated the play from scratch, straining to conclude that Sneed was still contacting Treadwell after Treadwell had secured possession of the ball. The league got lucky that the Colts opted not to attack the end zone after getting an unwarranted reprieve. Ultimately, the league got lucky that the Chiefs won the game. If they had lost, it would have been a much bigger deal. It should still be a big deal, because it exposes the presence of a flaw in the replay machinery. The standard is "clear and obvious." It was not "clear and obvious" that the ruling on the field was incorrect. The game should have been over. And here's the next-level take. Given the persistent belief in some circles that the league and the officials favor the Chiefs, did the person who made the final decision on replay review (whoever it was) err on the side of making a finding that runs counter to the narrative, if only to avoid a Monday news cycle that would have included more than a few people spouting off the theory that, yet again, the NFL had found a way to help the Chiefs? Regardless of how it happened and why it happened and who specifically was responsible for it happening, the league in this instance did not honor the standard that is supposed to apply to replay review. The ruling on the field did not amount to a "clear and obvious" mistake. The game should have ended with the ruling that Treadwell had made the catch and fumbled the ball.
author: Mike Florio

title: Dak Prescott: "Super honored" to set Cowboys TD record, want to double it
summary: Dak Prescott owned most of the career quarterbacking records for the Cowboys before Sunday's game against the Commanders kicked off and he broke one of the other ones late in the fourth quarter.
full_text: Dak Prescott owned most of the career quarterbacking records for the Cowboys before Sunday's game against the Commanders kicked off and he broke one of the other ones late in the fourth quarter. Prescott's 24-yard touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb was the 249th of his career, which broke a tie with Tony Romo for the most of any player in Cowboys history. It also put the finishing touches on a 37-20 Cowboys win and Prescott discussed how much the record means to him while wearing a Roger Staubach jersey at his postgame press conference. Prescott also said he hopes to add a lot more touchdowns to the ledger before he's done in Dallas. "I'm blessed, honored," Prescott said, via the team's website. "As I told you earlier in the week, records are meant to be broken. This is my time to break this one. Pretty cool to do it against the team I threw my first touchdown against ten years ago or so. Definitely humbling, something I don't take for granted. The great history of this organization, of the past quarterbacks before me. . . . Super, super honored. Super thankful. God's great. Not taking it lightly. But as I told you, it's just the beginning. I want to double it and plan to play for a while, so just getting started ." Prescott's place in the franchise record book will be secure regardless of what happens from here, but his place in the history of the franchise overall is still lacking the signature postseason wins that predecessors like Staubach and Troy Aikman have in their bios. Sunday's win doesn't rank at that level, but it helps the Cowboys' bid to get Prescott in position to deliver one.
author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos think Jaylen Waddle's big day "only the tip of the iceberg"
summary: The Broncos traded for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle this offseason in order to add more explosiveness to their offense, but Waddle wasn't able to make a difference in their Week 1 loss to the Chiefs.
full_text: '' The Broncos traded for wide receiver Jaylen Waddle this offseason in order to add more explosiveness to their offense, but Waddle wasn't able to make a difference in their Week 1 loss to the Chiefs. Week 2 provided more proof of the concept that the Broncos had in mind. Waddle had five catches of at least 14 yards, including a 49-yard leaping grab over a defender to set up Denver's first points of the day in the second quarter. Waddle wound up with eight catches for 138 yards as the Broncos came back from 10 points down to beat the Jaguars 20-13 at home on Sunday. Head coach Sean Payton said Waddle's impact on the game was "significant" and fellow wideout Courtland Sutton said that he thinks even bigger things are coming. "I think that's only the tip of the iceberg for him," Sutton said, via the team's website. "We have more plays in our back pocket that we didn't even get to get to. And for him to be able go out there and do what he did and us be able to have the success, and him being able to go and put together a very efficient day today, it was very promising. And I look forward to seeing where that goes the rest of the season." The first seven quarters of the Broncos' season produced 16 points and 444 yards, which set the stage for a lot of hand-wringing about the state of the offense if the fourth quarter on Sunday went in a similar direction. The Broncos picked up 124 yards and 14 points to pull out the win, which makes it easier to talk about the brightness of a future with Waddle playing a central role in the passing game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patrick Mahomes: We showed we can do everything offensively
summary: The Chiefs cruised to a win in their season opener against the Broncos thanks in large part to running back Kenneth Walker's big night and they moved to 2-0 in a much closer game against the Colts on Sunday night.
full_text: The Chiefs cruised to a win in their season opener against the Broncos thanks in large part to running back Kenneth Walker's big night and they moved to 2-0 in a much closer game against the Colts on Sunday night. Walker shone again in the 33-30 overtime victory and finished the game with 178 yards from scrimmage. The big difference with the Chiefs offense this time around was that quarterback Patrick Mahomes joined him in putting up big numbers. Mahomes threw for 382 yards, which is his most in a game since the 2023 season, and Walker was one of five players to catch at least four passes over the course of the night. After the game, Mahomes said that Walker's presence has helped open things up offensively for the Chiefs in all phases because of how much stress the defense is under from snap to snap. "It's fun for me ," Mahomes said. "Him running the ball, our offensive line driving off the ball the way they're driving off — it's making the defense have to account for that. If not, we're going to run the ball for 200 yards or whatever we did the week before. You want to be able to do it all. We showcased that we can throw the ball down the field, we can play action and can also still run the ball. I thought coach [Andy] Reid and coach [Eric] Bieniemy did a great job calling the game, mixing it in everywhere so they couldn’t get a good gauge on what we were doing.” The Chiefs will have to go on the road for the first time next weekend, although they'll be heading to Miami to face the 0-2 Dolphins and that should provide the offense with an opportunity to keep things rolling at a high level.
author: Josh Alper

title: Patrick Mahomes tried to take advantage when Colts' captain didn't know OT coin toss rule
summary: The NFL is in its second year of its current overtime format, but some players still haven't learned the rules.
full_text: The NFL is in its second year of its current overtime format, but some players still haven't learned the rules. And Chiefs captain Patrick Mahomes tried to take advantage of that on Sunday night. Colts captain Cam Bynum called tails on the overtime coin toss, and when it came up tails, he had the choice to kick, receive or pick a goal to defend. But Bynum chose none of those, instead saying "defer." Deferring is only an option for the pre-game coin toss, when the team that wins the toss can choose to defer its choice of kicking or receiving until the second half kickoff. Deferring is not an option before overtime. As soon as Mahomes heard Bynum's mistake, he yelled to referee Craig Wrolstad, "They get the ball!" Mahomes figured that if Bynum was going to defer the Colts' choice, then the Chiefs would make their choice, which was to kick off and get the ball second in overtime. Unfortunately for Mahomes, Wrolstad asked Bynum follow-up questions until Bynum understood. "Would you like the ball? Would you like the ball? Would you like to play defense?" Wrolstad asked Bynum. Eventually, Bynum said the Colts wanted to start on defense — which is technically not a choice at the start of overtime, but Wrolstad knew Bynum meant the Colts wanted to kick off, and Wrolstad accepted that. "Indianapolis won the toss, they would like to play defense," Wrolstad announced to the crowd. After the game, Mahomes confirmed that he was trying to take advantage of Bynum's mistake. "You're supposed to say kick off. You can't defer in overtime. If you defer, then it's my decision. So I was like, then I want to kick off," Mahomes said. "You're supposed to say kick off, he said defer, so I said, Well, I'll kick off then. That's the rules, I guess, but it didn't work." Mahomes credited Mike Frazier, the Chiefs' longtime statistical analysis coordinator, for making sure the Chiefs' players always know exactly what their options are in such situations. Mahomes knew the rule, and Bynum didn't.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ranking 5 worst losses in Week 2: Falcons, Buccaneers and Commanders all in the running
summary: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers sputtered in New England, while Jayden Daniels suffered another major injury setback as ugly Sunday performances piled up across the league
full_text:
The second NFL Sunday of the year was much different than the first. Last Sunday featured the most combined points per game (53.3) in Week 1 of NFL history, while Week 2 didn't quite deliver.
The Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears had to play in a torrential downpour and mustered just 12 total points. The Houston Texans couldn't score a single touchdown against the new-look Cincinnati Bengals defense, and Aaron Rodgers couldn't get the Pittsburgh Steelers into the end zone against the New England Patriots either. The Atlanta Falcons were again atrocious, and the Los Angeles Chargers were again upset by a team they probably should have defeated.
There were several bad losses on Sunday and a lot of disappointing results. They say Week 1 is a liar, but many teams should hope that Week 2 is the actual liar. Let's power-rank the five worst losses from around the NFL this past Sunday.
Historical data courtesy of CBS Sports Research
The Steelers fell to the Patriots in New England, 20-3. It matched the fewest points in any game started and finished in Aaron Rodgers' career, going back to Week 1 of 2021.
Rodgers completed 23 of 39 passes for 187 yards and one interception, while fumbling twice. The Steelers went 2-of-12 on third downs, while recording just 235 yards of total offense. Pittsburgh has just 499 total yards through two weeks, which are the fewest through two games in Rodgers' Hall of Fame career.
It's not like the Patriots were fantastic either. They converted just four of 12 third downs, while Drake Maye threw for 208 yards and an interception. Fans want to know where the MVP finalist they had last year went.
So, what's the ceiling for the Steelers? They have a new head coach, but it's tough not to judge this team like we have the Steelers squads of recent years. This is a team that can potentially steal a playoff spot, but it isn't a legitimate contender. Rodgers is looking his age, the offensive line is struggling to protect and DK Metcalf can't catch.
Patriots defense pushed the Steelers back from 3rd & 7 to 4th & 43 😳 PITvsNE on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cuwaepRRDX
If you want me to overreact to Week 2, I can definitely do that with the Washington Commanders . You may say that a 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys shouldn't qualify for one of the worst losses of the week, but with what we saw on Sunday afternoon, the Commanders are cooked.
Washington is 0-2 for the first time since 2019, and 2-12 over its past 14 games. Dak Prescott may have proved that this is still one of the worst defenses in the NFL, as he threw for 279 yards, four touchdowns and just five incompletions.
The real reason the Commanders make this list is because star quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow again. Initial X-rays showed no fracture, but could he miss more time than he did in 2025? Daniels didn't have surgery on his elbow last year. Should he have? If he does now, how long will that keep him off the field?
Commanders fans can't be feeling optimistic about how the season is going, and Sunday was a disaster. They are already without star left tackle Laremy Tunsil , while his replacement, Brandon Coleman , left yesterday with a finger injury. Meanwhile, star guard Sam Cosmi is in concussion protocol.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to the Bengals in Week 1 after losing the turnover battle 4-1, and the Cleveland Browns in Week 2 provided a great bounce-back opportunity. Not only is Cleveland perceived to be one of the worst teams in the NFL, but this was also a revenge game for quarterback Baker Mayfield , who was drafted No. 1 overall by the Browns and then ditched by the organization for Deshaun Watson . There was no way Baker and the Bucs were going to lose as 8.5-point favorites. Right? Right?!
The Bucs fell to the Browns on Sunday, 23-19, while Mayfield threw for 182 yards, one touchdown and one interception. The Bucs are 0-2 for the first time since 2014, and 3-10 in their past 13 games after starting the 2025 campaign 5-1. Mayfield has committed 17 turnovers in his past 13 contests and is now 0-2 vs. his former team!
Everything about this game was gross, with a two-hour, 12-minute lightning delay late in the fourth quarter. It set the stage for Mayfield to lead a game-winning drive on a rain-soaked field, but that possession ended on downs at the Browns' 20-yard line.
What's going on with Todd Bowles' defense? Watson completed 24 of 30 passes for 238 yards and two touchdowns in what was his first win since Week 2 of 2024. It was actually reported before the game that Cleveland could be looking to make a change at quarterback depending on how Sunday went!
You don't want to overreact to Week 2 too much, but Bowles may be on the hottest seat in the NFL, Mayfield isn't playing up to the contract he just signed, and the Buccaneers don't look like the top dog in the NFC South. That honor may belong to the New Orleans Saints , who just upset the Baltimore Ravens . Or maybe it's the Carolina Panthers , who won the division last year. Right now, it's definitely not the Bucs. You can't lose to the BROWNS in your home opener.
If we were making a list of most disappointing teams through two weeks, the Chargers are likely headlining. They lost to the Arizona Cardinals in their season opener and then to the Las Vegas Raiders this past Sunday, 26-14. That makes the Chargers the first team in NFL history to start 0-2 with losses to 14-loss teams from the previous season.
It's clear that Justin Herbert hasn't been good. He threw for 192 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions on Sunday, but he's far from the lone issue. Not only is his offensive line and wide receiving corps struggling, but this Chargers defense has been a disappointment. Not many people saw Tre Tucker exploding for 119 yards receiving and a touchdown on five catches yesterday!
What's even more disappointing is that the Chargers' schedule gets much tougher immediately. At 0-2, are they done?
This eight-week stretch features three of last year's four conference championship teams, along with the last four NFL MVPs in Matthew Stafford , Josh Allen , Patrick Mahomes and Lamar Jackson . Best of luck to Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers in turning this thing around.
The Falcons are the worst team in the NFL right now, and they fell to the Panthers in their home opener on Sunday, 34-3.
With Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr . still out, it's been mostly Cooper Rush under center. With him, Atlanta has registered the worst passer rating (38.2) by any team through two games since the 2019 Miami Dolphins . The Falcons are apparently the fourth team since play-by-play was first tracked in 1978 to not have a red zone drive through the first two games of a season!
When the Falcons finally yanked Rush and inserted undrafted rookie Jack Strand at quarterback on Sunday, the fans in Mercedes-Benz Stadium responded with a standing ovation. Strand then threw a pick-six on his first NFL passing attempt.
Falcons fans…The moment you’ve all been waiting for…here’s Jack Strand pic.twitter.com/wk0px7dYWH
Rush and Strand combined to complete 18 of 32 passes for 129 yards and three interceptions in Week 2. It's hard to watch Drake London and Bijan Robinson shake their heads in frustration on the sideline. Sure, the Falcons offense should be "better" with Penix or Tagovailoa in, but how much better? I still think the Falcons are one of the worst teams in the NFL, and Sunday proved it.
You can be happy your favorite team is not the Falcons, but they are about to become a league-wide problem. Atlanta is scheduled to play its next THREE games all in prime time! The NFL needs to step in and do something.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Eagles lineman calls for change after 157-degree Titans turf melts players' cleats
summary: The turf at Nissan Stadium reportedly reached 157 degrees, and Nick Siriani needed an IV
full_text:
There was plenty of inclement weather around the NFL this weekend. The Browns vs. Buccaneers game was suspended for two hours due to a massive storm, and rain poured throughout in Vikings vs. Bears and Packers vs. Jets games.
But the most dangerous? That was in Nashville, where temperatures reached 95 degrees -- with a heat index of 105 -- for the Eagles vs. Titans game. According to the Fox broadcast, the temperature of the Nissan Stadium turf reached 157 degrees, a quite literally scorching number. Several players reported their cleats melting during the game, and Eagles coach Nick Sirianni received an IV to keep hydrated. Afterward, Eagles standout tackle Jordan Mailata called for change, per ESPN .
"I've never thought about how hot a stadium can be if it's turf," said Mailata, Philadelphia's NFLPA rep last year. "[The heat] just sits there and bounces up into you. We've got to bring it up. This is why we want all grass fields, to create a standard of play in the league where we're not putting players in dangerous positions if we don't have to."
Fellow Philadelphia offensive lineman Cam Jurgens said he went through multiple pairs of cleats during the Eagles' 24-20 win, and Titans safety Amani Hooker said the midsoles of his cleats "melted completely off." Mailata said he rolled his ankles twice and wondered if it was due to his own cleats melting, too.
"Halftime was like a NASCAR pit crew helping me get ready for the second half," Jurgens said. "That turf was just radiating."
The lasting image of the contest -- other than Jalen Hurts ' game-winning touchdown to Darius Cooper -- was Titans players getting their cleats sprayed with water.
When in Nashville… 😂 pic.twitter.com/NWepuwjpkP
The lasting quote? "It was hot as s--- and everybody was hot as s---," Sirianni said.
This was the second straight week temperatures crept up to dangerous levels -- in general, but especially on the Nissan Stadium turf. Last week, Jeffery Simmons ' cleats melted, a development Mailata didn't initially believe until he experienced it himself.
Players have long wanted natural fields, a position that only strengthened this offseason , when the World Cup was played on natural grass, often in stadiums that play NFL games on turf.
NFLPA president JC Tretter , a former NFL player, told ESPN , "There is something there that impacts the body" more on turf than on grass, and that's in normal conditions. Add in extreme heat, and the turf provided even more danger Sunday.

title: Falcons' Drake London gets into heated exchange with fan during blowout loss to Panthers
summary: London said the person said personal things to him as Atlanta fell 0-2 on the season
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons aren't exactly off to the best start for the 2026 regular season. It's certainly not the best sign when your fans are chanting for the fourth-string quarterback to come in, which is what was happening in their Week 2 34-3 loss to the Carolina Panthers .
When teams are struggling as much as the Falcons are, tension rises, and tempers can be more touchy than usual. That's what happened when Falcons wide receiver Drake London got into a verbal confrontation from the sidelines with someone in the home stands on Sunday.
It looked like London was yelling profanities to someone in the Mercedes-Benz Stadium crowd, as his teammate, wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus , held him back.
After the game, London said the fan said "personal stuff" to him, and he felt disrespected. The receiver added that he knows reacting is "not the right thing to do."
"I'm going to be honest here, I don't take light to disrespect at all," London said. "I don't care who you are. I'm a man, too, at the end of the day. So, if you want to get on a personal level, I can get there, too, but it's not the right thing to do. So, I got to take accountability for that, and I got to push forward and be the bigger man in some of those situations.
"But with how the game was going and what was said to me, I don't like it," London said.
When asked if it was a fan, London said, "It was somebody."
London finished the game with four receptions for 51 yards, the most receiving yards by far for the Falcons in Week 2. Again, not the best offensive showing.
With Michael Penix Jr . still sidelined as he recovers from an ACL injury and Tua Tagovailoa dealing with an oblique injury, it was once again veteran Cooper Rush at the helm. He went 10-of-17 for 86 yards, two interceptions and a lost fumble. He was eventually benched for undrafted rookie Jack Strand , who didn't fare much better with a pick of his own.
"I think we as playmakers, us in the backfield, us on the outside, on the wing, we got to go out there and make plays regardless," London said. "We're all in the league for a reason, right? We're all good football players. I don't care if you're fourth string or you're the starter."
This offseason, London signed a four-year, $141 million contract extension with the Falcons, keeping him there through the 2030 season.
Up next for the Falcons are three primetime games. First up are the Green Bay Packers , followed by the New Orleans Saints and Baltimore Ravens .

title: Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels injured in Week 2: What's the outlook for Bears, Commanders signal callers?
summary: Williams hurt his hamstring on a run; Daniels dislocated his elbow after an awkward fall
full_text:
Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels will forever be intertwined as the No. 1 and No. 2 picks, respectively, in the quarterback-loaded 2024 NFL Draft . But right now they're unfortunately tied together by a different bond: Both young stars suffered injuries in Week 2, with Williams hurting his hamstring on a non-contact play and Daniels dislocating his left elbow while trying to brace his fall after getting stepped on by an offensive lineman.
For Williams, it's his first significant NFL injury; he has started all 36 games (including playoffs) since being drafted by Chicago. For Daniels, it's the fourth significant injury he has suffered since the start of last season and his second left elbow dislocation in the last 11 months.
Both players will be out for at least some time, though further testing -- beginning Monday -- will provide a clearer timeline.
Playing on a rain-soaked field, Williams took a bootleg dropback and outraced Andrew Van Ginkel to the edge. But in doing so, he pulled his right hamstring and quickly went down in pain. He needed help getting to the sideline and was then carted off the field.
Caleb Williams - Took a long stride to avoid the tackle and went down non-contact. Not seeing too much at the knee. This one could just be a hamstring injury but I’ll keep analyzing it. pic.twitter.com/rGwh2a1xmD
Caleb Williams had to be helped off the field after that last play. 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/ecsgk7fwdi
The non-contact aspect was initially the most worrying part, but he and the Bears appear to have very much avoided the worst-case scenario.
You could kind of see in real time," coach Ben Johnson said. "I'm actually happy it's nothing with the knee; that was my first inclination. But yeah, the hamstring could be pretty damaging as well. So, we'll see how bad it is tomorrow and we'll go from there."
Daniels, meanwhile, suffered a dislocation of his left elbow in a very similar manner to the way he suffered his first one last year. This time, he got stepped on by left guard Chris Paul and, trying to brace is unnatural fall, put his left arm on the ground. Viewer discretion is advised below.
#JaydenDaniels @Commanders By video, clear left elbow dislocation Similar to last season Joint comes out easier 2nd time Original ligament tear heals "looser" Will be ruled OUT 2nd half #WASvsDAL pic.twitter.com/777bekF7pC
Daniels stayed down for several minutes before being carted off with a towel draped over his head and face. Coach Dan Quinn said X-rays showed no fracture and that Daniels would fly home with the team and undergo further testing on Monday.
Several reporters noted Williams (who did not meet with the media postgame) walked through the locker room without crutches and perhaps a slight limp . That's obviously better than "on crutches" or "with a significant limp," but hamstrings can be tricky, and the testing will reveal more.
On the "Sunday Night Football" broadcast, NBC's Mike Florio said, "It could be as slight as a grade 1 [hamstring strain]." That's the lowest-level strain (out of three).
Per the Princeton Sports & Family Medicine website , for a Grade 1 strain ...
Williams very much fits the high-speed athlete description, though. He is a mobile quarterback whose movement skills are paramount to everything he does. Johnson uses a variety of dropbacks, including from under center and rollouts like the one Williams got hurt on. If it is indeed a Grade 1 strain, Williams would likely miss at least one game, but perhaps more if the Bears opt for caution. And there's reason to opt for caution, as hamstring injuries can linger or be re-aggravated.
Last year, coincidentally, Daniels missed one game with a hamstring strain. If it is indeed a Grade 1 strain, Williams could be looking at a game or two missed, but again, there are several factors at play.
A Grade 2 strain would cause more time to be missed. In 2016, wide receiver A.J. Green suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain in Week 11 and did not play the rest of the season (though he had initially planned to return after a few weeks). In 2011, Patrick Willis suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain and missed three games, which would represent the earlier side of the return timeline.
Daniels was out for three weeks last year after suffering his first left elbow dislocation , though three things are at play here:
Daniels could again go the route of wearing a brace, though as the second bullet point shows, landing on the elbow again would be extremely painful. Football is an unpredictable sport, as Daniels' getting stepped on shows. Quarterbacks get hit at odd angles, and Daniels, as a player who runs a lot, can be prone to even more hits. The fact that this injury happened on a fluke play and Daniels had been so good about avoiding contact as a runner (he had 69 rushing yards in the first half alone) makes the injury all the more devastating. You simply can't control or predict how and why players get hurt in the manners they do.
Chao has a good explainer for why Daniels could miss less time -- perhaps a similar timetable to last year -- and play with a brace if he opts to avoid surgery again (or push surgery off until the offseason).
Jayden Daniels could return sooner than expected with an elbow brace, but he’ll likely need it for the rest of the season. Why surgery could still be considered, and why not operating after the first dislocation wasn’t a mistake. pic.twitter.com/4lhBk2dmuk
Again, like Williams, Daniels' testing will provide more detail. Unlike Williams, though, Daniels could be facing a larger decision regarding the long-term health of his injured shoulder.
Tyson Bagent will start for the Bears for as long as Williams is out. Marcus Mariota will start for the Commanders until Daniels returns.

title: Deshaun Watson responds to critics after win over Buccaneers: 'Monken said what he said'
summary: Watson enjoyed his highest passer rating in a game since September 2023, despite ongoing criticisms
full_text:
It was personal for the Cleveland Browns following Sunday's win in Tampa , a potential momentum-booster for first-year coach Todd Monken and his franchise quarterback, Deshaun Watson .
Monken's expletive-enforced postgame response to a take from Mike Tomlin was triggering for a franchise that has faced criticism nationally as one of the NFL's also-rans not expected to do much this season.
"I wouldn't say it was a topic of conversation, but Monk said what he said and that's how we all feel," said Watson, who threw for 238 yards and two touchdowns, including the go-ahead score with 3:51 to play.
After Monken refused to name a starting quarterback entering the season, Watson's numbers were pedestrian during last week's opening loss to Jacksonville and led to the former first-round pick saying outsiders have put unfair pressure on Cleveland's offense.
"I think the media has this expectation that I'm supposed to throw [for] 400 yards and five touchdowns every week. So, until that happens, I guess it's going to be the same situation," Watson said prior to Sunday's bounce-back victory. "Again, my job is to make sure I'm operating well so we can try to get a win and keep moving forward from there. Finding completions, operating well."
Watson carried out the game plan to near perfection against the Buccaneers , completing 80% of his throws and keeping the Browns on schedule while out-performing 2025 MVP candidate and former Brown Baker Mayfield .
"The attitude was amazing, it was good, you felt the energy," Watson said. "Guys want to win. Guys are passionate. It's going to be like that, especially when you have brothers in the locker room that are all together. Even me and Monk went head to head a couple times, but it's all good, it's all love."
ESPN reported prior to kickoff Sunday that the franchise was still evaluating who will start at quarterback in Week 3 against the Panthers . It's hard to fathom Monken moving to Shedeur Sanders after Watson's turnover-free outing on the road, however.
Monken defended Watson throughout fall camp and said after the season-opening loss he never anticipated his team's quarterback situation being a week-to-week issue.
Following Watson's best performance —  121.9 passer rating — since Sept. 24, 2023, he has made it easy on his coach in prep for Cleveland's next opponent.
"I'm so happy for him," Monken said of Watson. "Good for him. Good for 22 months working his (tail) off to get to where he's at. I'm gonna leave it at that."
Monken didn't officially name Watson as Cleveland's home opener against Carolina next week, but it's obvious which signal caller gives the Browns the best shot moving forward after Sunday's victory.
Monken's relationship with Watson was always going to be tested early in Cleveland. He inherited a quarterback room carrying expectations, then doubled down on Watson after an ugly opener.
This partnership remains a week-to-week evaluation, but Cleveland finally saw a glimpse of what Monken envisioned: Watson playing decisively and extending drives, which is exactly what the Browns' starting quarterback acknowledged as his primary job after Week 1.
"Our relationship continues to grow every day," Watson said. "The more we talk, the more we're around each other, the more we go through certain situations ... we're going to build that. That's part of this game and this league. You're going to have some ups and downs, but at the end of the day, we've got love and respect for each other."
author: Brad Crawford

title: Browns' Deshaun Watson-led win over Bucs was the worst thing for Cleveland in 2026
summary: Watson's victory robs the Browns of seeing what they have in their young quarterbacks before a QB decision in 2027
full_text:
Sometimes in life and in football, short-term success can get in the way of long-term growth and development. That's exactly what happened to the Cleveland Browns (1-1) in Week 2.
Quarterback Deshaun Watson has not come within the same zip code of the expectations the Browns bestowed on him when they traded a package centered around three first-round picks to the Houston Texans to acquire his services before extending him on a five-year, fully guaranteed $230 million contract. That's on top of his extensive off-field legal issues . It appeared as though perhaps a second straight down week for Cleveland after getting punked 34-10 in Week 1 at the Jacksonville Jaguars might have led to curtains on the Watson era ahead of the team's home opener in Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers (1-1).
Instead, Watson was able to conjure a faint outline of the three-time Pro Bowler that he was with the Houston Texans from 2018 to 2020. Now at 31 years old in 2026 after needing season-ending shoulder surgery (2023) and multiple Achilles tears (2024 and 2025), a less spry Watson cobbled together 238 yards passing and two passing touchdowns on 24-of-30 (80%) in a 23-19 weather-delayed win over his predecessor Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-2).
"I'm right where I want to be," Watson said postgame on Sunday, via ESPN . ... "I was making plays. I told Monk at halftime to just trust me with the ball in my hands and let me just go out there and operate."
Watson may be right where he wants to be, but the Browns are still a ways away from having any type of long-term success. And Watson's glimmer of hope on Sunday may have even set them back in getting there.
In the second half, Watson backed up what he told Monken at halftime, completing 17 of his final 21 throws for 183 yards, both of his touchdowns and 18 of his team-high 22 rushing yards. That provided his head coach a short-term high Sunday evening.
"He [Watson] played his rear end off in the second half, and he's doing it without us running the ball very well. ... That's hard. That's hard to win [without the run game]... I thought he was in control, not perfect," Monken said postgame, via ESPN . "None of us are. ... I'm very happy for Deshaun, and I'm happy for us and the team."
After the victory, first-year Browns head coach Todd Monken clapped back with an impassioned remark at ex- Steelers coach Mike Tomlin's recent "Browns is the Browns" diss .
"Browns are gonna Browns. F--k that! The guys took that to heart," Monken said postgame .
However, a get-right win against a struggling Mayfield, who has 17 turnovers in his past 13 games, doesn't mean Cleveland was vindicated for starting the season with Watson or will be by continuing to stick by him as their starting quarterback. Just days ago, Monken was having to defend his decision to start Watson in Week 2 by saying the players in his locker didn't have a choice as to who would be the starting quarterback between Watson and 2025 fifth-round pick Shedeur Sanders . That's because Watson has been profiled as one of the NFL's bottom-two quarterbacks during his Browns tenure, based on multiple efficiency statistics.
Expected points added (EPA) per dropback
* Only Zach Wilson ranks worse ** Only Cam Ward ranks worse *** Only Justin Fields ranks worse
Sunday was just his fifth game in 21 starts across the last five seasons with a completion percentage over 70% and just his fourth in the same span with a 100-plus passer rating. Watson has yet to rack up a 300-yard performance as a Brown. Cleveland knows what Watson is: a once-great quarterback who lost his powers and likely won't ever be able to regain them because of his mobility limitations after multiple Achilles tears and being on the wrong side of 30. Plus, Watson's off-field skeletons make it difficult for people inside and outside of the franchise to rally behind him.
70-plus completion percentage
There's a running clock for Cleveland and their time with Watson, and it will hit zero on March 11 at 4 p.m. EST at the start of the NFL's new league year. That's when they can void his contract with a post-June 1 designation and kick him to the curb with a limited dead salary cap responsibility of $34.663 million in 2027. Knowing exactly when their relationship with Watson will end should give Monken and the Browns' front office the clarity to bench their financial and public relations albatross at the next sign of failure. That very well could occur in Week 3 against the Panthers after they treated Atlanta Falcons quarterbacks, veteran Cooper Rush and undrafted rookie Jack Strand , like a couple of chew toys in a 34-3 romp. Carolina linebacker Devin Lloyd became the first player since 2012 with multiple interceptions, an interception return touchdown and a sack in a single game.
If something similar happens to Watson in Week 3, it won't be surprising. However, that will mean another week lost where they could have seen what they have in Sanders and/or uber-athletic but raw sixth-round rookie Taylen Green , They should have them starting alongside the rest of their young core of playmakers before having to decide if and/or when in the 2027 NFL Draft to invest one of their two first-round picks in a new quarterback. Every win and glimmer of offensive production with Watson is fool's gold that only delays the inevitable divorce between him and the Browns. That's why wins with Watson are still long-term losses.
