title: Browns vs Bucs Week 2: Lot of winners, a few losers as CLE pulls upset over Baker Mayfield
summary: Our beloved Barry Shuck will not be able to complete his weekly Brownies and Frownies for Weeks 2 and 3 of the Cleveland Browns 2026 season. That means you are stuck with Jared for Week 2’s game versus the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Can the Browns perform better in Week 2 after getting destroyed in Week […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) greets Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) after a game at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Our beloved Barry Shuck will not be able to complete his weekly Brownies and Frownies for Weeks 2 and 3 of the Cleveland Browns 2026 season. That means you are stuck with Jared for Week 2’s game versus the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Can the Browns perform better in Week 2 after getting destroyed in Week 1? Facing off against their former top overall pick, QB Baker Mayfield , Cleveland was not facing a vengeful player , but had a ton to prove after a terrible start to the season. With rumors that Shedeur Sanders would likely replace Deshaun Watson in Week 3 , unless the veteran could have a good game against the Bucs, a lot was on the line in Week 2. After weathering (pun intended) a long delay , the Browns pulled off a huge victory over the Bucs, 23-19 . Week 2 Winners – Brownies DT Mason Graham – The second year lineman, and GM Andrew Berry’s top pick in 2025, just keeps making plays with his second sack of the year, after just a half sack last year. Graham also was a big part of pushing the pocket throughout the game, adding three tackles with his sack. DE Derek Barnett – Far from perfect, the veteran late addition lost contain early in the game, but was a stable presence on the outside, helping to create uncomfortable pockets for Mayfield. WR Denzel Boston – Joining some history in Week 2, Boston not only had the big 55-yard touchdown, but was a reliable receiver on important downs for his quarterback. Boston’s size and smooth route running make him an easy target, and his hands make him a QB’s best friend. Boston had the most receiving yards in the game (95). QB Deshaun Watson’s 2nd half after QB sweep for 1st down – Who knows what happens after Week 2, but when Watson took the snap and ran for eight yards on 3rd and 3 early in the third quarter, everything seemed to change. After that, Watson completed five straight passes before Boston had a touchdown pass dislodged in the endzone. For the game, the veteran had one of his best games in Cleveland: 24/30, 238 yards, and two touchdowns. CB Tyson Campbell’s toughness – The veteran cornerback didn’t practice Thursday and was limited Friday, but he came to play on Sunday, including a couple of big hits in the run game. Campbell left the game after a collision in the endzone, but tried to play after the two-hour delay anyway. The Browns didn’t need him for the win, but the former Jags cornerback is proving he is Cleveland tough. HC Todd Monken’s 4th quarter play call, Blake Whiteheart’s recovery – On 3rd and 2, Monken dug out a tight end leak play that took advantage of Tampa Bay trying to stop the quarterback run to the right. With everyone flowing one direction, Whiteheart blocked, then leaked out to the left to be wide open. Watson gave him a floater to catch, but Whiteheart almost fell down. Thankfully, the big tight end recovered his balance by putting his hand on the ground, and WR Jerry Jeudy sealed his defender to let Whiteheart score what ended up being the game-winner. Mayfield doubters – There should be no one who thinks Mayfield is a bad quarterback; he’s quite good and much better than anything Browns fans have seen since he departed. On the other hand, some fans doubt he is good enough to lead a team to a conference championship game. Sunday, after giving the game away in Week 1, Mayfield missed quite a few open receivers, mostly on overthrows, and had a bad interception. At least to start the 2026 season, those who doubted if Mayfield would ever be a Top 10 to 15 quarterback have been proven right. Browns fans – We are not the sad end of the jokes after Week 2. The weather delay didn’t end in ruin, something many of our commenters were concerned about while we waited it out together . Even before the clock hit 0:00, Cleveland fans enjoyed watching their team just be competent for once. A great thing and why we love sports and keep coming back for more. Adding Monken again as a winner for this to end his press conference after the game: Todd Monken: Browns are gonna Browns. F— that! pic.twitter.com/loDcRzzF9T — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) September 20, 2026 Bring the Dawg Pound with you on the SB Nation app! Stay connected with Browns fans through every score, stop and game-changing play. Join the live game-day chat Enjoy fewer ads Seamlessly explore communities and conversations Comment and post faster Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Week 2 Losers – Frownies World Series rain delay flashbacks – Listen, Cleveland should have won the 2016 MLB Championship and, while on a much lower scale, there were some flashbacks going on as the two-plus-hour delay ticked on. Thankfully, this delay ended much better, but the experience for fans brought back some bad memories. Fans’ afternoon/evening plans – I’m sure there were plenty of spouses, kids, and families, like mine, who were frustrated waiting for the game to end or at least to have an idea of what time the game would end. HC Todd Monken’s early aggression – Going for it in the first half, on your side of the field, and then running a slower run play, instead of a QB sneak or a quick hitter, gave Tampa Bay the ball almost in scoring position. Thankfully, the defense held them to just a field goal, but Monken’s 4th-down decision-making reputation as a head coach took another hit with a few decisions so far this season. Thankfully, like “Dumb and Dumber,” he totally redeemed himself in the very same game. S Ronnie Hickman – After not getting a long-term contract this offseason and settling for the qualifying offer from Cleveland, Hickman’s season has not started off well. Two missed tackles, one on a Mayfield scramble and another that would have been a sack, led to the Bucs first touchdown of the game instead of their fourth field goal. Tackling – It was just horrible most of the game, not just Hickman. DE Sam Williams started to celebrate despite the ball carrier still being on his feet. Defenders missing tackles left and right. Trying to thump ball carriers to the ground, instead of wrapping them. Some fundamentals need cleaned up. Pass rush until it mattered – Most of the game, Mayfield had a lot of time to make his decisions. Besides Graham and a few timely blitzes, the Browns pass rush just couldn’t get home. Until they did. Late in the game, Mayfield was mostly uncomfortable in the pocket. Perhaps the rain delayed refreshed the defense just enough. Shedeur Sanders’ only fans – If you follow the Browns because of Sanders and expected he would be starting in Week 3, your wish is unlikely to come true. By unlikely, it is not happening, at least in Week 3. “ Deshaun Watson’s career is over” only fans – If you are a Cleveland fan that can’t stand Watson and thought maybe Week 2 would be his last game ever with the team, you might be disappointed, but you are probably a Browns fan who just wants their team to be good, so you are probably a winner either way. Mayfield champions – Understandably, it can be hard to have a fair opinion of Mayfield. While pretty much all Cleveland fans know he’s been better than Watson and anyone else the Browns have had at quarterback, there have been a handful who also think he’s a Top 10 quarterback. The start of the 2026 season has not backed that up. Week 2 Quick thoughts – Dawg Bones Wow, that was a lot of fun – There were times when it was easy to get down, and we really saw it in the game chat, but the ups were so great. Given how bad the team has been, it can sometimes be easy to wallow in the poor plays, questionable decisions, and each individual incompletion or missed tackle. Thankfully, at the end of a full game, Browns fans get to celebrate. Victory Monday is coming. Those penalties – At one point in the first half, Cleveland…

title: Cleveland Browns vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers recap: Deshaun Watson delivers in second half win, after long weather delay
summary: The Cleveland Browns gave a much better effort than the opening week. Instead of being down 24-0 early in the second quarter, they were only losing 9-6 at halftime to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The offense still couldn’t get into a rhythm at first, but the defense showed some more life to keep them in […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 20: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns passes the ball against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the third quarter of the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns gave a much better effort than the opening week. Instead of being down 24-0 early in the second quarter, they were only losing 9-6 at halftime to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The offense still couldn’t get into a rhythm at first, but the defense showed some more life to keep them in it. Then, the offense gained traction late in the third quarter, including their first touchdown of the game to tie things up at 16-16. In the fourth quarter, they took their first lead of the season at 23-19, as QB Deshaun Watson played perhaps his best half as a Brown. QB Baker Mayfield got his chance to try engineering a game-winning touchdown drive. Then, in a first experience for Browns fans, with Tampa Bay in scoring range at the two-minute warning, lightning and bad weather hit the area, resulting in a two-hour delay. The players came back after 6:00 PM to get the game restarted, and the defense held on for the victory! Let’s get to the full game recap. 1st Quarter – Browns vs. Buccaneers The Browns received the opening kickoff, and began with a 9-yard completion from QB Deshaun Watson to WR KC Concepcion . But then Concepcion was stopped for a loss of 6 yards on a jet sweep. On 3rd-and-7, a handoff to RB Quinshon Judkins went nowhere. That’s when the hat trick of penalties for the Browns began: on offense, Cleveland had an illegal formation (declined), then on the special teams punt they were flagged 15 yards for a facemask penalty, and before a defensive snap, DT Maliek Collins jumped into the neutral zone. QB Baker Mayfield got the Buccaneers into Cleveland territory, but overthrew a deep ball, and then a swing pass to WR Emeka Egbuka went for a loss of 3 yards. A safe dumpoff then got K Chase McLaughlin in range for a 59-yard field goal, which he hit to give the Buccaneers an early 3-0 lead. Cleveland started the next drive with another 9-yard gain, this time via the ground with Judkins. This time, they secured a first down by sticking with Judkins for 6 more yards. Off of a playaction fake with pressure in his face, Watson found TE Harold Fannin on the left side for 22 yards. A few plays later, a quick screen to RB Raheim Sanders gained 7 yards to set up a 4th-and-1 at the Buccaneers 27 yard line. Fannin lined up for the tush push, but a false start on Cleveland made them bring the field goal unit out. K Andre Szmyt was good from 50 yards out to tie things up at 3-3. On the next drive, the Browns were fooled by some misdirection, and S Ronnie Hickman missed a tackle, helping lead to a 38-yard run by RB Bucky Irving . After S Grant Delpit had tackles on back-to-back plays, RB Kenneth Gainwell could not hang on to the third down pass from Mayfield. McLaughlin came on again, this time from 45 yards out, to give Tampa Bay a 6-3 lead with four minutes left in the opening quarter. Two runs to Judkins did not pan out to start Cleveland’s third drive, as they faced a 3rd-and-12. Watson tried to check it down to Fannin, but he dropped it. P Corey Bojorquez came out and got a nice roll on his directional punt for 51 yards, out at the 18 yard line. The Browns’ defense had Mayfield in a 3rd-and-10 on the next drive and nearly got to him for a sack, but he escaped and ran for 14 yards and a first down. On the next play, though, CB Myles Harden dropped back in zone coverage and picked off Mayfield, returning it 25 yards to the Buccaneers’ 36 yard line. THAT'S OURS BABY! #CLEvsTB on CBS pic.twitter.com/YZ2Ep6LcmW — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 20, 2026 A swing pass to Junkins was followed by a late hit, which gave Cleveland the ball at the 12 yard line. A good run by Judkins was negated by a holding penalty on RG Austin Barber , and then a completion to WR Denzel Boston set up a 3rd-and-11 at the 13 yard line heading to the second quarter. 2nd Quarter – Browns vs. Buccaneers RT Tytus Howard was beat quickly on third down, allowing his defender to plow into Watson for a sack. Szmyt came on for a 34-yard field goal to tie the game at 6-6, and it was good. HOW 'BOUT DAVID WALKER ‼️ 📺: #CLEvsTB on CBS pic.twitter.com/4mg4fUdYs1 — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) September 20, 2026 Cleveland’s defense tried to keep their momentum going, getting Tampa Bay into a 3rd-and-8. Mayfield faced pressure in the pocket and looked like he was going to be brought down, but he evaded it and found WR Chris Godwin beyond the sticks. A holding penalty brought it back, but not getting that sack still hurt Cleveland, as on 3rd-and-18, Mayfield found WR Ted Hurst for 21 yards and a first down. The defense then got into a 3rd-and-7, but this time when Mayfield tried to escape, he got away from one defender, but couldn’t evade Hickman for the short sack. The Buccaneers punted into the end zone for a touchback. didn't give up the chase 😤 #CLEvsTB on CBS pic.twitter.com/9b1Vn83IDk — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 20, 2026 Howard’s rough day continued, as he was flagged for a hold on the next drive to make it 1st-and-20 back at the 10 yard line. The operation continued to be bad, as Watson was sacked two plays later, and Cleveland had to run it on third down just to get some breathing room. Bojorquez punted to the Buccaneers’ 44 yard line. DROPPED by 2️⃣2️⃣ 📺: #CLEvsTB on CBS pic.twitter.com/hS6tsUOsUQ — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) September 20, 2026 On 2nd-and-8, Mayfield completed a 3-yard pass to TE Cade Otton . CB Denzel Ward punched the ball out, but Otton recovered right away. Head coach Todd Monken challenged it, despite the low risk/reward. The challenge failed, keeping it at 3rd-and-5. A hold by the Buccaneers made it 3rd-and-15, and then Mayfield was sacked by DT Mason Graham for a loss of 6 yards. The Buccaneers’ punt was fair caught at the 25 yard line, surprisingly giving Cleveland better field position than where they previously started. atta boy Mason!! #CLEvsTB on CBS pic.twitter.com/9vODYK4e0F — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 20, 2026 Could the offense respond after sputtering out? After a few runs, they faced a 3rd-and-7. Watson found Concepcion on a crossing route, but he was tackled after 6 yards, setting up 4th-and-1. The offense stayed on the field, and they tried the quick handoff to Judkins. It was nothing but a wall right in the middle, and Judkins had nowhere to go for a turnover on downs at the Browns’ 34 yard line with 2:45 left in the half. Cleveland missed a few tackles on Gainwell that helped lead the Buccaneers into a goal-to-go situation at the (technically 10.5) yard line with 0:34 left. This time, they stuffed Gainewell for a loss of 2 yards, making it 2nd-and-12. The defense forced a throwaway, setting up a pivotal 3rd-and-12 to try holding the Buccaneers to only three. They held them, as Delpit blanketed his receiver for another incompletion. McLaughlin was good from 31 yards out to put the Buccaneers up 9-6 heading into the half. The Buccaneers had 126 yards of offense, and Cleveland just 59 yards of offense. Watson didn’t make any mistakes per se, but the results are what they are: another darn-near empty offensive output. 3rd Quarter – Browns vs. Buccaneers The Buccaneers got the ball to begin the second half, and Mayfield found Godwin down the field for 24 yards off of playaction. Tampa Bay’s fast start continued as Irving got a burst up the left side for 14 yards to the Browns’ 27 yard line. A completion to Ottman made it 3rd-and-1, and Mayfield did a QB sneak to get the first down. A few plays later, on 3rd-and-9, the Browns brought the blitz and Mayfield took off, stiff armed Hickman in the open field, and got the first down. On 1st-and-goal at the 5 yard line, Cleveland brought the heat again, but Hickman lost the grasp again, and…

title: Browns vs Bucs set the NFL’s weather delay record, game restarts after 2 plus hour delay
summary: To the surprise of many, the Cleveland Browns led the Tampa Bay Buccaneers going into the final two minutes of Week 2’s matchup. The home team Bucs struggled to convert drives into touchdowns, settling for four field goals and just one touchdown despite controlling the game on the ground, with 125 rushing yards to the […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; The game is suspended due to weather during the fourth quarter between Cleveland Browns and Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect To the surprise of many, the Cleveland Browns led the Tampa Bay Buccaneers going into the final two minutes of Week 2’s matchup. The home team Bucs struggled to convert drives into touchdowns, settling for four field goals and just one touchdown despite controlling the game on the ground, with 125 rushing yards to the Browns 45. Not so much a revenge game for QB Baker Mayfield , the Tampa Bay quarterback has a chance to drive his team for a win after quite a few overthrows and an interception. “Has a chance,” despite this article being published after 5 PM Eastern Time due to a weather delay, as we warned about before the game . The two teams and fans at the game in Florida were ordered off the field shortly before 4 PM, just as the broadcast was coming back from the 2-minute warning. An announcement at 5 PM in the stadium noted that the delay would continue and the next update would not come until 5:30 PM. According to the local weather, the delay will likely continue for quite a while: Per our weather team: Folks can expect storms/lightning to continue within 10 miles of Ray Jay for the next 1-2 hours — Aileen Hnatiuk (@AileenHnatiuk) September 20, 2026 Once the NFL approves a return to the field, players usually have a 10-minute warm-up period, but given that this delay has lasted over an hour, that period will likely be extended to at least 15 minutes. Each lightning strike also restarts the clock before the game can resume: Weather update: Very aggressive lightning bolt and a collective "OMG" in the press box just now. It looked close and it sounded close too. When those lightning strikes happen, it resets the clock. — JennaLaineESPN (@JennaLaineESPN) September 20, 2026 The longest NFL weather delay came in 2018, when the Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins had two huge ones: 2 hours, 2 minutes and 1 hour, 57 minutes. That game is also the longest game of all time, lasting just over seven hours. Fittingly, that game was also in Florida, hosted by Miami. As of 5:45 PM, the game will not resume for at least another 45 minutes: I just saw more lightning. Next in-stadium update 6:15 https://t.co/PtJPRu8mVB — Zac Jackson (@AkronJackson) September 20, 2026 With the delay passing 6 PM, and no update before 6:15 PM, today’s matchup has officially passed the 2018 record for longest single weather delay in NFL history. Based on the radar, the lightning continues all around Tampa, with a 10-mile radius used as the marker for when a strike restarts the clock on the delay: Not starting anytime soon. Two SNF games tonight? #GoBucs pic.twitter.com/ZpMpjDMRLy — Paul Dellegatto⚡️FOX (@PaulFox13) September 20, 2026 The teams are starting to return to the field with the hopes of getting the game restarted soon, but one lightning strike would change that: Browns and Buccaneers are back on the field — Shaun Bennett (@ShaunBennettct) September 20, 2026 The game restarted at 6:10 PM with a Tampa Bay run play. The official data on the delay and game length overall: Browns-Buccaneers, with the delay, was a 5 hour and 15 minute game, the third longest since 1991 (as far back as @NFL research has the data). Delay was officially 2 hours and 13 minutes. — Andrew Siciliano (@AndrewSiciliano) September 20, 2026 How did you spend the delay, and did you return to watch the end of the Browns victory? title: Cowboys vs. Commanders: The good, bad, and ugly from Week 2
summary: Compared to their embarrassing loss to the New York Giants last week inthe season opener, the Dallas Cowboys look like an entirely different team in their 37-20 victory over the Washington Commanders in Week 2. With a chance they could drop 0-2 in the NFC East division if they lost, the Cowboys came out and […]
full_text: Compared to their embarrassing loss to the New York Giants last week inthe season opener, the Dallas Cowboys look like an entirely different team in their 37-20 victory over the Washington Commanders in Week 2. With a chance they could drop 0-2 in the NFC East division if they lost, the Cowboys came out and played with purpose in front of their hometown crowd and did what they needed to do in order to secure the “W”. Despite the much-needed victory, this was probably a closer game in the score reflects. This hard-fought victory that had a lot of positives and negatives mixed throughout the ballgame. Fortunately, things bounced the Cowboys way this time around, resulting in their first win on the season. Below is the good, bad, and ugly from this week’s matchup. THE GOOD – QB Dak Prescott, WR CeeDee Lamb Shout out to Jake Ferguson for his four catches for 43 yards and two touchdowns. He definitely deserves recognition here, but it’s Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb who helped propel this team to victory. Prescott set a franchise record with 249 TD passes, eclipsing Tony Romo’s record. He threw for four of them during the game. Lamb caught a total of eight passes for 153 receiving yards and two touchdowns Sunday afternoon against the Commanders. There’s a reason why Dallas has leaned on him so heavily in the past, and this week was proof why he’s so important despite the multitude of weapon surrounding him. This offense runs through No. 4 and No. 88, and are at their best when they are productive. THE BAD – Christian Parker’s defense Compared to last week in the season opener, the Cowboys defense looked much improved in Week 2 against the Commanders. They did enough to help secure the victory and in the end that’s all that matters. However, there is still clearly a lot of work to do for Christian Parker. Dallas’ run defense still looks suspect and the tackling throughout was pretty abysmal. In fact, Donovan Eziruaku left at least three QB sacks on the field by not finishing. Overall though this was a much better showing and one that hopefully continues to improve week to week. THE UGLY – Injuries On the Commanders side of things, QB Jayden Daniels suffered an ugly injury as he dislocated his elbow. He had to miss half the game, and will probably miss more times as he tries to recover. The out-of-place elbow certainly looked gruesome. For Dallas, first it was P.J. Locke who exited the game with a foot injury, and then Cobie Durant with a hamstring injury. With Malik Hooker already out several weeks with a forearm injury, Locke’s further depletes the safety position. The same can be said at CB if Durant ends up having to miss time.
author: Brian Martin

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys 37-20 win over the Commanders
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are in the win column. It wasn’t pretty at times, and it was downright ugly at moments, but they got the job done beating the Washington Commanders 37-20. The game had a share of great plays, but also some that will leave us scratching our heads. We’ll take it, but we’re still […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys are in the win column. It wasn’t pretty at times, and it was downright ugly at moments, but they got the job done beating the Washington Commanders 37-20. The game had a share of great plays, but also some that will leave us scratching our heads. We’ll take it, but we’re still not overly thrilled. Here are 10 thoughts on the Cowboys’ victory on Sunday. 1. A great start for the offense After starting last week with two straight punts and only having six possessions total, it was great to see the offense drive down the field and score a touchdown on their opening drive. They kicked things off with a nice 10-play, 66-yard drive in less than five minutes. The opening drive was mostly the CeeDee Lamb show, who had nice catches for 16 and 23 yards before capping off the drive with a three-yard touchdown catch. That’s how we like games to start. 2. A great start for the defense Not only did the Cowboys’ offense score a touchdown on their opening drive, but the defense had an impressive start of their own with a quick three-and-out that took less than two minutes. Washington’s first three plays were a six-yard pass play, a run play for a loss of a yard, and then a two-yard completion on a third-and-six. It was nice to see the defense get off the field so fast after the Giants hit them with a slow burn last week. If only they could have continued with that level of play. 3. Couldn’t contain Jayden It was pretty obvious that the key to stopping the Commanders’ offense was to keep quarterback Jayden Daniels from scurrying away. It didn’t seem like the Cowboys’ defense got the memo, and time and time again, they just couldn’t contain him. The defense brought the pressure, but they were overcharged, and Daniels just sidestepped danger and took off running. The Cowboys had no answer for his legs as he outgained what Jaxson Dart did last week, and Daniels only played in one half, which brings us to… 4. Crazy end to the first half After a promising start to the game, things started to slowly unravel. The defense couldn’t make stops, and even the offense’s last possession of the first half was a quick three-and-out. It appeared that the Commanders were going to tie things up with a touchdown drive to finish off the half, but a freaky play caused them to come up short. Daniels’ foot was stepped on as he took the exchange from the center and hurt his left arm as he tried to brace his fall. The play went nowhere, and the Cowboys kept their 17-10 halftime lead. Unfortunately for the Commanders, Daniels didn’t return to the game. 5. CeeDee is still great Last year was considered a down year for the Cowboys star wide receiver as he got hurt and his statistics weren’t the typical numbers we were used to seeing. On this day, Lamb reminded us that he is one of the league’s greats. He finished the day with eight catches for 153 yards and two touchdowns. When the offense needed a big play, Dak Prescott looked his way. It was nice to see 88 still doing great things. 6. Catching a break In the first half, the officials initially ruled a Commanders’ touchdown when receiver Terry McLaurin and Cowboys’ cornerback DaRon Bland were both fighting for the reception. Replay showed that McLaurin didn’t have control of the ball through the catch, and the call was overturned. That seemed like the right call. On the Commanders’ first possession in the second half, it looked like receiver Dyami Brown had made a great catch in the end zone when he got one knee in bounds. The play was ruled incomplete, but Washington challenged the play; however, replay officials upheld the call. That one was a little puzzling, and the Cowboys might have caught a break on that play. 7. Barham’s big play Last week, the Cowboys were so close to creating so many turnovers, but the ball rarely bounced their way. Fortunately, their bad luck didn’t carry over to this game. Rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham sniffed out a quick pass to Commanders’ receiver Dyami Brown and was all over him. Just his thundering presence forced the ball out of Brown’s hands and onto the turf where linebacker Dee Winters pounced on it. The Cowboys immediately took advantage and turned it into points, putting themselves in the driver’s seat. 8. Still can’t run the ball Despite the big win, the Cowboys struggled to run the ball. They finished the day rushing 21 times for 66 yards for a measly 3.1 yards per carry. And most of those numbers were aided by Prescott taking off. Running back Javonte Williams only had 30 yards rushing on 12 carries (2.5 ypc). Even with the lead, they couldn’t run effectively. The good news is they didn’t just stubbornly run into a wall, but instead kept the ball moving through the air. The bad news is this team is still struggling to figure out their rushing attack, and unless they get that fixed will be a one-dimensional offense. 9. Same ol’ issues The win is nice, but the defense did not look good. They got pressure at times, but never got home. No sacks. They also had problems in coverage with wide-open receivers finding creases similar to last week. Despite losing by 17, the Commanders still ran more plays, gained more yards, and had the ball longer. This Cowboys’ defense still has issues. Was it an improvement over last week? Yes, but not by a lot, and one can’t wonder that had Daniels not gotten hurt, the Cowboys could be looking at an 0-2 start. 10. New franchise leader The Cowboys offense had four touchdowns in this one, and each one was a touchdown pass from Dak Prescott. The first and last went to Lamb, while the middle two went to tight end Jake Ferguson. Prescott now has a total of 249 touchdown passes, passing Tony Romo for the franchise’s new all-time leader. Dak also continued his home dominance against the Cowboys, where he’s now won all eight games at AT&T Stadium and has 24 touchdowns and no interceptions.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Dak Prescott sets franchise TD record in win over Commanders
summary: After a dissapointing week one performance against the Giants, Dallas rebounded with a 37-20 victory over the Commanders. Dak Prescott in particular looked stellar, completing 84% of his passes on the road to setting the Cowboys franchise TD record. CeeDee Lamb and Jake Ferguson both caught two touchdowns, while Brandon Aubrey nailed a 60-yard field […]
full_text: After a dissapointing week one performance against the Giants, Dallas rebounded with a 37-20 victory over the Commanders. Dak Prescott in particular looked stellar, completing 84% of his passes on the road to setting the Cowboys franchise TD record. CeeDee Lamb and Jake Ferguson both caught two touchdowns, while Brandon Aubrey nailed a 60-yard field goal. On defense, Jaishawn Barham looked good wearing the green dot, and injuries in the secondary made the struggles against the pass more understandable. Cowboys win home opener 37-20 over Commanders, improve to 1-1- Shane Taylor, Inside The Star Dallas’ offense looked nearly unstoppable, and yet even with a backup quarterback, the defense struggled to create negative plays and get off the field on third down. The Cowboys’ offense scored on 7 out of their 8 possessions of the game. Read that again, the offense did what it needed to do regardless of who was in the game for the Commanders. Dak Prescott finished the day 26/31, 279 yards, 4 touchdowns and zero turnovers. The defense is still the issue. Prescott throws 4 TDs as Cowboys beat Commanders, who again lose Jayden Daniels to dislocated elbow- Schuyler Dixon, AP News It’s hard to overstate just how impressive Dak Prescott looked in this game. Just one week after the same defense held Jalen Hurts to a 56% completion percentage, Dak Prescott finished 26 of 31 (84%). Dak Prescott threw four touchdown passes to break Tony Romo’s career franchise record , and the Dallas Cowboys beat Washington 37-20 on Sunday after the Commanders’ Jayden Daniels went down with another gruesome-looking dislocated left elbow. Prescott’s record-breaking 249th TD pass was his second TD of the game to CeeDee Lamb, who had 153 yards receiving. Tight end Jake Ferguson had the other two scoring catches. Game Recap: Dak leads Dallas to win, 37-20- Kurt Daniels, DallasCowboys.com It was a game of runs. Dallas got up early as they were able to get their offense going right away. After stumbling out of the gate in last week’s season opener, Prescott and the offense came out firing on all cylinders in this one, jumping out to a 10-0 first-quarter lead. The team’s first series saw the quarterback complete five of six passes for 53 yards and add another 11 on a scramble to account for 64 of the 66 yards during the 10-play drive. 4 instant takeaways as Cowboys get back on track vs. Commanders in Week 2 – Jerry Trotta, The Landry Hat With another week in the books, fans are getting a clearer picture of what the 2026 Dallas Cowboys are. Unfortunately, it is not all good, but a win is a win nonetheless. 1. Yes, the Cowboys’ offense is still elite Week 1 was very weird. The offense started off slowly, partly due to Brian Schottenheimer coaching scared. And by the time it found a rhythm, the defense couldn’t get off the field. Dak Prescott Just Made Dallas Cowboys History With Latest TD Pass- Randy Gurzi, Sports Illustrated Dak made history, passing Tony Romo for most TD passes in Cowboys history. While fans obviously expect more than stats and numbers from their QB, it is another good reminder of the talent Dallas currently has behind center. Dak Prescott went from a fourth-round compensatory pick to the most decorated quarterback in Dallas Cowboys history. Prescott, who entered Week 2 as the franchise leader in passing yardage with 36,164 yards, was three touchdown passes shy of the most in Cowboys’ history. Cowboys vs Commanders: Jaishawn Barham’s green-dot debut shows plenty to build on- Mike Poland, Blogging The Boys There were more signs of life on the defensive side of the ball than last week. Barham and the defensive line looked better, and without three key secondary players, the struggles against the pass are more understandable. Washington still found success at different points, particularly with Daniels using his legs, but the Cowboys looked much more organized than they did against the Giants in Week 1.

title: Skill or luck? Cowboys defense gets the job done in week 2
summary: The Dallas Cowboys defense played better in week two, but still struggled in multiple areas. They had a difficult time stopping the mobile Jayden Daniels until he left with a horrible injury. That injury made things easier for the defense in the second half, but there were still issues. Tackling continues to be a problem. […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks (13) extends for a pass against the Dallas Cowboys during the second half at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys defense played better in week two, but still struggled in multiple areas. They had a difficult time stopping the mobile Jayden Daniels until he left with a horrible injury . That injury made things easier for the defense in the second half, but there were still issues. Tackling continues to be a problem. The inability to convert pressures into sacks might be the most frustrating part of this unit. But they did make a handful of plays when it mattered, while also grabbing some assists from Lady Luck herself. Sometimes, you just get lucky Late into the second quarter, Jayden Daniels let a ball rip 55 yards downfield into the endzone intended for Treylon Burks. With Cobie Durant trailing five yards behind, Dallas found themselves with a bit of luck on their side as the ball just barely skimmed off the receivers fingertips. The Commanders were SO CLOSE to a touchdown here. pic.twitter.com/jehvJ8RBG7 — Greg 🇺🇸 ✭ (@GregB_TX) September 20, 2026 Again in the third quarter, Dyami Brown found himself attempting to haul in a perfectly thrown pass from Marcus Mariota for a touchdown. Initially called incomplete, the play wound up in review. Analysists and fans alike agreed that this would be overturned, resulting in a touchdown for the Commanders. However, after the review, it was determined that the receiver did not complete the process of a catch soon enough. Much to the surprise of nearly everyone watching, the incompletion was upheld. The Commanders would end up settling for a field goal. Should this have been ruled a touchdown for the Commanders? pic.twitter.com/NCjkCq0iuc — Rate the Refs (@Rate_the_Refs) September 20, 2026 Lady Luck once again favored Dallas near the end of the third quarter. The Commanders reached into their bag of tricks with a wide receiver pass from Antonio Williams to Terry McLaurin in the endzone. DaRon Bland busted the coverage, leaving McLaurin wide open for six. Fortunately for Dallas, the receiver couldn’t swing his head around and adjust to the throw. The ball dropped harmlessly to the ground in the endzone. Here's the failed receiver pass play from the Commanders #WASvsDAL pic.twitter.com/XZ6Y1PiG6J — crunchypuddle (@crunchypuddle1) September 20, 2026 While it wasn’t pretty, it wasn’t all luck One of the most notable plays in the game came in the third quarter when Jaishawn Barham rapidly closed in on a pass to the running back in the flat and forced a fumble. Dee Winters was there in a hurry for the recovery. Dak Prescott and Jake Ferguson would turn the recovery into seven points, returning it back into a two possession game. With the score 13-20 at the time, this was a clutch play at a key moment when the Commanders has the chance to drive down the field to tie the game. . @jaishawnbarham forced fumble and the @dwintersdos recovery 🫡 📺: #WASvsDAL on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/PVbUXHj4SO — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) September 20, 2026 In a game where the ball is an odd shape, sometimes it bounces your way and sometimes it doesn’t. Dallas found themselves in bad shape defensively multiple times throughout the game, but good timing on key plays along with a bit of luck saw them hold their division rival to 20 points in a must-win game. There were certainly improvements on the defensive side of the ball this week, but they still weren’t good enough as a whole. After the first drive ended in a three-and-out, Jayden Daniels was having his way with them until his night was cut short by an injury. Dallas will need to continue to improve this week when they head to Brazil to face yet another mobile quarterback in Lamar Jackson, and the ageless wonder behind him in Derrick Henry. They’ll need a bit more than some luck to walk away with a win versus that Ravens squad. Afterall, you can’t count on luck every week in the NFL. But every once in while, it sure is nice when it’s on your side.

title: Cowboys vs Commanders: Jaishawn Barham’s green-dot debut shows plenty to build on
summary: There was already plenty being asked of Jaishawn Barham before the ball was even kicked off against the Washington Commanders. With DeMarvion Overshown sidelined by a hamstring injury, the Dallas Cowboys handed their rookie linebacker the green dot and asked him to become the voice of Christian Parker’s defense. That meant receiving the calls from […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Washington Commanders running back Rachaad White (1) is tackled by Dallas Cowboys linebackers Jaishawn Barham (55) and Dee Winters (53) during the first half at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There was already plenty being asked of Jaishawn Barham before the ball was even kicked off against the Washington Commanders. With DeMarvion Overshown sidelined by a hamstring injury, the Dallas Cowboys handed their rookie linebacker the green dot and asked him to become the voice of Christian Parker’s defense. That meant receiving the calls from the sideline, relaying them to the rest of the unit, setting the front and making sure everyone was lined up correctly. Cowboys rookie LB Jaishawn Barham, who will wear the green dot today for Dallas’ defense pic.twitter.com/e5H7nVghjp — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) September 20, 2026 That is a sizeable responsibility for any linebacker. Barham was doing it in just the second regular-season game of his NFL career. Brian Schottenheimer had backed the rookie during the week, saying Barham had shown “great command” of the defense. He had also handled similar responsibilities during his college career, but doing it on an NFL field against Jayden Daniels and a divisional opponent was an entirely different test. For the most part, Barham passed it. The important thing when judging his performance with the green dot is separating Dallas’ overall defensive execution from Barham’s ability to run the unit. Washington still found success at different points, particularly with Daniels using his legs, but the Cowboys looked much more organized than they did against the Giants in Week 1. There were fewer moments where defenders appeared completely lost before the snap or where obvious communication breakdowns resulted in easy plays. . @jaishawnbarham forced fumble and the @dwintersdos recovery 🫡 📺: #WASvsDAL on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/PVbUXHj4SO — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) September 20, 2026 There was an early example when Barham made a strong open-field tackle on third-and-five, stopping Washington three yards short of the first-down marker. It was a small play compared with what came later, but it showed the rookie was processing what he was seeing and then reacting without hesitation. Then came his biggest contribution of the afternoon. Barham briefly left the game and went into the injury tent. Cowboys LB Jaishawn Barham is in the injury tent — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) September 20, 2026 On his very first snap back on the field, he delivered one of the biggest defensive plays of the game. He arrived with force and knocked the football loose, with Dee Winters recovering at the Washington 13-yard line. Dallas made Washington pay. Two plays later, Dak Prescott found Jake Ferguson over the middle for a 12-yard touchdown, turning Barham’s takeaway directly into points and extending the Cowboys’ advantage. Perhaps just as encouraging was everything surrounding the play. The rookie had already dealt with the responsibility of calling the defense, briefly leaving through injury and, in one of the more comical moments of the afternoon, even puking on the field. Jaishawn Barham with the pre-snap double-puke, which feels like a pretty good excuse to jog through the ensuing snap pic.twitter.com/QbMEEPQIEw — Christian D'Andrea (@TrainIsland) September 20, 2026 It was certainly one way of introducing yourself to life as an NFL starting middle linebacker. Yet he kept going. He finished with seven tackles and one forced fumble, but his performance was about considerably more than the box score. There will be mistakes to correct. There will be tougher communication tests as offenses use different motion, tempo and personnel changes specifically to challenge the young linebacker. Wearing the green dot successfully for one afternoon does not make him a finished product. What it does provide is evidence that Dallas may have something important developing. Seven tackles, a game-changing forced fumble, an injury return, one unfortunate encounter with his own stomach and responsibility for running the defense. For a player appearing in just his second NFL game, that is quite an afternoon, and the huge 37-20 victory in AT&T Stadium shows something went right in Week 2 with Barham steering the defense.

title: Cowboys beat Commanders handily as Dak Prescott passes Tony Romo’s record
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are on the board in 2026. At the end of their game against the Washington Commanders the scoreboard read 37-20 in favor of the home team, a welcome sight given the way the season opener went against the New York Giants. It feels like the offense was the story of the day, […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson (87) celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown against the Washington Commanders during the first half at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys are on the board in 2026. At the end of their game against the Washington Commanders the scoreboard read 37-20 in favor of the home team, a welcome sight given the way the season opener went against the New York Giants. It feels like the offense was the story of the day, and how could it not be on a day that Dak Prescott tied Tony Romo for the franchise lead in passing touchdowns with 248? The offense was clearly on a mission though and started off hot, potentially wanting to make life easier for their defense. The thing is, the defense definitely still had some issues. They were getting beat fairly often by Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels, but unfortunately for him he was injured on the final play of the first half. It was hardly the same game against Commanders backup Marcus Mariota, but even he found opportunities against Christian Parker’s group. Those are definitely things to work on across the rest of the season and definitely this coming week in preparation for the Baltimore Ravens in Brazil. For now the Cowboys are officially winners for the first time in a long time, and that counts for a lot. Below you will find our recap of everything as it unfolded. First Quarter Washington won the toss and deferred. “GOTI” was on deck to start a game for the second week in a row. GOTI really did arrive. The Cowboys moved 66 yards in 10 plays and with extreme authority. Dak Prescott even got on the move for a big-time run at one point in time, but he capped it all off with a throw for a score to CeeDee Lamb. DAK. CEEDEE. TOUCHDOWN. pic.twitter.com/R0UffLwRBL — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 20, 2026 The good vibes continued on the defensive side of the ball as the Cowboys pitched a three and out on their first defensive possession of the game. It was about as perfect of a start as you could have drawn up. It was not the same sort of success for the Cowboys as they were forced to settle for a Brandon Aubrey chip shot field goal, but points are points and it was nice to get out to a 10-0 lead. Soon on the next drive it seemed like things were snowballing against Washington. In the blink of an eye they were staring at a 3rd and 18 with the AT&T Stadium awake and alert. They converted though which was certainly frustrating. The period ended with Washington in scoring range. Second Quarter As the second quarter began it looked like Washington was going to grab their first touchdown of the day. A fumble on a pitch from Jayden Daniels to Jacory Croskey-Merritt, one the Commanders recovered, moved them back considerably though, and the Cowboys were the real benefits of it as Washington wound up having to settle for a field goal to cut things to 10-3. The Cowboys offense kept their foot well on the gas. George Pickens got more involved on this possession and even picked up a big penalty after a huge catch. Soon enough Dallas was back in the endzone, this time thanks to Jake Ferguson. DAK. FERG. TOUCHDOWN. pic.twitter.com/HnPGfqKgmL — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 20, 2026 It didn’t take long for Washington finally match a score. A penalty aided things, but they moved 59 yards in 8 plays before Jayden Daniels hooked up with Stefon Diggs in the endzone. To make matters worse the Cowboys offense went three and out when they got back on offense and the Commanders started to move again as the first half was coming to a close. Unfortunately, it was about as perfect of a drive as Washington could have drawn up. They took up all of the clock, critically as they were set to receive the ball to start the second half, and then disaster struck. Washington gambled by going for it with 3 seconds left before halftime, clearly only enough time for a single play. Jayden Daniels appeared to get stepped on by his left guard and went down awkward and was unable to get any kind of play off. The Cowboys were fortunate within the game that the Commanders didn’t get any points, but it was a moment where Jayden’s health suddenly became the most important thing going on. That sent the teams to halftime. As they went in Daniels was carted off. Jayden Daniels got up on his own power but rode in the cart off the field with a towel covering his head. He suffered a dislocated left elbow last year. Based on replay it looks like he might’ve hurt his left elbow again. https://t.co/658Bc0hoSS pic.twitter.com/walQ4kuDkk — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) September 20, 2026 Third Quarter As the second half started the Commanders ruled Daniels out for the remainder of the game. Obviously our best thoughts are with him and Hogs Haven will surely cover the story as things unfold in the coming days. Transitioning back to football after injuries like that is difficult, but the Commanders picked up where they left off as a team under new quarterback Marcus Mariota. In fact, Mariota looked to hook up with Dyami Brown for a game-tying touchdown very early into the half. While it was ruled incomplete, it looked like Brown got a knee in bounds. Washington challenged it and, shockingly, lost. They were unable to move the chains, but they did get points by way of a field goal which left Dallas up 17-13. This is when the game turned. On Washington’s first play… Jaishawn Barham announced himself and forced a fumble that the Cowboys recovered. It was a huge moment that gave Dallas a chance to finish their last drive off, so to speak. BARHAM!!! pic.twitter.com/XaASZXOBsR — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 20, 2026 And the Cowboys did indeed finish it off. Dak Prescott found Jake Ferguson for their second touchdown connection of the day, and this one was notable as it was Prescott’s 248th passing touchdown of his career which tied him with Tony Romo for the most in franchise history. 248!!! pic.twitter.com/pfyZy0c3lM — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 20, 2026 This game also marked Prescott’s 79th with multiple passing touchdowns, a mark he also tied Romo for in terms of most in franchise history. But the game was hardly over and the Cowboys went back to work on defense. After failing on a couple, literally a pair, of trick plays the Commanders settled for a field goal attempt that sailed wide right. Dallas held a 27-13 lead as the third quarter was closing down. Fourth Quarter The Cowboys were able to mine out their own field goal attempt that Brandon Aubrey converted on. This gave them a 30-13 lead and established that the fourth quarter was basically a formality. Washington was having none of that talk, though. After coming close a few times Mariota finally delivered a touchdown for Washington by way of a huge pass to Stefon Diggs. Amazingly, not really based on current times, Diggs was wide open and Washington closed the gap to 30-20. That did not last long. The Cowboys marched down the field to put the game away and that they did… as Dak Prescott took hold of the franchise’s all-time passing touchdown record all by himself with number 249. 249!!!!! pic.twitter.com/RMIPspem4M — Blogging The Boys (@BloggingTheBoys) September 20, 2026 The game wore down at that point. Cowboys win! 37-20!

title: Should Jonah Coleman be the Broncos’ starting running back?
summary: Entering Sunday’s game, the Broncos were already down second-year running back RJ Harvey, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. This meant rookie running back Jonah Coleman would see an elevated role on offense vs. the Jaguars. He was still behind veteran starter JK Dobbins, who took the majority of the snaps early on, but […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball during the fourth quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Entering Sunday’s game, the Broncos were already down second-year running back RJ Harvey, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. This meant rookie running back Jonah Coleman would see an elevated role on offense vs. the Jaguars. He was still behind veteran starter JK Dobbins, who took the majority of the snaps early on, but he too suffered a hamstring injury and would be sidelined for the remainder of the game. This gave rookie running back Jonah Coleman an opportunity to shine in a big moment, and he did not disappoint. He would enter the game late in the 4th quarter while the Broncos were leading, with a chance to ice the game and kill the clock. This has been a scenario that the Broncos have struggled with and have typically gone three-and-out and had to send their defense back out to close the game. Well, Coleman called game and had multiple big runs for first downs and would smartly slide down inbounds to avoid stopping the clock. Not only did he look like a veteran player out there, but he also looked like a future starter. "That didn't feel like a rookie" 🗣️ Sean Payton PRAISES Jonah Coleman after Broncos win vs Jaguars pic.twitter.com/AUvBwhWTSm — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) September 21, 2026 After the game, head coach Sean Payton told reporters that Coleman played well and that the rookie back did not feel like a rookie out there on Sunday. “He played well. Then the very end, that last carry was… We work on four-minute [situations], but that certainly didn’t feel like a rookie series, if you will. He came up big, and we needed it. You carry three [running backs] on gameday like everyone else. We were down to two and the fullback. Those guys did a good job, and then we found a couple schemes that we liked and stayed with it. His play right at the end, staying in bounds, that was something you cover, but maybe he doesn’t get those same reps in practice. He did a good job.” Payton said Coleman came up big, and he did. He closed that game out for the Broncos, made the Jaguars waste their timeouts, and did not allow Trevor Lawrence and the explosive Jaguars offense to take the field again. That is huge and something the team has struggled to do in the past. Quarterback Bo Nix also praised Coleman’s late-game IQ and told reporters that Coleman does a really good job of paying attention and that he’s really smart and that he has great football IQ. “Jonah played very smart for a young kid, especially at the end there for a minute when everybody knows we’re running the football. He has to protect the football, run in bounds, a lot of things are going through his head while he’s trying to run the ball well. So he did that extremely well, very efficient and then obviously capped it off with the run down the sideline where he slid in bounds and that’s just really good for a young guy. You can tell he does a really good job of paying attention and he’s really smart and he’s got a great football IQ.” A big part of football is trust. Can you trust a player in a big moment to come up with a big play? Nix trusts Courtland Sutton in big moments, and Payton has the players on the roster that he trusts to fill the needed roles on the 53-man roster. A performance like this in a big game and in a key late-game situation likely earned rookie Jonah Coleman some trust from Payton and Nix moving forward. So, with Dobbins and Harvey currently banged up, has Coleman earned the right to be the Broncos’ starting running back? I think as long as Dobbins is healthy, he will be the guy, but Coleman is making a strong case for that job. I don’t think Harvey’s role is in danger, but Coleman is putting everyone on the hot seat, and the reality is, it’s only a matter of time before he takes it. He looked effective in short yardage against a good run defense and scored his first career touchdown; he picked up key first downs, bounced one run outside, and looked explosive in the open field. I want to see more Jonah Coleman moving forward, and I believe a real discussion needs to be had about him becoming the Denver Broncos’ starting running back sooner rather than later.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Sean Payton on Jaylen Waddle: ‘I’m glad he is ours’
summary: 1 catch for 2 yards. That was the stat line for Jaylen Waddle’s debut with the Broncos. His lack of involvement in the offense was curious, and it was a disappointing start to his Broncos career after all the talk and hype this offseason. Well, it appears Waddle was saving his big debut for the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Jaylen Waddle #17 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during the fourth quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images 1 catch for 2 yards. That was the stat line for Jaylen Waddle’s debut with the Broncos. His lack of involvement in the offense was curious, and it was a disappointing start to his Broncos career after all the talk and hype this offseason. Well, it appears Waddle was saving his big debut for the home crowd in Mile High because the Broncos receiver exploded for 8 catches for 138 yards vs. the Jaguars on Sunday. He showed off his big-play ability with a 49-yard reception from quarterback Bo Nix while also making big plays in key moments throughout the game. After the game on Sunday, head coach Sean Payton told reporters: “I am glad he (Waddle) is ours”. "Glad [Jaylen Waddle is] ours!" Sean Payton on Waddle's impact vs the Jaguars 🔥 pic.twitter.com/PrDmLi6rX2 — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) September 21, 2026 Payton added that Waddle’s impact on Sunday’s game was “significant” and that he just got done giving his explosive wide receiver a game ball for his performance. “It was significant. I just gave him a game ball. You can see the explosiveness, the run after the catch, all of those things. I’m glad he’s ours.” Waddle showed off his playmaking ability throughout this one and lived up to the hype we heard all offseason. The Broncos have been lacking a true playmaker like this for years now, and it is exciting to see what Waddle can do from here on out. The players are excited too. Veteran wide receiver Courtland Sutton told reporters after the game that he has been “cheesin” and that he believes that this is just the tip of the iceberg for Waddle . He added that they have more plays in their back pocket for the Broncos’ explosive wide receiver that they haven’t even gotten to yet. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix couldn’t hold back his excitement for Waddle either. During his postgame press conference, he was initially asked about rookie running back Jonah Coleman, but Nix wanted to talk about Waddle. “First, [WR] Jaylen [Waddle] played great. He had a great game. [He] did a great job in man, did a great job in zone. Started off with that big completion down the field and that sort of got him going. He just showed his swagger all day, he showed enthusiasm, he’s got a passion about him, he’s just a great teammate and he just plays the right way, and he gets rewarded because of it.” Head coach Sean Payton is excited, quarterback Bo Nix can’t hide his excitement, and Courtland Sutton is still somewhere cheesin’. There was a lot of hype and excitement for Waddle heading into the season, and he proved why on Sunday. This should be the first of many big games for Waddle, and like Sean Payton, I am glad Jaylen Waddle is ours too.

title: Stock Up, Stock Down After the Broncos’ Week 2 Comeback Win Over the Jaguars
summary: Stock Up, Stock Down After the Broncos’ Week 2 Comeback Win Over the Jaguars What a difference a week makes. The Denver Broncos were coming off an embarrassing blowout loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football, and things looked dire in Broncos Country. The offense looked bad, Bo Nix had one of […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos leaves the field after his team's 20-13 win against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Stock Up, Stock Down After the Broncos’ Week 2 Comeback Win Over the Jaguars What a difference a week makes. The Denver Broncos were coming off an embarrassing blowout loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football, and things looked dire in Broncos Country. The offense looked bad, Bo Nix had one of his worst career games, Davis Webb’s debut as a playcaller was a failure, and the defense looked bad and had a ton of missed tackles. To make things worse, the Broncos would be hosting their home opener vs. a very good Jacksonville Jaguars team that has been playing like one of the better teams in the league and beat the Broncos by double digits last season. Well, the Broncos bounced back and had one of their classic 4th-quarter comeback victories. Things started rough early on, but the defense played well, and Bo Nix, Jaylen Waddle, and rookie Jonah Coleman helped lead the Broncos to a victory. Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos roster and give you stock-ups and stock-downs on every player currently on the 53-man roster. After a bounce-back performance like that on Sunday, we are going to see a lot more stock-ups than we did last week. Quarterback Bo Nix – Stock up: After having one of the worst games of his career on Monday Night, Nix bounced back and gave us a classic Bo Nix performance. There were some struggles early on, but he was moving the ball up and down the field fairly easily against the Jaguars’ defense. However, red zone struggles really hurt what could have been a big game for Nix. Still, he passed for 288 yards and a touchdown and led yet another 4th-quarter comeback vs. a pretty good Jaguars team. Jarrett Stidham – Unchanged: Remains the backup quarterback Sam Ehlinger – Unchanged: Remains the emergency third-string quarterback Running Back JK Dobbins – Stock down: The veteran back left the game due to a hamstring injury, which thankfully sounds minor, but we’ll see how it trends as the week progresses. With his injury history, it is concerning to see an injury pop up this early in the season. Pair that with his multiple goal-line failures and rookie Jonah Coleman looking really good, and you have to go stock down on JK Dobbins. RJ Harvey – Unchanged: Harvey was inactive for this game due to a hamstring injury, but he was able to put in two limited practices, so it sounds like he may not miss much more time moving forward. I am going with unchanged simply because his role is not in danger. He is the Broncos third down/pass game specialist. We saw him get plenty of touches and snaps in the opener, and when healthy, I believe his role is locked in on this offense. Jonah Coleman – Stock up: Coleman entered the game late due to JK Dobbins leaving with a hamstring injury and played really well. He scored his first career touchdown, which was the go-ahead score, and helped the Broncos ice the game late, which has been something they have struggled to do in recent history. Coleman is the future starter of this backfield; it’s just a matter of when, not if. Tyler Badie – Stock up: I thought Badie played well. He had a 27-yard catch-and-run and had a couple of nice returns in the kicking game. That’s what he’s supposed to do, and I thought he played well, all things considered. Adam Prentice – Stock down: He played just 8 snaps of offense and wasn’t used in the Broncos’ goal-line failures in the first half. He was a short-yardage specialist last season and in the preseason, but the Broncos have yet to pull that trigger this season. Wide Receiver Jaylen Waddle – Stock way up: That’s more like it. After a 1-catch for 2-yard performance in Week 1, Waddle exploded for 8 catches for 138 yards. He made multiple key plays in big moments and looked like the explosive playmaker the Broncos traded for this offseason. This should be the first of many big games from the Broncos’ explosive wide receiver. Courtland Sutton – Stock down: His role in this offense appears to have taken a step back. Had a down Week 1, and unlike Waddle, the veteran didn’t do too much in Week 2. He finished with 3 catches for 25 yards and was targeted just 4 times. I still feel like we’ll have a few big Sutton games, but his week-to-week performance is probably going to continue to be inconsistent. Pat Bryant – Unchanged: 0 targets and 1 end-around for 16 yards. It wasn’t a great game on paper for Bryant, who was also flagged for another holding call (Like the other ones on Monday Night; it seemed kinda BS), but I am not going to overreact here. The team really likes their second-year wide receiver, and this week was just the Jaylen Waddle show. Marvin Mims Jr. – Stock down: Injuries suck. The Broncos All-Pro returner has been dealing with multiple injuries throughout the summer. He missed time during camp, returned for the preseason, and then was hurt again; he played in Week 1, got hurt, and then missed Week 2. He just needs to get healthy and stay healthy. Troy Franklin – Stock up: I went with stock down due to his bad OPI on Monday Night, but I am going with stock up due to his nice one-handed catch on Sunday. He played just 13 snaps and was targeted 2 times, so the usage isn’t great, but he made the most of his opportunity on Sunday. Lil ’ Jordan Humphrey – Unchanged: He is who he is and fills a depth role on the offense and special teams. He didn’t play much on Sunday, but that was expected. Tight End Adam Trautman – Unchanged: An in-line blocking specialist who played 65% of the snaps, but you wouldn’t really know it if you watched the game. 0 targets and was strictly in for blocking. Evan Engram – Stock up: He was targeted just once on Sunday but made a tremendous catch late in the game. He played 52% of the snaps and made the most of his lone target, so I am going stock up. Nate Adkins – Stock up: Is Nate Adkins really the Joker? (Sorry). The blocking specialist led all tight ends with 3 catches for 32 yards and 1 touchdown. He actually had the second-most receiving yards on the team, only trailing Jaylen Waddle. He played 37% of the offensive snaps, contributed on special teams, and does all the dirty work that typically goes unrecognized by fans. Need games like this from your depth players throughout the year. Dallen Bentley – Unchanged: The rookie tight end was inactive and is likely having a red-shirt year for the Broncos. Offensive Line Garett Bolles – Unchanged: I’ll say this each week, I am not an OL expert, but the unit looked better this week. Nix was not sacked, and I did not see the pressure get to him as it did vs. the Chiefs. Ben Powers – Unchanged: Same story here with Powers. Did not really notice him, which is usually a good thing for a lineman. Luke Wattenberg – Stock down: Simply for the delayed snap on the 3rd-down goal-line toss play. It threw off the play from the start, which immediately doomed it from the start. Quinn Meinerz: Stock up: He pancaked a dude. Mike McGlinchey – Stock up: Struggled vs. the Chiefs but appeared to have a better game on Sunday. Alex Palczewski – Unchanged: Played just 4 offensive snaps and is your top reserve OL. Matt Peart – Unchanged: Didn’t play a single snap but is your backup tackle. Alex Forsyth – Unchanged: Did not play a single snap but is your backup center. Kage Casey – Unchanged: Inactive and likely having a rookie redshirt year. Defensive Line Zach Allen – Stock up: He’s unblockable at times and was in there on multiple pressures and sacks despite not being credited with one. DJ Jones – Stock up: The run defense was better, and he’s the man in the middle of the defensive line. I did not see him stand out much, but the overall play was better than last week, so stock up. Malcolm Roach – Stock…

title: Game balls for the Broncos 20-13 win over the Jaguars
summary: A thrilling 14-point fourth quarter catapulted the Denver Broncos ahead of the Jacksonville Jaguars as both sides of the football dominated late to secure the victory for Denver. It didn’t seem possible early in the third quarter when Jacksonville added another field goal to take a double-digit lead. However, from then on out the Broncos […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - SEPTEMBER 20: Jaylen Waddle (17) of the Denver Broncos hauls in a pass from Bo Nix (10) during the second quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, September 20, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images A thrilling 14-point fourth quarter catapulted the Denver Broncos ahead of the Jacksonville Jaguars as both sides of the football dominated late to secure the victory for Denver. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . It didn’t seem possible early in the third quarter when Jacksonville added another field goal to take a double-digit lead. However, from then on out the Broncos offense and defense controlled the game. They scored 17-unanswered and with over four minutes to go the offense controlled the clock and the downs to ensure Trevor Lawrence never saw the field again. It was a great team win and rally to avoid an 0-2 start. There were many game ball options in this game, but there were only so many of us to go around. Here’s who we’re giving our game balls to: Riley Moss I had to start with the defense. The offense were stumbling around for 2.5 quarters and if the defense hadn’t shown up with fire in the bellies, this game could have gotten out of hand early. Instead, every time it seemed the Jaguars were going to step on their throats the defense stood up and made a play. In my mind, none was bigger than this one in the late third quarter by Riley Moss. He’d already had himself a pretty good game with three passes defensed and two tackles, but with the Jaguars crossing midfield again up by a touchdown they couldn’t afford to let them add more points there. Riley Moss made a great play and turned the tide. Have a game ball, sir! – Tim Lynch RILEY MOSS INT pic.twitter.com/jjTTzYc7RN — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 Zach Allen Zach Allen didn’t do much that showed up on the stat sheet on Sunday. He finished the game with one tackle and one QB hit, but he was a disruptive force for most of the game. His pressure forced Trevor Lawrence off his spot multiple times and his disruption against the run allowed Malcolm Roach to get two TFL. Despite being double-teamed most of the game, Zach Allen had a dramatic impact that will go largely unnoticed on the stat sheet. For this he gets my game ball. – Joe Mahoney QUE ROBINSON AND ZACH ALLEN COMBINE FOR THE SACK pic.twitter.com/zReoz7tTTu — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 Bo Nix The Broncos quarterback showed some serious bounce back and resiliency in his play on Sunday. In the process, we saw the type of play we’ve grown accustomed to seeing from Nix. He was confident and making great decisions with his arm and legs. He was accurate. He and Jaylen Waddle showed the type of dangerous attack they can have. You could also see Nix and Davis Webb got into rhythm in the second half. Nix finished the game 22-for-31 passing for 288 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. This is the type of game and win that could propel Nix and the Broncos. – Ian St. Clair BIG PLAY JAYLEN WADDLE 🐧 pic.twitter.com/FLI7iIbGD1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 Jonah Coleman Jonah Coleman played a pivotal role in helping the Broncos to their first win of the season. His first opportunity to make a play as a running back resulted in the game winning touchdown. It was the first of his young career, but he wasn’t done yet. As time ran toward the 2 minute warning, Coleman made a veteran play. As he busted into the open field he found the first down marker and then immediately got down. A big heads up play to stay in bounds and essentially end the game. Big game ball for the rookie. – Adam Malnati JONAH COLEMAN'S FIRST CAREER TOUCHDOWN GIVES THE BRONCOS THE LEAD pic.twitter.com/GY72InQjjt — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 Jaylen Waddle Now THAT is what we all expected when Denver traded a first round pick for Jaylen Waddle. After just three targets and one catch on Monday, seeing Waddle pick up 10 targets, 8 catches for 138 yards and look absolutely dominant was extremely refreshing. Waddle showed what his full potential could be in this offense and the explosive element he brings with his 49 yard downfield catch. I was really excited to see him used on deep crossers and shaking DBs out of their socks up the sideline. This is just the beginning of a massive season for him and I’m sure the first of many gameballs. – Jeff Essary #Broncos Payton on Waddle. "Significant. Just gave him game ball. Could see his explosiveness." — Troy Renck (@TroyRenck) September 20, 2026 Vance Joseph We’ve talked about the players who performed well on defense, but shoutout to Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph. He gets my game ball for having a tremendous gameplan. Outside of a few busted plays, the players executed it tremendously. Everyone looked better prepared than what we witnessed versus the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1. Last year, the Broncos gave up 34 points to the Jaguars in December’s matchup. This time around it was only 13 and held them to less than 275 yards of total offense. Trevor Lawrence had a rough day completing less than 60-percent of his passes and throwing for under 200 yards. Limiting Lawrence’s impact was huge and Joseph’s coaching played a big role in that. – Chris Hart Who gets your game ball for the Broncos-Jags game? Share in the comments section below.
