title: Broncos rise to occasion; topple Jaguars in hard-fought gridiron battle
summary: When the going gets tough, the tough get going. The Denver Broncos started off slow but eventually found their groove on offense in the second half. That coupled with a terrific defensive performance helped them topple the Jacksonville Jaguars 20-13 on Sunday afternoon to move to 1-1 on the season. After the game, Head Coach […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Malcolm Roach #97 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during the second quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the going gets tough, the tough get going. The Denver Broncos started off slow but eventually found their groove on offense in the second half. That coupled with a terrific defensive performance helped them topple the Jacksonville Jaguars 20-13 on Sunday afternoon to move to 1-1 on the season. After the game, Head Coach Sean Payton called the matchup ‘a tale of two halves’ and was pleased with how the offense responded after several missed opportunities in the redzone early in the game. He also acknowledged the defense’s impressive turnaround being a huge factor in achieving victory. “That’s a really good offense. When you looked at last year’s game, I thought they were outstanding. They were going to make their plays, but it was a much different game than a year ago. We had our hands on a few others, but we got off the field on third down. That was good,” stated Payton. Denver’s defense slowed down Trevor Lawrence and the high-powered Jaguars aerial attack. Last December, Lawrence was able to scorch the Broncos with four touchdowns. He also had a penchant for extending drives on third down. This time around, Lawrence threw for less than 200 yards, converted just 5-of-12 third down attempts, and had zero touchdowns. Outside a few plays, the Broncos performed at a high level in pass coverage. Just three big plays accounted for most of Lawrence’s total yards through the air. Nickelback Ja’Quan McMillian, who had several key pass breakups, noted the team worked hard all week to respond the right way. Moreover, the execution being emblematic of their resilience. “It’s always been the standard. We didn’t do that last week. We responded the right way. We had a great week of practice on a short week. Just went out there and kept fighting and got the ‘W’,” stated McMillian. “It’s just the work that we put in. We know this is an imperfect game. It’s not going to always be exactly how we want it to be scripted when all we have to do is just keep fighting and do our job.” With the backs against their wall being down two scores in the third quarter, Denver’s confidence never wavered. They dug deep, gave it everything they had, and the result was a gutsy win against a top AFC team. It’s exactly what the Broncos needed after struggling mightily against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1. As I wrote earlier in the week, a sign of a great team is being able to rebound after adversity. The Broncos showed that on Sunday. There’s no doubt the team has toughness and determination. They also have the right mindset and approach to overcome future obstacles and challenges that will occur during the rest of the season. “When you get punched in the face, you’ve got to respond and we have a really tough team. We played with great grit today, and we responded really well and at the end of the day that’s the most important thing,” remarked Nix after the victory. Speaking about responding—how about the impact of Jaylen Waddle? After being limited to just one catch for two yards in his regular season debut with Denver, he was arguably the player of the game. He reeled in eight catches for 138 receiving yards. When the Broncos needed a big play, it was Waddle who consistently answered the call. His playmaking skills netted the offense several key first downs and put them in scoring position on multiple occasions. After last week’s outing, this is the type of performance fans across Broncos Country were hoping to see. Next on the docket for Week 3? The Los Angeles Rams in primetime on Sunday Night Football . The Rams also weren’t at their best in their Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. However, they’ll get a chance to get back on track against the New York Giants tonight on Monday Night Football . They’ll be hungry to another tough opponent for the Broncos. Though if Denver can pick up where they left off on offense and string together another tenacious defensive effort, they’ll have a good shot at being 2-1.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Victory in Broncos Country
summary: After a shaky first game and a half, the Denver Broncos finally turned in a winning performance against the Jaguars on Sunday. When budding narratives about the defense, Bo Nix, and Davis Webb began cast doubt on the positives from last season and hopes for this one, this first win of the season didn’t come […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Fans cheer prior to the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Denver Broncos of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a shaky first game and a half, the Denver Broncos finally turned in a winning performance against the Jaguars on Sunday. When budding narratives about the defense, Bo Nix, and Davis Webb began cast doubt on the positives from last season and hopes for this one, this first win of the season didn’t come a moment too soon. As Broncos fans, we collectively seemed to share this expectation that Denver would simply pick up where it left off last season, seconds before Bo Nix broke his ankle. Sure, the narrative made sense: The Broncos returned most of their 2025 squad during free agency and upgraded where the team needed it most, the high-octane receiving threat that is Jaylen Waddle. The less-than-stellar first 6-quarters of Broncos football to start 2026 were a reminder of just how difficult this game is. It’s a reminder of just how hard the players, coaches, and staff work to achieve the high level of success that’s a hallmark of Broncos football in Denver. What Broncos Country saw in the second half on Sunday was also a reminder — that patience and perseverance pays off. There will be highs and lows, but it’s important to manage those peaks and valleys, to not get so wrapped up in the momentary struggles that we get so annoyed we miss something special happening right before our eyes, much like the 17-0 run the Broncos rode to victory on Sunday over the Jags. It’s that growth that makes triumph possible. It’s that triumph that makes this game so damn special. Sure, when the product on the field looks like it did for the first 6-quarters of this young season, it’s natural to be frustrated and disappointed. Remember, though, it’s a long 17-game season and those struggles will may be a distant memory or may seem marginal compared whatever this season has in store. Finding out is what makes the season so exciting. Have expectations. Be emotional. Cheer your ass off and swear at your television. The Denver Broncos got their first win of the season on Sunday and it felt so damn good. The good news is that there are other wins right behind it, probably quite a few more. Sit back, buckle in, and let’s all enjoy the ride. Who knows, maybe when it’s all said and done, the ride could conclude on Super Bowl Sunday in Los Angeles.

title: 7 Things we learned from Broncos 20-13 win vs Jacksonville
summary: Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos just got a massive win. That second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars was a thing of beauty. Balanced offense. Great execution. Defensive dominance. It all led to a 20-13 win that the doomers said was impossible. With this win, the Broncos improve to 1-1 on the season and have […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos calls a play during the first quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos just got a massive win. That second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars was a thing of beauty. Balanced offense. Great execution. Defensive dominance. It all led to a 20-13 win that the doomers said was impossible. With this win, the Broncos improve to 1-1 on the season and have fans feeling much better. Here are the things that we learned from this victory in Denver’s home opener. The NFL is a week-to-week league This is one of the oldest clichés in the NFL, but it’s still true. And it was on full exhibit on Sunday. You never know what will happen. And to make judgments based on one game, especially the first of the season, on the road, no matter how ugly, is foolhardy. Nix and the Broncos showed why. In the second half, Denver looked and played like the team we’ve grown accustomed to seeing. Now the challenge is not to get carried away the other way because of this win. But it was fantastic for Nix and the Broncos to respond for the gritty win on Sunday. Nix and Waddle were much better BIG PLAY JAYLEN WADDLE 🐧 pic.twitter.com/FLI7iIbGD1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 The first half was a carryover from the game against the Chiefs, but something clicked in the second half for Nix and the offense. The Denver quarterback was efficient, hit on some big pass plays, and he used his legs to pick up some first downs. For the game, Nix was 22-for-31 passing for 288 yards, one touchdown, and one interception. Perhaps even better for the Bronos offense is that Nix and Jaylen Waddle clicked. Nix hit Waddle for eight catches and 138 yards. If this is the appetizer of what these two can do, yes, please. Balanced offensive attack, led by Jonah Coleman JONAH COLEMAN'S FIRST CAREER TOUCHDOWN GIVES THE BRONCOS THE LEAD pic.twitter.com/GY72InQjjt — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 Not only did Denver have success through the air, but it also did so on the ground against a stout run defense. The Broncos finished with just 104 yards rushing, but they were hard-fought yards that led to a balanced attack in the second half. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman led Denver with 39 yards on 10 carries, including a 12-yard run on second-and-11 that sealed the game. Coleman also had a 3-yard touchdown run. Great game from the rookie. J.K. Dobbins added 10 carries for 36 yards before dealing with a hamstring injury. What we saw from the Broncos offense in the second half will make this team hard to beat. Davis Webb got into a play-calling rhythm Of course, it helps to have players execute and make plays, but Webb deserves some credit for the game he called in the second half. You could tell he and Nix were gaining confidence and were in a great rhythm in the second half. After the struggles in Week 1, this was another great development for Denver. Mile High Salute to Denver’s defense https://t.co/cVOCF7k4i8 pic.twitter.com/u3octtBupa — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 There were a lot of doubters after the opening week in Kansas City. The Broncos defense responded in a big way and not only showed up, but showed out. Denver held the Jaguars offense to 95 yards rushing and just 173 yards passing for 268 total yards. The Broncos didn’t give up big plays and forced a big turnover from Trevor Lawrence. More importantly, the Broncos corrected the tackling issues. Kudos to Denver’s defense for that response. To hold Lawrence and the Jaguars to 13 points is a helluva feat. Vance Joseph deserves a lot of credit When your defense is shredded, the coordinator takes the flak. Well, Joseph should get credit for how his unit responded and played on Sunday. The Broncos looked like a completely different team against Jacksonville, but his defensive plan clearly worked. As well as the message he and the other coaches delivered earlier in the week. Sean Payton and the coaches did their job Getting your players to refocus and put an embarrassing showing behind you on a short week is a testament to Payton and his coaches’ masterful leadership. Whatever Payton did and said clearly worked, and the players responded. And while it may not mean much for this game, Payton showed excellent clock and game management by calling a timeout after the first play with under 3 minutes remaining, when Coleman lost a yard on first down. The thought being, regardless of the next play’s result, it would lead to the 2-minute warning. Obviously, it didn’t matter given Coleman’s 12-yard run, but that type of clock and game management from Payton will pay off as the season progresses. Now Payton can be even harder on his team after a win, which is what Hall of Fame coach Bill Parcells used to do.
author: Ian St. Clair

title: Winners and Losers from the Denver Broncos’ 20-13 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars
summary: The Broncos are back! After a rough week coming off a blowout loss in Week 1 to the Kansas City Chiefs, the Broncos bounced back in a big way in Week 2 vs. the Jaguars. They started slow and had some pretty bad red zone moments; however, they came alive in the second half and […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 20: Cornerback Riley Moss (21) of the Denver Broncos celebrates his interception of quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the second half a 20-13 win on Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colo. (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Broncos are back! After a rough week coming off a blowout loss in Week 1 to the Kansas City Chiefs, the Broncos bounced back in a big way in Week 2 vs. the Jaguars. They started slow and had some pretty bad red zone moments; however, they came alive in the second half and put together another 4th quarter comeback victory. VICTORY FORMATION BRONCOS WIN Jags put up a good effort for a small market team 😏 pic.twitter.com/chpaSeOi8B — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 At one point in this game, we had a lot of negative talking points, and we still have to touch on them, but the Broncos really turned it around in the second half and had some big performances from key players. Redemption for Bo Nix, Davis Webb, Vance Joseph, Jaylen Waddle, and the rest of the Broncos team. Here are your winners and losers from the Broncos’ big comeback victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars. WINNER – QB Bo Nix After playing arguably the worst game of his career on Monday Night, Nix bounced back and had a really good game today. The stat line should be better and include more than one touchdown, but he moved the ball up-and-down the field vs. the Jags and led yet another 4th-quarter comeback victory. BIG PLAY TROY FRANKLIN pic.twitter.com/9Vq1Kj5QqW — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 Nix finished the game going 22 of 31 for 288 yards, 1 touchdown and 1 interception. However, he had a deep ball to Jaylen Waddle go down at the one-yard line and would have led multiple touchdown drives if the Broncos could convert inside the red zone. Still, Nix and the offense came alive in the second half, specifically the 4th quarter, and he helped lead the Broncos to yet another comeback victory. This was a classic Bo Nix performance. WINNER – WR Jaylen Waddle One catch for two yards. Waddle’s stat line on Monday Night baffled me. They need more from Waddle if they want to achieve their big goals this season, and they got exactly that today from Waddle. He bounced back (the theme of today’s game) and had a HUGE game. He had 8 receptions for 138 yards, which included multiple big plays on 3rd down and in key moments. BIG PLAY JAYLEN WADDLE 🐧 pic.twitter.com/FLI7iIbGD1 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 This is the type of performance the Broncos expected from Waddle when they made the blockbuster trade for him this offseason. Week 1 was shockingly bad, but today’s performance is what we should expect moving forward from the Broncos’ explosive wide receiver. WINNER – RB Jonah Coleman The Broncos entered the game already down RJ Harvey, who is dealing with a hamstring injury, and would later lose veteran starter JK Dobbins with another hamstring injury late in the game. That put the spotlight on rookie running back Jonah Coleman, and the rookie did not disappoint. While the stat line will not blow you away, he helped put this game away late on the final drive and also scored his first career touchdown. JONAH COLEMAN'S FIRST CAREER TOUCHDOWN GIVES THE BRONCOS THE LEAD pic.twitter.com/GY72InQjjt — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 It remains to be seen if Harvey or Dobbins will miss games moving forward, but if they do, or are at least limited, this could be the big opportunity Coleman has been waiting for. The impressive rookie back had a strong offseason and showed off his talent late in this game. He looks like a future starter, and that future could be starting sooner rather than later. WINNER – Broncos secondary (PS2, Moss, J-Mac specifically) The Jags had some big plays, specifically to star wide receiver Parker Washington, but overall, the Broncos secondary did an excellent job against this high-powered Jaguars passing offense. Lawrence, who has been playing like an elite quarterback dating back to last season, finished the game with just 189 yards passing and 1 interception. It felt like Lawrence had a better day than that, but the Broncos’ secondary, specifically corners Pat Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja’Quan McMillian, played a damn good game. The biggest play of the game, the one that changed the momentum, was a huge interception by corner Riley Moss on a key 3rd down at midfield trailing 13-6 late in the 3rd quarter. RILEY MOSS INT pic.twitter.com/jjTTzYc7RN — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) September 20, 2026 This INT by Moss gave the Broncos life and led to an eventual game-tying touchdown. The momentum would be in the Broncos’ favor for the rest of the game. A huge play by Riley Moss. Pat Surtain II did PS2 things throughout this one, including a big PBU on the Jags’ final offensive drive to force 4th down and a punt. McMillian was good too and had a near INT in the 4th quarter as well. Sure, Parker Washington made some plays, but he’s doing that against everyone right now. The Broncos’ secondary locked down a high-powered Jags offense and was a big reason for this victory. WINNER – OC Davis Webb On Tuesday Morning, I wrote “Davis Webb’s OC and play-calling debut was an epic failure”, and it was. It was a rough showing that had fans and media calling for him to give up play-calling. The team had his back all week, and this morning, we had an Adam Schefter report stating the Broncos have faith in Webb’s ability. Still, the pressure was on Davis Webb today, and it did not start out well. The Broncos had two 1st-and-goal opportunities, including starting at the 1-yard line, and walked away with just 3 points. However, the Broncos were moving the ball well; they just couldn’t capitalize in the red zone. That all changed in the second half when the Broncos offense came alive, and they went from trailing 13-6 to winning 20-13. The Broncos had 392 total yards, 288 passing yards, 104 rushing yards, and beat the Jaguars ‘ high-powered offense in all of the offensive yardage stats. It may not have been always pretty and far from perfect, but Webb silenced all doubters today. Redemption. WINNER – DC Vance Joseph While all the heat was on Davis Webb, Vance Joseph’s defense played equally as bad on Monday Night. Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker ran all over the Broncos’ defense, and they allowed over 200 yards rushing while missing 28 or so tackles. They looked bad, unprepared, and honestly, soft. That had many, myself included, concerned about today’s game. The Jags put a whooping on the Broncos last season when they were playing their best football. Coming off a tough loss, it felt like the worst-case matchup. Well, they returned to form and shut down the high-powered Jaguars offense. His defense limited the Jags to just 13 points, under 200 yards passing, 95 rushing yards, and came up big late in the game. The pressure was also getting to Lawrence throughout the game. He’s good at avoiding the rush and making plays with defenders in his face, but the Broncos made him work for it. In the end, Joseph’s defense slowed down a hot Jaguars offense that has been unstoppable dating back to last season. LOSER – Red Zone failures Now, the bad. 1st and GOAL at the 1 – ends with a FG 1st and GOAL at the 8 – ends with a Nix INT This includes a 1st and GOAL at the 5 vs. the Chiefs that ended with a field goal. The Broncos NEED to convert these into touchdowns moving forward. They did in the second half, which helped fuel their 4th-quarter comeback, but those first-half failures could have cost them this game. LOSER – Penalties Their penalty woes continue. 10 flags for 53 yards. A few of those flags were declined, so the yardage isn’t as bad as it could have been. Still, the drive-killing penalties on offense were popping up again in the 1st half.…
author: Scotty Payne

title: Instant reaction: Broncos gut out gritty comeback victory over Jaguars
summary: The Denver Broncos hosted the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 2. After a bad loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football, it was a must-win game for the Broncos. They started off slow but showed some moxie and guts in the second half in order to reel off an impressive comeback victory. Here […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Nate Adkins #45, Jonah Coleman #20, and Ben Powers #74 of the Denver Broncos celebrate after Coleman's rushing touchdown against the Jacksonville Jaguars in the fourth quarter of a game at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos hosted the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 2. After a bad loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football , it was a must-win game for the Broncos. They started off slow but showed some moxie and guts in the second half in order to reel off an impressive comeback victory. Here are several instant reactions from this afternoon’s performance. After struggling early on, Broncos’ offense wakes up in second half Like most games, the Broncos struggle to start off fast. They won the coin toss and opted to receive the kick but proceeded to go three-and-out. That was just a sign of things to come. Early on in the game, Denver’s offense had two big blunders in the redzone. After a 49-yard Bo Nix to Jaylen Waddle connection, Denver stalled out at the one-yard line and had to settle for a field goal. Right before the two-minute warning in the second quarter, an ill-advised backfoot throw by Nix to Courtland Sutton was intercepted by Jourdan Lewis keeping points off the board. Settling for just three points with the potential of fourteen is absolutely maddening. Most teams wouldn’t be able to overcome that, but this afternoon—the Broncos did. One of the lowlights in Denver’s loss to Kansas City was the lack of impact from wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. However, he and Nix had quite the connection today. Waddle made a handful of catches over the middle of the field that moved the chains for the Broncos. He was the team’s top performer at the position and finished the game with 8 receptions for 138 yards. The Broncos didn’t have much success running the ball. The Jaguars’ defense is one of the best in the league at stopping it. However, rookie running back Jonah Coleman came on strong late in the game when the team needed him. Coleman grinded out some tough yards and got the go-ahead touchdown for the Broncos in the fourth quarter. Also, a tip of the cap to Nix. He played much better in the second half and finished the game going 22-of-31 for 288 yards with 1 touchdown and 1 interception. Hopefully, we can see him continue to improve and make sound decisions with the football moving forward. Broncos’ defense does great limiting the impact of Trevor Lawrence Limiting the impact of Trevor Lawrence was one of my big keys to the game. Under the tutelage and playcalling of Liam Coen, Lawrence has made the jump to arguably a Top 5 signal caller in the NFL. It was a big test for Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph and his players, but this afternoon they rose to the occasion. Outside of several long completions, Lawrence struggled to get things done through the air. He was 17-of-29 for 189 yards with 1 interception. Denver’s trio of cornerbacks in Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja’Quan McMillian all made great plays on the ball in key third down situations to stop opposing drives. I’m really proud of what the defense was able to accomplish. They gave up some big plays but played lights out when it mattered most and really dominated the second half. Way to go, defense! Those penalties have got to stop There aren’t many big things to gripe about in the game, but the Broncos’ penchant for penalties is one of them. Somehow, someway, they were able to win 14 games last season despite being tops in the league in penalties. Today they had ten more, a lot of them being pre-snap penalties. This is something that has to be corrected moving forward. Denver gutted out an impressive victory today, but they can’t continue to hamper themselves with penalties. This team has too many good coaches for this to keep happening. Hopefully this is fixed sooner than later.
author: Christopher Hart

Late in the fourth quarter of a tight game between the Chicago Bears and Minnesota Vikings, Bears quarterback Caleb Williams scrambled to his left. And while trying to escape a defender, he collapsed to the ground, with no apparent contact causing […]

(Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images That sound you hear is Chicago Bears fans sighing a collective breath of relief. Caleb Williams stays down after getting tripped up #bears pic.twitter.com/BWezgc9U2o — Colin (@ufcolin) September 20, 2026 However, despite it looking like a serious injury, Williams apparently only suffered a hamstring injury, and test on Monday confirmed it was minor. Bears QB Caleb Williams avoided any major injury to his hamstring Sunday, tests confirmed today — and the team isn’t even ruling him out for next Monday’s game against the Eagles, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . A massive sigh of relief in Chicago. pic.twitter.com/mfCT5x0JWR — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) September 21, 2026 While Williams wasn’t having a huge day against a feisty Vikings defense, he is certainly a pivotal piece to what the Bears do on offense. Last week against the Carolina Panthers, Williams completed 21-of-29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns—plus 10 rushes for 65 yards and two touchdowns. Behind Williams’ leadership, the Bears put up a league-high 59 points in Week 1. Tyson Bagent replaced Williams in the game. Bagent has been with the Bears since going undrafted in 2023. In his career, he’s started four games, completing 66.4% of his passes for 917 yards (6.2 Y/A), three touchdowns, and six interceptions. Chicago also has Case Keenum on their roster, though he was listed as inactive for Week 2.

title: Lions reportedly working out ‘group’ of defensive backs
summary: According to a report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, the Detroit Lions will be working out a group of defensive backs when the team reconvenes from their extended break on Monday. Fowler doesn’t have an exhaustive list of those players, but it will include two known names: Jordan Fuller and Jalen Mills. UPDATE: Fowler added one […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - DECEMBER 21: Jordan Fuller #4 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at SoFi Stadium on December 21, 2023 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to a report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, the Detroit Lions will be working out a group of defensive backs when the team reconvenes from their extended break on Monday. Fowler doesn’t have an exhaustive list of those players, but it will include two known names: Jordan Fuller and Jalen Mills. UPDATE: Fowler added one more name to the list: Mike Edwards Lions general manager Brad Holmes is likely very familiar with Fuller, as he was drafted by the Los Angeles Rams in the sixth round of the 2020 NFL Draft, when Holmes served as the Rams’ director of college scouting. Fuller would start 12 games his rookie season at safety, logging three interceptions and five passes defended. He continued to be a full-time starter in 2021, but a hamstring injury held him out of the majority of 2022. After another 17 games started in 2023, he ended up signing with the Panthers on a one-year, $3.25 million deal. Another hamstring injury sidelined him for about half of that season. And last year, he played just six games with the Falcons. While Fuller has dealt with a lot of injuries in his career, he’s an aggressive player that doesn’t mind getting active in the run game. He’s posted a PFF run defense grade above 68 in every year of his career, but he’s been comfortable playing both in the box and as the deep safety. Jalen Mills may sound familiar, because he was with the Lions briefly last season. The 32-year-old safety joined the Lions off waivers in December after Brian Branch suffered his Achilles injury, and he played 65 defensive snaps for the Lions over the final two games of the season. Edwards is a former 2019 third-round pick who spend his first four season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. He’s split time since with the Chiefs (2023, 2025), the Bills (2024), and Buccaneers again (2024). In total, he’s started 30 games and made 89 game appearances. Edwards is described as a “ ball hawk ” and is a two-time Super Bowl winner (Chiefs, Buccaneers). In addition to these two safeties, the Lions have also reportedly shown some interest in free agent cornerback Kenny Moore. The Lions searching for defensive backs could mean two things. For one, it could be a response to Avonte Maddox’s injury. The Lions’ veteran safety left Thursday’s game early with a foot injury, and he did not return. While coach Dan Campbell didn’t have a definitive update on Maddox after the game, he was not optimistic about the outlook of his injury. “I don’t know. Maddox is pretty tough, so when he doesn’t come back, that makes me nervous,” Campbell said. “But I won’t know until tomorrow for sure.” Detroit may also be in the defensive back market because their play in the secondary has been troublesome through two games. Saints quarterback Tyler Shough threw for 410 yards in Week 1 against the Lions, and Bills quarterback Josh Allen through for 248 yards and three touchdowns on Thursday. One other thing to keep in mind: Lions safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph started the season on the Physically Unable to Perform list. They cannot play until Week 5 at the earliest, but they can return to practice this week, if ready. We should have more clarity on this situation Monday, when Campbell is expected to speak with the media.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: How often NFL teams recover from a terrible defensive start
summary: The Detroit Lions defense is in trouble. After two extremely troubling performances, fans and analysts are already wondering if Detroit needs to make massive changes on the defensive side of the ball, while others are already claiming defeat for the team. The silver-lining crew points to the fact that it’s early in the season. September […]
full_text: Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard, left, and head coach Dan Campbell watch practice during mini camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions defense is in trouble. After two extremely troubling performances, fans and analysts are already wondering if Detroit needs to make massive changes on the defensive side of the ball, while others are already claiming defeat for the team. The silver-lining crew points to the fact that it’s early in the season. September is for ugly football and correcting those mistakes. So Detroit has plenty of time to right the ship. But what is the historical context of massive improvement when it comes to terrible play on defense? Does it actually happen a lot, or is it something coaches simply try to manifest by saying they’re all correctable mistakes? For this exercise, I looked at the bottom-five defenses (by points allowed) after two weeks over the last five seasons, exploring where each started and where it ended the season. We’ll start with the most recent data points from the 2025 season and work our way back to 2021. For context, the Lions have allowed 71 points through two games, which currently ranks 31st (before Monday night’s game). 2025 season After 2 weeks: 32. Bears — 79 points allowed (39.5 PPG) 31. Dolphins — 66 points allowed (33.0 PPG) 30. Jets — 64 points allowed (32.0 PPG) 29. Steelers — 63 points allowed (31.5 PPG) t-28. Cowboys — 61 points allowed (30.5 PPG) t-28. Giants — 61 points allowed (30.5 PPG) At the end of the season Bears: 24.4 PPG allowed (23rd) 25th in DVOA 21st in EPA/play Dolphins : 24.9 PPG allowed (24th) 24th in DVOA 25th in EPA/play Jets: 29.6 PPG allowed (31st) 31st in DVOA 20th in EPA/play Steelers: 22.8 PPG allowed (17th) 11th in DVOA 19th in EPA/play Cowboys: 30.1 PPG allowed (32nd) 32nd in DVOA 32nd in EPA/play Giants: 25.8 PPG allowed (26th) 26th in DVOA 27th in EPA/play Of these six teams, only the Steelers really pulled themselves out of the basement, which is kind of incredible, because you may remember they started the season by giving up 32 points to the lowly Jets. However, they bounced back nicely and held each of their last six opponents to 26 points or less. What was the reason for their improvement? A big schematic shift, moving from single-high safety looks to a two-high shell . Everyone else showed their true colors early. 2024 season After 2 weeks: 32. Panthers — 73 points allowed (36.5 PPG) 31. Rams — 67 points allowed (33.5 PPG) 30. Cowboys — 61 points allowed (30.5 PPG) 29. Commanders — 55 points allowed (27.5 PPG) 28. Ravens — 53 points allowed (26.5 PPG) At the end of the season: Panthers: 31.4 PPG allowed (32nd) 32nd in DVOA 32nd in EPA/play Rams: 22.7 PPG allowed (17th) 26th in DVOA 23rd in EPA/play Cowboys: 27.5 PPG allowed (31st) 24th in DVOA 28th in EPA/play Commanders : 23.0 PPG allowed (18th) 23rd in DVOA 22nd in EPA/play Ravens: 21.2 PPG allowed (9th) 6th in DVOA 11th in EPA/play There’s a little more hope in this data set. The Commanders and Rams were able to climb toward average, while the Ravens arguably turned into a top-10 defense. But there’s an interesting story to the 2024 Baltimore Ravens. At the start of the year, the defense was coordinated by former NFL linebacker Zach Orr—his first year as a coordinator. In October, the Ravens added senior defensive assistant Dean Pees to the staff. The actual defensive turnaround didn’t come until weeks later—and some coaches denied that Pees was the catalyst for the improvement —but it’s something to consider. Despite the turnaround, Orr would only last one more season as Ravens defensive coordinator. Again, however, it’s worth pointing out that the Panthers and Cowboys defenses were exactly as they seemed after two weeks. 2023 season After two weeks: 32. Giants — 68 points allowed (34.0 PPG) 31. Bears — 65 points allowed (32.5 PPG) 30. Chargers — 63 points allowed (31.5 PPG) 29. Seahawks — 61 points allowed (30.5 PPG) 28. Lions — 57 points allowed (28.5 PPG) At the end of the season: Giants: 23.9 PPG allowed (26th) 21st in DVOA 22nd in EPA/play Bears: 22.3 PPG allowed (20th) 17th in DVOA 16th in EPA/play Chargers: 23.4 PPG allowed (24th) 26th in DVOA 24th in EPA/play Seahawks: 23.6 PPG allowed (25th) 28th in DVOA 30th in EPA/play Lions: 23.2 PPG allowed (23rd) 13th in DVOA 21st in EPA/play Most of these defenses were able to climb out of the bottom five, but not much further. All remained in the bottom half of the league except arguably the 2023 Lions (by DVOA), coincidentally enough. The Bears managed to become an average defense, as well. Two things worth noting in the Bears’ turnaround: defensive coordinator Alan Williams resigned after two games due to health and family reasons. Additionally, they traded for Montez Sweat at the deadline, and he provided 6.0 sacks in the final nine games. 2022 After two weeks: 32. Cardinals — 67 points allowed (33.5 PPG) 31. Lions — 65 points allowed (32.5 PPG) 30. Titans — 62 points allowed (31.0 PPG) t-29. Falcons — 58 points allowed (29.0 PPG) t-29. Rams — 58 points allowed (28.0 PPG) t-29. Commanders — 58 points allowed (28.0 PPG) At the end of the season: Cardinals 26.4 PPG allowed (31st) 26th in DVOA 20th in EPA/play Lions 25.1 PPG allowed (t-30th) 27th in DVOA 31st in EPA/play Titans 21.1 PPG allowed (t-14th) 19th in DVOA 21st in EPA/play Falcons 22.7 PPG allowed (23rd) 31st in DVOA 29th in EPA/play Rams 24.6 PPG allowed (26th) 18th in DVOA 22nd in EPA/play Commanders 20.2 PPG allowed (7th) 10th in DVOA 5th in EPA/play Again, there is some hope here. The Titans, Rams, and Commanders all pulled themselves out of the bottom-10 by most metrics. Washington, in particular, turned into a top-10 defense. It’s interesting because Washington had one of the worst defenses in 2021 and 2023, but this one haven of a season under defensive coordinator Jack Del Rio worked with no clear reason why. He was fired the next year. 2021 After two weeks: 32. Falcons — 80 points allowed (40.0 PPG) 31. Lions — 76 points allowed (38.0 PPG) 30. Titans — 68 points allowed (34.0 PPG) 29. Ravens — 68 points allowed (34.0 PPG) 28. Chiefs — 65 points allowed (32.5 PPG) At the end of the season: Falcon s 27.0 PPG allowed (30th) 31st in DVOA 28th in EPA/play Lions 27.5 PPG allowed (31st) 29th in DVOA 30th in EPA/play Titans 20.8 PPG allowed (6th) 10th in DVOA 10th in EPA/play Ravens 23.0 PPG allowed (19th) 28th in DVOA 27th in EPA/play Chiefs 21.4 PPG allowed (8th) 22nd in DVOA 23rd in EPA/play We have one more example of a team pulling themselves out of a bottom-five performance and climbing to a top-10 defense by the season’s end: the 2021 Titans. They looked like a completely different unit after their Week 13 bye, allowing 24.2 points per game before the bye week and just 13.8 points per game in the six games after the bye (including playoffs). It’s hard to point to exactly what helped the turnaround, but in a funny coincidence given how many Lions fans want a similar move, it is worth noting that Jim Schwartz was added as a senior defensive assistant prior to the 2021 season. Only one other bottom-five defense was able to pull themselves out of the basement—the Chiefs, who remained in the bottom-10 in efficiency numbers, but the scoring defense jumped into the top-10 likely due to some help from a top-five offense. Conclusions Of the 27 teams that started the season in the bottom-five of scoring defense after two weeks: Only eight (29.6%) finished in the bottom-five in scoring defense However, 17 (63.0%) finished in the bottom-10 in scoring defense Similarly, 17 (63.0%) finished bottom-10 in DVOA, but, oddly, only 14 (51.9%) finished bottom-10 in EPA/play. As for the positive finishes, of the 27 teams: Only five (18.5%) finished in the top half of the league in scoring Five (18.5%) finished in the top half of the league in DVOA Four (14.8%) finished in the top half in EPA/play Of this…

title: Lions vs. Jets odds: Opening lines for Week 3 matchup
summary: The Detroit Lions (1-1) are back inside the comfy confines of Ford Field in Week 3, welcoming coach Aaron Glenn and the New York Jets (1-1 back to town, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7.5 points. In 2025, Glenn stepped away from his defensive coordinator […]
full_text: Lions coach Dan Campbell talks to defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn during minicamp in Allen Park on Wednesday, June 8, 2022. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions (1-1) are back inside the comfy confines of Ford Field in Week 3, welcoming coach Aaron Glenn and the New York Jets (1-1 back to town, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7.5 points . In 2025, Glenn stepped away from his defensive coordinator position with the Lions and accepted a head coaching position with the Jets, the team that drafted him in 1994. Unfortunately, his rookie season as head coach was rough, starting 0-7 before finishing 3-14. Glenn opened the offseason by revamping his coaching staff, beginning with the firing of both offensive coordinator Tanner Engstrand and defensive coordinator Steve Wilks. Former head coach Frank Reich was hired as the Jets’ new offensive coordinator, and Brian Duker—who coached under Glenn with the Lions from 2021-23—was named the new defensive coordinator. Several other coaching positions were also overhauled to match the new coordinators. The Jets were also aggressive with their roster, giving running back Breece Hall a contract extension, trading away quarterback Justin Fields, and acquiring quarterback Geno Smith, safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, and defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat. In free agency, the Jets signed several new starters, including left guard Dylan Parham, EDGE Joseph Ossai, linebacker Demario Davis, defensive tackle David Onyemata, and safety David Belton. In the draft, the Jets used three first-round picks to acquire three more starters: EDGE David Bailey, tight end Kenyon Sadiq, and wide receiver Omar Cooper; they also snagged corner D’Angelo Ponds in the second round and defensive tackle Darrell Jackson in the fourth. In Week 1, the Jets’ offseason moves looked like they paid off, as New York easily handled the Titans 23-10 in Tennessee. Then, in Week 2, the Jets and Packers traded blows in a defensive battle that opened up in the second half and eventually went to overtime. Glenn surprisingly had the Jets take the ball first in overtime, and when the offense went three-and-out, the Packers got the ball in great field position and easily kicked a field goal to secure the win. Detroit’s defense has been struggling, but their offense has been putting up points in volume. And although the Jets’ defense looks like it could give the Lions problems, Vegas doesn’t seem to think it will be enough to affect this game. title: Discussion: What is your level of panic for the Detroit Lions?
summary: On one hand, the sky is not falling for the Detroit Lions. They are still 1-1 to start the 2026 season, and with some easier matchups on deck, they have room to rebound before their Week 6 bye. On the other hand, a beatdown never feels good. The Buffalo Bills did just that against the […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions looks on against the Buffalo Bills during the second quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images On one hand, the sky is not falling for the Detroit Lions. They are still 1-1 to start the 2026 season, and with some easier matchups on deck, they have room to rebound before their Week 6 bye. On the other hand, a beatdown never feels good. The Buffalo Bills did just that against the Lions in a Thursday night tilt that saw them christen their new stadium with an offensive onslaught. The Lions defense could do little to stop Josh Allen and company, whether it was in run defense or pass defense. To call that performance an embarrassment would be harsh yet accurate. On the national stage, the Lions looked lost. We are still in the infancy of the season, but there are rumblings among the Lions fanbase. Was this loss to Buffalo a sign of things to come? How can the ship be righted? Are the Lions truly capable of making a playoff push by season’s end? Safe to say, there is some level of panic right now. Today’s Question of the Day is: What is your level of panic for the Detroit Lions? My answer: 5/10. Firstly, the elephant in the room: this defense is looking bad. Like, really, really bad. Aidan Hutchinson is practically carrying the unit by himself, leading the team with 16 pressures per PFF, whereas second has six (Alim McNeill) and third (Derrick Barnes) has five. In fact, of the Lions’ top nine pressure generators, only two of them are edge defenders: Hutchinson and DJ Wonnum (three pressures)—when Roger McCreary is generating more pressures, that is not ideal. I would like to see Wonnum take another step, whether that comes via pass rush or run defense. The same can be said about rookie Derrick Moore, who has made little impact in his 35 snaps so far (zero tackles to his name). I think the defensive line can improve (of note, I think McNeill and Tyleik Williams have been playing well despite little fanfare), but I cannot say the same about the secondary. Outside of D.J. Reed and maybe Christian Izien, the defensive backs are struggling. Unfortunately, I do not see an in-house solution beyond the players themselves turning it around. Ennis Rakestraw and Nick Whiteside should be given a chance at some point, but both players would have to blow expectations out of the water to turn around the secondary. Even then, the problem with this defense is not on one singular player, nor would adding Joey Porter Jr. be an instant cure. The real fix for this defense needs to come from fundamentals. That means good tackling, holding your gap, making the right read, sealing the edge, and, most of all, communicating. Most Lions defenders have been struggling with at least one of these aspects. Kelvin Sheppard is certainly part of the blame as well, since a poorly-organized defense is a reflection of its coordinator. The Lions simply cannot be a playoff-winning team with a defense like this. There is time for the Lions to improve, and the Bills are arguably the best offense they will face all year, but we need to see improvement in the next few weeks—the New York Jets, Carolina Panthers, Arizona Cardinals should be winnable matchups. I set my panic level at a five, but truthfully, the defense is accounting for at least four of that. I am simply left hoping that the defense will improve, because nothing on the field has shown me otherwise. The reason for my low-ish panic level is that I am genuinely satisfied with the offense. Jared Goff has looked incredible through two games. I will hear nothing about how he benefitted from “garbage time” against the Bills—some of the throws he made were amazing, regardless of score. Coupled with much-improved pocket presence, he is on track for another elite season. He and Amon-Ra St. Brown have been dynamite after a slow first half against the New Orleans Saints. If anything, this offense could be even better. Jahmyr Gibbs is putting on a clinic as a runner and, finally, as a receiver. Yet despite that, his longest play is just a 21-yard run against the Saints. When (not if) he breaks a long play, his totals could skyrocket. This is all coming with Cade Mays on Injured Reserve, Christian Mahogany having missed all but 11 snaps so far, and Blake Miller missing Week 2. When everyone is healthy on that unit, there could be some stout blocking up front for Gibbs. This is not even factoring in a slow start from Jameson Williams, who has been plagued by drops, and Isaac TeSlaa, who has just two catches across two games. Imagine telling a Lions fan that they would be averaging 31 points without significant contributions from either of them. Even Sam LaPorta’s contributions could see an uptick, a player who has been impactful when called upon and resolute as a blocker. I do not think that offensive coordinator Drew Petzing has been perfect yet (I did not like some of those second-down plays versus Buffalo), but I am encouraged by this start. The absence of Ben Johnson is not the reason for Detroit’s failures so far this season, contrary to many national “analysts” and critics. It comes down to the defense, plain and simple. The Lions have a runway to improve, but it gets shorter each week. The offense will have carry the team for most weeks, a difficult and unfair burden—if the Lions need the offense to be perfect in order to win games, then they do not deserve to win many games. How nervous are you about the current state of the 2026 Lions? Let us know in the comments below.
author: John Whiticar

title: Report: Detroit Lions have ‘checked in’ on free agent cornerback
summary: In the aftermath of their disastrous defensive performance against the Buffalo Bills on “Thursday Night Football,” the Detroit Lions are reportedly interested in bringing in some other options at the cornerback position. According to NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the Lions have “checked in” on former Pro Bowl cornerback Kenny Moore II. Moore II, who was […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - DECEMBER 28: Kenny Moore II #23 of the Indianapolis Colts warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Lucas Oil Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the aftermath of their disastrous defensive performance against the Buffalo Bills on “Thursday Night Football,” the Detroit Lions are reportedly interested in bringing in some other options at the cornerback position. According to NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the Lions have “checked in” on former Pro Bowl cornerback Kenny Moore II . Moore II, who was released by the Indianapolis Colts in the spring after the team failed to find a trade partner, is currently a free agent and available to sign with any team. “Sounds like he [Moore] has got a lot of interest from multiple teams in need of a cornerback because of depth reasons and injury reasons,” Garofolo said on a segment of “The Insiders” prior to the start of the 1 p.m. ET games on Sunday. “The Lions amongst the teams that have checked in on Kenny Moore. I’m expecting the veteran former Pro Bowler to sign with a team in the very near future.” Moore II was an undrafted free agent in 2017 out of Valdosta State, first picked up by the New England Patriots before being claimed by the Colts prior to the start of the season. Over the course of nine seasons with the Colts, Moore II played in 132 games—starting 111 of them—primarily as a slot cornerback. His performance in 2021, tallying four interceptions and 13 passes defended, earned him his lone Pro Bowl selection of his career. Despite being just 5-foot-9 and 190 pounds, one of Moore II’s most consistent traits over his career has been his work in run defense, earning PFF grades of 86.2 in 2019, 80.5 in 2022, and 84.4 last season—ranking fifth among all cornerbacks in 2025. Detroit may be even more shorthanded depending on the prognosis of Avonte Maddox after he suffered a foot injury in Thursday’s game against the Bills, and that could lead to some shifting in the Lions secondary. After a summer where Detroit had an open competition for the starting nickel spot, which appeared to be Christian Izien’s job before he suffered an injury prior to Week 1, Moore II could be the veteran help Detroit needs to get things back on track in the secondary.

title: Detroit Lions Week 2 rooting guide: Best outcomes from Sunday’s games
summary: Regardless of what happened on Thursday, I am thankful for a full slate of Sunday NFL games that I can watch from 1 p.m. ET until “Sunday Night Football” comes to a close around 11:30 p.m. ET. Covering the Detroit Lions exclusively makes it difficult to catch any other football happening, but in Week 2, […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; The Detroit Lions cheerleaders take the field prior to a game against the New Orleans Saints at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Regardless of what happened on Thursday, I am thankful for a full slate of Sunday NFL games that I can watch from 1 p.m. ET until “Sunday Night Football” comes to a close around 11:30 p.m. ET. Covering the Detroit Lions exclusively makes it difficult to catch any other football happening, but in Week 2, I can literally catch action from all 16 games. While it may be a little early to start thinking about the playoffs—especially after the game the Lions just played—the fact of the matter is that every game counts, so why not start our rooting guide for the 2026 season while we get to watch all of the games Week 2 has to offer? Here are the teams you should be rooting for while watching NFL football without the Lions this Sunday. Note: I am skipping all AFC vs. AFC games, because they have no (or very little) bearing on the Lions’ playoff chances. 1 p.m. ET slate Panthers (0-1) at Falcons (0-1) Root for: Whoever. The Lions play the entire NFC South this year and can take care of business against either or both teams to win the tiebreaker. That division is currently winless, so there’s not much at stake here. But maybe peek in and see how the Panthers are doing since they’re Detroit’s Week 4 opponent. Vikings (1-0) at Bears (1-0) Root for: Vikings. Personally, I think the Bears are the biggest threat to win the NFC North, and they are certainly riding high after scoring a league-high 59 points in Week 1. It would be nice to have Brian Flores humble Caleb Williams and company, even if it means moving Minnesota to 2-0. Eagles (1-0) at Titans (0-1) Root for: Titans. Always root for AFC over NFC when it comes to playoff standings. Packers (0-1) at Jets (1-0) Root for: Jets. I don’t have to convince you of this one. FTP, always. Though it would be interesting to see how Week 3 plays out with an undefeated Jets team coming to Ford Field. Browns (0-1) at Buccaneers (0-1) Root for: Browns. AFC over NFC, but good luck rooting for a hapless Cleveland team. Saints (0-1) at Ravens (1-0) Root for: Ravens. While it would feel a little better if the Saints turned out to be a really good team, you still have to go AFC over NFC. I know the Lions already have the tiebreaker up on the Saints, but a Ravens win only hurts Detroit in the unlikely event a tiebreaker goes all the way to strength of victory. 4 p.m. ET slate Commanders (0-1) at Cowboys (0-1) — 4:25 p.m. ET Root for: Commanders. Personally, I think the Cowboys are the better team and the less likable. So give them the L. But there is certainly still some residual Commanders hate for the 2024 playoffs, so I wouldn’t judge you if you go the other way. Seahawks (1-0) at Cardinals (1-0) — 4:25 p.m. ET Root for: Cardinals. The Cardinals picked up one of the most unlikely Week 1 wins over the Chargers, but I’m not ready to be afraid of them. The returning Super Bowl champs, however, are still a big NFC threat. Dolphins (0-1) at 49ers (1-0) — 4:25 p.m. ET Root for: Dolphins. Miami is a 13.5-point underdog, so probably won’t matter how hard you root for this one, but it would be nice to see the 49ers melt down. They were my NFC Champion pick this year, and they looked impressive against the Rams in Week 1. Monday Night Football Giants (1-0) at Rams (0-1) — 8:15 p.m. ET Root for: Giants. New York may be better than expected, but continue to root for the downfall of the “superteam” Rams. One, because it would be hilarious to watch the most hyped offseason team fall on its face. Two, because they still seem like the best of these two teams.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Discussion: What gives you hope about the 2026 Detroit Lions?
summary: Things have gotten a little dark around here since Thursday night. Of course, all of that is warranted. The Lions may have been underdogs against the Buffalo Bills, but there was an expectation for them to fight better than that. Falling behind 21-0 and showing no life of defense was undoubtedly a concerning development, especially […]
full_text: Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell reacts to a play against Buffalo Bills during the first half at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, NY, on Thursday, Sept. 17, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Things have gotten a little dark around here since Thursday night. Of course, all of that is warranted. The Lions may have been underdogs against the Buffalo Bills, but there was an expectation for them to fight better than that. Falling behind 21-0 and showing no life of defense was undoubtedly a concerning development, especially off the heels of nearly blowing a 21-0 lead of their own. But we’ve spent plenty of time, space , and breath on the serious concerns about the defense . Let’s spend some time talking about the positives for a minute, because this is far from a lost season just two weeks into the year. So today’s Question of the Day is: What gives you hope about the 2026 Lions? My answer: I still feel pretty darn good about the Lions’ offense. I think offensive coordinator Drew Petzing has designed some creative and effective plays in both the run and the pass game. That’s been especially true in the red zone, where the Lions have converted nine trips into seven touchdowns. And while the run defense took a significant step back from Week 1 to Week 2, I feel confident that when/if the offensive line gets healthy, they’ll be just fine on that front. Jahmyr Gibbs still looks like an absolute stud, and Detroit is finding ways to get him more involved in the passing game, as well. Jared Goff is still playing at a very high level, Amon-Ra St. Brown has looked uncoverable at times, and Sam LaPorta looks like himself after last year’s scary back injury. If the Lions offense can continue to average 31 points a game (or close to it), they will be in every game this season, even if the defense can’t find a way to improve. title: Jager Burton was entirely fine in relief duty
summary: The Green Bay Packers offense line management continues to completely befuddle me beyond belief. After Aaron Banks had to leave the game on Sunday due to a toe injury, which, as of the writing of this article, we still do not know the severity of, the Packers went back to Donovan Jennings at left guard […]
full_text: The Green Bay Packers offense line management continues to completely befuddle me beyond belief. After Aaron Banks had to leave the game on Sunday due to a toe injury, which, as of the writing of this article, we still do not know the severity of, the Packers went back to Donovan Jennings at left guard again. Jennings’ insertion promptly led to the Packers’ run game getting stuck in park. Jennings then had to leave the game due to injury, so Green Bay gave rookie Jager Burton, who had received most of the first-team snaps at left guard all pre-season, the remainder of the snaps in that position. And he was fine. Not great, but he was fine. He looked like an NFL player. I’m not going to highlight every snap he played, but there are a few good and bad ones worth pointing out. The first one here is a good one, as he and center Sean Rhyan pass off a T/T stunt cleanly. pic.twitter.com/BEBU3Eh0ch — rcon14 (@rcon14) September 21, 2026 On the flip side, here is the entire offensive line contributing to a play dying. pic.twitter.com/ZacXo9rjMB — rcon14 (@rcon14) September 21, 2026 Burton’s anchor here is pretty poor, and he loses so much depth that he then gets steamrolled by the end. Despite the left side kind of goofing the whole thing, the primary issue on the play is Belton just losing his one-on-one rep, but no one covered themselves in any glory on this play. pic.twitter.com/g1EDAMbgpT — rcon14 (@rcon14) September 21, 2026 Inside zone or duo? Probably duo based on the attack angles of the double/combos. Burton and Morgan don’t get the type of displacement they’d ideally like on this one, but the run still goes for four. Burton’s man does make the first initial tackle, but the run didn’t have a destiny much longer than that with multiple Jets showing up at the same time. This play kind of encompasses most of Burton’s reps in the run game: Just sort of fine. Tyler Brooke and I had a disagreement on the value of Burton but we saw the same thing, and you can see both sides of it in this play. Burton completes the assignment and doesn’t lose the rep, per se, but also just doesn’t have much physical juice after the point of contact to give you any splash. pic.twitter.com/K2hXRRcVZL — rcon14 (@rcon14) September 21, 2026 This isn’t stonewalling, but this is a pretty clean pass between Burton and Rhyan when the Jets run a mike/will stunt. These can be particularly hard games for interior offensive linemen because they’re usually at a pretty distinct athleticism disadvantage, but this little game doesn’t beat them. Despite Morgan washing out the edge around the loop and Burton being able to toss the linebacker out of the pocket, this is where you can see Jordan Love still be affected by the disaster from last weekend. He bails out of a pocket that was clean if he just steps up to his right, and basically kills the play with what is effectively a dirted ball. One big hop step up and to his right and Matthew Golden probably walks in with a touchdown as he roasted his man on a crosser. Unfortunately, we have to close on what is probably Burton’s worst rep of the day. pic.twitter.com/8gQKbQMwDn — rcon14 (@rcon14) September 21, 2026 To be fair to Burton, this is a tough spot for him to hang. T’Vondre Sweat is listed at 366 pounds and has alignment leverage on Burton before the ball is snapped. Because Morgan has to work up to the second level off the snap, and Rhyan is a full gap-and-a-half away from Sweat, Burton just has to take the big man one-on-one. While Burton gets nice initial contact, Sweat has him set up from the get-go. He keeps his helmet on the outside, baiting Kaleb Johnson to cut off Burton’s behind, and then chucks Burton out of the play entirely to make the tackle. This is just kind of what happens when a slightly undersized guard is matched up with an athletic nose tackle without a leverage advantage. Sometimes you just get beat. Even here, though, on a bad play, Green Bay still picked up three yards, so it doesn’t throw things completely off-schedule. I think the story of Burton’s snaps in this game are exactly what you’d hope for for a day three rookie. He was fine. The pass protection looks ahead of the run blocking, but Green Bay’s running game wasn’t necessarily setup for his game. While they ran a lot of outside zone early, by the time Burton got into the game, it was more duo and inside zone. There was one outside zone rep that went for a nice gain, but Burton’s man tried to jump the gap and basically washed himself entirely out of the play. I don’t see any reason, regardless of injury status for Donovan Jennings, and assuming Banks will be out for Thursday, why Burton shouldn’t be the starting left guard this week. And depending on how he looks in future snaps, could earn himself a full-time starting role at one of the guard spots for the long haul.

title: Packers’ win over Jets was the 3rd double-digit comeback win in the Jordan Love era
summary: The Green Bay Packers managed to flip the script on Sunday afternoon. After giving up big lead after big lead down the stretch on the 2025 season and in Week 1 against the Minnesota Vikings, the Packers came back from a ten-point deficit in the fourth quarter to defeat the New York Jets 20-17 in […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - SEPTEMBER 24: Romeo Doubs #87 of the Green Bay Packers catches a pass for a touchdown during the second half of an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2023 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers beat the Saints 18-17. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers managed to flip the script on Sunday afternoon. After giving up big lead after big lead down the stretch on the 2025 season and in Week 1 against the Minnesota Vikings, the Packers came back from a ten-point deficit in the fourth quarter to defeat the New York Jets 20-17 in Week 2. A post by our friends at the Cro Pack Cro podcast after last week’s game now seems like an odd and amusing omen: @callmematub.bsky.social is there one game over the last eight years in which MLF- led Packers won after overcoming a double digit deficit? — Cro Pack Cro (@cropackcropodcast.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T05:08:03.686Z Still, this post got me to thinking last week, so I did some research ahead of the Week 2 game. Since Jordan Love took over as the Packers’ full-time starting quarterback to start the 2023 season, the Packers had exactly two comeback wins when down by 10 or more points at any time in the game before Sunday’s win at MetLife Stadium, which became the third. Prior to Love’s tenure, however, the Packers successfully mounting big comebacks was a bit more common. In the four seasons with LaFleur as head coach and Aaron Rodgers at quarterback the team posted seven wins after facing a double-digit deficit. Let’s look at the first two Love comebacks first, then we’ll take a quick look at the earlier ones from the LaFleur-Rodgers era. 2023 Week 3: vs. New Orleans Saints Love’s third start of the 2023 season and his fourth start overall got out to an abysmal start. Facing an Alvin Kamara-less Saints squad, the Packers dug themselves a 17-0 hole by halftime thanks to touchdowns by former Packer Jimmy Graham and a punt return score from Rasheed Shaheed. Rashan Gary had his first and only three-sack game in this contest, however, and one of those knocked starting QB Derek Carr out of the game early in the third quarter. The score remained 17-0 heading into the fourth quarter, however, when the Packers eked out a field goal to finally get on the board. Green Bay’s leading receiver in the game was the Defensive Pass Interference flag. Love drew back-to-back DPI calls on the first two plays of the next drive, first a 45-yarder on Alontae Taylor then a 22-yard call on Isaac Yiadom. Love eventually ran the ball into the end zone on 4th-and-goal from the 1 to pull the Packers to within 8 points at 17-9, and LaFleur made the decision to go for two. Love converted with a pass to Samori Touré, bringing Green Bay back to within six points and giving them a chance to win with a touchdown. The defense forced a 3-and-out, and Love led the offense on another touchdown drive, picking up 24 yards on a scramble and a 30-yard gain on a pass to Jayden Reed. Love eventually found Romeo Doubs for an 8-yard touchdown on 3rd down and Anders Carlson hit the PAT to put the Packers ahead. The drama wasn’t over, however. The Packers’ win was not secured until a few minutes later, when Blake Grupe’s 46-yard go-ahead field goal attempt went wide right. 2025 Week 7: @ Arizona Cardinals The most recent 10-point comeback came last year in one of the crazier games of the 2025 season. You might not even remember that the Packers were down by double digits, however, because they only trailed by that amount of time for SEVEN SECONDS. The Cardinals took a 13-3 lead with 0:07 left in the second quarter, as Trey McBride scored a touchdown to give them that edge. Arizona booted the kickoff into the end zone, however, and one 22-yard completion from Love to Romeo Doubs over the middle and a timeout brought Lucas Havrisik on for a franchise-record 61-yard field goal to pull the Packers to within 13-6 at halftime. Green Bay then doubled up and tied the game on the first drive of the third quarter and traded scores throughout the second half, eventually winning 27-23 after Matt LaFleur kept his offense on the field late rather than kicking to tie the game. Remember that 4th down conversion to Tucker Kraft? We sure did, as it ranked #9 on our Top Plays of 2025 Countdown . This whole game was well-represented on that countdown, with Havrisik’s franchise record kick landing at #8 and a game-clinching sack from Micah Parsons earning an honorable mention . That’s three comebacks in just over three seasons of Love, but in the four years of the LaFleur-Rodgers, the Packers mounted seven such wins. Many of these were early deficits, however, not late rallies. In fact, only four of these games saw the Packers trail at any point in the fourth quarter. 2019 Week 6: vs. Lions The first double-digit comeback for Matt LaFleur as head coach was in his first game against the Lions early in the 2019 season. Detroit led 13-0 early in the second quarter before the Packers stormed back, tying the game on the first drive of the second half. The Lions kicked three straight field goals after that to take back a 9-point lead early in the fourth quarter, but Allen Lazard’s heroics — scoring on a 35-yard touchdown and hauling in three big receptions on the final drive of the game — helped set up Mason Crosby for a short game-winning field goal for a 23-22 victory. 2019 Week 17: @ Lions The Packers came back on Matt Patricia’s Lions in both 2019 matchups. With David Blough starting at quarterback, Detroit led 17-3 at the half, getting a field goal on a 20-second drive before the break. As in the previous matchup, Lazard scored a 4th-quarter touchdown, this time to tie the game at 20, and Crosby again gave the Packers the win as the clock expired. That sent the Packers into the playoffs at 13-3 and as the NFC’s second seed. 2020 Week 2: vs. Lions It was 3-for-3 in comeback wins for LaFleur against Patricia. Once again, Detroit led 14-3, this time at the end of the first quarter, but Green Bay stormed back with 31 unanswered points, including two Rodgers touchdown passes, a 75-yard score from Aaron Jones, and a pick-six by Chandon Sullivan, cruising to a 42-21 win. 2021 Week 14: vs. Bears It was a season and a half between big comebacks for the Packers, who trailed 10-0 to Chicago early in the second quarter on Sunday Night Football. The Packers bounced back with back-to-back scores, including a Rasul Douglas pick-six, but they gave the Bears two right back on a long pass from Fields to Damiere Byrd and then a 97-yard punt return by Jakeem Grant as the Bears retook a 10-point lead at 24-14. The Packers got a touchdown before the half from Davante Adams, then the Bears tacked on a field goal before the break, holding a 27-21 lead at halftime. After that, though, it was all Packers, as they cleaned up their issues and outscored the Bears 24-3 in the second half, eventually closing out a 45-30 victory. 2022 Week 10: vs. Cowboys The Packers, facing old head coach Mike McCarthy for the first time, were down 28-14 to start the fourth quarter. Aaron Rodgers found Christian Watson for two 4th-quarter scores to send the game to overtime, then they got a 4th down stop with the Cowboys in Packers territory and Mason Crosby kicked a short field goal to win the game 31-28. 2022 Week 12: @ Bears An eventual 28-19 Packers win started out poorly, with Chicago going up 10-0 in the first quarter. Justin Fields provided the early Bears touchdown with a 55-yard run and the Bears led 19-10 heading into the fourth, but the Packers were driving at the time. AJ Dillon scored on the second play of the fourth quarter to cut the lead to two, then the Packers got a go-ahead field goal from Crosby before Watson put the game away with a 46-yard run on an end-around for the final score of a 9-point win. 2022 Week 16: vs. Dolphins The Packers may have only won 8 games in 2022, but three of them were of the big comeback…

title: Green Bay Packers News: Anatomy of a comeback win
summary: Did Skyy Moore just save the Green Bay Packers’ season? The premise of the question is a bit absurd, yes. Short of catastrophic injuries, the result of one play is almost never the difference between a single win or loss, let alone the trajectory of an entire season. But Moore’s 63-yard punt return in the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 20: Skyy Moore #23 of the Green Bay Packers runs the ball against Troy Reeder #50 of the New York Jets during the second half of the game at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Did Skyy Moore just save the Green Bay Packers’ season? The premise of the question is a bit absurd, yes. Short of catastrophic injuries, the result of one play is almost never the difference between a single win or loss, let alone the trajectory of an entire season. But Moore’s 63-yard punt return in the fourth quarter on Sunday put the Green Bay Packers in position to tie the game even if they didn’t gain a single yard. And it’s a good thing, too, because the offense only picked up three. Moore’s return, with the Jets leading 17-14, was just one key play in the Packers’ comeback from being down by 10 points in the fourth quarter, but it might well have been the most important. The defense largely did its job all day long, save for one two drives when the Jets picked on cornerbacks Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse. But in the fourth quarter (and eventually in overtime), the defense locked down Geno Smith and company, getting sack contributions from five different players, most notably getting to Smith on back-to-back plays to start the extra frame. The Packers were sloppy, to be sure. The Jets were sloppy too. But the defense and special teams helped pick up an offense that again was struggling on the offensive line, though this time due in large part to injuries rather than an abysmal game plan. Comebacks take a village. In the 4th quarter and OT, the Packers rallied together and did just enough to avoid starting the season 0-2. Thank goodness. Rapid reaction: List of unsung heroes is long for Packers | Packers.com Skyy Moore, Chris Brooks, Dani Dennis-Sutton, Barryn Sorrell…each of these players (and many more) made huge plays down the stretch to help the Packers get their first win of 2026. 3 big things from Packers’ win over Jets: LVN erupts, Skky Moore shines | Packers Wire Lukas Van Ness’ breakout game was probably last year’s Ravens game, but this will probably be the one that fans remember because it ended in a memorable victory. He’s now up to 2.5 sacks on the season and is showing why the Packers had faith in him to continue developing. Packers’ Less-Is-More Gamble at Receiver Backfires After Jayden Reed Injury | SI.com The team’s receiver depth will certainly be tested by this injury, but the doom and gloom of the headline seems a bit overblown. Bet on the Packers leaning even more heavily into 12 and 13 personnel, which will lessen the blow of not having their top slot receiver. Week 2 impact on the NFC: Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels hurt | ESPN The severity of Williams’ injury has yet to be determined, but if his initial reaction is any indication, don’t expect him to play against the Packers in Week 5. LISTEN — The Repack, Week 2: More Weirdness at MetLife | Frozen Tundra Frequencies Strange things seem to happen every time the Packers and Jets get together. More absurdity! Golden retriever brings toys to the intruder who breaks into his house | AP If you’ve ever had — or even met — a golden retriever, you’ll know this is far more likely than the dog actually defending its home. title: Packers Injury Updates: Matt LaFleur addresses Jayden Reed and Zach Bako-Bewele injuries
summary: The Green Bay Packers lost two crucial players to their offense in the opening three plays of the game. First, slot receiver Jayden Reed was injured and left the field in a backboard. Immediately after that play, starting right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, who had been dealing with recovery from patellar tendon surgery, was carted off […]
full_text: (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers lost two crucial players to their offense in the opening three plays of the game. First, slot receiver Jayden Reed was injured and left the field in a backboard. Immediately after that play, starting right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, who had been dealing with recovery from patellar tendon surgery, was carted off the field in an inflatable cast. Usually, an inflatable cast means that there’s a broken bone involved. In the post-game press conference, head coach Matt LaFleur said that Reed has feeling and movement in his extremities, but that he will stay overnight in New York/New Jersey for extra tests. Go ahead and assume it’s going to be a while before you see Reed on the field again. The Packers’ receiver rotation is very, very rigid , and Skyy Moore has been the full-time backup slot, with no one else getting those looks dating back to the preseason. The assumption, as long as Green Bay’s plan doesn’t change, is that Moore will replace Reed’s reps moving forward. Bako-Bewele’s injury “could be out for a long time,” according to LaFleur. Bako-Bewele’s backup is Anthony Belton, who played the position for all but the three snaps that Bako-Bewele was on the field for. Belton has been the preferred backup at the position dating back to training camp, so it’s safe to assume that that’s where he’s going to slide in. While it wasn’t addressed specifically in the press conference, left guard Aaron Banks, who missed Week 1 with knee tendinitis, left the game on Sunday with a toe injury, too. He was initially replaced by Donovan Jennings and then rookie fifth-round pick Jager Burton. Injuries got so bad on the offensive line that at one point, the coaching staff discussed moving Tucker Kraft to offensive tackle until Jacob Monk was cleared by the medical staff. Jennings, Banks’ replacement, also left the game with a hand injury. There are no updates on the injuries to Banks and Jennings. We’ll know more on Monday, as the Packers will have to release injury reports starting tomorrow, because Green Bay will be playing the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday Night Football . — Update: Jayden Reed tweeted out that he’s feeling better. Doing much better, appreciate all the prayers and support 🙏🏾 #GPG 🧀 — j.reed11💂🏾 (@JaydenReed5) September 20, 2026 — Update: In an interview for the Packers’ YouTube channel, LaFleur stated that Bako-Bewele’s injury “could be a season-ender.”
