title: Rams takeaways we can glean from NFL Week 2 results
summary: We may look back at the end of the season and feel it is best to throw out the Los Angeles Rams’ opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. Week 1 can lie. It can also be the first sign of an unexpected problem. These are a few NFL narratives that flipped on […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers calls to his team during the first quarter of the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at SoFi Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images We may look back at the end of the season and feel it is best to throw out the Los Angeles Rams’ opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. Week 1 can lie . It can also be the first sign of an unexpected problem. These are a few NFL narratives that flipped on their head with another week of information collection: The Bills may have the best offense in football. Their defense could be trouble. Buffalo allowed 31 points in their opener to a Texans team that managed just six points in their encore against the Bengals. The Bills gave up 31 to the Lions on Thursday Night Football. Josh Allen looks unstoppable through two games. Opposing teams may be able to keep pace with how porous the defense seems without Sean McDermott. Buffalo is now an offensive team. The Rams host the Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5. If a team came out completely flat in Week 1, the whole game may be a lie Two of the most disappointing outcomes from the opening week were the Rams not showing up against the 49ers and the Denver Broncos looking completely inept against the Kansas City Chiefs. The Broncos rebounded with a 20-13 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, who had one of the most impressive Week 1 performances. That is an encouraging sign for the Rams, who need to bounce back on Monday Night Football against the New York Giants. Denver provides a proof of concept for LA. The real test will come in Week 3 when the Rams and Broncos clash on Sunday Night Football in Denver. We should get real answers surrounding the trajectory of both teams soon after we see how LA fares against the Giants. Justin Herbert as an allegory for Matthew Stafford The Rams entered 2026 with sky-high expectations. Similarly but to a lesser degree, most expected the Los Angeles Chargers to take a step forward this year as well. But the Chargers have now fallen to 0-2 . They’ve dropped games to the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders, neither of which were even close to competent a year ago. It seems the expectations are getting to Justin Herbert. He looks emotional on the field and has clearly regressed at this stage of his career. It’s early. The results are not encouraging. How will Matthew Stafford perform after posting one of the worst quarterback performances in Week 1? If Herbert can suffer a fall of grace, so can Stafford—and Herbert is in the prime of his career. The Chargers face the Rams at SoFi Stadium as the road team in Week 8. Is Sam Darnold along for the Seahawks’ ride? After failing with the New York Jets and Carolina Panthers, Sam Darnold spent time rehabilitating his career with the 49ers and Minnesota Vikings before leading the Seattle Seahawks to a Super Bowl victory. But his backup, Drew Lock, has now led Seattle to wins over the last two weeks and looked strong along the way. Seattle has taken down both the New England Patriots and the Arizona Cardinals with Lock behind the wheel. Has Darnold really taken a significant step forward from his days in New York and Carolina? Or is the Seahawks’ supporting cast so good that it makes whoever is under center irrelevant? The Rams won’t see the Seahawks until Week 16 and 18 this season. Final thoughts A dominant performance by the Rams on Monday Night Football against the Giants would dispel a lot of concerns surrounding this football team. However, LA is favored by 7.5 points and should be expected to win this game. Their next stretch of contests against the Broncos, Eagles, and Bills will tell us who they really are. Based on how many teams changed their trajectory following a disastrous Week 1 loss, there is certainly hope for the Rams. They must take care of business on Monday.

full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams passes the ball during the NFL football game at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Morgan Hancock/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are already behind the Seattle Seahawks, San Francisco 49ers and the Arizona Cardinals in the NFC West race with L.A.’s Week 2 game still to be played on Monday night. Even with a win Monday, the Rams will still be looking up at the 49ers and Seahawks, but a win puts the Rams back in business with a 1-1 record. An 0-2 record could mean the end of their season. Yes, that’s dramatic, and, yes, it could be true. I don’t make the rules. The rules are you need to win the in the NFL and so far, the Rams haven’t. Can they put a winning game together on Monday night? Even if the Rams lose, what fans and the team want to see is a better effort than they showed in Week 1. If L.A. comes out flat, or just plain bad again, the concern meter will rise. Will Matthew Stafford look better? Can the Rams overcome the loss of Myles Garrett? How does Aaron Donald look? Will Puka Nacua play? If Nacua doesn’t play, how will the Rams respond? Can Chris Shula and his defense improve? How about Harrison Mevis and the special teams? The Rams have a lot of questions. They get the chance to answer some of them (for better or worse) on Monday Night Football. 2026 NFL season, Week 2: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.com) “ Mike Macdonald’s defense smothers Cardinals . Arizona had one good drive – a 12-play, 61-yard, five-first down, TD possession – in the first half. The rest of the afternoon, Seattle’s defense dominated. The defensive line destroyed the Cards’ front, bringing waves of pressure and slamming the door on Arizona’s running game. Seattle allowed just 39 yards on 14 carries combined from Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier (2.8 yards per carry). With the run game silenced, Seattle was able to tee off on Jacoby Brissett . The Seahawks generated 18 QB pressures, per Next Gen Stats. On dropbacks under pressure, Seattle held Brissett to 4 of 11 for 9 yards, with an interception and a 7.0 passer rating. Give safety Julian Love some flowers for a gorgeous sliding INT, his second of the season. Facing a Cards team that put up nearly 400 yards in Week 1, Macdonald’s crew held Arizona to 151 yards, 3.2 yards per play, 10 first downs and 3 of 12 on third downs. Domination.“ 2026 NFL season, Week 2: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.com) “ Milestone day for McCaffrey, Kittle. On a day that was all about Kyle Shanahan’s offense, it was no shock that the heartbeat of the supporting cast shined brightest. Christian McCaffrey had just 67 scrimmage yards but made the most of his touches near the goal line. His pair of rushing scores put him in elite company, as he became the third player in NFL history to record 50-plus scrimmage TDs with multiple teams, joining Hall of Famers Marshall Faulk (Rams, 85; Colts 51) and Randy Moss (Vikings, 92; Patriots, 50). But perhaps the most exciting aspect of San Francisco’s offensive frenzy was George Kittle’s return to prominence. After missing six games in 2025 with an Achilles injury and a modest Week 1 outing in Australia, the seven-time Pro Bowler led the team with 80 receiving yards and his first touchdown, a 12-yard reception on a busted coverage, since the injury. Kittle’s third catch of the day also marked his 600th career reception, the 11th tight end in league history to accomplish that feat.“ Whose house? Rams return home as Aaron Donald makes long-awaited comeback against Giants (nypost) “The Rams surrendered 174 rushing yards, failed to record a sack on 34 pass attempts and generated just two quarterback hits. Myles Garrett finished with the same statistical line as Aaron Donald, who watched from the comforts of his couch at home in Los Angeles: zero tackles, zero sacks and zero pressures. Now Garrett is on injured reserve following a knee procedure, leaving Donald to make his anticipated return after more than two years away from football. The rams have 99 problems, but No. 99 will not be one, no pressure AD.“ Notable injuries, news from Sunday’s Week 2 games: Packers WR Jayden Reed (neck) carted off vs. Jets (nfl.com) “ San Francisco 49ers receiver Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was ruled out of Sunday’s game against the Dolphins. Head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters after the game Robinson and DT James Thompson Jr. have high ankle sprains. Wide receiver Mike Evans (hip) did not return to the game but the injury doesn’t look serious, per Shanahan. Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price (chest) did not return to Sunday’s game against the Cardinals. HC Mike Macdonald said after the game that X-rays came back negative on Price’s injury.“ New York Giants vs. Rams: 5 things to know before Monday night’s kickoff (giantswire) “Donald will be strapping on the pads for the first time since 2023, having retired after that season. No one knows what kind of physical or mental shape he’s in, what impact he’ll have, or how much he’ll play. He’ll be butting heads with Giants rookie guard Francis Mauigoa, which promises to be an interesting matchup. Nacua has been nursing a groin injury and is listed as questionable. He did not practice Saturday, but his track record suggests he’ll play. At what percentage is unknown. If Puka is limited, the Rams don’t have much depth behind him, with Jordan Whittington (quad) doubtful. Of course, they still have Davante Adams in their lineup, but he only caught three of six targets in the Week 1 loss to San Francisco.“ Donald in, Garrett out: How will Rams defense look with huge addition (and subtraction)? (espn) “Though the future Pro Football Hall of Fame defensive tackle said he knows it has been two full seasons since he walked off the field after the season-ending loss to the Detroit Lions , in a way, it feels like he never left. “[After] being back around, I feel like I was just here last year,” Donald said. “Time flies by so fast, and I forget that I haven’t play[ed] football for two years. I feel like I’m just back to my normal self.” Donald did not play in — or even travel to — the Rams’ season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia, as he worked to get up to speed after coming out of retirement Aug. 30.“ Giants vs. Rams: What to watch as Los Angeles looks to bounce back in ‘MNF’ (cbsports) “The Giants did whatever they wanted against the Cowboys on “Sunday Night Football” last weekend. New York ran the ball 37 times for 165 yards and a touchdown. Jaxson Dart completed 23 of 29 passes for 230 yards and three scores. The Giants controlled the ball for 36 minutes and 40 seconds of the 60-minute game. They had three second-half drives; they scored a touchdown on each of the first two and ran the clock out on the third. All three drives lasted 12-plus plays. It was surgical stuff.“ Sean McVay and Rams are being tested early, but it’s far too soon to write them off (nytimes) “The numbers speak to the depths of that performance, but also to the standard that made the Rams Super Bowl favorites even before their blockbuster trade for two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett or the return of three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald from retirement. Unlike some infamous preseason “ dream teams ,” these Rams weren’t microwaved through transactions in a single offseason. This team fell just short of a trip to the Super Bowl and returned every starter except the two it replaced with Garrett and All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie.“ Criticism of Chris Shula Is Missing the Bigger Picture With Rams Defense (si.com) “However, that doesn’t make the defense blameless. The Rams trailed by three points at halftime before the 49ers scored a touchdown to start the half and then allowed a 99-yard touchdown drive following a missed fourth-down conversion from the offense. Put together, it…

title: Rams one loss from joining Chargers as early-season disappointment
summary: It’s been a rough start to the football season for Los Angeles fans, as the LA Rams and Chargers are winless so far. The Rams must win against the Giants on Monday night or risk following in the Chargers’ footsteps as an early-season disappointment. Entering the 2026 season, the Chargers had the fifth-highest odds to […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers talks to his team prior to the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at SoFi Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been a rough start to the football season for Los Angeles fans, as the LA Rams and Chargers are winless so far. The Rams must win against the Giants on Monday night or risk following in the Chargers’ footsteps as an early-season disappointment. Entering the 2026 season, the Chargers had the fifth-highest odds to win the Super Bowl, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . They also have the fourth-most wins in the NFL since Jim Harbaugh took the head coaching job in 2024. So far, this season is trending to be a bust for the Chargers, as they’ve lost their first two games to the Cardinals and Raiders despite being favored in both matchups. View this post on Instagram Neither Arizona nor Las Vegas is expected to be a juggernaut or finish with a winning record this season. It was already bad (and odd) enough for the Chargers to lose 26-14 in the first two games. The other LA losing games to teams they should have beaten could spell the end of their season before Week 3. Their schedule is set to get EXTREMELY BRUTAL. The Chargers will play five teams that made the playoffs in 2025 in their next seven games, including the Rams and the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks. Holy strength-of-schedule, Batman! The Chargers are now 0-2. Their next 7 games are: At Bills At Seahawks Vs Broncos At Chiefs At Rams Vs Texans At Ravens — Field Yates (@FieldYates) September 20, 2026 Los Angeles won’t start 0-9, as they’ll figure out a way to win maybe one or two of those matchups. Either way, it doesn’t matter, considering the Chargers shouldn’t be in this position in the first place. The Rams cannot afford to stumble like their roommate any further. They have far more on the line than the Chargers. Falling short of expectations isn’t an option for the Rams. LA’s front office poured too many resources into the roster — trading for Myles Garrett and signing Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, for example — to allow that to happen, recent injury concerns be damned. As it’s been stated many, many times since the Rams lost to the 49ers, it was undoubtedly a major setback to begin the season. It certainly took the wind out of the sails of what could be a special season in Hollywood. Yes, the Niners are way better than both teams the Chargers have lost to, yet the Rams were still favored, so there are no excuses. The Rams can’t let that season-opening failure define them, as the Chargers have essentially allowed it to happen through the first two weeks. Similar to the Chargers, the Rams have a tough upcoming slate. Following the Giants game, the Rams will face four playoff teams from last season in their next seven, including the Chargers. They will also play the Raiders, who the Chargers lost to by 12 on Sunday. Simply put, the Rams must win on Monday night to avoid becoming an early-season disappointment like the Chargers. It might already be too late for the Chargers this early in the year, and the Rams could suffer a similar fate if they can’t beat an opponent in New York that they should be able to beat.

Earlier in the week star edge Myles Garrett was placed on the Injured Reserve List and ruled out for a minimum of four weeks. This disappointing news was compounded by the Rams final injury report […]
full_text: Joe Cardona #49 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the NFL football game against the San Francisco 49ers (Photo by Robert Cianflone/Getty Images) | Getty Images Although it’s only Week 2, it appears the Los Angeles Rams are already juggling the roster because of injury woes. Earlier in the week star edge Myles Garrett was placed on the Injured Reserve List and ruled out for a minimum of four weeks. This disappointing news was compounded by the Rams final injury report before their Monday Night Football tilt with the New York Football Giants. L.A.’s WR#1, Puka Nacua is a game time decision with an ailing hip, safety Kamren Kinchens has been ruled out, and Jordan Whittington, the Rams WR#3 and primary kick off returner, is designated as doubtful. Injuries in the NFL can unquestionably affect how a team performs, both offense and defense can feel the pain of individual players missing time, particularly when extended. How a team rallies around the replacements can make or break a season. The effect and rally extends to special teams as well. If Kinchens and Whittington can’t go, that leaves big holes in the Rams return and coverage units. Kinchens was used on coverage units in Week 1, while Whittington did gunner duty on both punts and kick offs to go with his return work. If you factor in L.A.s three other nicked up starters, Kamren Curl, Nate Landman and Omar Speights who were limited all week in practice, the Rams could be missing 42 special teams reps that were there in Week 1. Here’s last week’s special teams coverage/return snap counts and which unit they were accrued. I omitted the players with a single rep and did not list the field goal/extra point plays. Shaun Dolac – 17 – KO RET, P COV, KO COV Jaylen McCollough – 15 – KO RET, P COV, KO COV Grant Stuard – 14 – KO RET, P COV, P RET, KO COV Jordan Whittington – 13 – KO RET, P COV, P RET, KO COV Xavier Smith – 11 – KO RET, P COV, P RET Quentin Lake – 10 – P RET, KO COV Tyler Higbee – 10 – KO RET, P COV Omar Speights – 9 – KO RET, P COV Davis Allen – 9 – KO RET Josh Wallace – 8 – P COV Poona Ford – 8 – P RET Desjuan Johnson – 8 – P RET, KO COV Tanner Ingle – 8 – KO RET, KO COV Nate Landman – 7 – P COV, P RET Braden Fiske – 7 – P RET Terrance Ferguson – 6 – KO RET Trent McDuffie – 6 Myles Garrett – 6 Kamren Kinchens – 6 – P COV, KO COV Konata Mumpfield – 6 – KO RET Ty Hamilton – 5 Tyler Davis – 3 – P RET Emmanuel Forbes – 2 – P RET Josiah Stewart – 2 – KO COV Wesley Bailey – 2 – KO COV Rams punter Ethan Evans just deadlifted 800 pounds. THIS GUY IS A PUNTER! P-U-N-T-E-R pic.twitter.com/WrWvMNv0l6 — Spirit (@BOOK1R_) February 18, 2025 Why special teams are important Last season the Rams special teams unit was arguably one of the worst in the NFL. It’s not good policy to lay losses on play in a game, but a good argument could be made that special teams play had a big hand in at least three losses. As such, the L.A. braintrust fired coordinator Chase Blackburn late in the season and assistant Ben Kotwica at season’s end. Bubba Ventrone was hired to fill the void and he brought along his assistant from the Cleveland Browns, Kyle Hoke. Week 1 of 2026 was not exactly a Rams special teams renaissance. The specialists, Ethan Evans, Harrison Meevis, and Joe Cardona all did well and there was a glimpse of hope in the punt return game when L.A. double- teamed one of the opposing gunners, but overall, coverage and kickoff returns left fans wanting. Allowing an acceptable 17 yards on two returns was marred by 13 coming on one of them, but 37 yards per kickoff long term is a recipe for disaster. Although Xavier Smith got a bit of room and returned his only punt for 11 yards, the kickoff returns, and there were a few, only went for an average of 23,8 yards. The Rams have had a penchant for giving their special teams the short shrift under the Sean McVay regime. It seems he prefers a conservative approach and has little taste for returns, either for or against. He often seems content for a fair catch and to get right into the offense. Until the NFL changed the rules, Rams kickoffs could invariably be expected to traverse through the end zone without a return. Changing the coaching guard is only part of improving overall play. Teaching lane/angle discipline is important, but players with the proper skillsets must be added. The simplest path? Identify players who are athletic and are adept at tackling in space or running in the open field. In today’s NFL, explosive plays are key and can lead to points, flipping the field, and creating emotion/momentum. Not just on offense and defense, special teams as well.

title: How will Rams manage injuries to Kam Kinchens, Puka Nacua?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are starting to look fairly short-handed as they prepare for a clash against the New York Giants on Monday Night Football. The biggest uncertainty is Puka Nacua being listed as “questionable” for the game, although the star receiver seems to be trending in the wrong direction. Nacua’s backup, Jordan Whittington, is […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams is tackled in the first quarter of the NFL football game against San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are starting to look fairly short-handed as they prepare for a clash against the New York Giants on Monday Night Football. The biggest uncertainty is Puka Nacua being listed as “questionable” for the game, although the star receiver seems to be trending in the wrong direction . Nacua’s backup, Jordan Whittington, is “doubtful” for the Week 2 contest. Already ruled out are Myles Garrett—who was placed on injured reserve and will miss at least the next four games— and safety Kamren Kinchens . On a positive note, Aaron Donald is set to make his comeback from retirement official. Kamren Curl, Omar Speights, and Nate Landman carry no injury designation despite missing practice time earlier this week. It’s worth monitoring Nacua’s status ahead of gametime Monday evening. With his availability up in the air, how will the Rams manage his injury as well as Kinchens’? LA’s plan at receiver without Nacua, Whittington It’s unfortunate that both Nacua and Whittington are injured at the same time. Whittington has been a productive player when given the opportunity, and he’s stylistically more similar to Nacua than Davante Adams. There’s a chance that the replacement of Nacua’s production does not come from other receivers—the offset may instead be derived from the tight ends. Colby Parkinson received just two targets last week. Terrance Ferguson had one. The ball could find both players more often without Nacua. Parkinson has averaged 3.46 yards per route run without Nacua on the field, which would be an elite mark for a tight end. Ferguson scored touchdowns in all three games he played last season where either of Nacua or Adams were unavailable. If you are a fantasy football player looking to make due should Nacua be on the sidelines, the answer may be more challenging. Parkinson and Ferguson are the most likely beneficiaries. Don’t put your faith in Konata Mumpfield or CJ Daniels. How will Rams adjust secondary without Kinchens? Similar to how Nacua’s absence could signal a schematic change on offense, the defense may also flip the script without Kinchens. Quentin Lake was the team’s primary slot corner last week against the 49ers. He may play a more traditional safety role in order to man Kinchens’ ordinary duties. The other alternative would be deploying Jaylen McCollough at Kinchens’ spot, but McCollough is better suited playing closer to the line of scrimmage. Utilizing Lake in a safety role rather than in the slot would open an opportunity for Trent McDuffie to play more often inside. That likely means taking Emmanuel Forbes off the sideline and giving him significant run on the perimeter. LA’s only other deep safety, rookie UDFA Nick Andersen, is on the practice squad. He could be activated for Monday night’s game, although the Rams probably did not expect to see him play meaningful snaps this early in the season. I think it’s more likely that Lake moves to the defensive backfield and the Rams make due in the slot with a mix of McCollough and McDuffie. McSlot.

title: Rams-Giants final injury report: Puka Nacua trending ‘wrong way’ per report
summary: The LA Rams and New York Giants released their final injury reports ahead of their Monday night game and star receiver Puka Nacua is a game-time decision. But Adam Schefter hinted at bad news, reporting on Sunday that Nacua is trending the “wrong way” right now. LA Rams injuries The Rams have already scratched Kamren […]
full_text: The LA Rams and New York Giants released their final injury reports ahead of their Monday night game and star receiver Puka Nacua is a game-time decision. But Adam Schefter hinted at bad news, reporting on Sunday that Nacua is trending the “wrong way” right now . LA Rams injuries The Rams have already scratched Kamren Kinchens from the contest with a hamstring injury , while Nacua and Jordan Whittington will be game-time decisions. DPOY, Myles Garrett, was placed on IR on Thursday. Nacua and Whittington both appeared on the injury report for the first time on Thursday, and while Nacua is listed as questionable, he is more likely to play than Whittington, who is listed as doubtful. Said McVay regarding Nacua : “He’s got a little bit of soreness in that groin, being smart with him as a skill player,” McVay said. “Whether or not he plays is to be determined, and so we’ll see how he’s feeling.” While the Rams would obviously miss the two-time Pro Bowler, in the one game he missed last season, they posted their best offensive performance of the season against Jacksonville. Whittington is also a real contributor, albeit in a quieter fashion. He is the team’s main kick returner, best gunner on punts, and WR3. He was on the field for 41% of the Rams’ offensive snaps last week against the 49ers and caught the only pass thrown his way. Kamren Kinchens had 52 snaps against San Francisco last week, but most of them came after Kam Curl was removed from the game. Curl is listed as a full participant on Monday and, barring a relapse of his ankle injury, should make up for most of those snaps. Kinchens was responsible for two touchdown catches last week. Tanner Ingle has been elevated to the roster to fill in for Kinchens. New York Giants injuries Heading into their game against the Cowboys last week, the Giants had three corners listed on IR: Korie Black, Jarrick Bernard-Converse, and Rico Payton. Early in that Cowboys game, Paulson Adebo suffered an injury and has also been added to the IR. Now, to make matters worse, Deonte Banks has been added to this week’s injury report and is questionable for Monday. He was limited in practice Thursday and did not practice Friday or Saturday, and he is trending toward being scratched from Monday’s game. The Giants added two cornerbacks this week for depth. Nikko Reed was signed off the Los Angeles Chargers’ practice squad to New York’s 53-man roster. Jaden Robinson, formerly with the Denver Broncos, was added to the practice squad. Robinson could be a game day elevation for the Giants on Monday night. The Giants’ starting cornerbacks are likely to be Greg Newsome and rookie second-round pick Colton Hood.

title: The 13 personnel trend isn’t going anywhere for the Rams
summary: The Los Angeles Rams were at the forefront of the NFL’s 13 personnel movement last season. Expect more of the same from L.A. in 2026. There is a “no duh” element to this, which was discussed all offseason: The Rams have and had so many tight ends on the roster. L.A. rostered eight tight ends […]
full_text: Los Angeles Rams' tight end #84 Colby Parkinson (R) stands for the national anthem during the NFL match between Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) in Melbourne on September 11, 2026. (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) / --IMAGE RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE - STRICTLY NO COMMERCIAL USE-- | AFP via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams were at the forefront of the NFL’s 13 personnel movement last season. Expect more of the same from L.A. in 2026. There is a “no duh” element to this, which was discussed all offseason: The Rams have and had so many tight ends on the roster . L.A. rostered eight tight ends during training camp, kept five on the season-opening 53-man roster, they have another one stashed on the practice squad and had even done so well scouting the position that they traded a likely cut candidate for a Day 3 pick. “Follow the money” is generally a smart way to look at the world in many contexts. For football, when factoring cash value, draft capital and roster spots into the general idea of “money,” it’s almost always instructive. The Rams told us what they wanted to do and they’re doing it, that’s hardly a surprise. But it’s one thing to want to do something, it’s another thing to commit to it, it’s something else entirely to be good at it. Sean McVay says of Rams' pick of Max Klare that Rams want to "build on" what they did last year getting their tight ends involved in the offense — Adam Grosbard (@adamgrosbard.bsky.social) 2026-04-25T03:07:37.128Z An example of a team not hitting all three points, at least not yet, is the Cincinnati Bengals. They talked all offseason about deviating from the “Joe Burrow offense” and playing more from under center, using more play action, etc. They did a ton of work with it during the preseason. In Week 1 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, though? They ran just five snaps of under-center play action, with Burrow going 3-of-5 for 29 yards. Every other dropback came from the shotgun. There were also 11 run plays from under center, not including sneaks and kneel downs, but that makes for a siloed and more predictable offense if under center almost always equals run, shotgun almost always equals pass. What does that have to do with the Rams? They did hit all three points in the first game of the season. They have made it clear they want to continue using sets with extra tight ends, they ran those at a high rate in Week 1 and they did it to extreme success. According to Next Gen Stats, Los Angeles ran 13 personnel on 36.8% of snaps against the San Francisco 49ers last week, 6.3 percentage points higher than their league-leading rate in 2025. And on a day when Matthew Stafford struggled mightily, he was at his best by far with 13 personnel on the field. Rams tight ends routes run against the 49ers (with Stafford on the field):Colby Parkinson: 16Terrance Ferguson: 12Tyler Higbee: 4Davis Allen: 2 — JJ Zachariason (@lateroundqb.bsky.social) 2026-09-14T13:16:12.525Z Again, per Next Gen Stats, Stafford went 5-of-5 passing for 96 yards with 13 personnel on the field; in all other personnel groupings, he was 10-of-20 for 59 yards. As a team, the Rams averaged 7.5 yards per play out of 13 personnel in Week 1, 1.3 yards more per play than they gained in those groupings last season. The Rams talked the talk about 13 during the offseason, then walked the walk in the opener. After an unpleasant offensive showing in the opener, Sean McVay has to feel like those 13 personnel stats are his personal Green Goblin mask, just calling out to him, tempting him. If that’s the so-called “easy button” for this offense, at least for now, that seems like a great way to buoy this team and find a way to get back in a rhythm. Don’t be shocked if the Rams another outrageous percentage of their plays out of those formations against the Giants on Monday night.

title: Matthew Stafford can silence plenty of doubt with a big Week 2
summary: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford needs a bounce back performance from Week 1 as much as anyone on the roster. Sure, there were plenty of expected contributors who struggled mightily in the opener, from Myles Garrett’s quiet game to nearly zero production from Davante Adams and plenty of others in between. But nothing may […]
full_text: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford needs a bounce back performance from Week 1 as much as anyone on the roster. Sure, there were plenty of expected contributors who struggled mightily in the opener, from Myles Garrett’s quiet game to nearly zero production from Davante Adams and plenty of others in between. But nothing may be as concerning as the shaky-at-best start for the reigning NFL MVP. There’s no getting around how poorly Stafford performed last week. He went 15-of-25 passing for merely 155 yards and no touchdowns with an interception. Throw on a generic jersey and change the nameplate, and anyone who follows the league will tell you that’s not the type of quarterback performance you can live with. He didn’t move fluidly, his decision making was iffy, it felt like a shocking departure from who we saw dice up defenses last year. Obviously, a lot of factors are at play here. He’s another year older, sometimes it takes a while to get your legs back when you don’t play at all in the preseason, then there’s the fact Week 1 is often just a mess. Plus, did you hear about the Rams’ travel plans for the Australia trip ? Certainly that hasn’t been beaten to death over the last week. Whatever the reasoning is, Stafford didn’t cover himself in glory in Week 1, and it’s led to plenty of consternation around the NFL ecosystem, including worries about whether or not we’ve witnessed the beginning of the end for the Super Bowl LVI champion. waited this whole summer for the Rams to use no huddle and they finally do in the 2nd quarter (right on schedule). *sad trombone* pic.twitter.com/bvSMN1bnyQ — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 11, 2026 You know what would assuage a lot of those concerns? Shredding the New York Giants’ defense on Monday night. And it’s more than fair to think that’s on the table in the Week 2 finale. The Giants were one of the big winners beyond the basic record ledger in Week 1, thoroughly controlling their game against the Dallas Cowboys and earning some early praise for the start of John Harbaugh’s second act. But look under the hood and you’ll find reasons to believe that the opportunity is there for big quarterbacks performances. New York has one of the more fearsome groups of young pass rushers in the NFL, headlined by Brian Burns, 2025 third-overall pick Abdul Carter and this year’s fifth-overall pick, Arvell Reese. Despite all that raw talent, the Giants generated just a 33.3% pressure rate in Week 1 according to Next Gen Stats/NFL Pro, which was good for 18th in the NFL last week. Not terrible but not good, either, just fully mediocre. It’s understandable if you’re skeptical still of the Rams’ offensive line, which ranked 22 nd in the NFL in Pass Rush Win Rate last week per ESPN, but the early returns don’t indicate anything especially sinister from the New York pass rush.\ What’s more, the Giants’ defense was 28 th in EPA/dropback last week and 22 nd in dropback success rate. The Cowboys were still able to move the ball in chunks and with consistency against that defense. If the Rams are fundamentally broken, those numbers don’t mean as much. But it’s far too early for that to be proven true, even if the vibes are low, so to see a team on the schedule that gave up plenty of ground to Dak Prescott a week ago hopefully bodes well for the Rams and Stafford this week. If Monday night goes poorly for the passing game and the MVP looks progressively more pedestrian, concern levels will predictably and fairly rise. But this is simultaneously a great opportunity for Stafford to quiet the outside noise and the concerns about what his 18 th season will look like.

title: What’s your favorite Rams season when they didn’t win the Super Bowl?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are trying to win their third Super Bowl in franchise history, but the road to the first win of the season won’t come on Sunday. The Rams are off today and will not come back until Monday night against the New York Giants. Super Bowl expectations were as high as ever […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams are trying to win their third Super Bowl in franchise history, but the road to the first win of the season won’t come on Sunday. The Rams are off today and will not come back until Monday night against the New York Giants. Super Bowl expectations were as high as ever coming into the 2026, and they can still get back there with a couple of wins in a row to wash the bitter taste of a 49ers loss out of their mouths. In the meantime, what do you think is the most satisfying or best season in Rams franchise history that didn’t end in a Super Bowl win? It can be your personal experience, like maybe it was the year you became a Rams fan or at a time something great happened in your own life. Or it can be based simply on the football. A time when you think the Rams were making football fun for you, it just didn’t end in a Super Bowl. A few seasons that come to mind: 2023 Coming off of a 5-12 season, Sean McVay was questioning his commitment to the NFL. The Rams didn’t have a first-round pick to try and rebuild with and Aaron Donald’s salary accounted for more than 50% of all the money invested into the defense that year. To make matters worse, Cooper Kupp missed the first month of the season and the Rams started 3-6. But in the meantime, the rookie class looked amazing without a first-round pick: Puka Nacua was making history Kobie Turner and Byron Young were bargains on defense Steve Avila and Davis Allen were also rookie contributors 2023 is one of the best draft classes in team history, and since then has gotten even better with improvements by Warren McClendon, Desjuan Johnson, and the continued presence of Stetson Bennett and Davis Allen a few years later. Then the Rams rebounded, winning seven of their last eight games and making the playoffs out of nowhere. Just a one-point loss to the Lions separated L.A. from the second round of the postseason. 2017 Sean McVay took over a 4-12 team and immediately flipped the 32nd-ranked scoring offense to the top-ranked scoring offense. As usual, he did it without a first-round pick. The emergence of Todd Gurley as an MVP runner-up and Jared Goff as a decent starting quarterback really saved the franchise’s potential plunging into the ocean if those picks had been busts, as they were starting to become under Jeff Fisher. Cooper Kupp was one of the great picks of all-time for the Rams and Andrew Whitworth, Robert Woods were two of the best free agent signings. Aaron Donald won his first career Defensive Player of the Year award. The Rams did lose to the Falcons in the wild card round, but had set themselves up for a deep Super Bowl run in 2018. 1979 One of the all-time underdog stories, the Rams held a fourth quarter lead in the Super Bowl against the mighty Pittsburgh Steelers. L.A. had finished 9-7. Pittsburgh went 12-4 and had already won three Super Bowls in the 70s. A 24-yard touchdown pass from Lawrence McCutcheon to Ron Smith gave the Rams a 19-17 lead in the third quarter, but they just couldn’t hang on. A Cinderella team that had been 5-6 midseason, the Rams won four in a row, then made the playoffs at 9-7. Jack Youngblood has since been credited with 18 sacks that year. Wendell Tyler led the league with 5.1 yards per carry. Larry Brooks was an All-Pro defensive tackle. The Rams upended the Cowboys and Bucs in the playoffs to reach the Super Bowl, a win that would have been historic. I’m sure for many fans reading this, 1979 still was historic anyway. What is your favorite non-Super Bowl winning Rams season?
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Las Vegas Raiders overreaction to Week 2 26-14 victory
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are on pace to be a top-5 defense in the league, if not the best defense in the league. So dominant against the Los Angeles Chargers on the road that it begs the question: just how good are they? Especially when even the oddsmakers placed the spread at -6.5 for the […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are on pace to be a top-5 defense in the league, if not the best defense in the league. So dominant against the Los Angeles Chargers on the road that it begs the question: just how good are they? Especially when even the oddsmakers placed the spread at -6.5 for the Chargers. It was supposed to be a get-right game for Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel’s offense. Rob Leonard and the Raiders defense didn’t subscribe to that rhetoric; they came in and took the Chargers to the woodshed. Defensively, the Raiders continued their unexpected second week of dominance, forcing turnovers and pushing the Chargers into mistake after mistake. Herbert finished with 192 passing yards, two interceptions, one touchdown, and a 59.5 Rating. They kept running back Omarion Hampton under 100 yards rushing and limited him to one rushing touchdown. Maxx Crosby made Joe Alt submit to his greatness. Crosby beat him like a drum time and time again, causing Alt to stop relying on his technique and get discombobulated. Alt had an uncharacteristic three false-start penalties; two in a row, and ultimately finished off the game for the offense by being flagged for holding Crosby in the end zone. By rule, it was a safety, awarding the Raiders two points and a kick return opportunity. When the dust had cleared and the clock showed :00, the defense had produced three sacks, six total fumbles (four forced), two interceptions and a safety. Coaching matters Beating a division foe on the road without your best player on offense isn’t a small feat. When the defense loaded up the box intending to smother the short-yardage plays, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak got into his bag of tricks. Calling toss sweep flea flickers, the wildcat, set up deep shots and maintaining aggressiveness in his play calls. Bailing out his players in the most beautiful ways possible, there appears to be nothing that Kubiak can’t overcome thus far. When his quarterback displayed a lack of ability to push the ball downfield last week he called him out. This week, his quarterback unleashed a 40-yard touchdown pass to Tre Tucker, the smallest guy on the field and another 42-yard pass to Tucker, on a yolo ball. Activating practice squad receiver Cody White and feeding him multiple red zone opportunities, which he converted into touchdown passes, was next level. Whether defensive coordinators watch film and study past games, Kubiak always manages to have something new to throw at them. Over reactions The Raiders are getting better on a week-to-week basis and doing it without Brock Bowers. Does that mean they are compiling massive stats? No, not quite, but Bowers nearly played Sunday against the Chargers. When he takes the field and becomes a chess piece at Kubiak’s disposal, the Raiders will become an even more difficult opponent to contend with. At this point, the Raiders are tied with the Kansas City Chiefs for the division lead, with a head-to-head matchup in two weeks. The remaining schedule is a virtual murderer’s row of last year’s playoff teams, but at this point there isn’t a team they can’t beat. If they keep pace with what is being done and how it is being done, it’s very possible the Raiders could start getting flexed into primetime down the road.
author: Philip Robinson

title: Raiders Week 3: Meet the Saints
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are preparing to play their third regular-season game of the year and second on the road, at the New Orleans Saints on Sunday at the Caesars Superdome. Kickoff is set for 1:25 p.m. PT. Let’s take a quick look at the Saints: Record: The Saints are1-1 after a road 24-17 upset […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - AUGUST 15: Kellen Moore of the New Orleans Saints looks on against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Caesars Superdome on August 15, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are preparing to play their third regular-season game of the year and second on the road, at the New Orleans Saints on Sunday at the Caesars Superdome. title: Raiders News: Week 2 AFC West roundup, Kansas City Chiefs’ overtime win keeps pace with Las Vegas
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have plenty of momentum in the AFC West after a big Week 2 win over a division rival, the Los Angeles Chargers, which keeps the Raiders in first place and pushes the Chargers to the bottom of the standings at 0-2. On that note, let’s check in on how the Denver […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have plenty of momentum in the AFC West after a big Week 2 win over a division rival, the Los Angeles Chargers, which keeps the Raiders in first place and pushes the Chargers to the bottom of the standings at 0-2. On that note, let’s check in on how the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs fared on Sunday. Broncos vs. Jaguars Score: 20-13 Broncos win Key Stats: QB Bo Nix: 22/31 (71.0%), 288 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT RB Jonah Coleman: 10 carries, 39 yards, 1 TD WR Jaylen Waddle: 8 catches, 138 yards DT Malcolm Roach: 4 tackles, 1 sack, 2 QB hits, 2 TFLs CB Riley Moss: 2 tackles, 3 PDs Unlike the Chargers, the Denver Broncos managed to escape and avoid digging themselves into a 0-2 hole during their home opener on Sunday. But “escape” is the keyword there, as Denver trailed by two possessions early in the second half and didn’t take the lead until about halfway through the fourth quarter. The Broncos haven’t looked very impressive during the first two weeks, getting blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1. Then again, they have played a pair of good opponents, and this is a team that one-possession won its way to a 14-3 record and the AFC Championship last year. The scary part about Denver’s victory over Jacksonville is that Waddle, the club’s big offseason addition, announced his presence on Sunday. Next Week: vs. Los Angeles Rams (SNF) Chiefs vs. Colts Score: 33-30 Chiefs win in OT Key Stats: QB Patrick Mahomes: 32/47 (68.1%), 382 yards, 3 TDs, 0 INTs RB Kenneth Walker: 24 carries, 117 yards, 6 catches, 61 receiving yards TE Travis Kelce: 9 catches, 101 yards, 1 TD LB Nick Bolton: 13 tackles, 1 TFL LB Drue Tranquill: 8 tackles, 2 TFLs, 1 PD After Week 1, this game looked like it would be a cakewalk for the Chiefs. However, it was anything but, with an overtime victory that required two scoring drives from Mahomes and Co. Kansas City’s defense showed some cracks, giving up 119 rushing yards (92 to Jonathan Taylor) and 30 points while failing to sack Indianapolis Colts’ quarterback Daniel Jones. However, the Chiefs’ offense appears to be back after a couple of down years, especially with Walker accounting for nearly 180 yards from scrimmage after 191 last week. That could set up for an interesting battle at Allegiant Stadium in a couple of weeks… Next Week: @ Miami Dolphins Standings Las Vegas 2-0 (+26 point differential) Kansas City 2-0 (+24) Denver 1-1 (-14) Los Angeles (-24) In Other Raiders’ Links: Pressure is up: “The Las Vegas Raiders defense generated a 45.2% pressure rate (81st percentile) against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2,” per Sumer Sports’ Shawn Syed . “The Raiders defense currently ranks 2nd in the league with a 51.5% pressure rate (98th percentile over two games since 2022).” Brock Bowers close to returning: The tight end was spotted running routes (without pads) during pre-game warm-ups, and Klint Kubiak told reporters Bowers was “very close” to playing in LA, via ESPN’s Ryan McFadden . Raiders look well-coached: “But, they were, by far, the better, more efficient team Sunday as they beat the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 to improve to 2-0 under new head coach Klint Kubiak,” S&BP’s Bill Williamson wrote. “…Yes, it’s early, but the Raiders appear to be a much improved team and, just as importantly, a well-coached team by Kubiak and his staff.” Raiders still underdogs: Despite being 2-0, the opening odds have Las Vegas as 3.5-point underdogs against the New Orleans Saints next week.

title: Captain Kirk Cousins leads Las Vegas Raiders to first 2-0 start in 5 years with win over Los Angeles Chargers
summary: Despite winning the season opener, Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins faced some criticism heading into the Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. However, he silenced a lot of doubters (including myself) by completing 19 of 29 passes (65.5%) for 253 yards and three touchdowns (one interception), leading the Raiders to a 26-14 […]
full_text: (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite winning the season opener, Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins faced some criticism heading into the Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. However, he silenced a lot of doubters (including myself) by completing 19 of 29 passes (65.5%) for 253 yards and three touchdowns (one interception), leading the Raiders to a 26-14 victory and their first 2-0 start since 2021. One of the criticisms of Cousins in Week 1 was his inability to push the ball down the field. This time around, he connected on a handful of intermediate to deep passes, including a 40-yard score to wide receiver Tre Tucker for Las Vegas’ first touchdown of the afternoon. Tucker also had a strong performance, recording the second 100-yard game of his career with a team-leading five catches for 119 yards and the touchdown. Additionally, Captain Kirk did an excellent job of handling pressure. Vegas’ offensive line had a rough showing, giving up a pair of sacks and 10 quarterback hits. But Cousins kept getting up to lead the team to back-to-back double-digit victories, drawing plenty of praise on the internet. title: Raiders show signs of being  a well-coached team under Klint Kubiak
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders look different. They weren’t perfect Sunday. They had some trouble on the offensive line and the running game on both sides of the ball. But, they were. by far, the better, more efficient team Sunday as they beat the Los Angles Chargers 26-14 to improve to 2-0 under new head coach […]
full_text: (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders look different. They weren’t perfect Sunday. They had some trouble on the offensive line and the running game on both sides of the ball. But, they were. by far, the better, more efficient team Sunday as they beat the Los Angles Chargers 26-14 to improve to 2-0 under new head coach Klint Kubiak. It is the first team the Raiders have started 2-0 since 2021 when they last made the payoffs. Yes, it’s early, but the Raiders appear to be a much improved team and, just as importantly, a well-coached team by Kubiak and his staff. They made the plays when they needed and navigated through challenges. These are great signs of a team that continue to win. Let’s look at some key aspects of the win: Cousins pushes the ball down the field and delivers: Last week, in his first game as a Raider, quarterback Kirk Cousins struggled throwing the ball downfield. That wasn’t a problem this week and it appeared to be an emphasis of the Raiders’ offense. Cousins was 8 of 13 on passes of 10-plus yards for 181 yards and all three of his touchdowns came on those throws. He has the co-share of the NFL touchdown passing lead with six touchdowns after two games Receivers pitch in: Last week, the Raiders’ wide receivers had nine catches for 83 yards. This week, they had 11 catches for 205 yards and three scores. Tre Tucker led the way with five catches for 119 yards and a score. He had two catches of 40-plus yards. Tucker had 49 receiving yards or less in his last 12 games prior to Sunday. So this production was needed. Jeanty struggles: After a game in which he had a 147 combined scrimmage yards last week, Raiders’ running back Ashton Jeanty didn’t do much Sunday. He had just 48 yards on 21 carries and had four catches for 15 yards. He had three drops. Also, after blocking well last week, the Raiders’ offensive line struggled some in run protection. Rookie Mike Washington had just three carries for seven yards. Free-agent linebackers deliver: On the first day of free agency in March, the Raiders signed linebackers Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker in a span of about five minutes. The college teammates from Georgia were signed to finally give the Raiders difference makers in the middle of the defense. Sunday that was the case. They shared for the team high with 10 tackles each and Dean forced a game-sealing fumble. They’re balling. SoFi drought over: The Raiders won at SoFi Stadium since 2020, it’s opening year. This was the Raiders first win there with fans in attendance and the Raiders fans were loud. Need Bowers back: Raiders’ star tight end Brock Bowers missed his second game with a knee injury . Kubiak said after the game that Bowers was “very close’ to playing Sunday, so he will likely have a good chance to play next week at the New Orleans Saints. The Raiders are 2-0 without their best offensive player, but they could use him. His starting replacement, Michael Mayer, had a quiet day with three catches for 23 yards. Mayer had nine catches for 55 yards after signing a big contract extension. Run defense struggles some: The Chargers had 127 rushing yards and had 49 on one scoring drive. The right side of the Raiders’ defensive line was picked one. After a nice game last week, free-agent signing Kwity Paye had issues in the run game and had just two tackles. Power of being 2-0: The Raiders are 2-0 and that’s a big deal. The Raiders have made the playoffs 14 of the previous 19 times they started 2-0. In recent NFL history, teams that started 2-0 make the playoffs 66 percent of the time. The Chargers are two games back at 0-2. The Raiders are 2-0 for the first time since 2021 when they last made the playoffs. Klint Kubiak first Raiders coach to start his career there 2-0 since Bill Callahan in 2002. The Raiders went to the Super Bowl that year. Chargers are a mess: They fumbled four times. They threw two interceptions. They bobbled passes. They look like they very much deserve to be 0-2. Mack again: Former Raider and current Raider killer Khalil Mack registered his 14th sack against the team that drafted him in 2014 and traded him in 2018. He is tied with the fourth most sacks against the Raiders ever. Trouble at safety: The Raiders had safeties Tristian McCollum and Dalton Johnson were inactive so only Jermey Chinn, Treydan Stukes and Isaiah Pola-Mao were active. Stukes was out in the second half as he was being evaulated for a concussion. Pola-Mao took over. Cody White, grab a roster spot: Wide receiver Cody White put the Raiders in the lead with a great touchdown grab in the third quarter and then he put the game away with another score in the fourth quarter. He was elevated from the practice squad for the first two games. A player can be elevated three times. It wouldn’t be a surprise if White, who played f0r Kubiak in Seattle, is promoted to the 53-man roster. Nice response: After taking the lead at the end of the second quarter, the Raiders had a big opportunity as they got the ball to start the third quarter. But they went three-and-out. Kubiak responded well after the Chargers took the lead on their first second-half possession. He went for it on fourth down from their own 35 and converted. He had a trick play to get get into the red zone then White scored his go-ahead touchdown. It was an impressive answer. False start frenzy: Early in the second quarter, Chargers’ tackle Joe Alt was called for back-to-back false stats inside their own 5-yard line. He had another one in the fourth quarter. The Maxx Crosby affect. Crosby only had one tackle, but he was a force by his presence and he caused a late safety as well. Blown opportunity: After getting the ball deep in Chargers’ territory on an interception in the first quarter, The Raiders couldn’t score after getting first and goal. The Raiders ran Jeanty four straight times. On fourth and goal, Jeanty was stopped when he bobbled a direct snap at the 1. What a blown opportunity late in the quarter. Fourth-round pick. Big Chargers’ injuries: Chargers’ star safety Derwin James left the game in the first quarter with a hand injury. But he did return in the second quarter. Early in the second quarter, standout tight end David Njoku had to be cart off. Nice streak: The Raiders haven’t allowed an opening drive score in five straight games dating back to last season. Also, the Raiders held their opponents scoreless in the first quarter of the frist two games for the first time since 2019. Hezekiah Masses in his first two NFL games: 3 catches on 7 targets for 23 yards, 20 yards after the catch, 0TD, 2INT, 1PBU, and an opponent passer rating of… 11.9. https://t.co/WDv3W1iwue — Doug Farrar ✍ (@NFL_DougFarrar) September 20, 2026 Masses starts and makes big impact: Fifth-round pick Zeke Masses started at cornerback for the injured Darien Porter. Masses played the final 10 plays of Week 1 when Porter went out with a foot injury. Masses had a big run stuff and then got a bobbled pass for an interception in the first quarter and added one i the fourth quarter. Jermod McCoy, took over for Masses n the second quarter. It was McCoy’s first playing time of his career and his first regular-season action since hurting his knee at Tennessee in 2024. Masses replaced McCoy later in the second quarter. McCoy played some in the second half as well. It will be interesting to see fi that rotation continues if Porter is out next week at New Orleans as well. Inactive talk: Second-year linebacker Cody Lindenberg was active Sunday after being inactive last week. He was a core special teamer as a rookie.

title: Raiders are undefeated after win over Chargers
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are hosting the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. Here is everything to need to know about the contest: First quarter The Raiders won the coin toss, but deferred to the second half. The Chargers got into Raiders’ territory on the opening drive, but they missed a 58-yard field goal to start […]
full_text: (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are hosting the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. Here is everything to need to know about the contest: First quarter The Raiders won the coin toss, but deferred to the second half. The Chargers got into Raiders’ territory on the opening drive, but they missed a 58-yard field goal to start the game. The Raiders will get good field position to open the game. Kirk Cousins converted a big third and long pass to Tre Tucker. Yet, two plays later, Tucker slipped and a Cousins pass was intercepted and the Chargers took over at their own 17. It could have been a big play. It was Cousins’ third interception in less than five quarters, but it’s hard to blame him for that one. The Raiders’ defense responded though as the Chargers ended up having to punt. Malcolm Koonce and Nakobe Dean combined for a sack. The Raiders gave up their first sack of the season and Ashton Jeanyy dropped a first down, forcing the Raiders to punt with just more than four minutes to go in the quarter. A wide-open Chargers’ tight end David Njoku bobbled a pass and it went into the hands of Raiders’ rookie cornerback Zeke Masses who returned the ball deep into Chargers’ territory. Like last week, the Chargers are very sloppy. It would have been a long gain for the Raiders, instead the Raiders got the ball in the red zome. However, the Raiders went for it on fourth down and Jeanty was stopped when he bobbled a direct snap at the 1. Jeanty had four straight runs on that set of down. What a blown opportunity late in the quarter. Second quarter: . Cousins showed he can push the ball down the field as he hit Tucker for a 40-yard touchdown to give the Raiders a 7-0 lead with 11:51 remaining in the half. Justin Herbert hit Ladd McConkey for 19 yards on third and 11 and Chargers had 49 yards rushing on a long response as they tied the game at 7-7 with 5:266 to go in the half. Old friend Khalil Mack with the sack, forcing the Raiders to punt late in the quarter. Mack has been a Raider killer ince his 2018 trade. Fueled by a 42-yard pass from Cousins to Tucker (Have a half, fellas), the Raiders took a 10-7 lead into halftime on a 59-yard field goal by Matt Gay That was huge and the Raiders get the ball to start the second half. Third quarter: The Raiders couldn’t continue the momentum and went three and out to open the second half. The Raiders’ defense had a brutal first drive of the half, allowing a big 53-yard pass play on third down and some sacks on a drive the Raiders took a 14-10 lead with just less than 10 minutes to play in the quarter. The Raiders came roaring back. They converted on fourth down in their own territory. Then, they got into the red zone with a trick pass play and then Cody White made a great catch for a touchdown on third down. The Raiders lead 17-14. Raiders end quarter with a 17-14 lead and the ball. Fourth quarter: Dean made a big run stop to force a Chargers punt. But the Raiders had to punt. The Chargers were driving, helped by the Raiders having 12 men on the field on fourth down. But Dean caused a fumble and Jeremy Chinn took it 43 yards to the Chargers 16 late in the game. Another Cody White touchdown. The Raiders are up 24-14 with 2:59 to go. Final score: Raiders 26, Chargers 14. Now that the game is over, let’s take a look at the key aspects: Team records: The Las Vegas Raiders are 2-0. The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-2. What the win means for the Raiders: The Raiders are 2-0 and that’s big. The Raiders have made the playoffs 14 of the first 19 times they started 2-0. In recent NFL history, teams that started 2-0 make the playoffs 66 percent of the time. The Chargers are two games back at 0-2. The Raiders are 2-0 for the first time since 2021 when they last made the playoffs. Klint Kubiak first Raiders coach to start his career there 2-0 since Bill Callahan in 2002. The Raiders went to the Super Bowl that year. The was the Raiders’ first at SoFi Stadium with fans in attendance. Turning point of the game: The Raiders took the lead at 17-14 in the third quarter and then sealed the win after the fourth-quarter fumble recovery and touchdown. Injury report: Dean was shaken up in the first quarter, but he returned shortly later. Rookie safety left the game with a concussion. Receiver Dareke Young injured his hamstring in the second half. Ashton Jeanty seemed to be banged up late. He returned. What’s next for the Raiders: The Raiders stay on the road as they play at the New Orleans Saints. Kickoff is at 1:25 p.m. PT. The Saints won at the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday and they are 1-1. Raiders-Chargers game thread

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 2 loss to the San Francisco 49ers
summary: Fresh off of a Week One loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, the Miami Dolphins traveled to northern California to square off against the San Francisco 49ers in Week Two. Despite a competitive first half, the boys in aqua and orange imploded in the second half — ultimately losing the game by a score of […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks to pass against the San Francisco 49ers in the first quarter of a game at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off of a Week One loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, the Miami Dolphins traveled to northern California to square off against the San Francisco 49ers in Week Two. Despite a competitive first half, the boys in aqua and orange imploded in the second half — ultimately losing the game by a score of 35-13. In a year when we weren’t expecting the Dolphins to amass a lot of wins, they’re certainly meeting those expectations. However, despite the current struggles, there are glimmers of hope to be found if your sights are set on the future and not necessarily on the here and now. Taking their lumps in 2026 could allow the team to blossom in 2027 or 2028 once the organization establishes a solid foundation and clears out the massive amount of dead cap currently on the books. Still, it still hasn’t been a pleasant experience watching the Dolphins play through two games this season. Regardless, we’re going to trudge along and bring to you the good, bad and ugly from each contest. Let’s dive in. GOOD Malik Willis connects with Ryan Miller for deep touchdown late The San Francisco 49ers defense is loaded with stars. From Nick Bosa to Fred Warner, Dre Greenlaw and others, the 49ers boast a ferocious opposition for offenses to face. They took it to Miami’s offense for most of Sunday’s clash, however, late in the contest, Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis uncorked a beautiful deep ball to wide receiver Ryan Miller — finding the pass catcher streaking up the sideline. Miller brought the ball in and took it all the way to the house — good for a 77 yard score. It’s in moments like that where you see the vision new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan had when signing Willis to a three-year deal in the offseason. Of course, with little weaponry surrounding him besides running back De’Von Achane, it isn’t always going to look pretty for Willis this season. However, with Sunday’s bomb to Miller, Willis has now thrown his first touchdown as a member of the Miami Dolphins. Here’s hoping there are plenty more to come. BAD Dolphins defense couldn’t stop 49ers passing attack While the 49ers’ defense is loaded with talent, the Dolphins’ defense isn’t. To make matters worse, their top pass rusher, third-year EDGE defender Chop Robinson, missed Sunday’s game due to a concussion suffered in practice just a few days prior to the game. On Sunday, 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy had his way with Miami’s defense to the tune of 20 completions on 22 attempts for 287 passing yards and and two passing scores. Tight end George Kittle reeled in 4 balls for 80 yards and a touchdown. Wide receiver Mike Evans tallied 3 receptions for 54 yards, while running back Christian McCaffrey added 4 catches for 43 yards. Whenever the 49ers needed a play to be made, they let Purdy go to work — and he rewarded that faith by finishing with a 149.1 passer rating against Miami. UGLY Dolphins offensive line dominated by 49ers defense While Miami’s defense faltered, San Francisco’s didn’t. All day long, 49ers defenders had their way with the Dolphins’ offensive line. Kadyn Proctor struggled. Jonah Savaiinaea struggled. Austin Jackson struggled. Patrick Paul had his share of mistakes as well. The 49ers finished with four sacks on Sunday. That’s 9 sacks through two games for this Dolphins team. If offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik wants his side of the ball to play better, he’s going to have to scheme up some help for his offensive line. Malik Willis and his mobility is propping this unit up as best as he can, but it still hasn’t been enough. ___ The Dolphins went winless on their West Coast roadtrip to open the season. The team starts off the Jeff Hafley era with an 0- 2 record with the Kansas City Chiefs coming to town next Sunday. Do you think the Dolphins can keep it close against Patrick Mahomes, Ken Walker III, Travis Kelce and company this week? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up.

title: Dolphins vs. 49ers final score: 5 immediate reactions
summary: The Miami Dolphins are who we thought they were, and they showed it on Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers. The Dolphins looked like a young team, making rookie mistakes, throughout their Week 2 contest, and the game quickly got out of hand. The Dolphins looked better in the first half this week than they […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Kyle Juszczyk #44 of the San Francisco 49ers jumps past Chris Johnson #3 of the Miami Dolphins while scoring a receiving touchdown in the third quarter of a game at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are who we thought they were, and they showed it on Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers. The Dolphins looked like a young team, making rookie mistakes, throughout their Week 2 contest, and the game quickly got out of hand. The Dolphins looked better in the first half this week than they did at any point last week against the Las Vegas Raiders. The offense focused on running back De’Von Achane, and it worked. They could not finish, however, and had to settle for two first-half field goals. The defense struggled to stop the 49ers, in large part because they are young players trying to get up to the NFL speed. The Dolphins do not have the proven talent on defense right now and the 49ers, a potential NFC representative in the Super Bowl, outclassed Miami throughout the game. The second half quickly turned ugly, with the 49ers putting up 21 points in the third quarter. Miami could not answer. The second-half highlight was a beautiful go-route from wide receiver Ryan Miller down the sideline late in the fourth quarter. Quarterback Malik Willis found him for the 77-yard touchdown. The Dolphins’ struggles are real this year. Butevery mistake is a learning opportunity, and. hopefully they are turning those opportunities into corrections and growth. Final score Dolphins 13 – 35 49ers Week 2 Immediate Winner: De’Von Achane Week 2 Immediate Loser: Special Teams Immediate reactions Focus on De’Von Achane The first half cemented a major change from last week. At the end of the team’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders, Pro Bowl running back had 15 total touches, 11 carries and four receptions. In the first half today, Achane had rushed 14 times with three receptions. Miami’s offense needs to run through Achane, and offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik seemed to make an adjustment to his play calling to make sure it did this week. Even as the game got out of hand in the second half, Miami stuck to making sure Achane got the ball. He finished with 20 carries for 74 yards and three receptions for 19 yards. He was targeted six times in the passing game. Achane gets the nod as the immediate reaction winner for this week. Special teams continue to be everything except special I do not even know how to describe the craziness that is Miami’s special teams through two games this year. Last week it was a return fest for the Raiders. This week, it is just dumb mistakes. When your punter drops the ball – not misses a kick, not has a bad snap he has to field, just drops the ball as he steps into the kick – there is a problem. Bradley Pinion worried me in the summer with his inconsistent punts, but this takes it to a different level. You cannot be dropping the ball. It is inexcusable. Add in a missed 51-yard field goal, and special teams continue to be everything except special. Miami has to do something to shore up the special teams. Growing pains on defense are expected, but special teams can’t add pressure on defense when they cannot execute something as simple as holding onto the ball before a punt. The special teams take the losers spot this week and continue to be a major concern heading into Week 3. Dolphins’ heart The Dolphins’ have heart. They are professionals and they are laying it out on the field. They do not give up. They do not quit. They do not head to the sideline and take themselves out of a game just because it is not going their way. They continue to compete, even when the game is out of hand, and that mentality is important in a year that is more about the future than it is about the now. This team’s heart is unquestionable. They are physical. They are going to hit you. They are going to get back up whenever you knock them down. And they are going to keep doing everything they can to compete. The team is not the most talented in the league. They are not going to make a surprising run into the playoffs. But they are going to make you remember you played them. Pass rush makes cameo The Dolphins’ pass rush, non-existent last week, at least made a cameo this week. They did not routinely get to 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy or create a constant sense of pressure, but they at least made a few appearances. A couple of times during the game, someone was at least near Purdy. Zero sacks is not acceptable, but, without Chop Robinson, the pass rush at least started to show up a few times. Pass coverage still a work in progress The Dolphins’ secondary has been a major point of concern throughout the summer and into the start of the season. Today’s game did nothing to alleviate those concerns. The 49ers picked apart Miami’s pass coverage seemingly at will. A major part of the issues is simply the young roster Miami is putting on the field each week. Repeatedly, multiple players would follow one receiver, leaving someone else open. That is going to be a problem when you are relying on multiple rookies and players who still need development time.

full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 29: Chop Robinson #44 of the Miami Dolphins looks on from the sidelines during an NFL football game against the New York Jets at Hard Rock Stadium on September 29, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins and San Francisco 49ers are down to the final 90 minutes before they kickoff their 2026 Week 2 game. Both teams have been hit by the injury bug already this year, with starters having to sit out today’s game. The Dolphins will be without edge rusher Chop Robinson, who sustained a concussion during practice this week and will have to sit out today’s game. Miami officially listed him as inactive, along with wide receiver Jalen Tolbert, cornerback Marcellas Dial, Jr., guard DJ Campbell, tackle Chukwuebuka Godrick, and tight end Justin Joly. Quarterback Brady Cook is inactive but listed as the team’s emergency third quarterback. The designation allows Cook to enter the game if both starting quarterback Malik Willis and backup Kyle McCord are injured. The good news for Miami is that long snapper Tucker Addington, who sustained a shoulder injury during last week’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders, is active and expected to play. Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez would likely be the backup if Addington’s injury worsens. The Dolphins signed long snapper Cal Adomitis to the practice squad during the week to provide depth if Addington was unable to play, but he will not be available for the game. With the Robinson injury, Miami elevated both Clelin Ferrell and Max Llewellyn from the practice squad. The moves give Miami added depth with two additional edge rushers joining the game-day roster. The 49ers will be without wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling who is dealing with an ankle injury. Rather than just listing him as inactive for the game, San Francisco moved him to the injured reserve list this week, sidelining him for at least four games. The team’s inactive list includes cornerback Ephesians Prysock, wide receiver Jordan Watkins, linebacker Tatum Bethune, offensive lineman Enrique Cruz, Jr., and quarterback Kurtis Rourke. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. Eastern.

full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jacob Rodriguez #10 of the Miami Dolphins tackles Ashton Jeanty #2 of the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter of their game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada.
