What do the Dolphins need to change to succeed this week? What does the team need heading into the future? Our mailbag opens this morning as a primer to get you ready for today’s game. We talk Jacob Rodriguez, Malik Willis, scouting needs, and much more in this packed mailbag edition. We also bring back Marek Brave to turn the mailbag back into a round-table discussion. Without further ado, it is time to head into the mailbag and see what was on your minds this week: MB: Absolutely! I think the sky is the limit for Rodriguez after his stellar pro debut. He is second in the entire NFL in tackles — unfortunately, Anthony Hill Jr. of the Tennessee Titans is first, and he’s also a rookie. When JRod gets some forced fumbles with his “Peanut Punch,” his counting stats will look even more impressive, which should help his case. KN: Completely agree. He has taken on the responsibility of being the play caller, getting the entire defense into position, and he is doing really well at it. He has already shown he can be a tackling machine and he is doing that while still adjusting to the speed of the game. Sacks and interceptions are the sexy stats that usually get the attention when people vote for major awards like this, but if Rodriguez can keep playing like he did against the Raiders, he can definitely be in the conversation. MB: I don’t think I was surprised, but I do expect him to use his legs more going forward. On Thursday, offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik called Malik’s mobility his “superpower,” so I would assume some conversations about him scrambling took place after Week One’s showing. Let’s just hope he avoids big hits so that he can stay on the field. KN: I feel like there is a push for Willis to prove he can be a drop-back, pocket passer. Based on Slowik’s comments, I think it is probably an internal thing for Willis, consciously or subconsciously. He wants to prove he is a starting NFL quarterback, so he wants to make all the throws like a pocket passer. I think we see that with all quarterbacks known as “dual-threat” or “mobile quarterbacks.” I think there were times when Josh Allen, Lamar Jackson, Jalen Hurts, Kyler Murray, and others were all trying to prove they could sit in the pocket and throw the ball, which led them to wait too long to decide to run. I think Willis will get back to using his legs as well as his arm as he gains comfort and trust that the coaches want him to be the starter, and with continued reminders from the coaching staff that they want him to run. MB: Bobby Slowik helped CJ Stroud win Rookie of the Year in Houston, so he does have that on his resume, but those questioning Week One’s play-calling have a legitimate gripe. I felt Slowik coached the second half like the team was down 30 points and needed to throw it downfield every play to catch up — which wasn’t the case. I’m hoping for more Achane touches this week and every week throughout the rest of the season. KN: I think that is a fair assessment – the team definitely went away from De’Von Achane and tried to throw the ball way more than needed in the second half. It did feel like a Mike McDaniel game plan, where the talk was all about the run game but the execution fell back to the passing attack. I also think that is where the criticisms and complaints come in – Slowik is a holdover from McDaniel’s staff, so seeing things that feel like the McDaniel era does not sit well with the fans right now. Slowik does come from the same tree as McDaniel, based in the Shanahan-McVay-Kubiak West Coast offensive style. That offense does work, but after the last couple of years of McDaniel’s offense sputtering, Dolphins fans are not going to be comfortable seeing the same thing happening under this new coaching staff. I think it will be fine, but that assumes Slowik realizes his mistake in going away from Achane last week and corrects it starting this week. MB: Jalen Tolbert is not a building block for the Miami Dolphins. Their rookies — Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr. — are. I think it’s as simple as that. They are focusing on the future and not necessarily on the “here and now,” and I think that’s a sound strategy. I’d rather our young guys get the reps they need now so that they can be meaningful contributors when the team is better in 2027 and 2028. KN: Exactly. I think they believe in the young players, and they want to get them on the field and gain the experience they need to overcome the NFL learning curve. I do not think there was any point during the game I thought Tolbert would have made a difference. MB: I would focus on pass rushers, cornerbacks and defensive tackles. The first two are probably obvious answers, but the last one may surprise. Unfortunately, despite the success of Zach Sieler in the past, age is catching up to him and I can’t see him being a member of the Dolphins beyond this season. Miami’s three second-year defensive tackles didn’t have a positive impact on Week One’s game (Kenneth Grant is on IR currently). KN: I think edge is going to be a huge focus for the team. Head coach Jeff Hafley’s defense is all about the edge rushers creating havoc, and I think the Dolphins will look to address the position early (and possibly often) next year. Like you said, cornerbacks are the second priority because they have to keep building the position. If Storm Duck can come back this year and prove to be a starter once again, maybe they feel a little better about the position moving forward, but even then I think they are looking to add another piece to the group. I will turn to the offense for my third spot. I think tight end becomes a need for next year. Greg Dulcich is a free agent after the season and, while he is fine for this year and can be a solid all-around tight end, they could look to add a young, dynamic pass catcher at the position. If you have an offense with Achane out of the backfield and have Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, and Kevin Coleman, Jr., reach their potential, then add an upper-level tight end, the weapons are suddenly there to attack in multiple ways. Of course, all of that assumes Malik Willis is the guy at quarterback. The scouts have to keep an eye on quarterbacks until the front office and coaches have their answer on Willis as a franchise quarterback for Miami. MB: Coaches have recently said that joint practices are more important than preseason games. I don’t know if I agree with them. There’s something about an actual game that feels more beneficial, in my opinion, and I could see coaches placing more importance on preseason game reps in the years to come. KN: I think coaches around the league are really starting to move away from the preseason games for their starters. Obviously, plenty of starters around the league got playing time this summer, but as you said, joint practices are becoming more important than preseason games. The reluctance to put things on film, injury concerns, and the desire to get extended looks at younger players lead to limited playing time for starters. Did I think the Dolphins would have used their starters more during the preseason this year? Absolutely. But I do not think it makes or breaks this season either way. MB: If you’re expecting a juggernaut on offense, then Week One should be very concerning to you. I didn’t go into that game expecting a huge offensive output, so I wasn’t as offended by what I saw. I just want to see improvement as the year goes along and I think that’s what…

title: Miami Dolphins review: 5 Things I Think I Think About Week 1
summary: Did Week 1 go as well as I had hoped? Am I optimistic about the Miami Dolphins’ chances in Week 2 against the 49ers? Are the Dolphins going to go 0-17? I say: No, no and gosh I hope not. Here are five things I think I think about the Dolphins after their disappointing Week […]
full_text: Did Week 1 go as well as I had hoped? Am I optimistic about the Miami Dolphins’ chances in Week 2 against the 49ers? Are the Dolphins going to go 0-17? I say: No, no and gosh I hope not. Here are five things I think I think about the Dolphins after their disappointing Week 1 loss to the Raiders. The future showed up early. OK, so we know this is a young team. As Marek pointed out a few weeks ago , the average age of the Dolphins 53-man roster (as of 8/31) is 25.3 years, easily the youngest in the league. You’d expect a massive learning curve with all that youth – yet, by and large, the rookies held their own. Caleb Douglas caught 5 of 7 targets for 94 yards and proved to be physical, polished and an accomplished run blocker. Jacob Rodriguez’s 14 tackles were the most from a Dolphins rookie since Zach Thomas’ 16 in 1996. (Here, go take a look .) Chris Johnson had 11 tackles and 2 passes defensed. Rookie Michael Taaffe and second-year safety Dante Trader each had picks. (Trader was PFF’s top-rated Dolphin, with a 91.8 defensive grade that was two points higher than Jordyn Brooks’.) Was it perfect? It was not. But if this is the baseline for what we can expect going forward, it’s hard not to be excited. Our trench play has to get better. Simply put, we were manhandled on both sides of the line of scrimmage. Offensively, we struggled to establish the run – Achane finished the game with only 11 carries for 36 yards – and Malik Willis was sacked 5 times. Defensively, we could not get any pressure on Raiders QB Kirk Cousins, who is 85 years old and needs a walker to cross the street. It wasn’t just the zero (!) sacks – Chop Robinson finished the game with exactly 1 tackle. By comparison, Riley Patterson had 2 tackles for the game, and he’s the kicker. The kicker! Maybe we should put him on the defensive line! To be fair, Robinson might have suffered a concussion during the game. Regardless, Jeff Hafley’s defenses have historically been good at stopping the run and forcing opponents into uncomfortable down-and-distance situations. Against the Raiders, Cousins and company had little trouble moving the ball. Malik Willis was better than the box score. With all the money Willis received in the offseason to be our starting quarterback, it’s easy to forget that he entered the season with only 155 career passes under his belt. While he had some impressive game tape from his time in Green Bay, much of that was against defenses that had prepared all week for Jordan Love. The big question entering Week 1 was what Willis would look like with an offense built around him. All in all, I think he acquitted himself reasonably well. He made some strong, NFL-caliber throws, especially downfield near the sidelines. He also showed good processing and was able to make things happen with his legs (including a TD run). There were problem too: He held the ball for longer than 3 seconds on average, which was a major reason behind his five sacks. He also missed some easy throws and seemed to press on the interception. Still, there’s a lot to build on. The coaches need to prove themselves as much as the players. I have a lot of faith in Coach Hafley – already I think we’ve shown more heart and discipline than the team did at any point with Mike McDaniel, and the fact that we actually won a challenge makes me feel we’re playing with house money. Offensively, I’m not sure we were prepared with the right game plan for the Raiders, one of the easiest teams we’ll face this year. We had runs and deep balls, but not much in between to keep the pass rush at bay. And our special teams were anything but special – it felt like the Raiders were starting each drive at midfield throughout the game. To be sure, it was only one game, and when you’re starting so many first- and second-year players, it’s not always going to look pretty. Still, it’s something to keep an eye on. This team is better than the score might suggest. Although any loss is disappointing – and especially to a team that is decidedly beatable – we weren’t outclassed despite our youth. Look at how many plays the team left on the field: For as impressive a debut as he had, Caleb Douglas had opportunities for an even bigger afternoon. Malik Willis narrowly missed several explosive plays. There were scramble-drill opportunities that never connected because Willis and his receivers weren’t on the same page. A tipped pass late could have been a touchdown. Several defensive busts were one assignment away from becoming stops. The Dolphins were often a step late, a yard short or a read away from turning negative plays into game-changing ones. You don’t get consolation prizes for losing, but on a rebuilding team, there’s a lot to work with here. The good news? Many of the Dolphins’ mistakes looked like inexperience rather than a lack of talent, which means they should be correctable in time. The bad news? The 49ers won’t be nearly as forgiving as the Raiders. Let’s see how much this young team learned from Week 1.

title: Vikings Week Two Stock Market Report
summary: The Minnesota Vikings won an ugly game at a rainy and sloppy Soldier Field on Sunday 9-3, making it a 2-0 start to the season- both against division opponents. Stock Up Brian Flores. His out-generaling Ben Johnson and holding the Bears to 3 points, after crushing the Packers last week with his unique blitzing scheme, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Dallas Turner #15 of the Minnesota Vikings sacks Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears during the fourth quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings won an ugly game at a rainy and sloppy Soldier Field on Sunday 9-3, making it a 2-0 start to the season- both against division opponents. Stock Up Brian Flores . His out-generaling Ben Johnson and holding the Bears to 3 points, after crushing the Packers last week with his unique blitzing scheme, is raising eyebrows around the league. Dallas Turner. He continues to show he has made the leap into the top tier of edge rushers in the league. He was credited with ten quarterback pressures against the Bears, according to preliminary PFF charting, including a sack to seal the victory. Jalen Redmond. He stepped up his disruptive play against the Bears. He was credited with 2 quarterback pressures, a batted pass, a key forced fumble on the one yard line, and four tackles- all of them stops. Those plays made a difference in the game. Will Reichard . He’s been automatic for a while now, and once again made all three field goal attempts. But he also did so in poor conditions for a kicker which added a degree of difficulty. Isaiah Rodgers . He allowed just one reception on two targets for seven yards in his coverage, with a PBU that was nearly an interception to ice the game and a blocked field goal to prevent the Bears from tying the game late. Caleb Banks. It was still a rough game for Banks overall, but he did make a few plays and showed some progress. He had four tackles- three of them defensive stops- and one quarterback pressure. Still a long way to go in terms of consistency among other things, but he did show progress in his second game. Aaron Jones. Jones ground out over 100 yards rushing (23/105, 4.6 ypa) when the Vikings needed him to be a bell cow, absorbing some big hits including a big helmet-to-helmet shot, while also holding on to the ball in adverse conditions. Defensive Secondary. On a day when one slip on a sloppy field could have cost the game, the Vikings defensive secondary provided next to nothing for Caleb Williams to capitalize on down the field. Tyson Bagent was able to take advantage of a prevent defense on the last drive to hit some shots down the field, but other than that the Bears didn’t have much success in their downfield passing game. Kevin O’Connell . While the execution was limited by Carson Wentz and the weather- in that order- KOC had the team well-prepared to win a tough road game in sloppy conditions. No turnovers, few penalties, and just enough playmaking on both sides of the ball to prevail. It wasn’t pretty, but 2-0 with both wins over division opponents starting a backup quarterback is impressive. Stock Down Demond Claiborne . Claiborne was active for the Bears game but seems to have been eclipsed by DeeJay Dallas on the depth chart. He only played two snaps on offense. Buy The Vikings ability to leverage situational football, special teams, and turnovers to make up for otherwise poor offensive production. The Vikings are 2-0 despite an offense that ranks last in total yards and most yards-based metrics. Sell The Vikings offensive production. Granted it was poor conditions in Chicago on Sunday, but for the second straight week the Vikings offense has been fairly anaemic in its ability to drive the field and score touchdowns. The Vikings rank last in total yards after two weeks. That’s not a recipe for success the rest of the season. Buy Carson Wentz as a capable backup quarterback. Sell Carson Wentz as a starting quarterback. Buy Playing on grass. I’m not a zealot when it comes to grass or turf, but most players prefer a well-prepared grass surface and I get that. Slide once on turf and you understand the difference. Sell Playing on a soggy, rain drenched Soldier’s Field. I’m not that nostalgic for old-school football when it comes down to it, at least the bad weather variety. It makes for a frustrating, lackluster game most of the time. And this type of field adds to injury risk. They say hamstring injuries are more likely on this type of field and guess what- there was a high profile hamstring injury. Follow me on X/Bluesky @wludford

title: Vikes Views: Sunday King – Vikings at Bears
summary: The Minnesota Vikings visited the Chicago Bears and the result was the same as it has been for quite a while now: a Vikings victory. Minnesota has now won seven consecutive games at Soldier Field, a stadium that used to be a house of horrors for Vikings fans. The offense never really found its rhythm, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - SEPTEMBER 2026: Minnesota Vikings linebacker Dallas Turner (15) chases Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) out of the pocket in the fourth quarter at Solider Field in Chicago, Illinois, on Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026. (Photo by Jerry Holt/The Minnesota Star Tribune via Getty Images) The Minnesota Vikings visited the Chicago Bears and the result was the same as it has been for quite a while now: a Vikings victory. Minnesota has now won seven consecutive games at Soldier Field, a stadium that used to be a house of horrors for Vikings fans. The offense never really found its rhythm, but the defense more than made up for it. Brian Flores’ unit was all over Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent from start to finish. The pass rush consistently disrupted the pocket, the secondary kept everything in front of them, and the Bears struggled to generate any explosive plays. It wasn’t flashy; more like an old school NFC Central matchup. The Vikings played great defense, won the field position battle, controlled the line of scrimmage, and found a way to leave Chicago with another win and that’s all that matters. Dallas Turner Turner finished with four quarterback hits and two sacks, and those numbers hardly tell the whole story. He lived in the Bears’ backfield all afternoon, and if not for Caleb Williams’ ability to escape pressure, Turner might have added two or three more sacks to his total. This is exactly what the Vikings envisioned when they selected him in the first round. His game-clinching sack of Tyson Bagent was the perfect ending to another dominant performance. Jalen Redmond Redmond’s third-quarter play may have been the biggest moment of the game. His forced fumble on D’Andre Swift completely changed the momentum and prevented what looked like a potential scoring drive. Redmond continues to be a disruptive force in the middle of the defense, creating opportunities for others while making plenty of plays himself. His impact doesn’t always show up on the stat sheet, but it was impossible to miss in this game. Isaiah Rodgers Rodgers delivered two of the biggest plays of the afternoon. His blocked field goal in the fourth quarter helped preserve the Vikings’ lead at a critical moment. Earlier, he recovered the fumble forced by Redmond near the goal line, preventing the Bears from capitalizing on a scoring opportunity. He also turned in another strong performance in coverage against an offense that had put up impressive numbers the previous week. Brian Flores I had high expectations for this defense entering the season. I had no idea it could be this good. Flores has built one of the most disruptive defenses in football. The pass rush comes from everywhere, the secondary is disciplined, and opposing quarterbacks rarely look comfortable. The unit has been so dominant that there are times I feel more confident when the defense takes the field than when the offense does. The Vikings’ defense has become the identity of this team, and Flores deserves enormous credit for what he has built. It’s hard to imagine anyone doing a better job than he has this season.

The Vikings are one of just four teams in the NFC who currently sit with a 2-0 record after Week 2 (though the New York Giants can join them if they win on Monday Night Football this evening). title: Vikings Set Another Unique NFL Record In Win Over Bears
summary: It wasn’t necessarily pretty, but the Minnesota Vikings did just enough to get a victory on Sunday afternoon at Soldier Field, knocking off the Chicago Bears by a final score of 9-3. It was their seventh consecutive victory in Chicago and their seventh straight victory dating back to last season, but it also allowed them […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Carson Wentz #11 of the Minnesota Vikings reacts against the Chicago Bears after the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images It wasn’t necessarily pretty, but the Minnesota Vikings did just enough to get a victory on Sunday afternoon at Soldier Field, knocking off the Chicago Bears by a final score of 9-3. It was their seventh consecutive victory in Chicago and their seventh straight victory dating back to last season, but it also allowed them to do something that no team in NFL history had ever done before. According to CBS Sports researcher Doug Clawson , the Vikings are now the first team in NFL history to win four consecutive games with four different starting quarterbacks, going back to last year. Now, it’s important to note that the rules for quarterback wins in the NFL are different from those in, say, pitchers in Major League Baseball. In baseball, whoever is on the mound whenever a team takes the lead for the last time gets credit for the win. In the NFL, whichever quarterback takes the first snap of the game gets credit for the win, regardless of how the ebb and flow of the game works out. In the case of the Vikings, here’s how that winning streak has gone: Week 17, 2025: Max Brosmer starts vs Detroit, Vikings win 23-10 Week 18, 2025: J.J. McCarthy starts vs Green Bay, Vikings win 16-3 Week 1, 2026: Kyler Murray starts vs Green Bay, Vikings win 39-22 Week 2, 2026: Carson Wentz starts at Chicago, Vikings win 9-3 (Hey, all those games were against division rivals, too. That’s neat.) So, by NFL rules, it doesn’t matter if the Vikings were trailing when Murray went out of the Week 1 game, and Wentz led the comeback for the victory. Murray still gets credit for the win. Unless the Vikings sign a street free agent and throw him out there next week, however, they won’t be extending that streak to five wins in five weeks with five different quarterbacks. But I think we can all agree that’s probably a good thing. Incidentally, the 56-point difference between the Bears’ scoring output in Week 1 and Week 2 that the Vikings’ defense was responsible for represents the second -largest drop-off in NFL history by one team from one week to the next. The largest drop-off belongs to the 1973 Atlanta Falcons. That team put up 62 points against the New Orleans Saints in Week 1 of that season. . .and proceeded to get shut out by the Los Angeles Rams the following week. But holding a team completely out of the end zone after they crossed the goal line eight times the previous week is a damn impressive feat, even if it isn’t an NFL record.
author: Christopher Gates

title: Vikings Win Battle of Field Goals, Defenses Over Bears at Soldier Field
summary: After the Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears combined for 98 points in Week 1, it was reasonable to expect more offensive fireworks when the teams got together at Soldier Field in Week 2. And what unfolded was about as far from that as you could possibly get. It was nothing but field goals on a […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Byron Murphy Jr. #7 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates after a play with Isaiah Rodgers #2 against the Chicago Bears during the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images After the Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears combined for 98 points in Week 1, it was reasonable to expect more offensive fireworks when the teams got together at Soldier Field in Week 2. And what unfolded was about as far from that as you could possibly get. It was nothing but field goals on a wet, sloppy, windy track in Chicago on Sunday afternoon, but the Vikings got more of them than the Bears did, and also got some big plays on defense and special teams to escape with a 9-3 victory over their division rivals to get their 2026 season off to a 2-0 start. The Vikings won the coin toss and elected to receive the opening kickoff rather than defer to the second half, giving Carson Wentz and the offense the first opportunity at possession. Wentz found Justin Jefferson on the second play of the drive for a 30-yard catch to put the Bears into Chicago territory, a catch that gave Jefferson possession of second place in franchise history in receptions with 588 for his career, passing Randy Moss for that mark. . @JJettas2 moves into 2nd place in #Vikings history for career receptions. 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/OCLTxvWe77 — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) September 20, 2026 After Wentz was nearly intercepted by Devin Bush, the drive stalled out, and the Vikings settled for a 35-yard field goal from Will Reichard to take an early 3-0 lead. The Bears took over and caught a break on their second play, when a fumble by Caleb Williams was recovered by the third-year quarterback and turned into a 19-yard gain. The Bears moved into Minnesota territory but saw their drive stall out after a holding penalty and a near-sack from the Minnesota defense. Cairo Santos then got the Bears even with a 50-yard field goal to tie things at 3-3 with five minutes left in the first quarter. The Vikings’ next offensive possession was a bit of a disaster, as Blake Brandel’s snap on third down went over the head of Wentz for a 22-yard loss on 3rd-and-2, resulting in a three-and-out. Brett Thorson’s punt set the Bears up at their own 42-yard line. After a couple of penalties on both teams, the Vikings’ defense generated a turnover as Williams overthrew his receiver and the ball landed in the arms of Byron Murphy Jr. for his first interception of the season. Byron Murphy Jr. INT! MINvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vfUjS4Ea1a — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Unfortunately for the Vikings, they could not take advantage of the turnover as Wentz missed an open Addison on third down for another three-and-out, and the Vikings punted it away as the first quarter came to an end. The Vikings’ defense then forced the first three-and-out from the Chicago offense all season to get the football back, and the Minnesota offense got themselves into scoring position once again. However, the drive stalled out and the purple once again had to call on the right foot of Reichard, who connected from 49 yards out to put the Vikings back on top by a score of 6-3 with just over eight minutes remaining in the first half. The Bears’ next possession pushed fairly deep into Minnesota territory, including a 4th-down conversion that stood up after a challenge by Kevin O’Connell that put the ball at the Vikings’ 30-yard line. Then a series of penalties, including an intentional grounding call on Williams, pushed the Bears to a 2nd-and-35 on their own side of midfield. Ultimately, the Bears ended up punting it away after what looked like a potential scoring opportunity. That meant the Vikings took their 6-3 lead into halftime. Chicago got the ball to start the second half and immediately went to work with their run game, with Kyle Monangai putting together a couple of long gains to help push the Bears into the Minnesota red zone. Williams then made a great third-down play on a scramble drill to find Khalif Raymond to set up a first-and-goal for the Bears at the Minnesota 1-yard line, but then the Minnesota defense came up big again. Jalen Redmond forced a D’Andre Swift fumble at the goal line, and Isaiah Rodgers recovered the loose ball to end the scoring threat and give the Vikings their second turnover of the day. Vikings force a turnover at the goal line 😳 MINvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7RgeAkxkX9 — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 The Vikings could not take advantage of the turnover and punted the ball away again, with Thorson’s punt rolling to a stop inside the Chicago 15-yard line to flip the field position. Nobody added points in the third quarter, so the Vikings stayed on top by the same 6-3 score heading into the fourth quarter of play. The Bears punted it away to start the fourth quarter, and the Vikings returned the favor with a three-and-out to give the ball back. With the Vikings unable to sustain drives, the Bears’ offense pushed the ball down the field and got into a goal-to-go situation. After Williams went down with a non-contact leg injury, the Vikings’ defense got backup Tyson Bagent to throw a couple of incompletions, and the Bears settled for a 23-yard field goal attempt. But, once again, the Vikings came up big. This time the big play came on special teams, as Isaiah Rodgers came through and blocked the kick to keep the Vikings ahead by three points with just over six minutes left in regulation. Isaiah Rodgers blocks the FG 😳 MINvsCHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/B8JL5qhKPT — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 The Vikings then put together one of their best possessions of the day, as Wentz converted a big third down to Jordan Addison to keep the drive alive, and then found T.J. Hockenson for another big play to move into Chicago territory. The Bears burned their timeouts, and the Vikings got themselves to the Chicago 21-yard line with 1:13 left on the clock. Facing a 4th-and-7, they lined things up for a 39-yard field goal attempt for Reichard, and he caromed it off the right upright and through to put the Vikings ahead 9-3 with 1:09 left on the clock. The Bears then rallied behind Bagent, who completed a pair of passes to Luther Burden to get the Bears into Vikings territory, and then found Rome Odunze to put the Bears into the red zone. It appeared that Rodgers intercepted a Bagent pass in the end zone, but the officials ruled that he was out of bounds and called it incomplete. Then, a Bagent pass intended for Colston Loveland was ruled incomplete, but the officials ruled that there was one second left on the clock after it appeared that the time had expired. On the final play of the game, Dallas Turner ended things with a sack of Bagent, and the Vikings escaped with a 9-3 victory to capture their seventh consecutive victory at Soldier Field. DALLAS TURNER WALKOFF SACK FOR THE VIKINGS pic.twitter.com/8wGRHUIMKW — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 The win gives the Vikings sole possession of first place in the NFC North at 2-0, and it’s the first time they’ve won consecutive divisional games to start a season since 2003, when they also defeated the Packers and Bears in consecutive weeks to start the season. The Vikings will hope to continue their undefeated start to the season next week, when they head to Raymond James Stadium to face off with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Minnesota Vikings hang on to defeat the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field by a final score of 9-3. Thank you to everyone who got their coverage of this week’s game right here at The Daily Norseman!

full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings warms up prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings found Justin Jefferson early in their Week 2 matchup against the Chicago Bears, and with that, Jefferson continued to climb the ladder in the team’s record books. With his 30-yard reception in the first quarter, Jefferson officially passed Randy Moss for the second-most receptions as a member of the Minnesota Vikings with 588 for his career. If you’re wondering, he has a little ways to go before he gets to #1, which is currently held by Cris Carter with 1,004 career receptions in purple. Jefferson has set his mark in significantly fewer games than Moss did. This is Jefferson’s 96th career game as a member of the Vikings, while Moss got his 587 receptions in 113 games in a Minnesota uniform. He is now 714 yards behind Moss after his 30-yard reception this afternoon. Congratulations to Justin Jefferson on now having more receptions than all but one player to ever wear a Minnesota Vikings’ uniform!

title: Fan Notes from the Patriots’ win over the Steelers
summary: And just like that, we’re back in the win column. The Patriots needed to bounce back after a rough season opener, and they were able to take care of business at home against the Steelers. It wasn’t the greatest win in team history, and losing Mike Onwenu really, really sucks. But 20-3 against a 2025 […]
full_text: And just like that, we’re back in the win column. The Patriots needed to bounce back after a rough season opener, and they were able to take care of business at home against the Steelers. It wasn’t the greatest win in team history, and losing Mike Onwenu really, really sucks . But 20-3 against a 2025 playoff team isn’t anything to laugh at. Opening the season on a Wednesday night made it feel like nine years had passed between Week 1 and Week 2 for this team. It also feels like an unfathomable amount of activity has transpired between then and now. But honestly, there really hasn’t been that much. What should be familiar, though — at least to those who have been around for a while — is the narrative surrounding a win like this one. Double digits, kept the opponent out of the end zone, plenty to be happy about, a strong bounceback, incredible defensive performance… and all the Boston media can talk about is what a disaster this team is. We used to get wins like this all the time during the Brady Era; the Patriots would beat the Ravens or the Bills or the Steelers by 14 or 23 points and Tom Brady would throw for 248 with a TD and a pick and all anyone could hear was how many points the team left on the field and how sluggish the offense looked. I’d be totally fine with New England racking up wins like this one for the rest of the season. That said… did Drake Maye look great out there? Not at all. That’s four interceptions in two games for him. And this New England offense hasn’t found its second gear yet. No Patriots receiver caught more than three passes all game and other than a few chunk plays, there weren’t a ton of offensive highlights. But that’s just fine with me. This was as close to a must-win game as you can get in Week 2, and the Patriots were in control from start to finish. Mostly because of the defense, which looked lights-out. If Pittsburgh had an offensive highlight, I certainly missed it. And this isn’t a terrible Steelers team. They aren’t great, but they aren’t trash either. If history is any indicator, Rhamondre Stevenson will fumble three more times over the next two weeks, and then he won’t have another one for the rest of the year. I’m trying to be as objective as possible on the heels of this win, as it’s easy to become a prisoner of the moment. It felt like New England had this one well in hand from the opening kickoff, and game-planned accordingly based on that confidence. I’m not overly concerned about Drake Maye, and I’m not sure whether or not I should be. I can’t figure out whether or not Romeo Doubs is any good. I don’t really know what this offense is supposed to look like sans A.J. Brown. I’m very concerned about the offensive line depth now that Onwenu is out with what seems to be a broken ankle . I’m happy with what I saw from the defense and feel like the offense doesn’t need to score 40 points a game if the D can remain consistent. But mostly, I’m just happy with the win. I apologize for the brevity of today’s Fan Notes; this was my annual game that I attended with my old man, bringing our streak up to 27 years now of going to at least one game per year. My plan was to jot some thoughts down on my phone as I was watching, but the degernates in Section 307 made that very difficult. I’m also still reeling from the price of beer at Gillette these days. Two aluminum bottles of Bud Light can run you damn near $40 if you’re not careful. If drinking alchohol didn’t have so many scientifically proven health benefits, I’d probably give it up due to lack of affordability. But I’m glad I got to see Aaron Rodgers play live at least once, even though he’s nowhere close to what he once was. I know he has said that it’s his last season a few times now, but I imagine that this really has to be it. The things I’m going to be paying attention to this week, besides how they’re going to reshuffle the offensive line: What will the backfield split look like? Henderson is clearly the big-play threat, but Stevenson is still a more consistent between-the-tackles runner when he actually hangs onto the ball. I don’t think there’s anything to be worried about in regards to the kicking game. But I also don’t trust how not worried I am about the kicking game. With two road games coming up against the Jaguars and Bills, I can’t see a duplicate of today’s performance leading to a 2-0 record over that stretch. I also think that the Patriots could very easily go 2-0 over that stretch. This might not be an overly exciting offense, but they have the pieces in place to win games. I’d love to see Drake Maye go all Chad Pennington on the NFL in 2026 and put together a series of 18-play, 48-yard drives that eat up nine minutes of play clock and end in points. That might be the formula going forward . I think we’re going to know a lot more about this team by this time next week. The Jags looked like a completely different team yesterday than they did Week 1, and the Pats have a legit chance to build some momentum. I can also 100% see a scenario where they play like complete crap and close out the first quarter of the season at 1-3. But there are a lot of positives to build on here.

title: Patriots’ young pass rushers make their mark in win over Steelers
summary: On their way to a Week 2 victory, the New England Patriots held the Pittsburgh Steelers to just three points in their Sunday home opener at Gillette Stadium, claiming the matchup 20-3. The defense generated quick and consistent pressure on opposing quarterback Aaron Rodgers, with emerging outside linebackers Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas helping lead […]
full_text: On their way to a Week 2 victory, the New England Patriots held the Pittsburgh Steelers to just three points in their Sunday home opener at Gillette Stadium, claiming the matchup 20-3 . The defense generated quick and consistent pressure on opposing quarterback Aaron Rodgers, with emerging outside linebackers Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas helping lead the way and each forcing a turnover. Amidst a multitude of injuries across the roster on Sunday, including outside linebacker Dre’Mont Jones , head coach Mike Vrabel credited some unheralded players for rising to the occasion and making an impact. “These guys have all been practicing and working really hard, and I’m just proud of them,” Vrabel said after the game. “You look [at the Steelers], and they’ve got T.J. Watt, [Alex] Highsmith, and [Nick] Herbig; we have Ponder, Jacas, and Quintayvious Hutchins. So, I’m proud of our guys for going out there and being ready.” New England, holding a 13-3 advantage early in the fourth quarter, faced a second-and-long defensive snap with Pittsburgh at its own 30-yard line. As Rodgers dropped back to pass, defensive tackle Christian Barmore stripped the ball loose, and Ponder quickly shifted his focus, scooped the ball up and raced the opposite direction into the end zone. That touchdown was the 24-year-old’s first career score. And along with his pivotal fourth-quarter sack as the Steelers began a new set of downs at New England’s four-yard line, Ponder finished his afternoon with five additional tackles (three for a loss) and two quarterback hits. “I think all the credit goes to the players. But certainly, seeing Christian Barmore affect the quarterback with a holding penalty and a forced fumble, seeing everybody work and compete, but [also] work together, to affect the quarterback,” Vrabel said of his defense’s pressure on Rodgers. “Ponder had a couple of fumble recoveries last year and was able to score. It was fun to see him be able to get into the end zone today.“ Jacas, playing opposite Ponder, also made his presence felt, doing so in an unexpected way for a player operating along the line of scrimmage. One play after Ponder’s takedown, Rodgers’ pass popped into the air as cornerback Charles Woods made contact with the intended receiver, allowing Jacas to snatch the loose ball for an interception. “Gabe [Jacas] is going to be a great player,” Ponder said. “He’s taking the steps. You can tell he’s engaged with everything we do from 8 a.m. to whenever we leave the facility. He’s always there and looking for ways to get better. I appreciate that, and I think everybody appreciates that — to see a guy come in, focus on what he needs to do and get it done.” Effectively closing out the matchup with his forced turnover, Jacas concluded his performance with three tackles, one quarterback hit and a pass deflection. He’ll look to carry that momentum into next week against the Jacksonville Jaguars, especially with Jones’ unclear availability. “He cares extremely,” Vrabel said about Jacas. “[Jacas] comes in early, he stays late, he works with me, he works with all the coaches, he cares about his teammates … And the thing about Gabe is that he can work through mistakes, and I think that’s really critical for any young player trying to improve: you have to be willing to make new mistakes and be okay with that, be able to be coached and I think he’s been able to do that.”

title: Christian Gonzalez dominates DK Metcalf in Patriots’ win over Steelers
summary: When Christian Gonzalez first saw the Pittsburgh Steelers on the Week 2 schedule, he knew it meant one thing: D.K. Metcalf. On Sunday, that became reality. In the New England Patriots’ 20-3 win over the Steelers, Gonzalez followed Metcalf almost anywhere he went on the Gillette Stadium field. The two were matched up for 34 […]
full_text: When Christian Gonzalez first saw the Pittsburgh Steelers on the Week 2 schedule, he knew it meant one thing: D.K. Metcalf. On Sunday, that became reality. In the New England Patriots’ 20-3 win over the Steelers , Gonzalez followed Metcalf almost anywhere he went on the Gillette Stadium field. The two were matched up for 34 snaps, the most Gonzalez has had against a single receiver in a game during his career. “Gonzo wants those challenges. You can see the competitive spirit,” head coach Mike Vrabel said post game. “Had a fun match-up,” Gonzalez added. “It is always fun seeing their best guy and just going out there and competing. That’s what you love as a corner. Being a corner is just going out there, playing ball and competing against the best.” Gonzalez won the matchup decisively on Sunday. Across the 34 matchups, Gonzalez held Metcalf to just three catches for 11 yards, with two of those receptions coming behind the line of scrimmage. In total, Metcalf ended the day with four catches for 27 yards and a pair of drops. “I don’t think he had a lot of fun at all. I don’t know how many catches he had, but it wasn’t a whole lot,” safety Kevin Byard said. “I think anytime I’m lining up in the post and I see Gonzo out there at number one or on the outside, I have full confidence that I don’t really need to give him any help.” With trust in Gonzalez and New England’s secondary, the Patriots were able to heat up Aaron Rodgers throughout the afternoon. New England blitzed Rodgers 21 times (47.7%), helping produce four total sacks and an interception to steer the Patriots to their first victory of the season. “We played good team defense,” Gonzalez said. “We left some plays out there that we can obviously come back and get in the film room and fix. I am proud of this defense and proud of this team. We went out there and fought hard. That’s a physical team. The Steelers are a physical team. They came in and always want to be physical. So, our challenge was to be more physical as a defense. I think we did that, and we are going to enjoy this one.”
author: Brian Hines

title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Steelers
summary: The New England Patriots got their first win of the season in their first home game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday in Foxboro. The game itself was not the prettiest nor the most impressive display of power, but it is always good to get in the win column early. Let’s get into the lessons […]
full_text: The New England Patriots got their first win of the season in their first home game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday in Foxboro. The game itself was not the prettiest nor the most impressive display of power, but it is always good to get in the win column early. Let’s get into the lessons we learned from the Patriots’ 20-3 victory. A win is a win You’re not always going to play a perfect game. Drake Maye looked uncomfortable in the pocket for much of the day and made some bad decisions with the football, but not too many for the Patriots to lose. Ultimately, they will need more from their franchise quarterback moving forward, but he also took some sacks and made some throwaways instead of forcing low-percentage passes. Overall, Maye has struggled to start the season — that interception when he was targeting Hunter Henry off his back-foot was horrific — but he also started slowly last year too, and it worked out well for him and the team. The hope is that more experience and improved chemistry within the entire offense, plus the eventual return of A.J. Brown from his ankle injury, this season will end up playing out like the last. Getting TreVeyon Henderson back was important The Patriots were without TreVeyon Henderson in Week 1, and you could see how important it was for them to have him back this week. He is a threat to take it to the house every time he touches the ball, meaning that the defense constantly has to have their eyes on him. Having the second-year back running well is also important for the Patriots in case Rhamondre Stevenson’s ball security should become a weekly concern again. As a side note: Henderson’s touchdown run was a great play by him, but it was really Morgan Moses and DeMario Douglas who should get the most credit. A great pull by Moses into the hole, and he put Logan Wilson on roller skates, driving him 15 yards downfield. Douglas came in and absolutely trucked the safety, pancaking him and taking out another safety in the process. That left only one guy from Henderson to beat, which he did, scampering 39 yards for the touchdown. The highlight on SportsCenter, if that’s still a thing, goes to Henderson, but the highlight in the film room belongs to Moses and Douglas. Injury woes are real Arguably the biggest concern about the Patriots entering this season was their depth, and it’s being tested early on. Mike Onwenu went down with what is believed to be a broken ankle; Dre’Mont Jones and Craig Woodson both hurt their shoulders and did not come back into the game; Eli Raridon was lost with a thigh injury, and Dell Pettus also failed to finish the game with an ankle issue. On top of it, they have already lost A.J. Brown for at least four games. Their depth is going be seriously tested in the next few weeks, and it will be fascinating to find out how they respond — and who they will rely on moving forward. Young defenders step up One of the reasons the Patriots had struggled before last year was their lack of young impact players, whether from the draft or as undrafted signings. Well, that has certainly changed, and it was evident on Sunday. Former UDFA Elijah Ponder had a sack and a scoop-and-score touchdown. Rookie Gabe Jacas had a second consecutive solid game. Joshua Farmer played well in the middle and even Quintayvious Hutchins contributed some good reps. Combine that with some solid play by Jaylen Reed, who they acquired in the Kayshon Boutte trade, and you have to walk away impressed with the young talent on this defense. The Patriots have a few elite defenders in Milton Williams, Christian Barmore, and Christian Gonzalez. If the young guys can continue to contribute the way they have as well, their defense is going to be a force this season. Gabe Jacas looks like a player When the Patriots took Jacas out of Illinois in the second round of the draft, there was excitement about what he could be . A contract dispute, combined with an injury recovery, forced him to miss time at the beginning of training camp, and he was never able to get anything going in camp. As rough as he looked in camp, however, he looked significantly worse in the preseason. It was bad enough that people, including me, were concerned that this could end up being a redshirt year for Jacas. Well, we could not have been more wrong. Through two games, Jacas has made a bunch of splash plays, regularly worked his way into the backfield, and even got an interception on Sunday. If he continues this strong play, the Patriots are going to be extremely happy with their choice to select him, and so will all their fans. Christian Elliss has quite the highlight reel Christian Elliss was a relative no-name when he came to the Patriots in 2023, with his best work previously coming on special teams. However, he has started developing quite the highlight package with his hard hits. The hit on Jaxson Dart along the sideline last year against the Giants made the rounds, and is sure to be one that has staying power as well. The sack against Aaron Rodgers on Sunday that resulted in a huge loss for the Steelers will be on every Patriots highlight package the rest of the season as well. Elliss, after all, nearly sawed Rodgers in half; when he gets a clean shot, it’s a bad thing for whatever opponent has the ball. Forget the fact that the fumble resulted in a Benny Hill-like scramble for the football, the hit is sure to live on the rest of the year, and maybe longer. Christian Gonzalez puts the clamps on DK Metcalf Christian Gonzalez is a stud, we already knew that going into this game, but he completely erased DK Metcalf on Sunday. Maybe Metcalf isn’t as good as he used to be, but wiping him off the board made it a lot more difficult for the Steelers to move the ball. Gonzalez traveled with him everywhere, including in the slot. This is why you pay him all that money, because he is a true shutdown corner capable of carrying out every assignment. Player safety worries There is nothing too bad to complain about when it comes to the refs, but there were still some questionable calls. Marcus Jones was involved with two of those. Mike Vrabel was quite agitated at the end of the first half because of what was a pretty clear pick play that ended with Marcus Jones injured on the ground. Thankfully he was fine, but it was a missed call nonetheless. Later in the game, Jones appeared to clearly be interfered with on a punt, but no penalty was called either. Officiating is never going to be perfect and on the whole did not make any egregious mistakes on Sunday. Still, in a billion-dollar business like the NFL you would still like to see the refs and the replay officials do a better job than they did on those plays — especially with a player-safety perspective in mind. Aaron Rodgers is washed Aaron Rodgers is certainly going to be a first-ballot Hall of Famer, but it’s pretty clear that his best years are behind him. He looked panicked and uncomfortable on Sunday, and it led to a tough game where the Steelers offense could only muster three points. There were chances to try to push the ball down the field, but he simply did not want to do it. Whether he was unsure of what he was seeing, or he thought he couldn’t get the ball there, Rodgers chose to check the ball down instead of making the deep throw. He finished the game with only 187 yards passing, two fumbles, and an interception. The Steelers seemed to have hired Mike McCarthy as their head coach in order to keep Rodgers, and that plan worked. However, from a bigger-picture perspective the logic might not have been that sound. Then again, they did win last week, so maybe they bounce back in Week 3. On to Jacksonville The Patriots travel to Jacksonville next week to take on a Jaguars team that looked fantastic for a game and a half, and then fell apart in the second half this Sunday to lose to Denver and drop to 1-1. The Jags offense has looked solid with Trevor Lawrence, and the defense had a pick for the second week in…
author: Pat Lane

title: 7 winners and losers from Patriots’ win over the Steelers
summary: The New England Patriots got in the win column during their home opener on Sunday with a 20-3 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Patriots’ Week 2 contest. Winners OLBs Elijah Ponder & Gabe Jacas: The Patriots young edge duo each played 36 […]
full_text: The New England Patriots got in the win column during their home opener on Sunday with a 20-3 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers . Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Patriots’ Week 2 contest. Winners OLBs Elijah Ponder & Gabe Jacas: The Patriots young edge duo each played 36 snaps on Sunday as they were relied upon following the injury to Dre’Mont Jones. Success followed. Ponder ended the day with a sack and additional QB hit to go along with three TFLs and a scoop-and-score touchdown to seal Sunday’s victory. Jacas continued to build upon his early season momentum with a pair of pressures and a QB hit on a bootleg, while also recording his first career interception. New England’s four-man front saw their pressure production improve this week, and the young pass rushers were a key part to that success. CB Christian Gonzalez: New England’s top cornerback embraces matching up against other team’s top receivers. He did that with success in Week 2, as he limited DK Metcalf to three catches for 11 yards across 34 matchups — Gonzalez’s most matchups against a single receiver in a game in his career. Two of those receptions came behind the line of scrimmage, as it was another dominant effort from Gonzalez. DT Christian Barmore: The Patriots defensive tackle continued his strong start to the season by once again making an impact as a pass rusher. Shortly after drawing a hold, Barmore kickstarted the play of the day by beating right guard Spencer Anderson 1-on-1 with a hump move before swiping the ball loose from Aaron Rodgers. RB TreVeyon Henderson: After missing last week with an ankle injury, Henderson made his season debut on Sunday and immediately made his impact felt. The speedster took his third carry of the season 39 yards up the middle — behind strong blocking across all three levels — to open the scoring. In total, the second-year back went on to lead the team with 16 carries for 78 yards on the ground. Losers Health: The Patriots are coming off of a year in which they had relatively strong injury luck. It’s tough to have such fortunes two straight seasons, which is what the Patriots realized on Sunday. After losing starting right guard Mike Onwenu to what is believed to be a season-ending ankle injury , the Patriots ruled out ED Dre’Mont Jones (shoulder) , S Craig Woodson (shoulder), TE Eli Raridon (thigh), and S Dell Pettus (ankle) . Woodson, who was spotted in a sling in the post game locker room, and Jones’ shoulder injury appeared more on the serious side as New England’s depth will be tested moving forward. “We have to get healthy and figure out who’s available next week for a huge challenge,” Vrabel said. “That’s what we have to be able to do is create those opportunities for the next guy in and be able to coach everybody the same.” QB Drake Maye: The offense remains a work in process early in the year as Maye noted the unit is “not where we want to be” following the victory. In a positive department, Maye generated some explosive plays in the passing attack such as a 63-yard completion to Romeo Doubs on a “dash” pass. But, the turnovers and negative plays continued to keep the unit out of the end zone. That was highlighted by Maye throwing another downfield interception when he failed to localize a dropping linebacker. Honorable mentions It was deja vu early on Sunday after a Rhamondre Stevenson fumble — his second since the Steelers game last season. Stevenson saw limited touches afterwards but made them count, ending the day with 43 yards on just six carries. Quiet game for the wide receiver room in their first game with A.J. Brown. It was promising that Romeo Doubs got going leading the team with 96 yards on three catches. A 63-yard explosive on a dash pass was Doubs’ longest reception of his career, but he did see a pass slightly behind him go through his hands later in the day. Eli Raridon had an impressive 30-yard catch working through a DPI before exiting with injury. Hunter Henry finished with a steady 3/40 receiving line but took the blame for Drake Maye’s interception after the game. It was a bounce-back performance from Alijah Vera-Tucker, who did not allow a pressure in 29 pass blocking snaps. Will Campbell continued to play mostly well while Jared Wilson and the right side of the offensive line were up-and-down against a talented front. Passing off stunts remains a work in progress early on. Another impressive showing from Christian Elliss with a strip-sack, TFL, and team-high 12 total tackles. Him and Robert Spillane were effective blitzers. Joshua Farmer with three pressures and a sack on just 18 pass rushes. Charles Woods also had a solid showing in place of the injured Carlton Davis. Woods allowed just four catches and flashed in run support en route to piling up 10 tackles. The defensive game plan was simple against Aaron Rodgers: heat him up. New England blitzed on 18 drop backs and held the Steelers to 43 passing yards (2.7 yards per attempt) and 22.2% success rate while also recording eight pressures, two sacks and one interception on those plays. Credit to Cameron Latu, Greg Van Roten, and Jaylen Reed as three newly acquired players who were thrusted into key roles due to injuries. Andy Borregales missed a 47-yard field goal but bounced back to connect from 45 the following drive. Honorable loser: meteorologists. So much for the rain all game .
author: Brian Hines

title: Patriots defense finds the right formula in win over Steelers
summary: The New England Patriots won their home opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers in large part because of their defense. The unit coordinated by Zak Kuhr actually managed to out-score its opponent: whereas the Steelers scored three points all game, Kuhr’s unit put up seven — contributing significantly to the Patriots’ 20-3 victory. How did the […]
full_text: The New England Patriots won their home opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers in large part because of their defense. The unit coordinated by Zak Kuhr actually managed to out-score its opponent: whereas the Steelers scored three points all game, Kuhr’s unit put up seven — contributing significantly to the Patriots’ 20-3 victory. How did the group do that? By sticking to the formula. “That has to be the formula: you have to affect the quarterback each and every week,” said head coach Mike Vrabel. “Zak and everybody over there does a fantastic job [but] all the credit goes to the players. Being able to see Christian Barmore affect the quarterback with the holding and a forced fumble and seeing everybody compete and work together to affect the quarterback — and the coverage has to be there long enough for the rush to get there.” The Patriots sacked Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers four times on Sunday and applied pressure throughout the game, highlighted by the aforementioned Christian Barmore strip-sack in the early fourth quarter. Teammate Elijah Ponder picked up the loose ball and returned it 19 yards for a touchdown, putting the Patriots up by 17 points and giving the defense its first turnover to celebrate this season. The second, a Gabe Jacas interception, followed shortly thereafter. “We played good team defense,” said cornerback Christian Gonzalez after the game. “We left some plays out there that we can obviously come back and get in the film room and fix. I am proud of this defense and proud of this team. We went out there and fought hard. That’s a physical team. The Steelers are a physical team. They came in and always want to be physical. So, our challenge was to be more physical as a defense. I think we did that.” The physicality was one part, the overall battle plan another — a combination Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy had plenty of praise for in the aftermath of the game. “Good pressure plan,” McCarthy explained. “I think the biggest thing is the pressure and challenging our routes man to man. We expected that this week. That’s the way we prepped to come into the game. We did not execute, so you’ve got to give them credit.” The Patriots achieved the pressure against Rodgers by regularly sending extra rushers his way. According to initial charting by Pro Football Focus, Kuhr called for the blitz on 21 of the Steelers’ 46 dropback plays. On average, 4.8 pass rushers attacked the opposing pocket on each dropback. “They were just giving us different looks, bringing different pressures, stunts,” Steelers offensive tackle Troy Fautanu said. “Obviously, the coaches go over it during the week. We’ve got to be able to execute, go out there and block our man, regardless if we’re 1-on-1. We’ve got to do a better job.” The Patriots’ own execution was not flawless either, but given the circumstances — multiple players were lost to injury — the group performed well. It also managed to play by the formula its head coach has in mind. Moving forward, doing so repeatedly will be key especially if the injury bug keeps biting.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots teammates react to ‘heartbreaking’ Mike Onwenu injury
summary: Mike Onwenu’s game, and potentially his season, came to an end in the second quarter on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The New England Patriots’ veteran guard was rolled up from behind on a sack and did not get up. He later left the Gillette Stadium field on a cart and was quickly ruled out […]
full_text: Mike Onwenu’s game, and potentially his season , came to an end in the second quarter on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The New England Patriots’ veteran guard was rolled up from behind on a sack and did not get up. He later left the Gillette Stadium field on a cart and was quickly ruled out due to an ankle injury. The show had to go on without Onwenu, but his departure was nonetheless one of the biggest talking points after the Patriots’ eventual 20-3 victory . “It is heartbreaking,” said quarterback Drake Maye. “A guy like Mike, who has played through injuries, been here since he was a rookie, playing multiple positions and just — he is just gritty. He leaves it all out there and I’ll make sure to check in on him, see how he is doing.” Selected in the sixth round of the 2020 NFL Draft, Onwenu is the longest-tenured player on the Patriots’ roster and one of the best guards in franchise history. He also has been impressively durable, appearing in 104 of a possible 107 games since his rookie season and playing over 5,900 offensive snaps along the way. How many more, if any, he will be able to add this season is unclear at this point. Early prognostications are not optimistic, however, with initial X-rays reportedly revealing a broken ankle. “It’s been a pleasure being able to play beside somebody so dominant,” said right tackle Morgan Moses. “Just the relationship that we’ve built over the last couple of years. I care more about the person than the football player. What he brings to the table and just helping me every day. I can’t sit here and say that I can do all these things myself without having a good partner in crime. Anytime you lose somebody of that caliber, it’s hard. Mike knows we got him and we’ll do anything for him. The biggest thing is keeping him around here and keeping him as a part of this team. He’s a building block for us, so you can’t replace a guy like that with that type of his stature and what he stands for as an offensive lineman.” “Losing Big Mike is tough,” added left tackle Will Campbell. “He means so much not only to this team but our room. Such a great player. Such a good leader. He’s played really good football ever since he’s gotten here. Obviously, somebody’s going to have to step up and fill his shoes. I’m praying for him and just thinking about him.” Onwenu, who reworked his contract in the offseason, is set to enter unrestricted free agency after the season. Now, his outlook both this year and beyond is very much in question.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Mike Onwenu injury: Patriots guard reportedly feared to have suffered season-ending injury

Onwenu is now expected to miss the remainder of the season. Update (9/20/26): Patriots guard reportedly feared to have suffered season-ending injury After […]
full_text: Update (9/20/26): Mike Onwenu suffered broken ankle against Steelers, X-rays reportedly show Mike Onwenu’s X-rays showed the right guard suffered a broken right ankle in Sunday’s win, according to ESPN’s Mike Reiss. Onwenu is now expected to miss the remainder of the season. Update (9/20/26): Patriots guard reportedly feared to have suffered season-ending injury After being carted off in Sunday’s game during the first quarter, Patriots right guard Mike Onwenu is feared to have suffered a season-ending leg injury, according to reports . In his relief, veteran Greg Van Roten played 40 snaps in the win over the Steelers. “It is heartbreaking when you see a guy like Mike who has played through injuries, been here since he was a rookie, playing multiple positions and just does the — he is just gritty. He leaves it all out there,” Drake Maye said after the game. “But at the same time, Greg comes in there and guys are stepping up, and you have got Greg and Mo [Morgan Moses] over there. That is combined at least 70 years over there, so they have got a lot of experience, they know how to play together, and they have been on teams before. So, I have got full confidence in GVR when he came in there.” Original story (9/20/26): Patriots guard carted off with ankle injury against Steelers New England Patriots starting right guard Mike Onwenu has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday’s game with an ankle injury. The injury occurred with less than one minute remaining in the first quarter against the Pittsburgh Steelers, as quarterback Drake Maye was sacked on first down. The play also saw Steelers pass rusher T.J. Watt roll up on Onwenu’s right leg from behind. The 28-year-old stayed down before being carted off the field. He was then immediately ruled out by the team. Veteran offensive lineman Greg Van Roten then took his place at right guard. Ben Brown is also on the game day roster as a reserve option along the interior. Onwenu has been one of the Patriots’ best and most consistent linemen over the past few seasons. He started all 38 games at right guard over the last two years as he has led the team in offensive snaps in that stretch.
author: Brian Hines

title: Instant analysis from Patriots’ 20-3 win over Steelers
summary: There was a chance to clear the air at Gillette Stadium. The New England Patriots saw it through to defeat the Pittsburgh Steelers by a score of 20-3 in Sunday’s home opener. Here’s a glance back on the 1 p.m. ET kickoff as head coach Mike Vrabel’s side moves further into September at 1-1. Maye […]
full_text: There was a chance to clear the air at Gillette Stadium. The New England Patriots saw it through to defeat the Pittsburgh Steelers by a score of 20-3 in Sunday’s home opener. Here’s a glance back on the 1 p.m. ET kickoff as head coach Mike Vrabel’s side moves further into September at 1-1. Maye throws fourth interception of season What transpired at Lumen Field against the Super Bowl LX champions could not carry over in Foxborough. A week removed from throwing three interceptions in three drives to fall to the Seattle Seahawks, Drake Maye needed to be aggressive and not reckless. He fell somewhere in the middle on a rainy Sunday. The 24-year-old Patriots quarterback completed 14-of-22 passes for 208 yards with no touchdowns and one pick. Taking the field in “12” personnel, New England’s offense got the afternoon underway with a turnover that the QB was not responsible for. That collapsed an opening drive that featured a 29-yard sail route to fellow captain Hunter Henry. The next series brought a 7-0 lead on the ground, however. And then it was back to the air with a 30-yard connection to rookie tight end Eli Raridon, who later suffered a thigh injury, through defensive pass interference that got things to the red zone. New England’s punt unit did not need to take the field until the final two possessions of the first half. By intermission, the score read 10-3 while Maye had gone just 7-of-9 passing for 89 yards and the offense had gone 2-of-5 on third down. Out of intermission, where things had melted down in the season opener, Maye went from a 29-yard completion to an underthrown interception by linebacker Patrick Queen on consecutive plays. The next opportunity gave way to a missed field goal. But a 63-yard strike set the Patriots up for a 13-3 lead that would lengthen with complementary football. Down No. 1, Doubs stretches the field for 96 yards A high ankle sprain sent A.J. Brown to injured reserve after September began in the loss column. But Sunday provided a snapshot for how New England’s wide receiver room can go forward without No. 1. With Romeo Doubs going forward, too. After a debut to forget, the March signing caught three passes on four targets for a team-high 96 yards. He turned in a diving conversion of 29 yards on third down and followed it up with a field-stretcher worth 63 yards for longest play of New England’s young season. Versus a secondary missing Joey Porter Jr., the rest of New England’s wideouts combined to finish with five receptions for 35 yards. DeMario Douglas also drew the start while Mack Hollins, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III, who had been healthy scratch last week, rounded out the depth chart. Stevenson’s fumble sets up Henderson’s breakaway touchdown The keys were in Rhamondre Stevenson’s hands. But New England’s downhill running back lost his 10th career fumble with the help of linebackers Nick Herbig and Payton Wilson on Sunday’s opening drive. It was just his second touch and a flashback to Pittsburgh’s 2025 visit to Gillette Stadium. The starter went on to handle 46 scrimmage yards across seven chances, led by an angry A-gap pickup of 24. An ankle injury that lingered since August didn’t linger into Sunday, though. TreVeyon Henderson was on the field by the second series. The No. 38 overall pick last year’s draft class showed second effort to move the chains on third down and soon showed the breakaway speed, too, rushing for a 39-yard touchdown up the middle through sea of Steelers. Henderson finished Sunday with 76 rushing yards and the score through 16 handoffs. Onwenu carted off as Steelers close in Two sacks had been allowed by the Patriots in the season opener. Both of those takedowns surfaced during the final quarter in the Pacific Northwest on a night that saw the offensive line charged with one false start, one illegal block in the back and one holding penalty. The competitive stamina would be put to the test against the Steelers’ rising blitz rate. There stood Will Campbell at left tackle, Alijah Vera-Tucker at left guard, Jared Wilson at center and captain Morgan Moses pulling the way to paydirt at right tackle. But the right guard spot lost its anchor as Pittsburgh got in the sack column with 1:08 remaining in the first quarter. Mike Onwenu had his ankle rolled up from behind by perennial NFL Defensive Player of the Year candidate T.J. Watt while engaged in pass protection. The 92-game starter with north of 5,600 offensive snaps to his name was carted to the locker room and quickly ruled out. August signing Greg Van Roten took over at right guard on an afternoon that saw the visitors tally three official sacks. All three took place before halftime. And Maye held on as time expired in the pocket on the last. Rodgers held out of the end zone with 187 passing yards Aaron Rodgers first faced the Patriots during the 2006 campaign. Time did not turn back on Sunday. The Steelers quarterback went 23-of-39 passing for 187 yards with no touchdowns and two turnovers during the visit to Foxborough. There would be no Michael Pittman Jr. out wide for him due to a foot injury. But there would be two straight three-and-outs to begin the matinee. And the first completion did not find the gamebook until tight end Pat Freiermuth was found in the flat versus Christian Gonzalez on the third drive. Pittsburgh’s stagnant offense began 2-of-8 on third down and went into halftime averaging 3.4 yards per play on the heels of a 56-yard field goal. The red zone was not visited until 5:46 was left in regulation. The Patriots kicked things off in the base defense with captain Marcus Jones alongside the extended All-Pro cornerback. Charles Woods stepped on in the nickel package with Carlton Davis III downgraded to out after missing three consecutive practices with a neck issue. Pick-collecting safety Kevin Byard III joined them in the starting secondary while respective ankle and shoulder injuries sidelined Craig Woodson and Dell Pettus. Pittsburgh’s receivers would be paced by rookie Germie Bernard’s 35 yards on eight targets. Past Pro Bowler DK Metcalf, who was shadowed by No. 0 both on the perimeter and in the slot, had 27 yards and a key drop across nine targets. Four sacks and then some for New England’s front Bringing down a 42-year-old with a quick trigger was the task. The Patriots were up for it. Inside linebacker Christian Elliss teed off for the defense’s first sack with 8:05 to go before halftime on a blitz. It was felt on a drive that spanned a dozen snaps. It turned a third-and-7 on the doorstep of the red zone into a loss of 36 yards as the Steelers sputtered and recovered. There was more where that came from. Christian Barmore, who started along the interior next to Milton Williams and Cory Durden, broke into the backfield for a forced fumble on second-and-21. Outside linebacker Elijah Ponder cleaned up what the defensive tackle created. The 2025 undrafted addition out of Cal Poly took the turnover back 19 yards for a touchdown and a 20-3 advantage in the final quarter. He’d get in the sack column next time out. And defensive lineman Joshua Farmer also had a hand in New England racking up four sacks. But a veteran edge exited in the midst of Sunday, as Dre’Mont Jones was downgraded to out with a shoulder injury that sent No. 50 overall pick Gabe Jacas on in his place. The Illinois product corralled his first NFL interception a week after corralling his first NFL sack. That’d be the last snap for Pittsburgh’s quarterback. Behind Rodgers, the Steelers’ committee of running backs managed 81 rushing yards over the course of 20 handoffs. Borregales goes 2-of-3 from range With incumbent Bryce Baringer on injured reserve , the punting and holding duties were again up to a veteran who signed to New England’s practice squad at its formation. Mitch Wishnowsky averaged 46.3 yards per punt on Sunday and had one effort downed inside the opposing 20-yard line. The back-to-back standard elevation delivered a long of 54…
author: Oliver Thomas

title: Week 2: Saints vs. Ravens social media reactions
summary: After a gutsy comeback attempt fell short a week ago, the New Orleans Saints responded in week two and in a big way with a 24-17 road victory over the Baltimore Ravens to improve to 1-1 overall on the young 2026 NFL season. In a game where many were not giving the Saints a chance […]
full_text: After a gutsy comeback attempt fell short a week ago, the New Orleans Saints responded in week two and in a big way with a 24-17 road victory over the Baltimore Ravens to improve to 1-1 overall on the young 2026 NFL season. In a game where many were not giving the Saints a chance on paper, QB Tyler Shough answered the bell and led his team to another come from behind performance with a much more positive result this time around. Let’s check out what some fans had to say on social media about the game.
