title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly from the Saints win against the Ravens
summary: The Good: Tyler Shough and Chris Olave Shough and Olave once again had a great day, as Shough threw for 252 yards and Olave went for 86 yards while the pair connected for the game tying touchdown. Juwan Johnson and Devaughn Vele also had very good days, as they each converted a few tough third […]
full_text: The Good: Tyler Shough and Chris Olave Shough and Olave once again had a great day, as Shough threw for 252 yards and Olave went for 86 yards while the pair connected for the game tying touchdown. Juwan Johnson and Devaughn Vele also had very good days, as they each converted a few tough third downs and had 60+ receiving yards in their own right. Shough is the NFL’s passing yards leader through two games and Olave trails only Jaxon Smith-Njigba in receiving yards. This combination is only going to continue to get better as the season goes along, as after two tough road games to start the year the Saints now have three very winnable games in the Superdome over the next three weeks before they head to New York and then Paris. The Bad: Rushing offense The Saints trailed much of the game, so they did not need to rely on the ground game that much, but even still they did not produce much in that area this week. As a team they ran 27 times for 65 yards which is an average of 2.4 yards per carry. This is going to be a problem if they manage to get a lead early in some of their next few games against weaker opponents and need to milk the clock a bit, as so far through two weeks the Saints and new addition Travis Etienne Jr. are averaging just 3 yards per carry on the ground. The Ravens and Lions both have above average run defenses, but still we need to see a bit more considering how good we know Etienne and Alvin Kamara can be. The Ugly: Another slow start The Saints started slow again on Sunday, thankfully not as slow as they did last week in Detroit but they still eventually needed a +15 point fourth quarter to secure the win. The defense kept it close throughout as they had a very good day and deserve a lot of recognition for the win. The offense managed just three field goals through the first three quarters before turning it on in the fourth. They did not have any turnovers like last week but only had one drive of more than 50 yards before the fourth quarter. While exciting, this is a dangerous game to be playing week in and week out, and lets hope that the Saints returning home against lesser competition will have them take and hold a lead throughout a game rather than having to rely on fourth quarter comebacks most of the time.

After opening the 2026 season with back-to-back road games, the Saints will make their long-awaited return to the Caesars Superdome on Sunday afternoon when they host the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3. And they are returning home with plenty of momentum. New Orleans comes into this game after getting a shocking 24-17 victory over the Baltimore Ravens, a matchup that very few expected the Saints to win. After trailing 14-3 in the first half, the Saints once again showed their resilience and battled back to score 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to secure their first victory of the season. Quarterback Tyler Shough continued to show why the Saints have so much confidence in him, completing 27 of 34 passes for 252 yards and a touchdown. He then delivered when it mattered most, scoring the go-ahead touchdown on a 1-yard quarterback sneak with 1:28 remaining in the fourth quarter. Chris Olave caught eight passes for 86 yards, including a 21-yard touchdown that tied the game at 17. But it was Julian Blackmon who sealed the Saints’ victory, intercepting Lamar Jackson on Baltimore’s final drive with just 20 seconds remaining. Now sitting at 1-1 after two difficult road games, the Saints finally get the opportunity to play at home in front of the Who Dat Nation, with kickoff against the Raiders set for 3:25 p.m. CT on Sunday. There will also be a familiar face on the opposing sideline, as former Saints offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak returns to New Orleans now as the head coach of the Raiders. According to FanDuel, the Saints are currently 3-point favorites against the Raiders, with an over/under of 43.5 points. However, those odds could move as kickoff approaches. title: Giants vs. Titans odds: Opening lines for Week 3 matchup
summary: The New York Giants haven’t played the Los Angeles Rams yet, but it’s already Week 3 for the 30 other teams. The Giants still have business to take care of, but they’ll be hosting the Tennessee Titans Sunday at MetLife Stadium at 1 p.m. The Giants open as 6.5-point favorites at home against the 0-2 […]
full_text: New York Giants helmets on the sideline. | Getty Images The New York Giants haven’t played the Los Angeles Rams yet, but it’s already Week 3 for the 30 other teams. The Giants still have business to take care of, but they’ll be hosting the Tennessee Titans Sunday at MetLife Stadium at 1 p.m. The Giants open as 6.5-point favorites at home against the 0-2 Titans, per FanDuel , though the line may change based on what happens tonight. This is one of the games that we’ve had circled since January and it promises to be rich with storylines. The Giants and Titans are inextricably linked after an offseason rife with cross-pollination. These two teams last met in 2022, with the Giants stunning the Titans who were coming off of a 12-4 season. The Giants came away with a win when the Titans missed a last-second field goal. That game started the Titans’ decline, while the Giants rode the momentum to a 9-7-1 season, a trip to the playoffs, and their first post-season win since 2011. This time around, the game will feature a gaggle of former Giants making their return to the Meadowlands. Starting slot receiver Wan’Dale Robinson, starting center Austin Schlottman, and second tight end Daniel Bellinger are all featured on the Titans’ offense. Meanwhile, cornerback Cor’Dale Flott is starting for Tennessee’s defense, though he missed last week’s game with a quad injury. His status will be something to monitor. The Giants attempted to re-sign both Robinson, who was the Giants’ leading receiver a season ago, and Flott, but were outbid by the cap-rich, talent-poor Titans. This will also feature a different reunion of former teammates. Tennessee drafted Ohio State wide receiver Carnell Tate with the fourth overall pick. The Giants drafted his teammate, LB Arvell Reese with the very next pick. The highlight of the storylines is the return of Brian Daboll to New York. Daboll was, as we all remember, the Giants’ head coach from 2022 to 2025, when he was fired mid-season. He was hired by Robert Saleh to be Tennessee’s offensive coordinator and develop quarterback Cam Ward. On the flip side, former Titans’ head coachBrian Callahan is now the Giants’ QB coach and passing game coordinator. Adding to the intrigue, the Titans nearly took down the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. The Titans were almost completely bereft of talent a year ago, and they’re going to be a work in progress this year. But perhaps their rebuild is progressing fast than we anticipated — or perhaps the Eagles aren’t as good as many believe. It feels odd to see the Giants as strong favorites on game day — whether at home or on the road — and this game promises to be far more interesting than the spread may suggest. title: 5 questions about the Rams: Aaron Donald, Super Bowl, MNF preview
summary: The New York Giants will be in California Monday night to face a Los Angeles Rams team that got off to a disappointing start with a 27-7 Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. To preview this game, Evan Craig of SB Nation’s Turf Show Times is our guest for this week’s ‘5 questions’ […]
full_text: Sean McVay | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants will be in California Monday night to face a Los Angeles Rams team that got off to a disappointing start with a 27-7 Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. To preview this game, Evan Craig of SB Nation’s Turf Show Times is our guest for this week’s ‘5 questions’ segment. Ed: After all of the offseason hype, how shocking was the loss in Australia? How does the team seem to be handling it? How is the fan base handling it? Evan: Truthfully, I didn’t think it was shocking at all. During my exchange with Niners Nation last week, I even predicted the 49ers to win it. I thought the Rams would stumble out of the gate and make it closer towards the end; the latter obviously didn’t happen. They had some good moments early on, but failed to maintain that momentum the rest of the way. LA was doomed from the start since they had a ridiculously stupid travel plan, which was getting to Australia just over a day before kickoff. Yeah, they never stood a chance. The team seems to be handling it the best they can by learning from their mistakes and living to see another day. That’s really all they can do. There’s some slight panic amongst the fanbase. The loss overseas certainly wasn’t how they expected to start a new season while hyped as a Super Bowl favorite. If things continue this way, especially with the schedule toughening up, the panic will only grow louder, but for now, it’s been fairly muted. Ed: How much does the injury to Myles Garrett take the edge off the return of Aaron Donald? Is Donald expected to play this week? If so, what sort of impact do you expect him to have? Evan: Quite a bit. Aaron Donald coming back after two seasons out of the league was already iffy enough, and now he’ll likely be asked to do more. Not ideal at all. Donald should play this week, but how much is unknown. I expect the coaching staff will have him on a limited snap count in the first few games before gradually letting him see the field more. Rams fans shouldn’t expect him to have much impact early on, yet that can change quickly as the season progresses. The defense should be fine, though, as they held up for the most part last season without Myles Garrett or AD in the lineup. [ NOTE: These questions were asked, and answered, before we knew whether or not Donald would play]. Ed: Considering the hype, Matthew Stafford’s age, the Garrett trade, the return of Donald, the Rams’ “push all the chips to the center of the table” mentality, is anything other than a Super Bowl title an acceptable outcome this season? Evan: That is an extremely fair statement to make … for the most part. This season got off on a bad note, but I don’t expect the negative vibes to last. All contenders have a rough game or two every season. Unfortunately, that bad game happened to the Rams in the opener. However, I don’t entirely believe that if LA fails to win the Super Bowl this season, it’ll be unacceptable. At most, the Rams have next season as well to make a run, assuming all their pieces return for another go. Ed: If you could take one player off the Giants’ roster and put him into the Rams’ lineup, who would it be? Why? Evan: Easy — Isaiah Likely . The Rams love their tight ends and use them a ton in various offensive packages. Likely is a solid tight end who is quite effective in the passing game. He would be a fun target for Matthew Stafford, that’s for sure. Ed: Let’s skip the prediction thing. I will ask you this. If there is a path to the Giants winning on Monday, what does it look like? What weaknesses can they exploit? What, if anything, worries you about the Giants? Evan: For the Giants to win on Monday, they have to steal a page out of the 49ers’ Week 1 playbook. New York has to play physical football and work to disrupt the timing of the Rams’ offense. San Francisco’s gameplan worked to perfection. The Giants aren’t exactly at the 49ers’ talent level to make that happen, but they’re a young, scrappy team and one that will get better as the season goes on. NY must attack the offensive line and LA’s new corners. The secondary is working to gel through these first few games with all the new pieces, so lapses and coverage breakdowns are going to happen as they figure things out. What worries me most about the Giants is their running game. San Francisco rushed for 174 yards on them, and now they’re about to face a team that dominated the Cowboys on the ground. Their physicality in that department really stood out to me when watching Sunday’s game, and certainly gave me plenty of “well, crap” moments thinking ahead to this one.

title: NY Giants news: John Harbaugh’s impact, Ernie Accorsi, Joey Porter, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans. Here are the stories you need to know before the Giants face the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football. An ode to my friend and ultimate sports fan Ernie Accorsi | NY Post This one hurts. This one stings. Ernie Accorsi was a great many things in a […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans. Here are the stories you need to know before the Giants face the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football. An ode to my friend and ultimate sports fan Ernie Accorsi | NY Post This one hurts. This one stings. Ernie Accorsi was a great many things in a full, vibrant life that spanned 84 years before that enormous heart of his was stilled at last Saturday night. He was a sports fan. He was a sports writer. He was a sports executive. He provided the questions for the “Colts Quiz” that Eddie gave his fiancés on the eve of their wedding in “Diner.” He was first an acolyte, then a co-worker and later a close friend of the great John Unitas, of whom Ernie once said: “God had a good day the day He came up with Johnny U.” He was also a gentleman, and exceedingly good company, and it was my privilege to call him a friend for the last 30 years. Ranking all 32 backup NFL quarterbacks for the 2026 season | ESPN Jameis Winston checks in at No. 6. I might put him higher than that. Winston is well into the second phase of his career as a high-end backup. His results have been solid in aggregate, though his play style ensures a roller-coaster ride. Over the past four seasons, Winston has recorded a very high 3.9% turnover rate but still managed a 49.7 QBR in that span. This is because he’s willing to push the ball downfield. Winston’s 9.6 air yards per attempt since 2022 is higher than any qualifying quarterback registered last season. Inside the saga around Joey Porter Jr.’s future with Steelers | ESPN “I don’t know if he ever puts on a Steelers uniform again,” a source with knowledge of the situation told ESPN. In just a few months, John Harbaugh has imprinted his identity and culture on Giants | NY Post They are two of the most commonly used words when discussing a team. Culture and identity. Changing the Giants’ culture off the field and identity on the field was always going to be one of the greatest challenges for John Harbaugh when he took over as head coach. He inherited a team whose culture was nonexistent and whose recent identity was of a perennial loser. He conversely brought with him a longtime and sustained winning culture and identity with the Ravens. Already, some of it was noticeable in their Week 1 win over the Cowboys. “I’d say it’s really his identity, his culture,” tight end Isaiah Likely told The Post after practice on Friday. “Obviously with the Ravens, he had been there for so long, it feels like it was the Ravens identity. But coach Harbaugh was always the head coach. I feel like he instilled the Ravens mantra and everything. So when he got over here, I guess you can quote-unquote say it was the Ravens mantra, but it’s coach Harbaugh’s culture.” Giants can prove their ‘ticked off’ mentality and answer key questions in big Week 2 matchup | NY Post “Everyone’s probably saying, ‘Oh, the Giants are this and that, they’re so good, they’re so great,’ because we won,’’ Ricard said. “We’re trying to stay humble. We’re trying to stay hungry. It’s a week-to-week thing. Those human emotions, we’re trying to stay level, we’re trying to stay even keel throughout this whole thing.’’ Ricard was with the Ravens the past nine years. He knows the drill. Harbaugh has been there, done that, as far as winning loads of games with the Ravens and then winning some more of them. “I feel like it goes to culture,’’ Nubin said. “The best teams when they win they come in the next day and they feel like they lost, because you’re just so meticulous on the details. That’s exactly coach Harbaugh’s mindset. That’s how I felt coming into the building the next day, I didn’t feel like we were on top of the world.’’ They want to feel pissed off. Can they? Will they? title: Former NY Giants GM Ernie Accorsi passes away
summary: The New York Giants announced Sunday afternoon that former general manager Ernie Accorsi passed away on Saturday night at the age of 84. Accorsi was born on October 29th, 1941 in Hershey Pennsylvania and spent 37 years as an NFL executive, the final 12 of which were spent with the Giants. He first joined the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - NOVEMBER 14: Former Defensive End Michael Strahan puts a coat on 2016 Giants Ring of Honor Inductee Ernie Accorsi during the halftime ceremony of the game between the Cincinnati Bengals and the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on November 14, 2016 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Giants announced Sunday afternoon that former general manager Ernie Accorsi passed away on Saturday night at the age of 84. Accorsi was born on October 29th, 1941 in Hershey Pennsylvania and spent 37 years as an NFL executive, the final 12 of which were spent with the Giants. He first joined the Giants’ front office as an assistant under George Young, serving in that capacity for four years. Accorsi became the Giants’ GM in 1998 and ran the Giants’ front office until 2026. Accorsi built the Giants’ 2000 NFC Championship team, and along with Jerry Reese and Dave Gettleman, laid the foundation for the Giants’ 2007 Super Bowl Championship. Prior to joining the Giants, Accorsi worked for the Baltimore Colts (1970-1974, 1976-1983), and the Cleveland Browns (1985-1992). He was famous for his “Planet Theory” of drafting, as well as originating the adage that “You can never have enough pass rushers.” Accorsi’s crowning achievement came in 2004 with the hiring of Tom Coughlin and the bold trade of fourth overall pick Philip Rivers, as well as three draft picks, to the Los Angeles Chargers for Eli Manning. Though Accorsi retired before the Giants’ legendary 2007 season, he was still given a Super Bowl ring for his work in laying the foundation for that team. Accorsi was inducted into the Giants’ Ring Of Honor in 2016 along with Michael Strahan. Coughlin recounted after Accorsi’s passing, “Ernie was very decisive, very opinionated. His mind was as sharp as a tack. He loved to laugh. He was a great storyteller, great storyteller. He loved to have an audience and laugh, and then everyone else would laugh with him. He was great with punchlines. He was one of those. He was very loyal. Very, very loyal. My experience, of course, Ernie and John Mara interviewed me when I became the head coach back in 2004. I didn’t realize that within a couple of years, Ernie was getting ready to retire. Nevertheless, we had a great challenge and we went forward from there. I always enjoyed working with Ernie, I always enjoyed talking with Ernie.” “Ernie will always be remembered, and I say this out of great respect, he’s the guy that made the trade for Eli Manning. That will go down in Giants history as one of the great moves of all time. Was it risky? Sure it was risky. Ernie did it. Shut the door, went in, he did it on his own. It was his move. He had followed Eli from the time Eli was a very young player at Ole Miss, and he was convinced that Eli was the franchise quarterback that the Giants needed. He was not going to be deterred. ” Giants’ president John Mara said of Accorsi, “Ernie helped shape the course of New York Giants history through his vision, leadership and unwavering belief in building a championship organization. Beyond his accomplishments as a football executive, he was a trusted advisor and dear friend. His legacy will forever be part of the Giants, and he will be greatly missed.” Our thoughts are with all those who knew and loved Ernie Accorsi. Rest in peace.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Survey results: Giants fans were surprised by the defense
summary: It’s safe to say that the New York Giants Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys was a stunner. While most Giants fans picked the Giants to beat the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, fewer fans and very few in the media actually expected the Giants to win. But even the fans who predicted the […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants linebacker Tremaine Edmunds during a play against the Dallas Cowboys. | Getty Images It’s safe to say that the New York Giants Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys was a stunner. While most Giants fans picked the Giants to beat the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, fewer fans and very few in the media actually expected the Giants to win. But even the fans who predicted the Giants’ win didn’t see how coming. How the Giants beat the Cowboys has been one of the storylines of the past week and many around the NFL media landscape have started to view the Giants in a new light. This week we asked Giants fans which aspect of the Giants’ win surprised them the most, and the best answer seems to be “Everything.” I won’t go so far as to say that fans expected how well quarterback Jaxson Dart played. His command of the offense and the improvements in his footwork, as well as how well he read the defense and navigated his reads is definitely a storyline. But considering how much of a pain point the Giants’ defense was over the last couple years, it isn’t a surprise that a full 71% of fans were surprised by some aspect of the defensive play. The Giants were aided in the passing game by George Pickens drops, but the Cowboys were also aided by some questionable pass interference calls (and a non-call). But even so, considering many were expecting Greg Newsome II, Deonte Banks, Jevon Holland, and Tyler Nubin to be an abject disaster, their play to contain a potent Dallas passing attack was impressive. Likewise, the Giants’ run defense was nearly as surprising. Expectations may have been tempered a bit by the Cowboys losing their best offensive lineman, however the Giants’ front 7 was generally stout and did a good job of swarming the ball. Both aspects of the defense were aided by an absolutely suffocating offense that allowed the Giants to fully dictate the pace and flow of the game. We didn’t know quite what the Giants’ offense would look like, or how well it would function. The early results are an interesting, and fun, blend of Greg Roman’s unga-bunga caveman ball with creative misdirection and passing concepts. The combination of philosophies went well together and not only allowed the Giants to control the game on the ground, it gave Jaxson Dart answers to attack Dallas through the air. There is, of course, the reaction that the Giants’ offense only looked good because it went against Dallas. The upcoming game against the Los Angeles Rams should provide a stiffer test on both offense and defense. As of this writing, FanDuel still lists the Giants as 7.5-point underdogs on the road against the Rams. For now, however, Giants fans are probably the most confident in their team that they’ve been since February 6th, 2012. Giants fans currently feel better about their team than any other fanbase in the NFL, at least according to our weekly confidence polls. The fact that 95% of fans were already confident that the Giants were heading in the right direction prior to week 1 was already among the highest marks in the SB Nation network. But confidence has only risen after seeing how the Giants beat the Cowboys. Almost universal fan confidence likely isn’t sustainable over the course of a full season. There will be losses, bumps in the road, and missteps from the coaching staff or players. But at least for now, fans are riding the high of a domineering win over a hated division rival. ( Note: As in previous years, I’ll be providing a chart to follow fan confidence over the course of the season. However it needs more than two data points before it’s worth including .)

title: Patrick Ricard makes Cam Skattebo feel ‘safe,’ more NY Giants notes
summary: New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo likes to run into — and over — things. That’s fun and stuff, but moms worry about their boys. Which is why Skattebo’s mom loves full Patrick Ricard, Skattebo’s personal bodyguard on many of his runs. “I feel safe,” Skattebo said of running behind 300-pound ’Pancake Pat’. “When […]
full_text: Cam Skattebo tkes a handoff from Jaxson Dart. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo likes to run into — and over — things. That’s fun and stuff, but moms worry about their boys. Which is why Skattebo’s mom loves full Patrick Ricard, Skattebo’s personal bodyguard on many of his runs. “I feel safe,” Skattebo said of running behind 300-pound ’Pancake Pat’. “When he hits the first linebacker and I don’t have to take them both on, it’s really nice. “My mom – when we first signed Pat, my mom didn’t really know who he was at first. And then I kind of showed her some videos and kind of taught her what he was going to be doing. And she goes, ‘I want to meet that guy.’ So, my mom says it’s safer, and me, 300 pounds in front of me as a lead blocker on top of the o-line is awesome. It feels awesome.” Tyrone Tracy, kickoff returner When Deonte Banks was in and out of the Giants’ lineup against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 1, the Giants turned to Tyrone Tracy to join Braxton Berrios as one of the two kickoff returners. It is a job Tracy has done before, with eight kickoff returns over the past two seasons for an average 24.1 yards per return. Perhaps the only surprising part of Tracy getting that call is that he had fumbled the ball away on his second — and last — carry of the game against Dallas. He also had a fumble in a preseason game. Banks is questionable to play vs. the Rams with a calf injury. Even if he does play, the Giants might not want to risk using him on kickoff returns. So, we could see Tracy regularly in that role. “Just gives us the running back, the vision. A guy, again, that can run returns downhill. They’re downhill plays. And a guy that can bounce off tackles,” said special teams coordinator Chris Horton. “We just want guys that have a lot of skill, guys that can make plays on their own, and guys that can make people miss in the hole. Because a lot of times it’s going to be one guy that you might have to make miss.” But, the fumbles? “Not concerned at all,” Horton said. “Just things that we talk about. Just from a fundamentals standpoint, you’re going through traffic, let’s make sure we protect the ball.” "It's a question we're asking ourselves, in all honesty. I think it comes back to what he's capable of handling." John Harbaugh was asked how close Malik Nabers is to being able to handle a full workload: pic.twitter.com/2k7s6YDz8w — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) September 18, 2026 Is Malik ready for more? Malik Nabers led the Giants with nine targets in Week 1, his first game back from last season’s torn ACL. Nabers, though, played only 36 of 68 snaps, 52%. Is Nabers ready for more? “It’s a question we’re asking ourselves, in all honesty,” said head coach John Harbaugh. “I think it comes back to what he’s capable of handling. He had a good workload today again, so as he’s ramping up his volume in practice, which would be bringing him closer to that kind of mindset in the games, we’ll see as we get through the games. He looks strong. He does.” Nikko’s adventures New Giants cornerback Nikko Reed was signed off the Los Angeles Chargers’ practice squad on Thursday. Reed hopped on a flight from Los Angeles to New Jersey, practiced with the Giants on Friday and Saturday, then got on a flight back to LA on Saturday afternoon for the team’s trip to LA to face the Rams. I wonder if Reed is still on West Coast time. Harbaugh seemed happy to acquire Reed. “It’s good to be aggressive, especially at that position,” Harbaugh said. “There’s still guys on the practice squad who won’t last on the practice squad probably too much longer, so it was a good get for us.” Giants CB Nikko Reed pic.twitter.com/Z2fFXz2xrd — Giants Nation Show (@GiantsNationPod) September 17, 2026 Numbers to know The Giants’ offensive linemen gave up 10 pressures across 192 combined pass-blocking snaps, third-lowest in the NFL in Week 1. The Giants surrendered the third-lowest quarterback pressure precentage, 5.2. The Giants have a 10-game streak of gaining at least 100 yards rushing, longest in the NFL. The Giants’ 81.82% third-down conversion rate against the Dallas Cowboys led the NFL and was the team’s best since 1991. The Giants were fifth in the NFL in total yards allowed (244) and rushing yards allowed (69) in Week 1.

title: Jets vs. Packers: When will we see the progress?
summary: So frequently over the last decade and a half, the definition of success for a Jets season has been nebulous. With regime after regime attempting rebuild after rebuild, the team has frequently begun a season with low expectations. The 2023 and 2024 seasons with Aaron Rodgers are the only from the last decade where the […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 20: Skyy Moore #23 of the Green Bay Packers celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second half of the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images So frequently over the last decade and a half, the definition of success for a Jets season has been nebulous. With regime after regime attempting rebuild after rebuild, the team has frequently begun a season with low expectations. The 2023 and 2024 seasons with Aaron Rodgers are the only from the last decade where the Jets were viewed as a team that had a legitimate chance to make noise in the AFC heading into Week 1. Phrases, “You can’t judge this team solely by its record,” and, “We need to see progress,” have become staples of Jets preseason analysis in recent years. In broad strokes, these statements have largely been fair. The rosters the Jets have put on the field just haven’t been very good. They have been full of holes and flawed young players hoping to develop with extensive game reps. What has bothered me is that over and over the concept of rebuilding has been used as a blanket excuse to rationalize all of the team’s shortcomings. If we are judging the Jets on progress, shouldn’t there actually be tangible progress throughout the season? There’s a pretty large middle ground between expecting the Jets to immediately go from the bottom of the league to the Super Bowl and accepting any and all failures because the team isn’t a contender. That brings us to Week 2 as the Jets fell to the Green Bay Packers 20-17 in overtime. On paper it was easy to pencil this game in as a loss. Green Bay has been one of the league’s most consistent franchises recently with trips to the Playoffs in six of the last seven seasons. Surely the Packers should be expected to handle a rebuilding team. That’s logical enough in theory, but the Packers were dealing with pretty significant injury issues. They also were not in top form, looking shaky in their Week 1 loss to the Vikings. And the Jets got Green Bay in their home opener at MetLife Stadium. The Jets were never going to be favored over the Packers at any point when these two teams play in 2026, but it’s tough to imagine this matchup happening at a more favorable time for New York. Making progress for a rebuilding team isn’t just about winning the few games you are expected to win like Week 1 against Tennessee. It means occasionally punching above your weight class and stealing a game you aren’t expected to get. Heading into the day, the Packers appeared potentially ripe for the picking. By the time the game started, it was clear this was the case. Green Bay was anything but sharp. The Packers committed 14 penalties and otherwise were sloppy with miscue after miscue. Simply put, it felt like they were trying to hand the Jets this game. The Jets weren’t exactly sharp themselves. They had to work around two wasted timeouts in the first half and a bad challenge that left them without a timeout in an end of half situation where the time expired on them while driving. The offense struggled to gain traction, struggling in the trenches. There wasn’t much room for Breece Hall to run, and Geno Smith was erratic. The Jets had their own penalty issues, and couldn’t so much as jump on fumbles right in front of them. Still, they cobbled together enough production when combined with Green Bay’s struggles to gain a 17-7 lead in the fourth quarter. What better way for the Jets to show progress than closing this game out? What followed can only be described as a classic late game collapse. It began with the Packers backed up on a first and 25 due to two penalties. Matthew Golden got a step or two on Azareye’h Thomas. Jordan Love fired deep. The ball was underthrown. Golden pulled up. Thomas extended his arms and tapped Golden. Golden fell. If Thomas turned his head, it wasn’t much of a head turn. If he contacted Golden, it wasn’t much contact. Still, that’s a situation in the modern NFL where a flag is almost always thrown. The few instances it isn’t, fans of the offensive team scream about the injustice. It was a shame because Thomas was otherwise playing a strong game. Then he was central at the point where the game began to unravel. The Packers scored a touchdown to cut it to 17-14. The Jets got the ball back with around 8:00 left and a chance to put the game away with a long scoring drive. They quickly were forced to punt, and their vaunted special teams failed, allowing a 63 yard return which immediately put the Packers into range for a game-tying chip shot field goal. The Jets got it back with 3:00 left and a chance to win the game. The Jets got to midfield where the drive stalled, stuffed on runs on third and fourth and short. From there, the defense actually came through, tackling Christian Watson short of the sticks after a 5 yard reception on a fourth and 10 with over 40 seconds left. This should have given the Jets an opportunity to win the game in regulation after a Green Bay punt. However, Aaron Glenn inexplicably did not call a timeout after the stop, allowing the Packers to run the clock down with the aid of a delay of game penalty and a rules loophole. The clock went down to 2 seconds, which allowed Green Bay to attempt a low risk Hail Mary. Glenn robbed his offense a chance to win it in regulation. Instead he gave the Packers a chance, even if it was a longshot that failed with a sack. Overtime came. The Jets took the ball, but two of their three plays resulted in sacks, resulting in a punt and a net of -8 yards. From there the result seemed predestined. The Packers drove 58 yards in 5 plays, aided by an undisciplined 15 yard penalty on a late hit by Jarvis Brownlee, Jr. Rookie Trey Smack converted a chip shot 26 yard field goal, and the Packers had an improbable win. After a meltdown like this, I have one simple question to ask. Where is the progress? The Jets let a golden opportunity to start 2-0 for the first time since 2015 slip through their fingers. A victory would have given them a cushion with a challenging two game road trip on the horizon. Beating Green Bay would have guaranteed the Jets entered their Week 5 home date with the Cleveland Browns .500 at worst. Perhaps it could have been a springboard to bigger things. Seven of the sixteen teams in each conference now make the Playoffs. Having one of the top seven records doesn’t require a team to be great or even necessarily good. Opportunistic rebuilding teams sometimes arrive in the postseason ahead of schedule by taking advantage of the chances like this. It would be one thing if the Jets had maintained their level of play from their Week 1 win over the Tennessee Titans. The Packers are objectively a better football team right now. There were scenarios where the Jets played a strong game, but Jordan Love just hit a bunch of tight window passes under duress. Then you’d just have to tip your cap and move on. It’s tough to argue the Jets did anything other than give away a game on this September Sunday in the Meadowlands. Normally a hallmark of progress is young players shining. You can live with losses as a rebuilding team if your future cornerstones play strong games. Again, this wasn’t the case for the Jets. Two of the team’s four highly drafted rookies didn’t play due to injury. Of the other two, David Bailey did register an early sack on a nice play where he first identified a screen, but he was largely ineffective as a pass rusher looking as raw as one might expect a rookie playing his second game to look. Kenyon Sadiq was essentially a nonfactor. Of second year players, Armand Membou struggled, and Mason Taylor was invisible. Thomas had some moments, but that pass interference loomed large. Of course nobody should argue that one bad game should be used to make sweeping judgments on these players. Membou in particular has shown great promise in his…

title: New York Jets News: Matt LaFleur Takes Shot at Jets HC Aaron Glenn
summary: There is just no other way to put it: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn blew it. He made so many critical mistakes that cost his team dearly. At the end of regulation, he had a chance to get the ball back one more time and refused. He had the timeouts. He didn’t use […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur on the sidelines during the fourth quarter against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There is just no other way to put it: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn blew it. He made so many critical mistakes that cost his team dearly. At the end of regulation, he had a chance to get the ball back one more time and refused. He had the timeouts. He didn’t use them. “Oh yeah, I was really confused by that. That’s why we called the timeout and tried a Hail Mary,” Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said after the game. The game was tied at 17. Had the Jets used a timeout at the end of regulation, they would have had about 50 seconds to play with on offense. Maybe the game would have never gone to overtime? We will never know. Instead, the Jets blew a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter. Instead of being 2-0 for the first time since 2015, this team is 1-1, facing more questions about the head coach than answers. J-E-T-S! Take the game-day conversation with you! title: Jets vs. Lions odds: Jets open as Week 3 underdogs vs Lions
summary: After opening the 2026 season with a dominating win over the Tennessee Titans last week, this week the New York Jets fell back down to earth with a resounding thud. The Jets dominated the Green Bay Packers for most of the game. They led by double digits early in the fourth quarter, before imploding and […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 18: D'Andre Swift #32 of the Detroit Lions carries the ball against the New York Jets during the first quarter of the game at MetLife Stadium on December 18, 2022 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images After opening the 2026 season with a dominating win over the Tennessee Titans last week, this week the New York Jets fell back down to earth with a resounding thud. The Jets dominated the Green Bay Packers for most of the game. They led by double digits early in the fourth quarter, before imploding and letting the game slip away in overtime. Poor coaching, questionable decisions, dumb penalties, a key breakdown on special teams, terrible clock management, a nonexistent running game, poor quarterback play and an offensive line that did not live up to its billing all contributed to the disappointing 20 – 17 Jets overtime loss to the Packers. The Jets dominated the Packers on paper. They outgained the Packers on the ground and through the air. They controlled the clock with an overwhelming 37:40 to 26:57 advantage in time of possession. They converted 42% on third down compared to a miniscule 11% for the Packers. They won the turnover battle, 1 to 0. Despite all this, the Jets somehow managed to blow a double digit fourth quarter lead and lose as the Packers closed the game with 13 unanswered points. The loss gave the Jets a 1-1 record to start the season. Now the Jets go on the road to take on the Detroit Lions next Sunday. Like the Jets, the Lions won their first game and lost their second this season. They have excelled on offense, scoring 31 points each game, while struggling mightily on defense, giving up 30+ points each game. The Jets should have some success on offense against a Lions team that has given up 30+ points and 446+ yards in each of their first two games. On defense, this game should present a serious challenge for a Jets defense that has been dominant for the most part over the first two games, ranking 2nd in the NFL to date in both points and yards allowed. The Lions’ explosive offense may be difficult to contain. Let’s take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 6.5 points. The game has an over/under of 47.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +270 while the Lions are -335. title: Jets vs Packers: Jets collapse, blow double digit 4th quarter lead as they fall in home opener
summary: In the New York Jets’ 2026 home opener, on a dreary, cool and rainy day in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Jets fell to the Green Bay Packers, 20 – 17. The game opened with the Jets on defense. They quickly forced a Packers three and out. That started an uneventful first quarter of offense […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 20: Marshawn Lloyd #32 of the Green Bay Packers celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the New York Jets with Skyy Moore #23 and Kitan Oladapo #27 during the second quarter of the game at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the New York Jets’ 2026 home opener, on a dreary, cool and rainy day in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Jets fell to the Green Bay Packers, 20 – 17. The game opened with the Jets on defense. They quickly forced a Packers three and out. That started an uneventful first quarter of offense from both teams, as the defenses dominated and neither team came close to scoring. Isaiah Williams endured a nightmare of a first quarter for the Jets, incurring two penalties and fumbling two punt returns. Fortunately for the Jets they recovered both fumbles. The first quarter ended with the score tied at 0-0 and the Packers on offense near midfield. The Packers finally got something going on offense as they put together a 64 yard touchdown drive highlighted by a 20 yard strike from Jordan Love to Christian Watson. With less than 10 minutes left in the first half the score was Packers 7, Jets 0. The Jets quickly responded. On their next possession they put together a long drive highlighted by a pass interference penalty that got the Jets into scoring position. Braelon Allen eventually ran the ball in and the Jets tied the score at 7 -7 with a little more than six minutes left in the half. Neither team scored the rest of the half. The Jets closed out the half with another shockingly inept two minute drill, as they continue to look like the concept is utterly foreign to them. The quarter and the half ended with the score still Jets 7, Packers 7. The Jets opened the third quarter on offense and got the ball near midfield before being forced to punt. The Packers responded with a fruitless drive and a punt of their own. The Jets then got going on offense, putting together a nice looking drive that ended when Geno Smith found Garrett Wilson in the end zone for a touchdown and a 14 – 7 lead late in the third quarter. The third quarter ended with no further scoring. With a little over 12 minutes remaining in regulation the Jets forced a Packers fumble and recovered it at the 18 yard line with a golden opportunity to stick the dagger in with a touchdown. Unfortunately, the Jets could only manage a short Jason Sanders field goal to take a two score lead at 17 – 7 with just over 11 minutes left. Just when it looked like the Packers were cooked, they put together their best drive of the game. Aided by a long pass interference penalty against the Jets, the Packers marched quickly down the field for a touchdown as they cut the Jets lead to just three points at 17 – 14 with nearly 8 minutes remaining in the game. Could the Jets hang on? The Jets were forced to punt on their next possession. Then disaster struck. Skyy Moore broke a 66 yard punt return all the way to the Jets 19 yard line. The Jets defense held from there, forcing a short Packers field goal. Just like that, a double digit Jets lead evaporated in just eight minutes. With just over three minutes to go in the fourth quarter the score was tied at 17, and the Jets were looking for a way to salvage a victory in a game they had dominated up to this point. The Jets advanced to midfield before failing to convert on third and fourth and short, giving the Packers the ball at midfield and needing just a dozen or so yards to set up for a game winning field goal. The Jets, however, had other plans as they shut down the Packers offense and forced overtime. The Jets went backward on their first possession in overtime as Geno Smith was sacked on back to back plays. The Jets were forced to punt and the Packers went to work on offense. It wasn’t long until a dumb and tremendously damaging unnecessary roughness penalty on Travis Brownlee gave the Packers the ball deep in Jets territory. A couple of plays later Trey Smack hit a short field goal to win the game for the Packers. The Jets collapse was complete as they blew a double digit fourth quarter lead in a game they should have won. Final score: Packers 20, Jets 17 in overtime. The devastating loss brought the Jets’ record to 1-1. Now the Jets have to put the loss behind them and get ready for a difficult challenge as they prepare to go on the road to face the Detroit Lions next Sunday.

full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - SEPTEMBER 14: Quarterback Geno Smith #7 of the New York Jets turns to hand off against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on September 14, 2014 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Al Pereira/New York Jets/Getty Images) Last week the New York Jets opened the 2026 season on the road with a thorough thrashing of the Tennessee Titans. Breece Hall rushed for more than 100 yards as the Jets offensive line dominated. Special teams, other than a Jason Sanders shanked kick, were outstanding. It was a complete win in all phases of the game. Join Gang Green Nation on game day! Stay on top of every Jets update and debate every snap with other diehard fans. Game-day discussion is smoother in the SB Nation app. Fewer ads Jump easily between conversations Faster commenting and posting Download on iOS or Android . Now things get tougher. The Jets were fortunate to open the 2026 season against a Titans team that is expected to be one of the worst teams in the NFL this season. Today they up the ante against a Packers team that is expected to challenge for a playoff spot, as usual. The Packers opened the 2026 season with a thud. They were beaten by the Minnesota Vikings, 39 – 22. It was an odd game, as the Packers seemed in control much of the game. More than halfway through the fourth quarter the Packers led 22 – 17, only to collapse over the last seven minutes of the game. The Vikings closed with 22 unanswered points as the Packers offense unraveled under intense pressure from the Vikings defense. The Vikings blitzed Packers quarterback Jordan Love relentlessly (70+ % of passing downs!), eventually leading to game changing sacks and turnovers that turned what looked like a comfortable Packers win into a double digit Packers loss. The Packers’ 419 total yards on offense nearly doubled the Vikings’ 239 yards offensive output, but the Vikings won the only battle that counts, the final score. The Jets will hope to duplicate the pressure the Vikings got on Jordan Love, though the Jets defensive scheme and personnel make that somewhat difficult. This game will likely be a much more formidable challenge for the Jets than the Titans were last week. Jordan Love is no Cam Ward, and the Packers have multiple weapons in the passing game that have the potential to give a suspect Jets secondary fits. The Jets are not without hope, however. A strong Jets running game could keep the Packers offense off the field, and a weak Packers offensive line and running game may open up opportunities for the Jets front seven to pressure Jordan Love and create some turnovers. If Geno Smith can manage another mistake free game perhaps the Jets can get to 2-0 on the season for the first time since 2015. Wouldn’t that be nice? It’s the Jets and the Packers in game 2 of the 2026 season. Enjoy the game everyone.

title: Eagles News: “Sean Mannion took a big step forward this week”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Music City Magic – Iggles Blitz I thought Sean Mannion took a big step forward this week. The Eagles gained 341 yards and had 23 first downs (only had 10 last week). There are still things to work on, like getting […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 04: Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion looks on during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 4th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Center in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Music City Magic – Iggles Blitz I thought Sean Mannion took a big step forward this week. The Eagles gained 341 yards and had 23 first downs (only had 10 last week). There are still things to work on, like getting rid of the passes to Makai Lemon behind the line of scrimmage. But overall Mannion did a good job. The run game was more creative. We saw Hollywood Brown on a couple of end around plays. And Mannion made a nice adjustment on the winning TD. Judging the biggest overreactions to NFL Week 2 games – ESPN Sure, Hurts was pressured a lot, but he was awesome Sunday when pressured. He was 11-for-20 for 137 yards and two touchdowns, including the winning TD in the final seconds. Saquon Barkley left this game early with an injury, and although he came back briefly in the second half, he wasn’t able to finish the contest. That surely emboldened the Titans’ pressure plan. I get that it doesn’t look great or smooth. But it’s Week 2, and the Eagles are 2-0 while they’re putting things together. Two of the big questions coming into this season were whether Hurts could thrive with all the change that was made around him and whether DeVonta Smith could fill the No. 1 receiver role with A.J. Brown traded to New England. Well, Hurts was heroic in leading the comeback, and Smith caught 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown. There are a lot of offenses with a lot less hope than the Eagles deserve to have in theirs right now. Eagles vs. Titans: 7 winners, 5 losers, 5 IDKs – BGN If you didn’t watch the game and only looked at the box score, you might think Hurts had a relatively pedestrian day at the office: 26/37 (70.3 completion), 264 yards (7.1 average), 2 TD, 2 INT, 85.9 passer rating … 5 carries, 16 rushing yards. But such a sentiment couldn’t be further from the case. Hurts was a huge reason why the Eagles won this game. Let’s start at the end. The Eagles were down three points at their own 35-yard line with 1:56 on the clock and zero timeouts to work with. Hurts led a nine-play, 65-yard drive where he accounted for all of those yards (61 passing, four rushing) and the game-winning touchdown pass. His only two incompletions were a short drop by Dontayvion Wicks and a throwaway to avoid a sack with pressure quickly reaching him. Hurts delivered in the clutch. It was a well-deserved ending for him, too, since he was tasked with carrying the offense for most of the game. The Eagles did Hurts no favors by insisting on sticking with an ineffective running game on early downs … which forced the offense into way too many third-and-longs. Hurts made some really good throws in those situations to sustain drives. Eagles 24 Titans 20 quick recap – Music City Miracles There are no moral victories in the NFL, but the Tennessee Titans, as a team, have a lot to be proud of even in the 24-20 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. After the way they played last week, I was 100% sure they were going to lose by 3 touchdowns. They fought all the way to the finish today. There is still a lot of stuff to clean up. The defense was on the field the entire first half. They have to find a way to get off the field. To their credit, they were much better in the second half. They also picked Jalen Hurts off twice in the loss. They still need more from the offense. Part of the reason the defense was on the field so much in the first half was because the offense couldn’t sustain a drive. Eagles-Titans Postgame: Eagles 2-0, Jalen Hurts Delivers Game-Winning TD To Darius Cooper – PHLY Eagles Super Bowl champion Vinny Curry is with us to break down Jalen Hurts’ game-winning drive that delivered the Eagles a 24-20 win and included two spectacular DeVonta Smith catches. We break down a wild game that included two interceptions by Jalen Hurts, injuries to Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert, and some weird football. No matter, the Eagles escaped to stay undefeated. Miles Johnston, Brandon Lee Gowton and Bo Wulf join Curry, with insight from EJ Smith from the Eagles locker room and Fran Duffy on the plays you need to know. Eagles and Titans players had their cleats melting in 157-degree heat – SB Nation Not only did players see their cleats physically melting on the field, but the heat caused the composition of the cleats to change, with Jordan Mailata saying that he rolled his ankle twice on Sunday — and believed it could have been caused by the plastic of his cleats becoming soft due to the heat. Conditions were so extreme that Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni got an IV at halftime to prevent dehydration, which came from just standing on the surface for 90 minutes. Players struggled to keep cool, and it’s raising more questions about player safety due to weather-related events, especially as it pertains to playing surfaces. Given the chance to mask Eagles’ offensive woes, Jalen Hurts ‘didn’t flinch’ in clutch time vs. the Titans – PHLY Eagles He found Dontayvion Wicks for a 20-yard completion with the Eagles facing third-and-6 near midfield and hit DeVonta Smith, who pulled off two acrobatic catches on the final drive, for a 19 yard completion facing the same down and distance a few plays later. And with the Eagles facing first-and-goal from the three-yard line, Hurts rolled to his right and found Darius Cooper wide open in the middle of the end zone to secure the decisive lead. “That motherfucker balled out today,” Eagles left tackle Jordan Mailata said. “Jalen really got in his bag today and just started dialing everything up and hitting everyone.” Handing out 10 awards from the Eagles-Titans game – PhillyVoice 4) The ‘Dirty Work’ Award 🧹🧽: Darius Cooper. Being the dirty work receiver is hard. You play special teams and when you get in the game on offense you’re usually just blocking or running pick plays for the star players. And yet, when you get your opportunities, you sure as hell better be ready because you’re not going to get many of them. Cooper had two catches for 26 yards, and the game-winning TD. 2026 NFL season, Week 2: What We Learned from Sunday’s games – NFL.com Hurts comes in clutch after tough outing. It wasn’t the best day at the office for Jalen Hurts, but when met with a deadline — needing to lead a game-winning drive with 1:56 remaining — the Super Bowl LIX Most Valuable Player delivered. Hurts, who threw a bad interception in the end zone during his first possession and another pick during the drive immediately preceding his last, led Philly on a nine-play, 65-yard drive to take the lead and the win from the Titans. He did so by becoming laser-focused on DeVonta Smith, throwing to the Eagles’ No. 1 wide receiver on four of eight passes, including a pretty 19-yard gain on third-and-6 to set up Philadelphia at the goal line. On the next play, he hit Darius Cooper for the wideout’s first career touchdown to propel the Eagles to a surprisingly difficult win. He wasn’t nearly perfect Sunday, going 26 of 37 for 264 yards, two touchdowns and the two picks, but he was clutch as ever when called upon to leave Titans fans with some achy, breaky hearts. The Eagles need Jalen Hurts 2.0 now more than ever. His evolution and clutch gene are carrying a rough offense. – Inquirer But there was something unique about Hurts carrying the offense at the scorching Nissan Stadium on Sunday. He’s strapped the Eagles on his back before. He’s had better games against better opponents when the stakes were much higher. He’s been clutch on many previous occasions. No, this was a different Hurts. This was the 2.0 version. This was Hurts evolving as a quarterback in a new scheme that gives him more freedom as a…

title: Eagles-Titans Takeaway: Jalen Hurts can handle the heat
summary: They wanted to make Jalen Hurts beat them as a quarterback. That’s what Tennessee star defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons (who was a monster on Sunday) said about the Eagles’ star QB ahead of the Birds’ come-from-behind 24-20 win on Sunday that was orchestrated by Hurts’ arm and, in no small measure, a wonderful game by […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks to pass the ball against the Tennessee Titans during the second half of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images They wanted to make Jalen Hurts beat them as a quarterback. That’s what Tennessee star defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons (who was a monster on Sunday) said about the Eagles’ star QB ahead of the Birds’ come-from-behind 24-20 win on Sunday that was orchestrated by Hurts’ arm and, in no small measure, a wonderful game by a wide receiver corps filled with question marks. The plan was simple: keep Hurts in the pocket and, as Simmons said, “make Jalen Hurts be a QB.” Hurts was not perfect. He almost never is. He threw two interceptions, one of which was almost returned for a 90+ yard pick-six and the other late in the fourth quarter as he was hit while he was throwing. They were uncharacteristic of him, but in the new Sean Mannion offense, we may have to get used to things like this. But for most of the game and, most importantly, in their final drive, Hurts was masterful. He was 26-for-37 passing with 264 yards and two touchdowns and, with under two minutes remaining and trailing 20-17, went 6-for-8 on a 65-yard drive that culminated in 3-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper with 9 seconds left. View this post on Instagram It was not an easy game. The Titans were fired up and the Eagles had never won a game in Tennessee since the Houston Oilers moved to Nissan Stadium in 1999. It was also about 357 degrees Farenheit on the field. Players’ cleats were melting. Hurts also had to deal with an offensive line that is still finding its footing in the new Mannion scheme. He was under pressure for much of the day, yet managed to pass his way through it. Jalen Hurts' passing chart vs. the Titans. Per @NextGenStats , Hurts was pressured 17 times on his dropbacks, including 14 of them vs. four-man rushes (three sacks too). Hurts completed a career-high 18 passes on 28 attempts and both TD throws that took longer than 2.5 seconds to… pic.twitter.com/8wWwQjnyDd — Devin Jackson (@RealD_Jackson) September 20, 2026 With Landon Dickerson out, the Eagles moved Cam Jurgens from center to left guard and started Drew Kendall at center. That didn’t seem to work out too well. The running game provided little support, averaging 2.8 yards per attempt. Saquon Barkley missed almost the entire first half with a stinger and finished with just 9 yards on 4 attempts. Tank Bigsby scored a touchdown on the ground but managed just 33 yards on 13 carries. Will Shipley added 24 yards on 7 carries. So, it was all on Hurts. Hurts threw over the middle of the field more, threading the needle in some cases and layering passes over linebackers in others. There were times he took too long to get rid of the ball, but also seemed more inclined to let it rip than in seasons past. He was also aided by his top two veteran wide receivers, as well as a second-year training camp star. DeVonta Smith showed why everyone was excited for him to take over as WR1. He hauled in 10 of his 13 targets for 117 yards and a touchdown, making several acrobatic catches in traffic along the way. Especially clutch was his last catch of the day on the final drive. View this post on Instagram One of the more important developments early in the season is the play of Dontayvion Wicks, who is emerging as a more-than viable No. 2. He caught 5 of his 6 targets for 74 yards, including a 27-yarder that helped get the Eagles’ offense moving early. And while Cooper did not pile up big stats on Sunday, he did come up with the biggest catch of the day in the game’s final seconds, and even Makai Lemon showed up with a clutch 14-yard catch. Hurts completed passes to nine different players, an offensive coordinator’s dream. Hurts will never be confused with Joe Montana, but he is proving to be one of the most adaptable QBs in franchise history. It’s only been two games, and we haven’t truly seen Mannion’s offense “work” yet. The running game needs to be functional in order for that to happen. In the meantime, Hurts is doing more than enough inside the system and, improvisationally, to win. Yes, it feels a lot like last year still. It seems unlikely the Eagles are going be blowing people out this year, at least not yet. In the meantime, Hurts is showing that, after an off-season of uncertainty, he can handle the heat.
author: John Stolnis

title: Eagles vs. Titans: 7 winners, 5 losers, 5 IDKs
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-0 after beating the Tennessee Titans. The Birds losing this game would’ve been pretty unserious behavior. Even their own supporters didn’t think they stood a chance ahead of this matchup. The Eagles entered this tilt as seven-point road favorites against a team that looked listless in Week 1 …. while playing […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Tank Bigsby #8 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Tennessee Titans with Jalen Hurts #1 during the first quarter of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-0 after beating the Tennessee Titans. The Birds losing this game would’ve been pretty unserious behavior. Even their own supporters didn’t think they stood a chance ahead of this matchup . The Eagles entered this tilt as seven-point road favorites against a team that looked listless in Week 1 …. while playing in a stadium mostly filled by Philly fans. And this team sure did flirt with disaster! After mostly controlling the game, the Eagles’ win probability dipped as low as 21.6% with the Titans kicking a field goal to take a late lead. Visual form via ESPN: But then the Eagles went on a game-winning touchdown drive to prevent a frustrating loss. That was fun to watch! Time to hand out winners, losers, and I don’t knows. For even more analysis, check out my appearance on the PHLY Eagles postgame show along with Vinny Curry, Bo Wulf, Miles Johnson, Fran Duffy, and EJ Smith! WINNERS JALEN HURTS If you didn’t watch the game and only looked at the box score, you might think Hurts had a relatively pedestrian day at the office: 26/37 (70.3 completion), 264 yards (7.1 average), 2 TD, 2 INT, 85.9 passer rating … 5 carries, 16 rushing yards. But such a sentiment couldn’t be further from the case. Hurts was a huge reason why the Eagles won this game. Let’s start at the end. The Eagles were down three points at their own 35-yard line with 1:56 on the clock and zero timeouts to work with. Hurts led a nine-play, 65-yard drive where he accounted for all of those yards (61 passing, four rushing) and the game-winning touchdown pass. His only two incompletions were a short drop by Dontayvion Wicks and a throwaway to avoid a sack with pressure quickly reaching him. Hurts delivered in the clutch. It was a well-deserved ending for him, too, since he was tasked with carrying the offense for most of the game. The Eagles did Hurts no favors by insisting on sticking with an ineffective running game on early downs … which forced the offense into way too many third-and-longs. Hurts made some really good throws in those situations to sustain drives. Hurts obviously wasn’t perfect on Sunday. He did throw two picks, the first of which ended up being at least a 1o-point swing in this game. It wasn’t easy to see what he was looking at on that play since, even if a defender didn’t jump the route to make the interception, he was throwing to a tightly covered DeVonta Smith in the end zone. The second one wasn’t just about Hurts getting hit by Jeffery Simmons as he threw. It was also about a perplexing sequence where the Eagles went from 2nd-and-7 at the plus 39-yard line to 3rd-and-12 after the call was for Hurts to throw backwards to Makai Lemon, who got blown up for a five-yard loss. The good way outweighed the bad on Sunday. And Hurts had success despite missing Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert for most of the game in addition to dealing with substandard offensive line play. It’s hard not to be encouraged about Hurts’ outlook after the first two games of the season. Jalen Hurts has eight fourth-quarter comebacks since 2023. That's tied for the second-most in the NFL during that span. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) September 21, 2026 The only two quarterbacks in NFL history to start their careers with six consecutive wins in road openers: Jalen Hurts Roger Staubach (Elias Sports) — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) September 20, 2026 Jalen Hurts passed Carson Wentz in all-time Eagles completions today. 1) Donovan McNabb: 2,801 2) Ron Jaworski: 2,088 3) Randall Cunningham: 1,874 4) Jalen Hurts: 1,582 5) Carson Wentz: 1,562 — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) September 21, 2026 DEVONTA SMITH Smitty was targeted 13 times on Sunday. He logged 10 receptions for 117 yards and one touchdown. While Hurts deserves a ton of credit for leading the Eagles on a game-winning touchdown drive, he couldn’t have done it without his No. 1 receiver. Smith produced 38 yards on the Eagles’ final drive, including a 19-yard grab along the left sideline to get out of bounds while converting a 3rd-and-6 to set up goal-to-go from the 3-yard line. Really good football player. Also, one of DeVonta’s best plays in this game didn’t even count. He Mossed a Titans defender just out of the end zone on a Hurts throw that didn’t allow the receiver enough room to get two feet in bounds. DeVonta Smith had the sixth-highest fantasy points performance of his career against the Titans. His 13 targets produced 10 receptions, 117 yards (11.7 avg), and 1 TD for the Eagles. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) September 21, 2026 DONTAYVION WICKS I repeat: the Eagles only had to give up a 2026 fifth-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick in the deal with the Green Bay Packers to acquire Wicks. Early on, it’s looking like a bargain. Wicks was extremely efficient in this game, seeing six targets for five catches and 74 yards. And all of those grabs came on either third or fourth downs! First catch: 27-yard gain on 3rd-and-12 Second catch: 7-yard gain on 3rd-and-4 Third catch: 5-yard gain on 4th-and-2 Fourth catch: 15-yard gain on 3rd-and-12 Fifth catch: 20-yard gain on 3rd-and-6 Wicks is looking like a real nice WR2 to DeVonta’s WR1. And Howie Roseman is looking smart to have signed him to a one-year contract extension through 2027 as opposed to just letting him play out his rookie contract this year. Dontayvion Wicks was money for the Eagles against the Titans in high-leverage situations. His five receptions for 74 receiving yards all came on either third or fourth down. Generated the fifth-most EPA of any NFL receiver in a game over the last two seasons. — Brandon Lee Gowton (@BrandonGowton) September 21, 2026 DARIUS COOPER Couldn’t be happier for my guy. Pretty cool that his first career touchdown was a game-winner. And while he was left open, it wasn’t like it was a gimme catch. DC had to go up and get the ball while also making sure to stay in bounds: Couldn’t wait until tomorrow for this one pic.twitter.com/XFMhhsEppq — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) September 21, 2026 It wasn’t just the touchdown. Cooper also had the second-longest reception of the game with a 23-yard catch-and-run. He could’ve had another grab had Hurts not put the ball just a little too far out in front of him at one point. I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again: good things happen when Hurts throws the ball to Cooper. The Eagles did themselves a disservice to not even get him a single target in Week 1, though it obviously worked out in terms of winning that game. But Cooper deserves a role in this offense. Darius Cooper told me he was supposed to set a pick for DeVonta Smith on the game winning touchdown, but DeVonta fell down and the Tennessee defenders did not cover Darius so he was wide open. Eagles teammates were thrilled for Darius that he was rewarded for all the dirty work… — John Clark (@JClarkNBCS) September 20, 2026 DeVonta Smith said he had a great view of Darius Cooper's game-winning catch from the turf after he fell down. "I was on the ground just looking up like, ‘Why is the ball floating so high? Is it going out of bounds?’ And then he just came out of nowhere." — Dave Zangaro (@DZangaroNBCS) September 21, 2026 Time well spent https://t.co/Wib7ctaFmP pic.twitter.com/iMaQ3AiyFs — PHLY Sports (@PHLY_Sports) September 20, 2026 JAKE ELLIOTT Jake Elliott’s 58-yard field goal make was a big kick. Good to see him hit from distance like that after his struggles from 50+ in recent seasons. Including training camp practices (28/31), preseason games (7/7), and the 2026 regular season thus far (8/8), Elliott is 43/46. It continues to look like he’s bouncing back from two down seasons. NOLAN…

title: Jalen Hurts to Jeffery Simmons: “You started that sh*t, I had to finish it”
summary: Early last week, Titans star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons made comments about forcing Jalen Hurts to be a quarterback in their Week 2 matchup, insinuating they could beat the Eagles if they made the offense rely on the passing game. Jordan Mailata wouldn’t entertain the comments when asked about it days later, and Nolan Smith […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles passes the ball against the Tennessee Titans during the second half of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Early last week, Titans star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons made comments about forcing Jalen Hurts to be a quarterback in their Week 2 matchup, insinuating they could beat the Eagles if they made the offense rely on the passing game. Jordan Mailata wouldn’t entertain the comments when asked about it days later, and Nolan Smith expressed his disinterest in similar tactics and instead complimented Tennessee QB Cam Ward. All of this culminated in Jalen Hurts leading the Eagles on a nine-play, game-winning drive late in the game on Sunday afternoon, and Simmons and Hurts having a moment on the field post-game. The Eagles QB was in the middle of an interview when Simmons came over to show respect, and thankfully Kristina Pink of FOX Sports inched the mic closer to the pair so we could hear the exchange. Hurts was sure to let Simmons know, “You started that shit, I had to finish it.” And with that, the QB went back to finish his interview. A dramatic road victory for Philadelphia 🦅 @JalenHurts caught up with our @Kristina_Pink after the @Eagles completed the comeback in the final seconds pic.twitter.com/OGCnBKXUnT — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 20, 2026 Hurts finished the game 26-of-37 for 264 yards and two touchdowns. The quarterback did throw two interceptions, but overall, had a really impressive performance considering Saquon Barkley was in and out of the game , Dallas Goedert was sidelined in the first half , and they were dealing with a new combination up front . After the game, Simmons tried to clarify his comments from earlier in the week, and walk back the intent behind them. He explained that he meant no disrespect to the former Super Bowl MVP, and only meant that keeping Hurts from being able to escape the pocket and use his legs would be their best chance to win. #Titans Jeffery Simmons explained what he meant by saying make Jalen Hurts play QB: He's a Super Bowl MVP. That wasn't a shot at Jalen. The thing was if we can keep him contained in the pocket and eliminate him from making plays running, we'd have a chance at being successful. pic.twitter.com/za5mB0kOtB — TURRON DAVENPORT (@TDavenport_NFL) September 20, 2026 Whether he intended to disrespect Hurts or not, the QB made it clear in his post-game press conference that he heard Simmons’ comments.

title: NFL Week 3 odds: Eagles open as road favorites against Bears
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-0 after narrowly beating the Washington Commanders and Tennessee Titans. But now the Birds will face their toughest test of the 2026 season in Week 3. Or will they? It’s hard to know what to make of the Chicago Bears right now. Ben Johnson’s squad looked like an absolute juggernaut in […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 28: (L-R) Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles congratulates head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears after the game at Lincoln Financial Field on November 28, 2025 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-0 after narrowly beating the Washington Commanders and Tennessee Titans. But now the Birds will face their toughest test of the 2026 season in Week 3. Or will they? It’s hard to know what to make of the Chicago Bears right now. Ben Johnson’s squad looked like an absolute juggernaut in Week 1, dropping 59 points on the Carolina Panthers. But then they only scored three points during a home loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2 … in a game where Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring injury . The Eagles are currently listed as 3.5-point road favorites against the Bears, according to FanDuel. One would imagine the Eagles would be underdogs if Williams was a sure bet to suit up for this Monday Night Football matchup. If Williams can’t play, the Bears will be rolling with Tyson Bagent. The fourth-year signal caller hasn’t played much over the past two seasons after logging four starts as an undrafted rookie in 2023. He went 2-2 in those games with three passing touchdowns to six interceptions for a 73.0 passer rating. Bagent was active with his legs, logging 23 rushing attempts for 109 yards and two touchdowns. Bagent has earned the Bears’ belief because he’s shined in preseason settings; he’s produced 10 total touchdowns to two interceptions over the past three summers. How much does that matter? Maybe not much since the regular season is an entirely different beast. But there are less inspiring backup options than Bagent. (See: Andy Dalton.) The Eagles are 0-2 against the spread so far this season after failing to cover a 5.5-point home line against the Commanders and a seven-point road line against the Titans. Do you think they’ll beat the Bears comfortably enough to cover in this spot? I feel really good about Jalen Hurts. But I have questions about this Eagles team when it comes to the trenches right now. Their defense could potentially get a boost if Jonathan Greenard is able to return for this game. I lean towards taking the points right now but I reserve the right to change my mind by next Monday. Maybe the Eagles will be out to make a statement after getting embarrassed by this Bears team on Black Friday last year. What say you?
