full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles and Jordan Mailata #68 celebrate after game winning touchdown during the second half of the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jalen Hurts won again. The Eagles should have smoked the lowly Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but they did not. What they did do, however, was win, 24-20 at Nissan Stadium, in Nashville, Tennessee—thanks again to Hurts’ will power. He completed 26 of 37 for 264 yards passing, including two touchdowns, and two interceptions. When pressed, when he had to be the game-changing player some in the past may have questioned, Hurts did what it seems he always tends to do, go into “Jordan mode” and carry the Eagles with a three-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper with nine seconds to play. Hurts completed six of eight on the game-winning drive for 61 yards, including converting a pair of third-and-six plays. What added to Hurts’ accomplishments is that he did it with very little help—again, despite some stumbles of his own, despite missing both Saquon Barkley for much of the first half and tight end Dallas Goedert for the much of the game, on-field turf temperatures that reached 157 degrees by the third quarter and behind a revamped offensive line, which continues to stir more questions than answers heading into Week 3 of the NFL season. Hurts finally solved Titans’ head coach Robert Saleh, though the Eagles’ offensive line struggled mightily against Titans’ game-wrecking defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. It was the first time the Eagles won in Nashville since the Titans moved from Houston in 1997. Hurts also beat a Saleh-led defense for the first time after previously going 0-2 (when Saleh was head coach of the Jets and in last year’s Wild Card playoff loss to San Francisco). There was a lot of good, some bad and some cringing ugly in the Eagles’ 24-20 win over the Tennessee Titans. The Good Jalen Hurts continuing to do the “Jalen Hurts thing,” carrying the Eagles to victory. He threw down the middle again, this time to some mixed results, but what matters to Hurts— the only thing that matters to Hurts —is that the Eagles won and he willed it. He completed 26 of 37 for 264 yards passing, including two touchdowns, and two interceptions. He scrambled to make plays. He was not dragged down by the two mistakes he made. He idolizes Michael Jordan and it’s what Hurts is turning into—the football Jordan, grabbing the game by the scruff of the neck and putting it on him to win. He says he does not listen or pay attention to the “outside noise.” He does. He likes it. He embraces doubt. He would rather hear the negative and flush out the positive, because it pushes him to play like he is right now. Right now, fresh into a new season, there may not be a better clutch performer currently in the NFL than Hurts. The game-winning drive. The Eagles went 65 yards on 9 plays with no timeouts and endured a ton of pressure. Hurts converted two third downs. He did it with poise and the underlying feeling he would win the game. The 19-yard Smith completion between two defenders was the play of the game, DeVonta Smith proving he is a No. 1 receiver. He led the Eagles with 10 catches for 117 yards and a touchdown. He continues to come through each time the Eagles need a big play. On the game-winning drive, Hurts went to Smith four times for 38 yards, including probably the play of the game when he hit Smith for a 19-yard reception on a third-and-six play with 20 seconds left at the Titans’ three. Hurts hit Darius Cooper—while looking for Smith—the next play for the game-winning touchdown. Darius Cooper catching the first touchdown of his career—and making it memorable. Cooper caught two passes on three targets for 26 yards, the most important the game-winning three-yard TD catch with 9 seconds to play. His first catch, down the middle of the field for 23 yards, came on a first-and-17 with less than eight minutes to play. Jake Elliott showing he still has it , nailing what turned out to be a big field goal when he booted a 58-yarder in the third quarter for a 17-10 Eagles’ lead. Third-down efficiency. The Eagles converted 11 of 18 third downs, including 6 of 9 in the first half. Tank Bigsby stepping in for the injured Barkley for 33 yards on 13 carries, including a second-quarter touchdown. Dontayvion Wicks continues to be impressive. He caught a 27-yard pass on a third-and-12 down the middle of the field on the Eagles’ first drive. By halftime, he had four catches for 56 yards, and had a huge 20-yard reception on a third-and-six on the game-winning drive. He finished with five catches for five receptions on six targets for 74 yards. Britain Covey’s 24-yard punt return to begin the Eagles’ first possession. Edge rusher Jalyx Hunt starting the game with a two-yard loss by taking down Tony Pollard on the Titans’ first play of the game at the Tennessee 29. Hunt finished the game with five tackles—all solo, that included three pressures in the first half. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell showing what kind of impact player the Eagles envisioned. The second-year pro made a team-high 10 tackles, six solo, andseemed to be playing with a chip on his shoulders from the major gaffe he made in the season opener against Washington, when he completely losing Antonio Williams for a 33-yard reception on a third-and-14 at the Eagles’ 47 with 12:12 left to play. It led to a Washington touchdown with 9:59 to play. Nolan Smith and Jalen Carter each registering a sack. Carter’s sack could have come at a better time, with 2:32 to play, rushing through the middle and taking down Cam Ward for a 9-yard loss at the Eagles’ 18. Safety Andrew Mukuba making six tackles and improving. He came up to stop Pollard on a second-and-goal at the Eagles’ two before Cam Ward tied the score 17-17 with 57 seconds left in the third quarter. The Bad Left guard Cam Jurgens flagged for holding for the third time in two weeks, this time on a second-and-nine at the Titans’ 12. Fortunately, Hurts hit Smith for a 22-yard touchdown on the next play. The Eagles third quarter offense. For thesecond-straight week, it was deplorable.The Eagles went three-and-out on two of the three drives for a total of five yards of offense and one first down. What was really embarrassing was the last three-and-out, which lasted 50 seconds. The Eagles punted the ball back to Tennessee with 7 seconds left in the third, after the Titans had scored with 57 seconds left in the quarter. In the season opener against Washington, at least they managed 59 yards of offense and one first down. They went three-and-out on their first three drives, and could not do anything until Smith’s 31-yard tip-toe reception down the sideline with two minutes left in the quarter. The Ugly Hurts second interception by cornerback Marcus Harris underthrowing an open Smith down the sideline with 6 minutes to play. Quite honestly, it seemed the Eagles were ripe for an upset. It was Harris’ first career interception. Simmons forced the throw, beating Jurgens thoroughly and getting up in Hurts’ face. He hit Hurts early and caused the underthrow. The Eagles certainly looked finished when Hunt lost outside contain, Moro Ojomo got thrown down, three plays after making a tackle for loss, and safety Marcius Epps took a bad angle as Tyjae Spears went down the left sideline for a 27-yard run—on a third-and-22 play. Plays like that happen all of the time in Pee Wee football. Hurts tossing the first of his two interceptions on a third-and-goal at the Titans’ eight on the Eagles’ opening drive. The interception by safety Amani Hookerwas returned 92 yards to the Eagles’ 10, before rookie first-round draft pick Makai Lemon caught up to him. It led to the Titans’ first touchdown. Hooker jumped the route seeing the ball was going to Smith. Hunt, Zack Baun, and Nolan Smith all missing…

title: Saquon Barkley injury: Eagles running back returns to Titans game
summary: On the very first play of the Eagles’ first offensive drive against the Titans on Sunday, Saquon Barkley was tackled for a loss, and subsequently suffered a stinger. The running back promptly went to the medical tent on the sideline, where he stayed for awhile before running back to the locker room, before being listed […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during warm ups prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images On the very first play of the Eagles’ first offensive drive against the Titans on Sunday, Saquon Barkley was tackled for a loss, and subsequently suffered a stinger. The running back promptly went to the medical tent on the sideline, where he stayed for awhile before running back to the locker room, before being listed as questionable to return. Barkley spent much of the first half on the sideline testing and stretching his neck and shoulder area, but thankfully the RB was able to return to the game after halftime. Unfortunately, Barkley only played through the third quarter, and came back off the field in the fourth. After the game, Barkley said he will get an MRI to see where he stands, but as reporter Cameron Wolfe noted , the RB was able to wear a backpack on his injured shoulder, so that should count for something. Saquon Barkley said he’s alright but will get an MRI, expects to know more later in the week. Barkley was comfortable enough to wear a backpack on his injured left shoulder leaving locker room. Eagles & Barkley said it’s a stinger. He initially returned but didn’t finish game. — Cameron Wolfe (@CameronWolfe) September 20, 2026 While he was out, Tank Bigsby was the Eagles’ primary backup running back and Will Shipley was also mixed in. Philadelphia’s run game already faced some challenges with several moves to the offensive line ahead of the game — including moving Cam Jurgens to left guard to replace Landon Dickerson, who is on IR , and then Drew Kendall at center. Barkley had an uneven performance in Week 1 and was looking forward to having more net-positive runs in his second game of the season. Unfortunately, he recorded just one carry for zero yards before leaving the game, and wasn’t able to do much in his short return back in the second half.

title: Jalen Carter injury scare in Eagles-Titans Week 2 game
summary: With the Eagles and Titans tied at 17 points each with under two minutes left to play, Jalen Carter stepped up on special teams, like he’s done so many times in the past, to try and block the field goal kick. This time, however, instead of getting a hand on the ball, Carter ended up […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter (98) and Tennessee Titans offensive tackle JC Latham (55) got up to the referee during the third quarter at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect With the Eagles and Titans tied at 17 points each with under two minutes left to play, Jalen Carter stepped up on special teams, like he’s done so many times in the past, to try and block the field goal kick. This time, however, instead of getting a hand on the ball, Carter ended up injured and holding his calf. He wasn’t able to put weight on his left leg as he tried to get off the field, but it turns out, it was just cramping. Jalen Carter said he was just cramping at the end of that game. He’s fine. He also said he didn’t feel too hindered by his wrist injury. — Dave Zangaro (@DZangaroNBCS) September 20, 2026 Anything more than a cramp would have been bad news for any number of reasons, including the fact that he’s one of the league’s top defenders, that he’s already been dealing with an injury to his right wrist from Week 1, and he’s incredibly valuable on special teams. Just months after signing a new contract extension making him the highest paid defensive tackle in the league, Carter has dealt with several different injuries, but thankfully this didn’t turn out to be anything else he has to work through. He spent the offseason recovering from procedures on both shoulders, and came back to work in good condition and better shape than last year. The Eagles defense struggled against the Titans, which means that the group definitely will need Carter’s help next week against the Bears — whether or not Caleb Williams is able to play .

title: Eagles-Titans final score: Jalen Hurts leads game-winning touchdown drive
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-0 after beating the Tennessee Titans in Nashville on Sunday! Final score: 24 to 20. It looked like this might be a terrible loss for the Birds. But it was not! Jalen Hurts ultimately led a nine-play, 65-yard game-winning touchdown drive capped off by a throw to Darius Cooper in the […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs with the ball against the Tennessee Titans during the first half of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-0 after beating the Tennessee Titans in Nashville on Sunday! Final score: 24 to 20. It looked like this might be a terrible loss for the Birds. But it was not! Jalen Hurts ultimately led a nine-play, 65-yard game-winning touchdown drive capped off by a throw to Darius Cooper in the end zone to give the Eagles a lead with just seconds remaining. As always, the Eagles have much to improve upon. The defense didn’t look as nearly as good as they should’ve. The offense had some really frustrating stretches. But the Eagles won. And the quarterback delivered when it mattered most. Next up for the Eagles is a road game against the Chicago Bears in Week 3. It’s a Monday Night Football matchup … and Caleb Williams might be in danger of missing it due to injury ? Read on for a recap and stay tuned for BGN’s postgame coverage. Also, be sure to check out the PHLY Eagles postgame show below! Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . FIRST QUARTER The Eagles won the coin toss and elected to defer, per usual, to put the Titans on offense first. Jalyx Hunt opened the game with a TFL on Tony Pollard. Facing 3rd-and-11, Cam Ward’s pass to Carnell Tate went through the receiver’s hands with Andrew Mukuba in position to blow the rookie up. Mukuba put his hands up in fear of getting called for hitting a defenseless receiver … but he held up well and there was no flag. Three-and-out. The Eagles took over at their own 28-yard line after a nice 23-yard punt return by Britain Covey. They immediately ran Saquon Barkley behind Cam Jurgens and the running back was tackled for a loss and banged up on the play. Not great! Facing 3rd-and-12 after a swing pass to Tank Bigsby went nowhere, Dontayvion Wicks got open in a soft spot in the middle of the field and Jalen Hurts hit him for a first down. Good ball. Facing 3rd-and-6, a Will Shipley run brought the Eagles to fourth-and-short. Facing 4th-and-1 (a long one, at that) the Eagles lined up for a tush push and it looked like Hurts got it but there was a flag on the Titans for being offside anyway for a first down. Facing 3rd-and-5, the Eagles lined up with an empty backfield and Hurts hit DeVonta Smith over the middle for a first down. Facing 3rd-and-4 after two Shipley runs, Hurts hit Wicks for another first down. Facing 3rd-and-goal from the 8-yard line after a Hurts designed run went nowhere and Hurts had to throw the ball away after Jeffery Simmons got pressure up the middle, Hurts got picked in the end zone and the Titans nearly had a pick six before Makai Lemon did a nice job of tracking down the receiver from behind to prevent the instant touchdown. Not sure what Hurts was seeing there! Even if another defender didn’t jump the throw, which he did, Hurts’ target (DeVonta) looked to be well-covered. 92-yard return on the interception. Disappointing to end the 15-play, 64-yard drive with zero points. Longest drive Week 1 was 8 plays, 3:57. — Jimmy Kempski (@JimmyKempski) September 20, 2026 The Titans took over at the plus 10-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-goal after the Titans dropped a touchdown pass, Ward spun out of a Hunt sack (gotta finish, Jalyx!) and ran just shy of the end zone. Facing 4th-and-goal, the Titans went with a tush push of their own for a touchdown. Ward was talking trash to Jordan Davis after the score. EAGLES 0, TITANS 7. Terrible pursuit by Jalen Carter on the 3rd down Cam Ward scramble. If Carter keeps hustling he could've made a play. — Jimmy Kempski (@JimmyKempski) September 20, 2026 The Eagles took over at their own 35-yard line. They slowly but surely moved into Titans territory. Facing 3rd-and-8, Hurts had to navigate pressure before finding Makai Lemon for a first down. Nice contested grab by the rookie to end the first quarter. MAKAI LEMON pic.twitter.com/rumONtwBLV — correlation (@nosyone4) September 20, 2026 SECOND QUARTER Bigsby ran hard on back-to-back carries to get the ball into the end zone! Good player who shouldn’t go so underutilized. Only had one touch in Week 1! Nice response by the offense to get a game-tying seven points on an 11-play, 65-yard drive. EAGLES 7, TITANS 7. Cartavious "Tank" Bigsby pic.twitter.com/evxOBcqJBm — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) September 20, 2026 The Titans took over at their own 29-yard line. Facing 3rd-and-1, the Titans easily picked up a first down with a Tony Pollard run. Calvin Ridley knocked the Titans’ offense back with an unnecessary roughness penalty against Marcus Epps. Dumb flag for a veteran player. Facing 3rd-and-16, Ward was pressured into a throwaway. The Titans were flagged for a facemask penalty that would’ve wiped out any kind of positive gain anyway. The Eagles took over at their own 19-yard line. The Eagles got Hollywood Brown involved on a designed touch to the left end for a nine-yard rushing gain. This after he played zero snaps in Week 1. Hurts hit DeVonta along the right sideline for a first down. Facing 3rd-and-9, Hurts took off running up the middle and slid shy of the marker. Facing 4th-and-3, Nick Sirianni kept the offense on the field … and took a timeout after the offense couldn’t draw the defense offside. Facing 4th-and-3 again, Wicks got WIDE open and Hurts hit him for an easy first down. Good design/call from Sean Mannion there. Also good by Sirianni to go for it. Facing 3rd-and-4, Hurts picked up a first down on a designed run to the right edge … and the Titans were also flagged for illegal hands to the face for another five yards. Facing 3rd-and-12, Hurts stood in the pocket against pressure bearing down on him and delivered a ball to Wicks for yet another first down. Wicks is a player. Also, kudos to Hurts for continuing to carry the offense on third-and-long. Facing 2nd-and-19 after a holding penalty on Cam Jurgens (his third holding flag this season), Hurts stepped right to avoid pressure and found DeVonta in the end zone for a touchdown! Again, Hurts is carrying the offense. EAGLES 14, TITANS 7. 3rd & Dontayvion Wicks pic.twitter.com/scZ9K0E79P — PHLY Eagles (@PHLY_Eagles) September 20, 2026 Floating it to 6️⃣ for 6️⃣ pic.twitter.com/0yR7DgLNE1 — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) September 20, 2026 Does Jeffrey Simmons still want to make Jalen Hurts be a quarterback today? Facing 3rd-and-13 after Nolan Smith sacked Ward (who tried to step up against the Eagles’ pressure), the Titans ripped off back-to-back explosive completions to move into the red zone (bad open field missed tackle by Zack Baun on a Tyjae Spears catch-and-run). What the hell, defense? Ward only had eight passing yards before two straight completions for 55 yards. Facing 3rd-and-14, Brian Daboll went with a coward’s draw. Lol, the Eagles gladly accepted that gift. The Titans’ 37-yard field goal attempt was good to end the first half. EAGLES 14, TITANS 10. Early down run game still the…

title: The morning after: Steelers need to make sweeping offensive line changes
summary: Sometimes when you add new people to new roles, it ends up working seamlessly. There is no layover of production, there is no adjustment period, it’s just full steam ahead and a big success that leaves everyone looking smarter because of it. Other times, you’re the Pittsburgh Steelers offensive line. Pittsburgh’s front five have been […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 23: Spencer Anderson #74 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 23, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sometimes when you add new people to new roles, it ends up working seamlessly. There is no layover of production, there is no adjustment period, it’s just full steam ahead and a big success that leaves everyone looking smarter because of it. Other times, you’re the Pittsburgh Steelers offensive line. Pittsburgh’s front five have been largely abysmal through two weeks, but Week 2 in their 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots was especially bad. If you spent the afternoon screaming at your TV about how bad Spencer Anderson was playing, your eyes certainly weren’t deceiving you. Anderson allowed seven pressures from the right guard position, which was the most of any right guard in the NFL, per Sumer Sports . No other player at his position allowed more than four pressures in Week 2, and he is currently third in the NFL in pressures allowed through the first two weeks. Zach Frazier was also credited with five pressures – and you know it’s a bad day when even Frazier is getting beat. However, how much of that can be credited with having Anderson next to him? I’d say that’s certainly not a small factor. Right tackle Dylan Cook hasn’t been any better, allowing six pressures through two games. Additionally, the Steelers cannot run to the right side. After two games, Rico Dowdle has just 13 rushing yards on seven carries when running to the right side – good for the fifth worst EPA per rush to that side in the NFL (min. 10 touches). Jaylen Warren has been slightly better, but he only has 37 yards on seven carries to the right side. The Steelers’ running backs also haven’t been able to get to the second level before getting hit by defenders. Through two weeks, Warren and Dowdle have a combined eight yards before contact on runs. EIGHT! That is comfortably the worst mark in the NFL. The Steelers’ plan at offensive line entering the season was one that left many skeptical and we’re now seeing why. They moved their rising star right tackle and quality right guard to the left side for precisely no reason, moved the former practice squad fill-in to right tackle after he played well at left tackle, and didn’t find a suitable replacement for Isaac Seumalo. All of these moving parts have led to a very discombobulated unit that can’t block its way out of a wet bag, and it’s destroying the offense. Under the previous regime, this would be a leak in the boat that wouldn’t get fixed for weeks on end. If Mike McCarthy wants to show that things truly will be different, he’ll ensure that both Anderson and Cook don’t start in Week 3. It’s the morning after game day, and your concerns are absolutely justified. Germie Bernard arrives There were very few aspects of Week 2 that could be considered good for the Steelers, but one of those things was the play of Germie Bernard. Entering Week 2, his counterpoint, Roman Wilson, had just one career game where he had four or more receptions – Bernard accomplished that feat in his second game. Aaron Rodgers found him three times on one drive that looked poised to end in points, but then the 3rd-and-7 sack happened and knocked the Steelers out of field goal range. Bernard did have a blunder at the end of the game that saw a ball bounce off his chest for an interception, but the game was already decided. We need to see more of No. 17 on the field going forward. Defense continues strong play Through two games, the Steelers’ defense has been great. They’ve allowed 26 points, taken the ball away four times, and lead the NFL in defensive EPA. per play. They comfortably have the best pass defense in the league from an efficiency standpoint, allowing -0.5 EPA per pass, and they are third in defensive pass success rate. T.J. Watt has 3.5 sacks – he had seven all of last season, and currently sits at No. 2 in the NFL behind only Greg Rousseau of the Buffalo Bills. Additionally, of all edge rushers with at least 25 snaps, Watt and Alex Highsmith are No. 1 and No. 2 in the NFL in sack percentage. The defense is more than holding up its end of the bargain, and Patrick Graham has already proven to be a massive improvement over Teryl Austin. The offense is holding back any potential of Pittsburgh being a real competitor. If they can fix it and become just a mediocre offense, they can win games. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots
summary: After an ugly but at times promising season-opening win over the Atlanta Falcons, any Steelers’ momentum ground to a screeching halt after a 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots on the road in Week 2. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. The Steelers need an offensive line fix You […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - SEPTEMBER 20: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks to pass the ball against the New England Patriots during the second quarter of the game at Gillette Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images After an ugly but at times promising season-opening win over the Atlanta Falcons, any Steelers’ momentum ground to a screeching halt after a 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots on the road in Week 2. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. The Steelers need an offensive line fix You could fill this entire article just writing about the shortcomings of any one Steelers offensive unit, but the offensive line might’ve been the most frustrating to watch on Sunday. Aaron Rodgers was sacked four times and pressured on a whopping 17 snaps, according to Patriots.com, with the Steelers averaging just 3.5 yards per play for the game. Rodgers was constantly under siege in the pocket, and once again, there wasn’t a ton of room to work with in the running game. It’s a tired line at this point: Pittsburgh has invested copious resources into its offensive line under the Omar Khan regime, and yet the results are looking as depressing as always. But the fairer way to look at things is that the right side of the line — which has clearly been the weak link through two weeks — does not contain any long-term starters with first-rounder Max Iheanachor and third-rounder Gennings Dunker still on the bench. And the left side of the line, which started on the right last year, still hasn’t settled. Of course, the Steelers had an entire offseason to prepare for those changes. If they’re a victim, it’s of their own plan. Pairing a young offensive line still clearly undergoing growing pains with a veteran, less-mobile quarterback was certainly a choice. But although some of Troy Fautanu and Mason McCormick’s struggles have been of the more surprising variety, easier fixes could exist for the right side. After rough performances from Dylan Cook and Spencer Anderson against New England, could it be time to look for Iheanachor to start at tackle and veteran backup Brock Hoffman (16 career starts) to get the nod at guard? (Dunker’s inactive status through two weeks tells me he’s not as pro-ready as many believe). All that to say: Yes, the offensive line was bad on Sunday. Yes, it’s a big concern moving forward. No, it’s not a finished product yet. 2. Explosives remain missing on offense Head coach Mike McCarthy said the Steelers were struggling with the “basics” on Sunday. Anyone who watched the game would agree. But his comments later in the press conference provided what I thought was a more insightful detail on why the Steelers’ offense so often looks to be lagging behind the rest of the NFL: a lack of explosive plays. “I don’t want to dink and dunk,” McCarthy said. “There’s a place for that maybe situationally, but that’s not the philosophy — we have to attempt to get the ball thrown downfield.” The broadcast showed an interesting statistic midway through the fourth quarter when the game was already out of reach: The Patriots had managed six offensive plays of 20 or more yards; the Steelers had zero. The New England offense actually struggled for the most part against the Steelers. Those explosive plays were the difference, whether it was TreVeyon Henderson’s 39-yard touchdown, Rhamondre Stevenson’s 24-yard run, or Romeo Doubs sneaking behind the Pittsburgh secondary for a 63-yard gain. The Steelers, meanwhile, had a long of 14 yards on the ground. Only one reception went past 20 yards by the time the clock hit zeroes — a 26-yard catch and run from Jaylen Warren late in the game when the score was already 20-3. NFL defenses are good. It’s unrealistic to expect any offense to score on every drive, or even consistently get a handful of first downs every possession. But defenses aren’t perfect, either, and offenses need to be able to take advantage of the open holes and creases when they become available. Pittsburgh is startlingly bad at achieving that. Nowhere is that more apparent than in the game of WR1 DK Metcalf, who had another Sunday of maddening inconsistencies. He recorded several drops, but even when the team did succeed in giving the blazing-fast, 6’4 target the ball, he couldn’t do much to push the ball forward, finishing with a stat line of four catches for 27 yards on nine targets. And Jaylen Warren, who has been the Steelers’ only consistent creator of chunk plays through two games, has averaged just 14 touches a week to start the season. Meanwhile, Rico Dowdle has averaged just 2.5 yards per carry over that same span. The Steelers do have some talent issues on offense — most analysts have been worrying about the lack of explosiveness all offseason — but the Steelers could be doing a better job of maximizing the talent they have, as well. 3. At least the pass rush is still good If you still want something Steelers-related to feel good about entering this week, the pass rush has been about as good as you could hope for them to be through two games. Against the Patriots, T.J. Watt notched another 1.5 sacks. Alex Highsmith also added another to his season total. And Nick Herbig recorded three tackles for loss — including a play where he perfectly read and blew up a wide receiver screen — as well as a forced fumble. FUMBLE! Nick Herbig punched the ball away from Rhamondre Stevenson. Looked like Payton Wilson came out of the pile with it. pic.twitter.com/S3y8a3bDnp https://t.co/n6nYDyRRwp — Alan Saunders (@ASaunders_PGH) September 20, 2026 The Steelers were able to generate consistent pressure against Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, holding him to just 208 yards, no touchdowns and an interception. Cam Heyward, to the surprise of no one, logged another batted pass at the line of scrimmage. Subtracting New England’s defensive score, the Steelers defense gave up just 13 points on Sunday. Yes, they’ve had some busts and given up more chunk plays than you’d want, but over two weeks Pittsburgh has only allowed two touchdowns and 26 points in total. Tougher opponents will come, but overall the Pittsburgh defense looks like a much improved unit from last year. The problem, of course, is that the same can’t be said of the offense. 4. The season is a roller coaster Sure, there were doom and gloomers following the Steelers’ somewhat ugly season-opening win over the Atlanta Falcons, but there were plenty of hopeful takeaways as well: A win! A new-look offense and defense! And Aaron Rodgers looking the best he had in a while, to name a few. And all it took was one painful game the next week to undo all of that optimism. But although I haven’t watched a Mike McCarthy Steelers team before, I have watched plenty of past Steelers teams, and for better or worse, this looks all too familiar. There are always some exceptionally ugly games sprinkled throughout the season, with final results that have the internet worrying that Pittsburgh has never lost this badly before. Enough of those games occurred over the last several seasons of Mike Tomlin’s tenure that it became an actual problem. But McCarthy? This is game No. 2. It’s more than fair to be critical of just how poorly the Steelers played on Sunday. But it’s still far too early to overreact. I promise: Pittsburgh will win some more games this year. 5. Odds and ends My “don’t panic” points aside, Mike McCarthy did seem unusually downtrodden in his postgame press conference. I’m curious to see how the team rebounds from losses such as Sunday’s under the new coaching staff. One of T.J. Watt’s sacks came on a power rush — a nice changeup from his usually speed- and effort-based approach. title: DK Metcalf has one of the worst contracts in the NFL
summary: If you’re reading this, you have the same amount of games with more than 50 receiving yards this season than Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf. The only difference being is that I assume you aren’t making $33 million per yer. The Steelers acquired Metcalf last March in a trade with the Seattle Seahawks. He […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - SEPTEMBER 20: DK Metcalf #4 of the Pittsburgh Steelers walks off the field for halftime during the game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you’re reading this, you have the same amount of games with more than 50 receiving yards this season than Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf. The only difference being is that I assume you aren’t making $33 million per yer. The Steelers acquired Metcalf last March in a trade with the Seattle Seahawks. He was given a four-year, $132 million extension shortly after being acquired, and through a full 17 games played, he hasn’t come close to living up to that lofty price tag. In 17 games as a Steeler, Metcalf has caught 67 passes for 917 yards and six touchdowns. In 2025, he ranked 47th in EPA per target, per Sumer Sports . Entering Week 2, he ranked 57th dating back to the beginning of last season in that same stat, behind the likes of Brandin Cooks, Kalif Raymond, and Lil’Jordan Humphrey. In terms of success rate when targeted, Metcalf is 89th dating back to last season despite ranking 22nd in target share. If we’re just focusing on this young season alone, he was 89th in EPA per target (min. 10 routes run) going into Week 2 – that ranking will drop considerably after Sunday’s performance. It would be one thing if Metcalf had a high rate of catching deep balls with that being a big reason why his success rate was so low, but that’s not the case. His average depth of target since he became a Steeler is 7.21 yards – that ranks 121st in the NFL. Yet, despite such a low average depth of target, Metcalf ranks 101st in reception percentage. And just in case you were wondering how poorly he’s been at separating, he’s averaging less than two yards of separation thus far in 2026, and averaged only 2.6 yards of separation in 2025. For the money Metcalf is making, the production – or lack thereof – is inexcusable. He has eight receptions for 67 yards in the first two games of the year, putting him at roughly $29,000 per yard if we break his contract down on a per game basis. He’s not just been bad, he’s been a net negative for the Steelers and borderline unplayable. And if it becomes a season-long issue, it’s not as if the Steelers can just cut him, at least not without it coming at a big cost. They’d eat $49 million in dead cap in 2027 should they release him, but the fact that we’re having this discussion just two weeks into the season speaks volumes. title: Steelers stock report after embarrassing loss to Patriots
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers were manhandled by the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on Sunday. The offense couldn’t find any consistency, and injuries to the offensive line kept piling up as Aaron Rodgers ran for his life all day. As always, here is my weekly stock report as we look around the team to see […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - SEPTEMBER 20: DK Metcalf #4 of the Pittsburgh Steelers runs with the ball during the second quarter of the game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers were manhandled by the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on Sunday. The offense couldn’t find any consistency, and injuries to the offensive line kept piling up as Aaron Rodgers ran for his life all day. As always, here is my weekly stock report as we look around the team to see who performed well and who didn’t. Stock Up: TJ Watt If you want to take any kind of positive from this game, TJ Watt’s Week 1 performance was no fluke. The veteran edge defender was unstoppable once again in Week 2. Watt recorded 1.5 sacks and looks to be displaying that same kind of jump off the ball we had become accustomed to seeing Watt have. Nobody is benefiting more from the rotation of edge rushers in Patrick Graham’s defense than Watt. The former Defensive Player of the Year is playing like he wants to add another one of those awards to his mantle. Patrick Queen Queen made a huge play when he intercepted a Drake Maye pass that looked like it was thrown right to Queen. Some great pressure on the play was provided by Jack Sawyer. Through two games, the inside linebacker room has shown flashes of quality play with both Queen and the emerging Payton Wilson. Stock Down: DK Metcalf DK Metcalf is becoming a net negative for the Steelers offense. He turned his nine targets into just four catches for 27 yards. Both Roman Wilson and rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard finished the game with more yards on fewer targets. The drops continued to plague Metcalf in this contest. Head coach Mike McCarthy clearly made it a point of emphasis to manufacture touches for the receiver early in the contest, which never amounted to much of anything. Metcalf continues to get the most targets of anyone in the offense, but it’s b becoming hard to justify that. The Steelers offense is going to have to change things, and one of those changes could very well be a lesser workload for Metcalf. Pass Protection We have to start with the offensive line here, which was absolutely manhandled by the Patriots’ front seven all afternoon. Starting tackles Dylan Cook and Troy Fautanu did not have their best showings, as the Patriots sacked Aaron Rodgers four times in the contest. Starting guard Mason McCormick went down with an injury in the second half, which means this offensive line could have even more inexperience stepping in for the near future. Rodgers had very little help from his receivers and his offensive line in this one, so I find it hard to put too much blame on him. However, the pocket movement was questionable at times from the veteran quarterback. The lack of mobility really showed up in this game, but Rodgers needs more help from those around him. Run Game Both Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle averaged under four yards per carry. Once again, it was Warren who was clearly more efficient and productive with the ball in his hands. Dowdle left the game twice with a toe injury. The Steelers have tried to run the ball on early downs so far this season, and it has not worked. It’s hard to imagine the running game seeing any kind of consistency until the passing agme becomes a serious threat, which is a taller task than anyone realizes. title: Mike McCarthy takes blame for Steelers’ offensive struggles vs. Patriots
summary: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy was notably deflated on the podium in his postgame press conference following a 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots on Sunday afternoon. “Offensively, clearly not good enough, And that starts with me,” he told the media. “Felt it in practice, frankly, coming off of (offensive struggles) last week. As […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - SEPTEMBER 20: Head Coach Mike McCarthy of the Pittsburgh Steelers reacts to touchdown by the New England Patriots during the fourth quarter of the game at Gillette Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Winslow Townson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy was notably deflated on the podium in his postgame press conference following a 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots on Sunday afternoon. “Offensively, clearly not good enough, And that starts with me,” he told the media. “Felt it in practice, frankly, coming off of (offensive struggles) last week. As I stated, felt we were real herky jerky in the run and pass. … We didn’t answer the bell. Our protections were not clean.” McCarthy noted several aspects of the game where the Steelers needed to improve. “The reality of it is the detail is not there,” he said. “And that’s on coaching. Starts with me; I’m calling the offense. I have to get the detail better. If you need someone, fire away, because I felt it on Wednesday and Thursday. I’m a veteran coach and I know better. And I didn’t do a good job.” Still, McCarthy made it clear he didn’t want to overreact when asked about potential personnel changes. “Well, I mean, it’s two weeks,” he said. But if you’re making the same mistakes, whether you’re young or a veteran, that’s what we have to address. We have to look at the volume, too. … If it’s not clean, you have to cut the volume down. And we’re not clean on offense, so the volume is getting cut down. So that’s the first starting point and that’s my fault because I felt it early in the week.” McCarthy, in his first year as the Steelers’ head coach, clarified what he meant about “volume” during practice — emphasizing the team needs to work on the fundamentals before expanding further. “You know when the volume is up, and you know when you’re pushing the envelope, too,” he said. “But it’s also the first year of the staff and players working together, and you want to push your players — but at the end of the day, you have to do it to win the game. … The basics weren’t there.” McCarthy shifted the blame from players such as quarterback Aaron Rodgers to himself. He also noted that the team needs more explosives on offense. “We got a quarterback who can play at any volume of game plan, but at the end of the day it’s a team game, and we have to give Aaron Rodgers better platforms to throw off of,” he said. “I don’t want to dink and dunk … there’s a place for that maybe situationally, but that’s not the philosophy — we have to attempt to get the ball thrown downfield.” One of the brighter spots from the Steelers’ loss was a defensive performance that kept the game in reach for a while. However, Pittsburgh wasn’t able to hang on through the fourth quarter. “Defense played well enough to win the game – you hold them to 13 points (on offense), I expect us to win every game we line up in,” McCarthy said. “Offense needs to be better. Mike McCarthy needs to be better.”

title: Steelers offense gets dominated in 20-3 loss to Patriots
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense may have left some plays on the field in Week 1 in their 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons, but the big plays were there to be had, which provided optimism for Week 2. All of that optimism was swiftly thrown out the window against the New England Patriots in a […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - SEPTEMBER 20: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers is tackled by Gabe Jacas #50 of the New England Patriots during the first quarter of the game at Gillette Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers’ offense may have left some plays on the field in Week 1 in their 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons, but the big plays were there to be had, which provided optimism for Week 2. All of that optimism was swiftly thrown out the window against the New England Patriots in a 20-3 loss. The Steelers averaged just 3.5 yards per play against the Patriots and were never able to get anything going in any facet. They went 2-of-12 on third down, making them 5-of-25 for the season through two weeks. Aaron Rodgers didn’t reach 200 yards, going 23-of-39 for 187 yards – good for a mere 4.5 yards per attempt. The offensive struggles can all be traced back to the putrid offensive line play put on display. Dylan Cook was abysmal for the second consecutive week, as was Spencer Anderson. Troy Fautanu allowed a pair of sacks, including one that sent the Steelers from 3rd-and-7 to 4th-and-43 after a strip sack. Overall, Rodgers was sacked four times and pressured constantly throughout the afternoon. Overall, Pittsburgh notched just one play of 20+ yards. The run game was better than it was a week ago, but still wasn’t anything to write home about with just 91 yards on 23 carries. Mike McCarthy needs to take a hard look at Cook and Spencer Anderson, and there should be strong consideration to start Max Iheanachor and Gennings Dunker in Week 3. An even larger story is the lackluster play of DK Metcalf, who was once again shutdown by a high quality cornerback. The former Seahawk was targeted nine times, making four catches for 27 yards and had two more drops, including one on 3rd-and-3 that would have gone for a first down. Metcalf now has eight receptions for 67 yards on 19 targets. Considering he is making north of $30 million per year, he is currently one of the worst contracts in football. Defensively, the Steelers did all they could until the dam just burst. Payton Wilson recovered a Rhamondre Stevenson fumble to end the Patriots’ first drive, and the unit held New England to 10 first half points. Unfortunately for the defense, any time they gave the offense a big play, it was all for not. The Steelers went three-and-out after the Wilson fumble recovery. Patrick Queen picked off Drake Maye on the first drive of the second half, and the Steelers turned around and punted seven plays later. The Patriots then missed a field goal, and the Steelers went three-and-out. The Steelers also sacked Maye three times, with T.J. Watt upping his season total to 3.5. While there were a few chunk plays given up, the loss certainly doesn’t fall on the shoulders of the defense. Pittsburgh will now get set to face the Cincinnati Bengals, who are about to get to 2-0 with a likely win over the Houston Texans and looking to take an early command of the AFC North by getting to 3-0. Should the Steelers lose, they will find themselves treading water before September ends. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Snap Reactions: Seahawks show depth in stomping Cardinals
summary: The Seattle Seahawks went on the road to take on the Arizona Cardinals Sunday in the first divisional match up of the year for either team. Arizona kept things close early, but Seattle pulled away in the second half, with the final tally giving the Seahawks a 31-7 win to keep pace with the San […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Abraham Lucas #72, Christian Haynes #64, Jalen Sundell #61, Grey Zabel #76, and Charles Cross #67 of the Seattle Seahawks look on during the first quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks went on the road to take on the Arizona Cardinals Sunday in the first divisional match up of the year for either team. Arizona kept things close early, but Seattle pulled away in the second half, with the final tally giving the Seahawks a 31-7 win to keep pace with the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West. That final score is so lopsided it makes it easy to forget that the many of the players who were on the field for the Seahawks for much of the game were expected to spend most of the season on the bench. Quarterback Drew Lock needed a little time to get loose when he was forced into action against the New England Patriots in Week 1, but has played some of the best football of his career since halftime of the opener. Third year offensive lineman Christian Haynes, a third round pick out of UConn in 2024, started for the first time in his career while rotating with 2026 Day 3 selection Beau Stephens, who made his regular season NFL debut against Arizona. Running back Emmanuel Wilson, whose 92 yards on the ground were the second best of his career, carried 21 times during the game, compared to 13 attempts for the first round pick of the Seahawks in the draft in April, Jadarian Price. Add in significant snaps for Brady Russell, Nick Kallerup and Eric Saubert, and it’s easy to see why other teams have been quick to improve their roster by claiming former Seahawks off the waiver wire. (Author’s Note: There is perhaps no better example of this than the Raiders, a team which won all of three games during the entire 2025 season, starting 2-0 after claiming Bryce Cabeldue off the waiver wire ahead of Week 1.) On the defensive side of the ball, practice squad elevatee Rodney Thomas led the group in snaps played, staying on the field for all 50 snaps the defense logged. Nick Emmanwori had a very light workload in his first action of the season, as there was no need to risk rushing things against Jacoby Brissett and the rest of the Cardinals offense. When the Seahawks special teams took to the field, just as it has been in years past, it was Brady Russell leading the way with 22 snaps. Right behind Russell were Tyrice Knight, Chazz Surratt, Patrick O’Connell and George Holani, with 17 snaps each. As for players who only saw the field on special teams and did not play a single snap on offense or defense, former Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Avery Smith led the team with 14 special teams snaps as he continues to learn the system and scheme after arriving in a trade on the day of roster cuts. And with the ghosts of Glendale in the rear view mirror, it’s a trip east to the DMV in Week 3 to take on Dan Quinn and the Washington Commanders.
author: John Gilbert

title: Seahawks Droppings: New starting quarterback, same results for streaking Seahawks
summary: It doesn’t matter who’s playing for the Seattle Seahawks right now…they’re on a freakin’ roll! Drew Lock stepped right in for Sam Darnold and led the Seahawks to a 31-7 drubbing of the Arizona Cardinals in the desert. This win pushed Seattle’s winning streak to a franchise record 12 games in a row, and was […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Drew Lock #2 of the Seattle Seahawks warms up during the second quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images It doesn’t matter who’s playing for the Seattle Seahawks right now…they’re on a freakin’ roll! Drew Lock stepped right in for Sam Darnold and led the Seahawks to a 31-7 drubbing of the Arizona Cardinals in the desert . This win pushed Seattle’s winning streak to a franchise record 12 games in a row, and was also the 10th consecutive victory over the Cardinals. The Seahawks are on an absolute heater right now. Seattle got off to a hot start on the first drive with an 82-yard TD pass from Lock to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. From then on until halftime, it was a bit of a struggle with some drops, fumbles, and a failed 4th down play. Heading into halftime, the score was 7-7 with the Cardinals hanging around and feeling good. Then, the Seahawks threw the Cardinals out the front door like Uncle Will from Fresh Prince of Bel Air . Seattle rallied off 24 straight points including a soul crushing drive that took up most of the fourth quarter. They kept ramming it down Arizona’s throat, and finished it off with a 1-yard AJ Barner “Barn Yard” TD. It was Seattle imposing their will and it was glorious! What a statement. Seahawks Droppings Drew Lock played a fantastic game, throwing for 3 TDs and taking care of the ball . His completion percentage would’ve been even better if not for some uncharacteristic drops by JSN and Rashid Shaheed. Lock was poised, escaped pressure, and whistled some truly beautiful throws in there. Sam Darnold will still be the QB when he’s healthy, but the Seahawks have to feel pretty good about their QB situation. Brian Fleury showed that he runs a QB-friendly system. Remember when Mac Jones looked great playing in the place of an injured Brock Purdy for the San Francisco 49ers? Same system. Fleury called plenty of run plays to soften the Cardinals defense before hitting them with the pass. Then, he used the run game to deliver the knockout blow. Just a beautiful execution of the game plan. JSN is inevitable . No matter how many people you put on him or how you try to stop him, it seems impossible right now. 9 catches on 11 targets for 155 yards and 3 TDs. Within those catches were some vital third down conversions. JSN can literally do everything at the wide receiver position, a total luxury for Seattle. Let’s give it up one time for the RBs! Price’s fumble notwithstanding, the RB room showed out. Emmanuel Wilson led way with 92 yards while Price chipped in 52 of his own. The rookie injured his chest, so hopefully that won’t hold him out. Wilson, taking the lion’s share of the carries after Price went out, looked quick, decisive, and powerful. He always fell forward and rarely was tackled by the first defender. When Charbonnet comes back, the Seahawks might now have a three-headed monster in the backfield. Seattle’s defense absolutely suffocated Arizona’s offense after allowing a TD on 4th down to Trey McBride . They shut down the run, only allowing 70 rushing yards, which was padded by a garbage time explosive run on the last drive. Jacoby Brissett didn’t do much better throwing the ball, managing 81 yards passing with an interception. In the postgame presser, Leonard Williams (who had a fantastic sack by the way), mentioned how they want to play defense like a boa constrictor. Mission accomplished today. I feel like I need to mention Julian Love once again . That was one of the best INTs I’ve ever seen, getting his hands underneath the ball and keeping it off the turf while sliding towards the boundary. Love has always been a good player, but I feel like he’s entering the blue-chip territory. It was good to see both Tory Horton and Nick Emmanwori get some snaps . They’ll be worked in even more in the coming weeks and will both provide explosive potential on each sides of the ball. The Seahawks made a statement with this victory. No matter what the starting lineup looks like, when they play like Seahawks, they’re going to be tough to beat. Relentlessly physical and opportunistic in all three phases, this 31-7 beatdown is an example of the tidal wave that Seattle can bring on their opponents. What a beautiful representation of the game of football!

title: Seahawks-Cardinals post-game analysis: Bullying, dastardly defense, and a ‘Jax trick’ in the desert
summary: While a mathematically desirous outcome, Seahawks 31, Cardinals 7, doesn’t really tell the full story of Seattle’s tenth straight win over their Sunset End Zone State rivals. And yet, in something of a pleasing paradox, it does. Because the way it began, which is competitively, matches exactly how uncompetitively it ended. ‘Twas a close game […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Seattle Seahawks walks off the field after his teams 31-7 win against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images While a mathematically desirous outcome, Seahawks 31, Cardinals 7, doesn’t really tell the full story of Seattle’s tenth straight win over their Sunset End Zone State rivals. And yet, in something of a pleasing paradox, it does. Because the way it began, which is competitively, matches exactly how uncompetitively it ended. ‘Twas a close game for a half because the Seahawks are a complete team and the spunky Cardinals aren’t quite there yet. So, makes sense the hosts could hang with the defending champs for a minute or thirty. Until the disparity made itself clear, which is when this brutally efficient Seahawks team began to stomp on some throats, and the Seattle defense handed the ball off to their offense to finish the job. Oh, they finished it all right. On a day the story could be Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s hat trick (Jax trick?), or the defense’s usual dominance, or Drew Lock’s outright elite quarterbacking from the backup position, the offensive line stole the show. They got to crunch time and told the Cards defense, out loud, for all who had eyes to hear, “You guys thought you would do some football, but now we will do the football. You can watch, if you’d like.” Witness 3rd and eight, halfway through a 16-play, 10-minute drive. Casual 3rd and 8 conversion on the ground halfway through the fourth quarter in your divisional rival's house to win your tenth straight against them — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-09-20T23:06:50.764Z Fifteen plays were runs. The lone pass was a third-down dart to JSN. It went, if you’ll forgive the glorious repetitiveness: Emanuel Wilson for 18, Wilson for 3, George Holani for 5, pass on the money, Wilson for no gain, Wilson for 2, the play pictured above, Wilson for 7, Wilson for 7 again, Wilson twice more for 1 each time, Holani for 6 plus the inevitable frustration penalty, then the four short runs culminating in A.J. Barner’s vulturian touchdown. The offense ran between 41 and 48 seconds off the clock each time, save for clock stoppages outside their control. It was a masterclass in imposing your will on a lesser team in their own house. And the Seahawks are the ones who did it. To cement the best game I’ve seen them play since they hung 46-350-5 on the ground vs. the Giants in 2014, the offensive line permitted only three QB hits on Lock. Let’s give everyone their due, though. The story can be about more than one outstanding play, player, position group or side of the ball. Why not? This is the most complete team in the league right now, period. Nobody need be greedy with the praise. There is more than enough to go around. It’s a renewable resource you know. Three of these. Remember the decade of consciously not drafting a Seahawks receiver early on for your fantasy team? If so, forget it this instant. Three of these! This is your WR1. This is maybe everyone’s WR1: JAX TRICK — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-09-20T22:50:36.656Z This is your backup quarterback. Maybe everyone’s backup quarterback, if the other 31 fanbases had a say: No, the 2013 Seahawks wouldn't have won the SB with Flynn, and no, the 2025 Seahawks neither with Lock, but Drew had one hell of a game today in Arizona against a quality defense — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-09-20T23:26:22.338Z I’m one more great Lock outing away from legally changing his first name to TheDrewth. He’s been that good since Sam Darnold’s season took an involuntary detour on the first drive. Against the Patriots there were money throws under pressure; against the Cardinals there were yards-seeking missiles hitting his receivers square in the hands. I’d argue that without the Rashid Shaheed and JSN drops, Lock’s stats could be even shinier. He’s outplaying his stat line, which already conveys elite production. Yes, he’s gotten away with two super interceptable throws and has personally bitten off the nails of every fan with his propensity to snap the ball between :01 and :00. But honestly, those are offenses Darnold is just as guilty of committing. There has been no discernible drop-off between QB1 and QB2, and in case the standings matter, Seattle is 2-0. For as good as the OL, the All-Pro, and the backup have been, the defense has outdone them with stunning regularity, however. Between the McBride catch that tied things and the Barnyard plunge that iced them, the Seattle defense was nigh impenetrable. They allowed Arizona to run 12 plays for 19 yards. They permitted less than six minutes of possession, took the ball away, and no single gain went for more than nine. In fact, they kept the Cards from gaining double digits on any play, until once on the final garbage drive. Post-McBride touchdown, Arizona didn’t run a play for positive yards in Seattle territory until their final snap of the game. One meaningless gain to run out the clock. And 3.2 yards per play is a way to remind your rivals who’s in charge of the division still. I could start with the superlatives, but then it’d be impossible to quit. You know this already, the Seahawks are anything but box score warriors. Julian Love made another disturbingly handsome play with the fingertip pick between blades of grass, Derick Hall is a constant menace with or without the short shorts, and the hornet-like swarming of defenders to the ball continues. Every week the defensive line is stouter than a Guinness. Drake Thomas is oft the forgotten man amidst a sea of stars, until he streaks into the backfield like the comet he is: Cardinals: fineSeahawks: goodDrakes: great — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-09-20T21:11:41.141Z Seattle’s unsolvable roadrunner defense turned Jacoby Brissett into Wile E. Coyote. Handed an entire barrel of TNT in Trey McBride, the only explosion Brissett managed was blowing everything up in his own face. So, yeah, 31-7 was pretty dang fair. Let’s see how we got there and name some predators and prey along the way. Q1: Seahawks 7, Cardinals 0 Your Predator-Prey encounter of the quarter isn’t difficult to locate. It comes on the Seahawks’ opening drive, congrats on calling it ahead of time, it’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba creating the most open touchdown of his young-ish career. Also happened to be his longest reception ever. Collateral prey on the play includes two DBs, not one: Will Johnson and Budda Baker. Goodbye. — John Fraley (@johndavidfraley.bsky.social) 2026-09-20T20:32:16.221Z The Cardinals had actually started auspiciously enough, with a big return to the 43 then a nifty completion to Trey McBride past midfield on their first offensive snap. We had the appearance of a game, which lasted exactly until halftime. Even though Arizona’s drive stalled right away in short yardage and later downs and even though the ensuing JSN touchdown on Seattle’s second play of the game made it 7-0, and even though the teams traded punts, the Cardinals early on looked rather like the team that upset the Chargers in Week 1. They looked even more the part when they drove for their only points of the game as the first quarter ended. To all who could objectively observe, it looked like the Cards had found a formula to keep pace. Get into favorable second downs, take advantage of over-aggressive Seahawks coverage, feed McBride, and don’t wimp out at the goal line. Q2: Seahawks 7, Cardinals 7 [NFL] Trey McBride finds the end zone on fourth down twitter.com/NFL/status/2… — NFL News Poster (@nflnewsposter.bsky.social) 2026-09-20T21:00:21.960Z Arizona’s plan worked perfectly for exactly one possession. Their other nine did not yield similar results. Yes, McBride had five early catches to extend his NFL record streak in that category for tight ends. Yes, they forced a fumble (something…

full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Seattle Seahawks celebrates with Drew Lock #2 after scoring a touchdown during the third quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks took care of business against the Arizona Cardinals. In other news, fork found in kitchen. Seattle didn’t blow the Cardinals out right away, but a 7-7 halftime score turned into a more appropriate 31-7 rout in Glendale . Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught all three of Drew Lock’s touchdowns, while the Cardinals barely cleared 150 yards of offense in another defensive masterpiece by Mike Macdonald’s group. We want to know what your takeaways are from Seattle’s victory. At 8:05 pm PT we’ll have a live reaction podcast with myself and Bryce Coutts on The Hawks Eye , and we’ll have all of our thoughts on Seattle’s win. It’s also Bryce’s birthday, so happy birthday to Coach Bryce! Our Seahawks-Cardinals post-game takeaways The Seahawks defense is looking better than last year and still not at full strength. Remember, Ty Okada has been out for both games and Nick Emmanwori didn’t play his usual snap count. This Seahawks passing game might be scarier than last year, and Sam Darnold has only played five snaps. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is continuing his Offensive Player of the Year form from last season. Drew Lock showed why he is QB2 (in a good way!). Three touchdowns, no turnovers, and a lot of timely third-down conversions and accurate throws. Seattle’s run game once Zach Charbonnet is back could be a real force. The Seahawks rushed for over 160 yards and beat the Cardinals defensive line into submission in the fourth quarter. title: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels out for Seahawks game after gruesome arm injury
summary: Despite missing Sam Darnold for the majority of their first two games, the Seattle Seahawks have started the season with two straight wins and they’re set to take on a shorthanded Washington Commanders squad next, who’s starting quarterback recently suffered an all too familiar injury. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn announced quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 20: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders looks on before being carted off the field after sustaining an injury against the Dallas Cowboys in the second quarter of a game at AT&T Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite missing Sam Darnold for the majority of their first two games, the Seattle Seahawks have started the season with two straight wins and they’re set to take on a shorthanded Washington Commanders squad next, who’s starting quarterback recently suffered an all too familiar injury. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn announced quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered a dislocated left elbow, the same one he injured last season, in the team’s 37-20 Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. He is set to undergo further testing on Monday, however the initial X-rays eliminated the possibility of a fracture. Quinn added there’s “optimism” he’ll suit up again this season, although testing should help determine an exact timeline and whether the star quarterback will require surgery. The injury occurred on 3rd and goal shortly before halftime when Daniels tried to brace himself on the turf after slipping while receiving the snap, and landed awkwardly. Jayden Daniels is down after the Commanders last play. 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/s6EE4exa6P — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 20, 2026 It’s a crucial blow for the third-year quarterback who’s coming off an injury riddled 2025 campaign where he suffered a knee sprain and hamstring injury before the disastrous dislocated elbow in Washington’s 38-14 loss to the Seahawks. Daniels missed three games after the previous elbow injury. Fast forward nearly a year later, and the Commanders are set to be without Daniels for the foreseeable future once again. Backup Marcus Mariota recorded 111 passing yards as well as a touchdown in limited playing time against the Cowboys and he’ll remain under center for Washington’s Week 3 matchup against Seattle. Seeking their first victory of the season, Mariota and the Commanders will be tasked with overcoming a dominant Seahawks defense who allowed just 151 total yards against Arizona.

title: Winners and Losers from another Seahawks demolition of the Cardinals
summary: Another year, another Seattle Seahawks win over the Arizona Cardinals in their building. Not since Russell Wilson’s rookie year have the Cardinals beaten the Seahawks at home in front of a full capacity crowd. Their one (very chaotic) victory over Seattle in Glendale since 2012 was in the COVID-19 pandemic 2020 season. That’s it. And […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Drew Lock #2 of the Seattle Seahawks runs off the field after his teams 31-7 win against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another year, another Seattle Seahawks win over the Arizona Cardinals in their building. Not since Russell Wilson’s rookie year have the Cardinals beaten the Seahawks at home in front of a full capacity crowd. Their one (very chaotic) victory over Seattle in Glendale since 2012 was in the COVID-19 pandemic 2020 season. That’s it. And it’s barely a home game when the Seahawks fans are so loud that they were doing a silent count in their own building . Let’s get to another rousing Winners and Losers from Seattle’s 31-7 romp ! Seattle Seahawks winners Drew Lock wheels and deals I’m giving Lock the biggest winner tag. He was calm, composed, accurate, and looked like he was in comfortable command of the offense. His stat-line of 19/26 for 235 yards and three wonderful touchdowns to Jaxon Smith-Njigba actually undersold his performance. JSN and Rashid Shaheed both had drops, otherwise his stats would look even better. Whether Lock is a Seahawk in 2027 or not is not something I’m thinking about right now, but in a league where backup quarterbacks, let alone starting quarterbacks, are hard to come by (see: Atlanta Falcons), Lock will have a healthy free agent market for him in some capacity. Jaxon Smith-Njigba might be going for OPOY again What more can you say about JSN? His first catch goes for a career-long 82 yards and a house call. You’d think the Cardinals would try and sell out to stop him instead of waltz free on a busted coverage. Budda Baker, whom I’ve respected for a long time as an opposition fan, was torched all afternoon by the NFL’s best receiver. It’s JSN’s first three-touchdown performance of his career, and his 155 yards is his fourth-highest total to date. There’s the Super Bowl repeat first and foremost, but what about another OPOY award? He’s doing this with the backup QB! Julian Love is astounding How in the hell did he come up with this interception? I thought for sure Love trapped the ball and it was going to be an incomplete pass, which only would’ve meant a punt return and likely worse field position. But the concentration and strong hands to come away with the ball here was otherworldly. WAIT FOR THE REPLAY. 😮‍💨 @_jlove20 📺: @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/c4mOKPiNFz — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) September 20, 2026 Emanuel Wilson shows why Seattle signed him in free agency I wasn’t totally wowed by Wilson as a free agent pickup, not when Tyler Allgeier was available and other cheap running backs were also on the market. My tune changed watching him at training camp and seeing how smoothly he moved in outside zone schemes and his willingness to quickly get up the field. Wilson is not going to juke you out of your shoes or wow with speed, but he is an effective north-south runner who is physical at the point of contact. Wilson led Seattle with 92 yards and 21 carries after a fairly uninspired first half. As the game wore on, Seattle’s ground game beat Arizona into submission. Chazz Surratt might have turned the game in Seattle’s favor for good The best special teams play came not from Rashid Shaheed (although he was involved) or Jason Myers or Michael Dickson, but Mr. Surratt. Seattle’s reserve linebacker and special teams standout pounced on a Shaheed fumble to start the second half. He not only got the ball but took it all the way inside of Arizona’s 40 to set up Seattle’s go-ahead touchdown. Cardinals fourth down stand! SEAvsAZ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/s1AfHMkhuv — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Seattle’s offensive line keeps Drew Lock upright, pounds Cardinals into submission Lock was sacked once by Budda Baker on the last play of the half, otherwise there were only three QB hits total and no other sacks. Seattle’s offensive line struggled to establish a run game in the first half before unleashing hell in the second half. That 10-minute touchdown drive to end the game was Seattle’s longest touchdown drive in terms of time off the clock… maybe ever? It’s certainly the longest in Stathead ’s drive tracker, which goes back to 2001. Beau Stephens and Christian Haynes split time at right guard, which is a nice way to get Stephens some reps while Anthony Bradford is out. I hope Charles Cross didn’t mess up his arm spiking the ball after the Barner TD, though. Leonard Williams is unblockable He had the first sack of the game and a key run stop on a 3rd-and-1. This is someone who is playing at the absolute highest level as an interior defensive lineman, and he will go down as one of the greatest mid-season acquisitions by John Schneider. I’d argue he’s one of the best mid-season trades made by any NFL team over the past decade. A.J. Barner can’t be stopped on the Barn Yard The tush push is here to stay, and the Seahawks use their all-around tight end to get that tough yard. Barner now has two touchdown rushes in his career, and he’s valuable as ever as a blocker in the run game. Seattle’s entire defense dominated Outside of a garbage time run by Zonovan Knight, the Seahawks didn’t allow a single offensive play to go for more than nine yards. Trey McBride had eight catches and a touchdown… and had 41 yards. Marvin Harrison Jr had as many catches as his dad did, and his dad hasn’t played in 18 years. Jeremiyah Love had a couple of good runs and early and finished with 29 on nine carries. Seattle Seahawks losers Rashid Shaheed was worse than the stats suggested I’m a little concerned about Shaheed’s slow start to the season. The first game I can write off because of a lack of snaps and the emergency situation of Lock coming in unexpectedly. Shaheed had three catches for 35 yards against Arizona, but he also had a bad drop that would’ve extended a drive and fumbled that kick return into something that fortunately beneficial for Seattle. He’s known as a speedster, which I stress is different for guys who specialize in 200 and 400 meters (which Shaheed did) than a 60- or 100-meter specialist, but he’s looked a bit hesitant on his returns and not in rhythm with the offense. It’s early days and his main connection is ultimately with Sam Darnold, but he’s not off to a flyer in his new contract. Brian Fleury’s red-zone playcalling needs to be tweaked I thought Brian Fleury called a good game, but I don’t think the Seahawks are obligated to go run-heavy in the low red zone. To end the first half with four runs inside the 10 (albeit one I think Lock audibled to) was not great. They need to at least have more of a passing threat in early downs when they’re goal-to-go. Otherwise, you know it’s a great Seahawks win when that’s one of the few things I can nitpick. Final notes Jadarian Price had his good and bad moments, plus an injury . I won’t put him in the Losers column for the fumble, but that was his “Welcome to the NFL” moment as far as ball security. He had 13 carries for 52 yards and hit a couple of explosives, plus his only catch went for a first down before he left with a chest injury. It seems he’s fine as far as a more serious injury, although it’s untimely given Zach Charbonnet won’t be back for another couple of weeks. Chris Myers was getting names wrong all afternoon . Drew Bledsoe (for Drew Lock), Jeremy Love (for Jeremiyah), Emanuel Lewis for Emanuel Wilson, it was irritating. Mark Schlereth was actually an enjoyable listen but Myers was out to lunch. For that matter, so was the FOX broadcast, which randomly switched to the Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders for a brief minute. Mike Macdonald probably wishes he had that Josh Jobe vs. Trey McBride touchdown play-call back. Any scenario in which Jobe is on a great receiving tight end is an unfavorable matchup. No safety help, just pure 1-on-1 ball that only ever had one winner. That’s essentially…

After the team’s 31-7 win, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said X-rays on Price’s chest came back negative, but didn’t expand on the severity of the injury. If Price does […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks runs with the ball during the second quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks closed out their 10th-straight victory over the Arizona Cardinals without their first-round pick, Jadarian Price, due to a chest injury on Sunday. After the team’s 31-7 win, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said X-rays on Price’s chest came back negative, but didn’t expand on the severity of the injury. If Price does miss time, the Seahawks would be left with only two running backs on the active roster, George Holani and Emmanuel Wilson. Zach Charbonnet is still recovering from a torn ACL he suffered in last season’s playoff run. Seattle has running backs Velus Jones Jr. and Jacardia Wright on the practice squad, who could be elevated to fill the void next week. Price, who combined with Wilson to propel the Seahawks’ offense for much of the day, was listed as questionable in the fourth quarter. Against the Cardinals, Price ran for 52 yards on 13 carries, including a 25-yard burst in the third quarter. He did commit his first career fumble, which the Cardinals recovered but failed to score off of. O rookie Jadarian Price TÁ BEM DEMAIS! 😎 📺: #SEAvsARI ao vivo e em português no NFL Game Pass pic.twitter.com/lBiGWWH7N4 — NFL Brasil (@NFLBrasil) September 20, 2026 Wilson had a fantastic day closing out Seattle’s win, posting 92 yards on 21 carries, which may give the Seahawks confidence to be careful with Price as they look forward to their matchup with the 0-2 Washington Commanders next Sunday.
