title: 49ers snap counts: Raheem Morris is adapting to his personnel
summary: The San Francisco 49ers dominated the Miami Dolphins. It’s not often the scoreboard tells the full story, but they beat up on the Fins as much as 35-13 indicates. It was a relatively clean game for the Niners in all three phases. Any concerns about jet lag and an emotional letdown were quelled after the […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers dominated the Miami Dolphins. It’s not often the scoreboard tells the full story, but they beat up on the Fins as much as 35-13 indicates. It was a relatively clean game for the Niners in all three phases. Any concerns about jet lag and an emotional letdown were quelled after the offense’s first drive. Brock Purdy capitalized on an aggressive game plan from Kyle Shanahan. The Dolphins offense couldn’t keep pace, and that’s how you end up winning by three touchdowns. Let’s look at the snap counts from this game and see what they mean for the depth chart hierarchy and what we can ascertain moving forward. Quarterback Brock Purdy: 42 Mac Jones: 7 You know things are going your way when you can put in a backup quarterback in the fourth quarter. That’s because the starter had an 80% passing success rate, which would be tough to do in practice. Purdy faced a blitz on 40% of his dropbacks, but you’d never know by his results. He had a “wow” throw and a couple of other impact plays. He rushed for 30 yards, which aided the offense when nobody was open. Purdy knows when to pick and choose his spots. He wasn’t perfect, but he wasn’t far off. Running backs Christian McCaffrey: 27 Kyle Juszczk: 23 Kaelon Black: 15 Jordan James: 7 McCaffrey led the team with 10 carries. This was a game where you don’t need to give CMC a bunch of touches, so credit the coaching staff for using a player like James in the fourth quarter. None of the running backs averaged more than four yards per carry. Here’s a funny stat: Black ran for 25 yards, with 28 of those coming after contact. McCaffrey ran for 23 yards, with 27 of those coming after contact. The 49ers didn’t need to run the ball because they were averaging a first down almost every time they dropped back to throw. Pass catchers Deebo Samuel: 30 Mike Evans: 28 George Kittle: 25 Luke Farrell: 25 Jacob Cowing: 22 KhaDarel Hodge: 17 Demarcus Robinson: 16 Brayden Willis: 11 Deebo ran more routes than anybody. Deebo and Kittle were the most targeted, but it was Kittle who ran away with most of the production. The average yards of separation numbers are silly. Kittle’s was 5.4. Deebo’s was 5.1. Robinson’s was 4.7. Evans was the only player under three. The scheme took advantage of a bunch of rookies. We’ll see how the 49ers replace Robinson, who clearly had built a rapport with Purdy. Maybe it’s more Deebo? Do they trust Cowing in that role? The better football shape Kittle gets in, the more he’ll be used, too. Offensive line Connor Colby: 49 Colton McKivitz: 49 Dominick Puni: 44 Jake Brendel: 42 Trent Williams: 42 Jarett Patterson: 7 Vederian Lowe: 7 Carver Willis: 5 Patterson came in for Brendel—Lowe for Trent, and Willis for Puni. The 49ers allowed only three pressures in the afternoon—one from Colby, McKivitz, and Williams. Every lineman was credited with at least two impact plays, save for Puni. Williams had three impact plays. No penalties of any kind for this group. Only 7.4% of their carries were stuffed, which was the fourth-best mark of the week. This unit will be underrated for most of the season. Defensive tackles Osa Odighizuwa: 37 (66.1%) Gracen Halton: 30 (53.6) CJ West: 26 (46.4%) James Thompson Jr.: 19 (33.9%) Around the third quarter in Week 1, it was obvious that rookie Gracen Halton was the best option at defensive tackle next to Osa Odighizuwa: I'm finding a way to get Gracen Halton on the field more after that drive. He had a couple of disruptive plays. Something the 49ers have been lacking at DT outside of Odighizuwa today. — Kyle Posey (@KP_Show) September 11, 2026 Technically, Halton started. The 49ers came out in a true man-front to begin the game. Morris replaced one rookie with another: Jaden Dugger off, Halton in. Morris stayed with that front in the first drive. Thompson Jr. subbed in for Halton after a handful of plays. On third and long, Odighizuwa was the only defensive tackle on the field. He doesn’t have many options at the position, but Morris is adapting to his personnel. It’s telling that Halton has already jumped West in snaps. It’s not surprising, though. Halton had a pressure rate of 21.4%, which was seven percentage points higher than Odighizuwa. Halton had a stuffed run and three run stops. None of the other defensive tackles had any. Halton looks like the real deal. EDGE rushers Nick Bosa: 36 (64.3%) Keion White: 30 (53.6%) Romello Height: 29 (51.8%) Ogbo Okoronkwo: 16 (28.6) Khalid Kareem: 11 (19.6%) White didn’t start, but still outsnapped Height. He outplayed the rookie, too. Height had one more pressure, but White added a run stuff and was in the backfield more. Both players notched sacks, which is what you want from your depth players. Life is much easier when Bosa is on the field. Bosa’s pressure percentage was 27.8%. He won at a 22.2% clip, which is hilariously high. Bosa added a pair of run stops. You’d have no idea that Bosa is coming off a season-ending ACL injury. Linebacker Fred Warner: 46 (82.1%) Dre Greenlaw: 39 (69.6%) Jaden Dugger: 18 (32.1%) Garret Wallow: 11 (19.6%) Luke Gifford: 1 (1.8%) For the second week in a row, Wallow replaced Greenlaw at WILL linebacker when Morris was expecting the offense to pass. In the fourth quarter, once the game was out of hand, Wallow was the lone dime linebacker on the field. It’s evident that Morris views Wallow as an asset in coverage, based on his usage. That might be because Greenlaw allowed all five of his targets to be completed for 40 yards. Greenlaw missed one tackle, but had two run stops, a run stuff, and continues to be aggressive on run plays. Warner had a “hustle” stop and one other. He also notched a half sack and a quarterback pressure on four pass rushes. He was the only linebacker to rush the passer. Warner extended his forced fumble streak to two games. And yes, we will track that all season. Dugger is mostly a run-first player early on in his career. He played 12 run-down snaps compared to six coverage snaps. He’s still making plays. Per Sumer Sports, Dugger’s three impact plays were one more than Warner and Greenlaw. Cornerback Renardo Green: 55 (98.2%) Deommodore Lenoir: 52 (92.9%) Upton Stout: 30 (53.6%) Jack Jones: 9 (16.1%) Morris used dime personnel 10.7% of the time in Week 2, which was the seventh-highest rate. As he continues to tinker with his personnel, Jones on the field with Lenoir and Stout on the inside remains the 49ers best coverage unit. On six plays, they averaged -0.24 EPA per play. That’s with the touchdown allowed, which skews the stats. Still, the Niners had a sack in this package and allowed 21 total yards on the other plays. Green was only targeted once. He had a pair of run stops, including one “hustle” stop — which is when you chase down a play from 20 yards away. In my mind, it’s more impressive when you’re not targeted. That tells me you are forcing the quarterback to look elsewhere because the receiver isn’t open. Stout had one of those as well. Stout allowed the touchdown, but had a pressure on his only pass rush, and chipped in for three run stops. Stout will be one of the most important defenders on the team this season. The theme is the cornerbacks tackle, as Lenoir also had three run stops. He gave up a first down, but when you’re only allowing 12 yards in a game, you’re doing plenty in coverage. Jones allowed one of his two targets to be completed. He joined Stout in the pass breakup category. Safeties Marques Sigle: 55 (98.2%) Ji’Ayir Brown: 52 (92.9%) Malik Mustapha: 3 (5.4%) Mustapha played the final series of the game once it was out of hand. Brown comes off the field when the 49ers are in their goal-line package. Sigle’s speed showed up on a sack. It seems like Sigle’s main priority in Raheem Morris’s defense is to take routes away before they can be thrown. He was only targeted once all game. Sigle had six tackles, but had three run stops. The team leader in run stops for the game was Brown,…
author: Kyle Posey

title: The 3 biggest stars from the 49ers’ home opener: No rust for George Kittle
summary: The San Francisco 49ers took care of business, and that’s all you need to know about their home opener on Sunday. The 49ers demolished the Miami Dolphins 35-13 in a game the Dolphins never had a chance in. Miami opened the game with a field goal, but the 49ers went on to outscore them 35-10 […]
full_text: (Photo by Robin Alam/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers took care of business, and that’s all you need to know about their home opener on Sunday. The 49ers demolished the Miami Dolphins 35-13 in a game the Dolphins never had a chance in. Miami opened the game with a field goal, but the 49ers went on to outscore them 35-10 over the remaining 55 minutes. San Francisco avoided a letdown spot after an impressive Week 1 win over the Rams and now carry the momentum of a 2-0 record into Week 3 against the Arizona Cardinals. These are the three players most responsible for the 49ers’ second win of the season: 3rd Star: TE George Kittle Allow me to be the first to mention that George Kittle tore his Achilles just nine months ago. He emphatically announced he’s healthy against Miami. Kittle led all pass-catchers with his 80 yards on four receptions, scoring one of two passing touchdowns for the 49ers on Sunday. But it was one drive in specific that helped Kittle en route to his monster day. With the 49ers up eight to start the second half, San Francisco was looking to extend that lead early in the second half. That’s when Kyle Shanahan smashed the George Kittle button. The offense opened the third quarter with a quick strike to a wide-open Kittle for 40 yards, teleporting the 49ers into plus territory. Three plays later, Kittle scored his touchdown on a 12-yard pass to put the 49ers up 15 yards. Kittle’s quick turnaround from such a devastating injury will continue to become more impressive with each week. If Week 1 was the first test of how Kittle could handle a real-speed game again, Sunday showed he can return to the level we’ve grown to expect from the tight end. 2nd Star: DE Nick Bosa He didn’t collect a sack on Sunday, but Bosa wreaked havoc in the Miami backfield, forcing others to get to Malik Willis. Osa Odighizuwa matched Bosa with four pressures against the Dolphins’ offensive line, but Bosa’s pressure caused issues for Willis. His first pressure of the game forced Willis to pass earlier than he wanted, resulting in an Upton Stout pass breakup. Later on the drive, Miami faced a third-and-goal, but when Bosa quickly got after Willis, the play quickly fell apart, and Bosa’s pressure led to Romello Height’s first-career sack. His next pressure would result in Marques Sigle’s first career sack. With the 49ers up 21-6, the defense looked to put Miami away. Bosa beat Miami right tackle Austin Jackson off the snap and wrapped around the tackle, getting behind Willis. Willis stepped up in the pocket, but in the gap Bosa left, Sigle came through to finish the play and force the third down. Bosa was effective in the run game in Week 1, but on Sunday, Bosa showed that pass-rush ability we’re familiar with. 1st Star: QB Brock Purdy Miami’s secondary was leaving 49ers pass-catchers open all game, and Purdy happily took advantage. Purdy threw an incomplete pass to Deebo Samuel with 9:20 left in the first quarter. He then completed his next 18 passes. In those 18 passes, Purdy threw for 275 yards and two touchdowns, attacking the Dolphins’ defensive weaknesses. You could tell we were in for a good Purdy day on his fifth pass attempt of the game. With the 49ers offense facing a third-and-5, Miami pressure forced Purdy into a scramble drill. As usual, Purdy excelled on the off-script play. He kept the play alive with his feet before settling and hitting Mike Evans along the sidelines (with Evans making an acrobatic catch) for the first down. Purdy would have to wait for the second half for his touchdown pass when he connected with Kittle, and he’d close his scoring with a six-yard pass to Kyle Juszczyk to put the 49ers up 22 in the third quarter. Oh, and did I mention Purdy led the 49ers in rushing yards? He gained all 30 yards on the same drive, with a 10-yard gain on his first carry followed by an 18-yard gain. His feet would close the drive, finishing his day on the ground with a two-yard score to put the 49ers up 14-3 in the second quarter. Purdy took what Miami was giving, and it resulted in a big day for the 49ers quarterback. Throughout the season, we will track the three stars of the season by tallying points for each star award using a complex scoring system: three points for being the first star, two for the second, and one for the third. Through Week 2, the standings are: QB Brock Purdy – 5 points LB Fred Warner – 3 points DE Nick Bosa – 2 points

summary: Starting off the week with a Niners victory never. Gets. Old. What a fun win. Brock Purdy is HOOPING. He’s hitting spin moves, he’s letting it rip, he looks really loose yet also dialed in at the same time. It looks like the game’s slowing down for him. What a joy it is to have […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Starting off the week with a Niners victory never. Gets. Old. What a fun win. Brock Purdy is HOOPING. He’s hitting spin moves, he’s letting it rip, he looks really loose yet also dialed in at the same time. It looks like the game’s slowing down for him. What a joy it is to have him as our quarterback. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Now we wait for injury updates and hate-watch the Rams… What Kyle Shanahan and others said after 49ers’ 35-13 win vs. Dolphins “Trent Williams: It’s hard for me to tell because I just see the ball coming over my head, but [Brock] was extremely accurate. He looked like he was just at practice out there, wheeling and dealing. Like I said, we’re starting to witness Brock’s prime and I think it’s going to be a sight to behold. To me, I’ve always loved Brock, but I think he’s starting to get his respect now. He doesn’t even relish in it. It’s all about next week, going 1-0, and that’s why he’s a great leader.” Brock Purdy was nearly perfect in the 49ers’ blowout win over the Dolphins “ Connor Colby was the only one to allow pressure on the quarterback, and it took 2.76 seconds to get there. Every other offensive lineman had a clean sheet in the first half; Purdy was 7-for-8, while the rushing attack had a 50% success rate. The offense was still humming, and they picked up where they left off to begin the second half.” Brock Purdy keeps 49ers rolling with ‘MVP’ game vs. Dolphins “Just two weeks into the season, it’s far too early for any sweeping award declarations, but Purdy’s performance against the rebuilding Dolphins on Sunday was so close to perfect that Warner wanted the world to know he sees where Purdy could go in his fifth NFL season. “Brock is unbelievable,” Warner said. “I’ve spoken on how great of a preseason he had and his camp, his command of the offense, but it’s different. We get judged on those three hours that we’re out there. For him to be operating the offense the way he is right now, it doesn’t matter who the other pieces are. As long as Brock’s the one that’s being the point guard, I know we’re good.” 49ers lose another WR as Demarcus Robinson suffers ankle injury “Robinson favored his right ankle as he quickly hobbled to the medical tent on the Niners’ sideline. A few moments later, Robinson was placed on a cart and taken to the locker room. The 49ers initially designated Robinson as questionable to return but ruled him out at halftime.” What we learned as Brock Purdy cooks Dolphins in 49ers’ emphatic Week 2 home wi n “The 49ers came out with a five-man defensive line because they knew the Dolphins would try to run the ball early and often. The 49ers knew it was coming, and they still had a difficult time stopping it. Running back De’Von Achane, the NFL’s fifth-leading rusher last season, got fed the ball a lot in the first half. The Dolphins challenged the 49ers to stop the run, and San Francisco’s run defense did not rise to the challenge. As a result, the 49ers’ defense could not get off the field in the first half. Miami’s three offensive possessions resulted in drives of eight plays, 16 plays and 11 plays.” Kawakami: Big wins, lost players — the 2026 49ers are worth some all-in trade moves (paywall) “Especially since their interior line hasn’t looked super-sturdy against the Rams’ and Dolphins’ run games. Shanahan said they’ve already had contact with Leonard Floyd, a solid contributor on the 2024 49ers, who would qualify as a moderate option. There are other medium options. And as noted, there are a few potential star possibilities. What I sense from this team is that it believes every addition could be meaningful through December and into January and maybe February. Cohn: Grading the 49ers After Their 35-13 Win Over the Miami Dolphins “Purdy clearly has improved from last season and is firmly in the MVP conversation after two games…[Kittle] looks so much better than last week, when he clearly was rusty. Once Kittle got involved, the passing game couldn’t be stopped…..[the offensive line] is still the weakest link of the offense, and that won’t change. Last week was an aberration against a team that wasn’t prepared….The 49ers need to add a quality defensive tackle immediately. This is the biggest weakness on the defense….On offense, Kyle Shanahan called a near-perfect game for the second week in a row. And when he had a 29-point lead in the fourth quarter, he actually pulled his starters instead of padding their stats. Who is this Kyle Shanahan? Has he finally grown up? If so, the 49ers just might win the Super Bowl this season. He always has been simultaneously their biggest asset and their biggest liability, considering he’s the reason they reach the Super Bowl and the reason they lose it. Maybe he’ll be the reason they win it this season.”
author: Yinon Raviv

title: 3 quick takeaways from the 49ers’ runaway win over the Dolphins
summary: The San Francisco 49ers entered the weekend as the biggest favorite in Week 2, and they played like it, dominating the Miami Dolphins 35-13 to start the season 2-0. In a slower-paced game, the 49ers scored touchdowns on each of their first five drives, including three in the third quarter, as their offense could not […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers entered the weekend as the biggest favorite in Week 2, and they played like it, dominating the Miami Dolphins 35-13 to start the season 2-0. In a slower-paced game, the 49ers scored touchdowns on each of their first five drives, including three in the third quarter, as their offense could not be stopped, despite Christian McCaffrey having just 23 yards on the ground. Brock Purdy flourished, while George Kittle and Mike Evans both had quality games in the air for the 49ers. Here are three quick takeaways from the 49ers’ 35-13 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Brock Purdy shines again Brock Purdy was the key to the 49ers’ Week 1 win, tossing for 205 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception, while rushing for 29 more on the ground in the 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams. Purdy had the rough interception last week, but played fantastic outside of that, as the 49ers dominated the Rams in a big surprise. On Sunday, Purdy was nearly perfect, completing 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards, two touchdowns, and no interceptions. He also added 30 yards and another touchdown on the ground, while completing his last 18 passes. Purdy has always been the key piece of the 49ers’ offensive ceiling. His issue has been turnovers and the costly turnover-worthy plays. Those weren’t present on Sunday, as Purdy made clean decisions with receivers open throughout the afternoon. He finished with a passer rating of 149.1 and has started the season strong for the 49ers. The pressure gets there In the keys to the game, I pointed out the need to stop Malik Willis and neutralize the rushing threat of the Dolphins. Well, San Francisco kept De’Von Achane under 4.0 yards per carry, but the 49ers really excelled with their pass defense. Malik Willis threw for just 120 yards (before a late-game touchdown), while rushing twice for six yards, and the 49ers sacked him four times. The young guys cleaned up, as Gracen Halton, Romello Height, and Marques Sigle each got a sack, while Upton Stout and Fred Warner combined for another. The pass rush was a major issue for the 49ers last season, and they’ve had to rely on younger players to start the year with injuries up front. So far, that room has done well enough, and the pressure got there several times against Malik Willis on Sunday. Red zone excellence The 49ers drove down the field on each of their first five drives, going 59, 71, 65, 71, and 28 yards, with all of those possessions going into the red zone. Each of those drives ended in a touchdown, making the 49ers 5 for 5 on red zone touchdown scores. Meanwhile, their defense wasn’t necessarily spectacular, as Miami got into 49ers territory on each of their first three drives. But those three possessions produced just six points, as the 49ers missed a field goal and forced two red-zone field goals. Despite facing 9, 17, and 12-yard drives, the 49ers secured stops when it mattered, limiting the Dolphins’ scoring chances and maintaining a firm lead. Last weekend, they scored on 2 of 3 red-zone drives and allowed just one touchdown on three defensive drives. It was good to see them continue that success on Sunday.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 49ers injury updates: 2 players likely suffered high-ankle sprains
summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided injury updates on wide receivers Mike Evans and Demarcus Robinson. Evans left Week 2 with a hip injury. Despite leaving, Evans stayed on the sideline with his helmet. That’s usually a sign that a player can return. Shanahan said if the game were different, Evans could have […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Demarcus Robinson #11 of the San Francisco 49ers scores a touchdown in the second quarter of the NFL football game against the Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided injury updates on wide receivers Mike Evans and Demarcus Robinson. Evans left Week 2 with a hip injury. Despite leaving, Evans stayed on the sideline with his helmet. That’s usually a sign that a player can return. Shanahan said if the game were different, Evans could have returned. As for Robinson, Shanahan said his injury looked like a high-ankle sprain, “so, unfortunate there.” According to the reporters on hand, Robinson walked out of the locker room with a slight limp, but he did not have any protective devices on his ankle/foot. Here’s what Shanahan said about whether the team would need to add another wide receiver: “We’ll see. It has been unfortunate. It was big losing Stribling last week. You guys know how big it was losing Ricky over the summer. Then losing D-Rob today was huge. Christian Kirk’s got a couple of weeks before he can come back. But we still have a group of guys out there that we have played with that have done things. I’m sure we’ll have to add somebody, whether it’s to the practice squad or to the roster, but those are things we’ll start discussing tonight, and hopefully have an answer by Wednesday.” Shanahan smirked and said, “No,” when asked if Brandon Aiyuk could be an option. Rookie defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. has an ankle injury. Shanahan said it looks like a similar injury to Robinson’s. He couldn’t confirm it, but believes the Niners may have lost another player for multiple weeks to a high-ankle sprain. He also said the 49ers had contacted Leonard Floyd and “a couple of people” as soon as they lost Sam Okuayinonu. We can expect the 49ers to work out multiple players in the coming days, and potentially add one or two to the practice squad or active roster.

title: Brock Purdy was nearly perfect in the 49ers’ blowout win over the Dolphins
summary: The worry that the San Francisco 49ers wouldn’t have the same energy as in Week 1 was on display from the start. Fred Warner forced a fumble on the second play from scrimmage, but it came on a pass that gained 18 yards. De’Von Achane strung together a few positive gains, but a penalty left […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The worry that the San Francisco 49ers wouldn’t have the same energy as in Week 1 was on display from the start. Fred Warner forced a fumble on the second play from scrimmage, but it came on a pass that gained 18 yards. De’Von Achane strung together a few positive gains, but a penalty left the Dolphins behind the sticks, and a 51-yard field goal was wide. The 49ers could play on the moon, and the expectation would be that they’d put up points the next week. The first drive featured a heavy dose of Christian McCaffrey. After Brock Purdy bought himself time, he found Mike Evans for the first “wow” play of Evans 49ers career. McCaffrey picked up 16 on the ensuing third down, before scoring a 1-yard touchdown to give the Niners an early 7-0 lead. Miami possessed the ball on their second drive for over nine minutes on a 17-play drive. Malik Willis used his legs on the drive, which gave the Niners’ defense fits. De’Von Achane’s speed seemed problematic. But the defense stood tall after Fred Warner and Upton Stout recorded the first sack of the season for Raheem Morris’s unit. Miami’s field goal was good this time around, and the score was 7-3. The 49ers’ second possession of the half ended the same way the first one did. An 8-play, 71-yard drive took just over five minutes off the clock. Purdy ran for 28 yards and a pair of first downs on the drive. But he threw the ball behind Demarcus Robinson on a would-be touchdown, which led to Robinson being carted to the locker room with an ankle injury . Purdy scrambled in for a score near the goal line to give the Niners a 14-3 lead. That would be the last drive for the 49ers of the half, after Miami had another time-consuming drive, this one before the half. A drive-extending play came when Keion White was flagged for roughing the passer on a 3rd-and-6 play. On the next third down, Willis’s legs were a factor again. After running around, Willis found a receiver 23 yards downfield to convert a 3rd-and-9. Ji’Ayir Brown had a tackle for loss on second-and-goal. Nick Bosa drew a holding penalty on rookie Kaydn Proctor on third-and-goal. Miami settled for a 23-yard field goal, which took us to halftime with a 14-6 score. The Dolphins held the ball for nine more minutes than the 49ers in the first half. They converted over 50% of their third-down attempts. The Dolphins had 52 yards after contact on the ground with a 45% success rate. The Niners were fortunate only to allow six points. The offense didn’t have much of an opportunity to do anything more. They scored a touchdown on both of their drives. Connor Colby was the only one to pressure the quarterback, and it took 2.76 seconds to get there. Every other offensive lineman had a clean sheet in the first half; Purdy was 7-for-8, while the rushing attack had a 50% success rate. The offense was still humming, and they picked up where they left off to begin the second half. George Kittle had the longest play of the season to open the third quarter. Purdy hit him down the seam for a 40-yard gain. Shortly after, Kittle was wide open in the end zone for a 12-yard gain. Four plays. 65 yards. And a touchdown in under two minutes, giving the 49ers a 21-6 lead. Bosa had been close to sacking Willis all afternoon. Marques Sigle recorded the sack, but Bosa forced Willis to move off his spot. The defense gave up nothing on 3rd-and-11, forcing a three-and-out. Purdy found an open Deebo Samuel on 3rd and 11. In the face of a blitz and a free runner, Purdy found Evans. On the next play, Kyle Juszczyk was wide open for a 21-yard gain. Juszczyk finished the drive with a touchdown, and the rout was on. The Niners took a 28-6 lead. Purdy was 15-for-16 with 200 yards and a perfect 158.3 quarterback rating. He had all day in the pocket, and his wide receivers were usually wide open by about five-plus yards. The Dolphins no longer had the threat of the run in their favor. The game script meant they’d have to drop back and throw for the remainder of the game, which is good news for how the 49ers are built. Unsurprisingly, Miami went three-and-out again. Defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. was questionable to return after he was shaken up with an ankle injury on the drive. Punter Bradley Pinion inexplicably dropped the ball, which gave the Niners a short field. Purdy found Mike Evans, then McCaffrey found the end zone. The 21-point quarter topped 18 teams’ total points for the entire game in Week 2 at the time. The Dolphins ran 28 plays in Niners territory in the first half. They didn’t cross midfield in the third quarter. KhaDarel Hodge joined the party on the next drive. He was on the field after Evans took himself out following his previous reception. Evans was officially questionable to return with a hip injury. Mac Jones entered the game. Purdy finished with 22 attempts and only two incompletions. Miami added a garbage-time touchdown on a busted coverage to make it 35-13. The 49ers outgained the Dolphins by nearly 100 yards and by more than 3 yards per play. The offense scored a touchdown on all five of its touchdown drives. The defense was stingy before garbage time, and that’s how you get a blowout victory.

Ricky Pearsall, Christian Kirk, and De’Zhaun Stribling were arguably going to be three of the top four receivers heading into the regular season. Pearsall is out for the year. Kirk is on injured reserve, and Stribling just joined him. Unfortuantely, the 49ers lost another receiver on Sunday, as Demarcus Robinson was carted to the locker room during the second quarter with an ankle injury. It came on a play where Robinson was wide open and should have walked into the end zone. But the throw was behind him, and it looked like Robinson’s ankle kind of got stuck in the field. Perhaps it’s a good sign that the team didn’t rule Robinson out immediately.

York pleaded to two misdemeanor charges on August 24 […]
full_text: (Photo by Alan Harvey/SNS Group via Getty Images) | SNS Group via Getty Images San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York will miss his second game in a row, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. York didn’t make the trip with the team to Australia and will now miss the 49ers’ home opener. He’s staying away to avoid any distractions, per Schefter. York pleaded to two misdemeanor charges on August 24 after being arrested in Ohio. He was arrested last month on suspicion of engaging in prostitution . According to Columbiana County court records in Ohio, York allegedly responded to an undercover ad on a known prostitution website where he “arranged to have sexual activity with a female in exchange for $140.” The original prostitution charge was amended to misdemeanor disorderly conduct as part of the plea agreement resolving the case. The other misdemeanor was possessing criminal tools, which wound up being York’s cell phone. Schefter said the NFL is expected to make a decision on any potential discipline for York “soon.” Back in August, around the time the incident occurred, the NFL said it was “aware of the matter, which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy.”

title: Buccaneers Week 2 Top Performers vs. Cleveland Browns
summary: A gloomy weather forecast gave way to an even gloomier result as the Buccaneers floundered their way to an 0-2 start against the Cleveland Browns, 23-19, in their home opener at Raymond James Stadium. Delayed at the 2-minute warning for 2-plus hours because of intense rain and lightning, the Bucs tried desperately to salvage a […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 20: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers is tackled by Quincy Williams #5 of the Cleveland Browns during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images A gloomy weather forecast gave way to an even gloomier result as the Buccaneers floundered their way to an 0-2 start against the Cleveland Browns, 23-19, in their home opener at Raymond James Stadium. Delayed at the 2-minute warning for 2-plus hours because of intense rain and lightning, the Bucs tried desperately to salvage a double-digit lead they squandered away to…*checks notes*…Deshaun Watson. Unfortunately, Baker Mayfield, supposedly full of moxie and vigor to claim revenge against his former team, played atrociously and failed to deliver on his egotistical ambitions. The Bucs now find themselves in dire straits early and facing a formidable gauntlet in the next month against the Minnesota Vikings, Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys before a seemingly easier task against the Pittsburgh Steelers. But that this point, nothing should be considered a gimme. Everything looks hard for Tampa right now, but we’ll do some brief shoutouts on the positives before moving on. Offensive Top Performer: Bucky Irving For the second week in a row, the Buccaneers offense primarily came from Bucky Irving and nary anyone else. Irving carried the ball 17 times for 89 yards, averaging 5.2 yards per carry. His explosiveness and proficiency at breaking tackles single-handedly kept the Bucs offense afloat as the passing game struggled to do anything. Bucky Irving breaks loose 😤 CLEvsTB on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/54tbo77wXW — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Emeka Egbuka caught his first TD since last November and generally looked good, but his quarterback failed to get him the ball — including on the final play of the game where he was wide open in the end zone. Chris Godwin and Cade Otton also had their moments, so it’s not like the individual talent has completely evaporated. This catch by Cade Otton 😮 CLEvsTB on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CJC0SvSh0o — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 It all relies on No. 6, the new $55 million man, getting his act together and orchestrating a competent operation. Defensive Top Performer: CB Ben Morrison Again, there’s not much to praise here. Morrison has rebounded well from his nightmare rookie season, looking very good against Cincinnati last week and holding well again in Week 2 in place of the injured Jacob Parrish. Morrison logged 7 total tackles and broke up a touchdown in the endzone. Benjamin Morrison disse: "aqui não, queridinho!" 😌❌ 📺: #CLEvsTB ao vivo e em português no NFL Game Pass pic.twitter.com/rxqaTntbHX — NFL Brasil (@NFLBrasil) September 20, 2026 Rookie Keonte Scott played like a pitbull in the nickel, recording his first career sack and another tackle for loss as part of a 3-tackle effort. Unfortunately, it was much more bad than good. The defense responded to the offense going up 10 points by immediately giving up the lead and looking toothless while doing so. It’s literally the same issues year after year, so I’m not sure what else we should expect at this point. The team can’t generate pass rush without blitzing, it can’t cover tight ends, and it plays coverage way too soft and allows the easy completions. Watson, who’s barely played in the last 2 years and has looked terrible when he has, was coming off a historically awful Week 1 performance by EPA, and he turns around this week with two rookie receivers and a second-year tight end and goes 24-for-30 for 238 yards, 2 TDs and no turnovers while also rushing 7 times for 22 yards. I don’t know, guys, seems pretty bad! Special Teams Top Performer: K Chase McLaughlin The one guy who deserved an extension the most this offseason continued to increase his price tag. McLaughlin accounted for 13 of the team’s 19 points, including a massive 59-yard drive. Kam Johnson flashed his return chops on the team’s final drive, putting them in excellent position with a 48-yard scamper out toward midfield that the offense simply couldn’t capitalize on. Special teams overall has looked very solid.

title: Week 2 Game Recap: Buccaneers fall to 0-2 in debacle against the Browns
summary: With week one feeling like a forgotten tragedy of the past, the Buccaneers welcomed the Cleveland Browns into Raymond James Stadium for their second game of the season. For Baker Mayfield, the fans in Tampa Bay, and all those watching at home, hopefully the team’s home opener would bring a new life to their young […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 20: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers congratulates Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns after the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images With week one feeling like a forgotten tragedy of the past, the Buccaneers welcomed the Cleveland Browns into Raymond James Stadium for their second game of the season. For Baker Mayfield, the fans in Tampa Bay, and all those watching at home, hopefully the team’s home opener would bring a new life to their young season— Something week one worked hard to zap out of the fanbase. First Quarter: Sunday’s week two contest kicked off with the Browns’ offense and Baker Mayfield’s replacement Deshaun Watson. Cleveland finished their opening drive by taking the ball out of Watson’s hands with an odd third-and-long handoff and subsequent punt. Baker Mayfield versus the Cleveland Browns: Part one— advantage Mayfield. The Buccaneers 2026 debut drive at home would lead to a Chase McLaughlin field goal. 3-0, Bucs. In a tit for tat response, Deshaun Watson walked Cleveland down the field on their second drive for a game-evening field goal. 3-3, All. Tampa’s second field goal attempted and second field goal made gave them another three-point lead, however, after another stop Baker Mayfield had another uh-oh moment with his fourth turnover in a game and a quarter. Mayfield’s first interception of the year was an ugly one and much like his turnovers a week ago would lead to points. Second Quarter: At the start of quarter number two, the Browns had possession and an opportunity to strike. Fortunately, for the Bucs, the Browns also aren’t the most reliably executing offense— A redzone trip that only netted three. 6-6, Tied up. With the ebb and flow of the game remaining consistent— sloppy offense, passable defense— Tampa took back over with 2:33 left in the half, after a shockingly aggressive fourth down attempt by Todd Monken. Monken, backed up inside his own 30, decided to leave his fledgling offense on the field for a fourth and one conversion attempt. Using creativity that knows no bounds, the former Tampa Bay coach ran the ball straight up the middle. The run resulted in no gain, no first down, and more Tampa Bay Buccaneers offense football. Tampa took two minutes and 21 seconds of the 2:33 they were given and gained about 20 yards to add a painfully short field goal. 9-6, Tampa Bay. Third Quarter: Sunday’s second half started with the Bucs’ offense and it was Tampa’s best drive of the season. The Bucs hit play action passes, used their run game, and got the ball to their playmakers. In a drive that featured Bucky Irving (with Baker Mayfield blocking), started with a play action crosser to Chris Godwin, and was capped off by Emeka Egbuka’s first touchdown of the 2026 season, the Buccaneers showed life and looked the offense that fans would have expected to see before entering the season and watching last week’s fumbling and bumbling— Tampa’s drive even featured a patented Baker Mayfield third down scramble before they secured the game’s first touchdown. 16-6, Bucs. A mixed exchange of kicks would pull the Browns within seven before Deshaun Watson had one of his best plays as a Cleveland Brown— Dropping back and finding Denzel Boston for a touchdown. Boston’s catch-and-run score featured what was unofficially Alex Anzalone 78th missed tackle of the season and officially his second in the final three plays of Cleveland’s scoring drive. 16-16, shocking. Fourth Quarter: The fourth quarter’s first big play for Tampa Bay was Chris Godwin on a crossing route for a second and 10 first down— Their second came the very next play. In the cherry on top of multi-deep ball sequence that spanned across two separate drives Baker Mayfield finally hit a deep shot. A diving Tez Johnson who was gliding through Cleveland’s secondary snared Mayfield’s pass and put the Buccaneers in position for Chase McLaughlin to add three more points and return the Bucs to the lead. 19-16, Buccaneers. To say Tampa Bay’s defense has been a disappointment through the first two weeks of the season would be a hard understatement. The 2026 Bucs have looked far too much like the 2025 Bucs for anyone’s liking and that trend would continue as the Cleveland Browns, amidst a quarterback controversy and as much turmoil as organization in the NFL took Todd Bowles to the matt again. Six more points on Bowles’ unit, one more blown fourth quarter lead, more Bucs beating Bucs. Trailing 23-19, the Buccaneers had an opportunity to pull out some of the magic that their 2025 campaign began with just a year ago. Baker Mayfield was in early MVP conversations mainly for his last-minute heroics. Moving down the field, Mayfield and the Bucs encountered a obstacle that they could not overcome— Mother nature. Hit by a storm, Raymond James Stadium was evacuated and placed into a weather delay. Almost two full hours after the initiation of the delay the Bucs and Browns took the field and prepared to resume battle. Drenched and dreary, the Buccaneers scooted Bucky Irving across the line to gain for a first down conversion. A quick slant to Ted Hurst III and the Bucs were moving. In what has become standard 2026 Bucs fashion, the vibes would sourly quickly. Hurst III would bobble and ultimately drop a perfect throw that could have resulted in the game-winning touchdown shortly after. From that point it would only take one Baker Mayfield scramble and one more incomplete pass to put the Bucs down in the hole they have dug for themselves, 0-2.

Part of the reason the defense was on the field so much in the first half was because the offense couldn’t sustain a drive. Again, there are no moral victories in the NFL, but the Titans actually have some things to build on from this loss. What were your biggest takeaways from today’s game?

title: Commanders report card: Team grades in NFL Week 2 loss to Cowboys
summary: What an absolute disaster.   The Commanders dropped a 37-20 result to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday at AT&T Stadium to fall to 0-2 on the season and in the NFC East.   They lost quarterback Jayden Daniels to a left elbow dislocation that looked to be significant. Right guard Sam Cosmi (concussion), left tackle Brandon Coleman […]
full_text: What an absolute disaster. The Commanders dropped a 37-20 result to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday at AT&T Stadium to fall to 0-2 on the season and in the NFC East. They lost quarterback Jayden Daniels to a left elbow dislocation that looked to be significant. Right guard Sam Cosmi (concussion), left tackle Brandon Coleman (finger), defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw (shoulder) also left with injuries of unknown severity. Most everything that could go wrong did after the Daniels injury , which occurred on the last play of the first half. This game wasn’t without bright spots, but everything seemed to go against Washington with a series of unfortunate events that could have a lasting impact beyond those four quarters. We’ll get more into the game than in most other stories, but we’ve still got a game to grade in this Week 2 report card: Rushing offense Daniels was dynamic when in scramble mode (and pre-injury), averaging 9.9 yards per carry. Bill Croskey-Merritt was inefficient in this one and not as effective as Rachaad White , who averaged 6.1 yards per tote on seven carries. Don’t be shocked if White starts eating into Croskey-Merritt’s snap count. He was the better runner, but it was hard to establish a designed running game when the Commanders were playing from behind all afternoon. Grade: C Passing offense Daniels and Mariota were both solid throwing the ball, with 207 yards and two touchdowns between them. Antonio Williams missed a wide-open Terry McLaurin on a receiver pass and Dyami Brown lost a fumble. Both of those moments were strikes against. Washington got screwed out of a touchdown from Mariota to Brown, where a bogus incompletion call in the end zone was confirmed on replay. The Commanders targeted Terry McLaurin nine times, but he only had two completions. Stefon Diggs had two touchdowns and the pass protection was generally okay. Grade: B Rushing defense The Commanders run defense wasn’t too bad. Javonte Williams averaged just 2.5 yards per carry and no one outside of Dak Prescott could move the ball on the ground. The effort from the front seven was strong in this regard, though the pass defense couldn’t stop a gosh darn thing. Why run when you can throw wherever you want, whenever you want? Grade: B-plus Passing defense The Commanders gave up four passing touchdowns to Prescott , who had a 143.8 passer rating. Let’s put this simply: when the Commanders don’t generate pressure, they can’t stop the air attack. CeeDee Lamb was dominant early and then again in the game’s latter stages. Mike Sainristil is borderline unplayable at this stage. The secondary is unreliable overall. Right now, coverage might be the team’s weakest link. Grade: F Special teams Drew Stevens has played two NFL regular season games. He has two misses in that span, including a wide volley from 51 yards out today. There’s little doubt that Stevens has a strong and accurate leg, but how much margin for error does he have before red flags start to go up? Jaylin Lane didn’t have his best day returning kicks or punts on Sunday, and he has to be better. Grade: C-minus Coaching Dan Quinn’s decision to go for a touchdown on that final (and fateful) play where Daniels got hurt is being called into question. Take the field goal and get some points and take JD5 out of harm’s way is the logic, I think. Don’t get that. He was being aggressive in a game where touchdowns were required. That was not a play call where Daniels was put in a bad spot. A crazy thing happened and that sucks. What happened is not on DQ. Overall, though, the defensive game plan didn’t work. Dallas is more talented, but Daronte Jones couldn’t generate the pressure required to get turnovers. David Blough’s play calling was better than in Week 1, and he kept his foot on the gas after Daniels was done. There’s no avoiding the fact that Sunday cemented an 0-2 start with two divisional losses. That’s unacceptable. A few more early losses and this whole season could spiral. Grade: D What grades would you give the Commanders in each of these phases of the game? Give us your report card in the comments below:

title: How Marcus Mariota, Commanders reacted to Jayden Daniels injury
summary: Jayden Daniels was being helped on a cart following his left elbow dislocation when Marcus Mariota trotted out to meet him.   The Commanders fallen starting quarterback and his veteran backup didn’t say much at the time, Mariota’s message was this:   “You’re not going through this alone.”  Mariota is with Daniels more than most […]
full_text: Jayden Daniels was being helped on a cart following his left elbow dislocation when Marcus Mariota trotted out to meet him. The Commanders fallen starting quarterback and his veteran backup didn’t say much at the time, Mariota’s message was this: “You’re not going through this alone.” Mariota is with Daniels more than most during the workday, and he knows how difficult missing so many games last year was on Daniels and how hard he worked to regain full health. This Daniels injury, to put it mildly, was a real blow. “It sucks. You can’t really put it into words,” Mariota said. “You watch that kid battle through all that he’d been through last year. It’s just unfortunate, but that’s an incredible locker room and he has an incredible support system. We’re going to everything we can to get him back and get him right.” While more detailed imaging on Monday is required, both head coach Dan Quinn and receiver Terry McLaurin expressed optimism that Daniels will return this season. That’s ultimately unknown. The Commanders found resolve at halftime, right after the injury, with Quinn, safety Jeremy Reaves and even rookie linebacker Sonny Styles speaking to the team at the break. The message from each guy was clear. This sucks. But we’ve got to rally. “I was disheartened for him,” Quinn said. “I know what he has gone through to go. I know we all wanted to play so well for him in that space. To see him in that spot, it stung for the guys. It was tough.” The Commanders weren’t able to overcome Daniels’ loss or an early deficit, and ended up dropping to 0-2. Daniels was seen by on-site reporters in a sling after the game, with an uncertain future regarding how much time he’ll miss. It’s a major blow for the Commanders, who will operate with Mariota as their signal caller, as they did for most of last season. Mariota played relatively well, completing 11-of-16 passes for 111 yards and a touchdown, and should’ve had another score if not for a terrible incomplete pass ruling on a Dyami Brown catch in the end zone. Mariota was heavily involved last season, when Daniels missed 10 games and finished only four. There’s confidence that the Commanders can carry on with their backup quarterback at the helm, but there’s plenty of time to talk about that. Right after the game, the focus was on Daniels and his latest injury. “Man, are we bummed for (Jayden),” Quinn said. “He was really playing his ass off. We will rally so hard around Marcus until Jayden gets back. That’s what we talked about as a team.”

full_text: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered what looked to be a significant injury at the end of the first half of Sunday’s game against the Dallas Cowboys. He was carted off the field in clear pain with a left elbow injury. The Commanders ruled him out with an elbow injury shortly after. Backup Marcus Mariota took over in the second half. After the 37-20 loss to Dallas, Commanders head coach Dan Quinn confirmed the elbow dislocation but said there was no fracture. Daniels is set to fly home from Dallas with the Commanders. He’ll have more imaging done on the elbow on Monday. Daniels also dislocated his left elbow last season, which eventually cut his 2025 campaign short. Daniels slipped taking the final snap of the first half — it looked like guard Chris Paul stepped on Daniels’ foot right after the snap — and he stuck out his arm to brace himself. title: Key takeaways from Washington Commanders Week 2 loss to Dallas Cowboys
summary: BOX SCORE The Commanders and Cowboys started their seasons with a tough divisional loss.   Washington mounted a comeback that fell a failed 2-point conversion short against the Eagles. Dallas got absolutely embarrassed by the New York Giants on national television.   To say that these teams desperately needed a rebound victory would be an […]
full_text: BOX SCORE The Commanders and Cowboys started their seasons with a tough divisional loss. Washington mounted a comeback that fell a failed 2-point conversion short against the Eagles. Dallas got absolutely embarrassed by the New York Giants on national television. To say that these teams desperately needed a rebound victory would be an understatement. Starting the campaign 0-2 on the season and within the division is a nightmare scenario. The Commanders are sitting right there after a 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday afternoon at AT&T Stadium. Another nightmare scenario unfolded before the final result, with franchise quarterback Jayden Daniels lost to a significant elbow injury. To make matters somehow even worse, the Commanders also had right guard Sam Cosmi, left tackle Brandon Coleman and defensive lineman Javon Kinlaw go down and not return. Here are some key takeaways after watching this mess of a game live: Jayden Daniels’ loss immeasurable Daniels was at his explosive best during the first half of Sunday’s game in Dallas. He was 11-for-17 passing for 96 yards and a touchdown. Daniels ran seven times for 69 more. He had the Commanders offense moving, proving accurate and elusive and all the things that makes him so special. Then, on the last play of the first half, disaster struck. Guard Chris Paul seemed to step on Daniels right after the snap, sending Daniels towards the turf. He tried to brace himself while falling down. Jayden Daniels injury to close the half absolutely sucks pic.twitter.com/2FJBrZxMps — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) September 20, 2026 He suffered a gruesome elbow injury that took him out of Sunday’s game at the very least. It’s highly likely that Daniels will miss more games than that after suffering that injury. Marcus Mariota’s a capable backup and can move the football, but Daniels is on another level and makes Washington a threat to beat anyone. They’re just a different team without him, losing that dynamic playmaking ability unique to No. 5. We’ll have to see how much time Daniels will miss, but his absence will have an irrevocable impact on this Commanders season just as it’s getting started. Washington struggled without him in 2025 — he dealt with several injuries last year, including a dislocated left elbow presumptively similar to the one he just suffered — and will have an uphill battle to remain competitive while he’s out. Commanders can’t catch a break The Commanders were one yard from the end zone with three seconds left in the first half. That’s when Daniels got hurt on a disastrous play where Washington failed to score and left that scenario without point. Washington got possession to start the second half, and Mariota pushed the ball down the field and found Dyami Brown with an excellent deep shot to the end zone. The play was ruled incomplete on the field, and the Commanders challenging the ruling, which sure looked like a touchdown in every possible way, as you can see below: Great throw by Mariota and great catch by Dyami Brown. Replay ruled this was NOT a TD. Refs need to be investigated @NFL pic.twitter.com/IOpovEsQ2Q — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 20, 2026 The incomplete pass call was somehow confirmed on review, and the Commanders eventually ended up kicking a field goal. Then Brown lost a fumble on the next drive which Dallas turned into a touchdown. The bad luck continued, with another seemingly easy touchdown unrealized. The Commanders fooled Dallas on a pass from receiver Antonio Williams, who just overthrew a wide open Terry McLaurin in the end zone. All those missed points added up and put the Commanders in a bind as the game progressed. Antonio Williams throws to the wrong shoulder, which would be a bigger concern if he were actually a QB pic.twitter.com/DR5Do0r0EP — Christian D'Andrea (@TrainIsland) September 20, 2026 Disastrous defensive start The regular season opener held some encouraging signs for an attacking Commanders that looked good outside of a few explosive plays allowed. That did not carry over. Washington’s defense was awful at the outset, allowing 17 points on Dallas’ first three series. The Cowboys drove into the red zone each time, with one third-down stop preventing a three-touchdown start to this game. Washington wasn’t able to get pressure and a suspect secondary therefore got gashed by Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott and receiver CeeDee Lamb. The Commanders were routinely penalized during that stretch as well, struggling to put up any sort of resistance. The defense should count itself thankful the Commanders offense kept the game close heading towards halftime. The Cowboys scoring run didn’t last forever, with the Commanders getting a stop and forcing the first Dallas punt with just roughly five minutes left in the first half. The Commanders defense played better after that, but Washington could’ve overcome an early deficit that proved costly. Overall, Washington had no answers for Prescott, who had 279 yards and four touchdowns. What are your immediate takeaways from the Commanders Week 2 contest in Dallas? Let us know in the article comments below.
author: Scott Bair

title: NFL Week 2: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 2.
full_text:
In the early window of NFL Week 2 on Sunday, last week's offensive explosion seemed like a thing of the distant past.

 Five teams failed to reach double-digits points, including both the Bears and Vikings at a rainy Soldier Field. The Panthers forced five turnovers against the Falcons, while the Patriots cemented their win over the Steelers with a fumble return for a touchdown. The highest-scoring matchup of the early window (44 points) came between the Titans and Eagles, which ended on a game-winning touchdown grab by Philly's  Darius Cooper .

 The scoring picked up in the late window Sunday, as the Cowboys and Commanders combined for 57 points. However, Washington lost QB Jayden Daniels to an elbow injury in the second quarter -- hours after Chicago lost QB Caleb Williams to a right hamstring injury. Meanwhile, the 49ers dominated the Dolphins in their first game back from Melbourne, Australia. And the Seahawks won their second straight game with backup quarterback Drew Lock . And the night game featured a wild ending, but ultimately the Chiefs improved to 2-0 with an overtime thriller over the Colts.

 Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

 
 Jump to: 
 KC-IND |  WSH-DAL | LV-LAC 
 SEA-ARI |  MIA-SF 
 JAX-DEN  |  CLE-TB  |  PHI-TEN 
 GB-NYJ  |  CIN-HOU | MIN-CHI 
 NO-BAL  |  CAR-ATL |  PIT-NE 

 Catch up on Thursday's game: 
 DET-BUF 

 
 

 

 Kansas City 33, Indianapolis 30 (OT) 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Chiefs 
 Did Patrick Mahomes' performance demonstrate the Chiefs are back as contenders? That appears to be the case after two weeks. In overtime, Mahomes orchestrated the 25th winning drive of his 10-year career, which is tied with Kirk Cousins for second most in that span. Last season, the Chiefs were bad in one-score games, finishing with a 1-9 record. Mahomes, though, proved he's capable of carrying the Chiefs yet again to another dramatic win. In just his second game after recovering from the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee, Mahomes finished with 382 passing yards and three touchdowns without committing a turnover.

 Most surprising performance: Of course, Mahomes spent most of Sunday relying on tight end Travis Kelce , who led the Chiefs with 101 receiving yards and a touchdown. Yet receiver Tyquan Thornton was just as impactful for the Chiefs' offense. At pivotal moments, Thornton was impressive in catching all four of his targets for 86 yards, including a 45-yard reception. That highlight was the first time in the game that the Chiefs' offense converted on third down. -- Nate Taylor 

 Next game: at Dolphins (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 
 

 

 Colts 
 Is this defense salvageable? The Colts' defense gave up its most yards in a game in three seasons in a Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens (506 yards). And the prospects for that unit didn't get better Sunday night, when the Colts consistently struggled to get stops against the Chiefs (523 yards). The question now is whether this is the permanent state of this defense, and if so, what does that mean for the 2026 Colts? Indianapolis approached this season knowing it needed a bit more from its defense to take some of the pressure of an offense led by QB Daniel Jones , who is coming off a torn Achilles tendon. But as of now, that plan is not panning out.

 Most surprising performance: The Colts got a valiant effort from backup cornerback Kapena Gushiken , who came off the bench after injuries to starters Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner to make two clutch plays. One of them, a pass breakup on a third down late in the fourth quarter, was one of the biggest plays of the game. The stop against Rashee Rice ended the Chiefs' best last chance in regulation. -- Stephen Holder 

 Next game: vs. Texans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 

 Fantasy football takeaway: Travis Kelce's 25.1 points were the second most among tight ends through the Sunday night game. Kelce caught nine of a team-high 11 targets, finishing with 101 yards and a touchdown. What stood out here? The play speed. We saw it with Kelce within the route and after the catch. Add that to his elite coverage awareness, too. It was a big night for Kelce, who is firmly in the TE1 ranks for the Week 3 game at Miami. -- Bowen 

 

 

 Dallas 37, Washington 20 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Cowboys 
 Are the Cowboys going to need QB Dak Prescott to outscore teams again this season? It looks that way. Prescott broke the Cowboys' record for touchdown passes in a career with four Sunday, eclipsing Tony Romo. But Prescott needed to be everything for Dallas, completing better than 80% of his passes, throwing the four scores and running for 26 yards. The defense had issues again, losing safety P.J. Locke (foot) and corner Cobie Durant (hamstring) in the first half. The Cowboys continue to struggle on third down, contain a running quarterback and turn pressures into sacks. Washington had three chances for touchdowns wiped out, but Prescott bailed the Cowboys out ... again.

 Trend to watch: The Cowboys want to be a team that relies on the running game to get things going. Through two games, that has not happened. A week after running 18 times for 69 yards against the Giants, the Cowboys followed with 66 yards on 21 carries. No Cowboys running back has a rush of more than 9 yards. The Cowboys miss Pro Bowl left guard Tyler Smith , who will be out for at least the next two games because of thumb surgery, but they shouldn't miss him this much. -- Todd Archer 

 Next game: vs. Ravens (Sunday in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, 4:25 p.m. ET)

 

 
 

 Commanders 
 What's next for Washington after QB Jayden Daniels' injury? This game resembled many from last season -- porous defense, an injured quarterback and a double-digit defeat. Daniels' status and length of absence remains uncertain. And he'll have to answer one giant question whenever he returns: Can he stay healthy? He has now exited four of his past five games with an injury. Also, the defense has struggled. In two games, it has forced zero turnovers and hasn't lived up to internal expectations. If the team is not careful, the season could get ugly.

 Trend to watch: The Commanders' pass defense has allowed seven touchdown receptions in the first two games -- including four Sunday. The offseason overhaul on defense was supposed to help the coverage with intense pressure and disguised coverages. However, the pressure has been sporadic and too many targets are left open -- whether from coverage confusion or botched assignments. Cornerback Mike Sainristil has been a frequent target, and he's not the only one breaking down. -- John Keim 

 Next game: vs. Seahawks (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 
 Fantasy football takeaway: Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson had 20.3 fantasy points in Week 2, catching all four of his targets for 43 yards and two touchdowns. He will remain a touchdown-dependent player in this offense, but he is a priority target in scoring position. Ferguson already has three red zone targets over his first two games after seeing 23 last season. -- Bowen 

 

 

 Las Vegas 26, L.A. Chargers 14 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Raiders 
 How have the Raiders fared without TE Brock Bowers ? Last year, the Raiders' offense fell apart when Bowers sustained a knee injury in Week 1. This year has been different. Las Vegas has been without Bowers (knee) for two weeks and has managed to make things work, which is a testament to coach Klint Kubiak . On Sunday, wide receiver Tre Tucker caught five passes for 119 yards and a touchdown. Las Vegas had eight players record a reception, including wide receiver Cody White , who had two touchdown catches. With Bowers expected to return for Week 3, the optimism for…

title: Eagles' Broadway jab at Titans leads NFL Week 2 trolls
summary: Teams across the NFL came with petty postgame energy after wins in Week 2, led by the Philadelphia Eagles.
full_text:
With half of the league looking to remain undefeated heading into Week 2, a win could lead to an even sweeter troll. Case in point? The Philadelphia Eagles .

 

 The Eagles used a late two-minute drive to steal a 24-20 win against the Tennessee Titans in Nashville.

 Tennessee took a 20-17 lead with 1:56 left and needed one stop for its first win of the season. But Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts led his team down the field with a nine-play, 65-yard drive that ended with a 3-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Darius Cooper with nine seconds left. It marked the Eagles' latest winning passing touchdown since 2012, according to ESPN Research.

 Nashville is home to the famous Broadway Street, but Philadelphia has its own notable street too: "Broad Street." Therefore, the Eagles posted a graphic of an Eagle on a "Broadway" street sign but covered "way" with a sticky note that read: "Street," putting a spin on Nashville's area.

 

 Here are more of the top trolls from NFL Week 2.

 

 Carolina Panthers 34, Atlanta Falcons 3 
 Carolina defeated its NFC South foe on the road Sunday in convincing fashion.

 Panthers quarterback Bryce Young passed for 287 yards and three touchdowns, two of which went to tight end Darren Waller . Carolina forced five turnovers -- three interceptions and two fumbles -- as Atlanta had only 286 total yards of offense.

 Carolina's blowout win came with an equally dominant social media performance. It first shared a victory post with the score and caption: "Feelin' Peachy," a reference to Georgia being known as the Peach State. The Panthers then posted a graphic of a Panther eating a bird's egg with the caption: "We cooked."

 

 
 New Orleans Saints 24, Baltimore Ravens 17 
 The Saints faced a 17-9 deficit heading into the fourth quarter but responded with consecutive touchdowns -- the final one coming with 1:28 left. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson threw an interception on the ensuing drive, and New Orleans secured the victory.

 The NFC South team directed its troll toward an unlikely source: a Baltimore fan who had choice words for Saints fans on X. They wrote that Saints fans were "talking crazier than Colts  fans," the Ravens' Week 1 opponent, and they'd similarly learn the "hard way" like Indianapolis' followers. Baltimore defeated Indianapolis last Sunday.

 New Orleans remembered the slight, quoting the post with a video of wide receiver Chris Olave celebrating his fourth-quarter touchdown with the caption: "Love those crazy Saints fans."

 

 
 Minnesota Vikings 9, Chicago Bears 3 
 Another divisional game brought another troll, this time from the Minnesota Vikings .

 Minnesota kept Chicago in check after the Bears put up 59 points in a Week 1 victory. The Vikings forced two turnovers, including one as Chicago running back D'Andre Swift  fumbled while diving for a touchdown. The Bears reached the red zone again but had a field goal attempt blocked with 6:23 left. Minnesota got one more stop to claim the win.

 The Vikings kept it simple after the victory. They shared a "W" graphic with the caption: "WINdy City DUB," emphasizing the "win."

 

 

 San Francisco 49ers 35, Miami Dolphins 13 

 San Francisco is off to a dominant start to the season with consecutive double-digit wins -- this time against Miami.

 The 49ers erupted in the third quarter with three touchdowns, two of which were delivered by quarterback Brock Purdy . Running back Christian McCaffrey added the final one after he had a score in the first quarter. Purdy threw for 287 yards and and completed 91% of his pass attempts with 30 rushing yards and a score. He's the first player with 250 passing yards on 90% completion and 30 rushing yards in a game in NFL history.  

 Consistently petty, San Francisco had trolls lined up postgame for Miami. The 49ers referenced the Dolphins' namesake, referred to making "a splash" and posted an image of a dolphin pool float.

 

 

 Las Vegas Raiders 26, Los Angeles Chargers 14 

 The Raiders are 2-0 for the first time since 2021 after a big win against the Chargers.

 Las Vegas pulled ahead in the fourth quarter behind consecutive turnovers by Los Angeles -- a fumble by running back Omarion Hampton then an interception thrown by Justin Herbert . Hampton's fumble resulted in a Raiders touchdown to put them up 10 with 2:59 remaining. Las Vegas quarterback Kirk Cousins had 259 yards passing and three touchdowns, and wide receiver Tre Tucker led the team with five receptions for 119 yards and a score.

 A massive victory came with a straight forward troll as -- not far from Hollywood -- the Raiders captioned their win post: "Roll credits." As Cousins walked off the field, he took a video thanking the fans who showed up at Sofi Stadium and said it "felt like a home game," which Las Vegas wrote in its caption. 

 

 

 Seattle Seahawks 31, Arizona Cardinals 7 

 It has been almost 10 months since Seattle lost a regular-season or postseason game, and Arizona is the latest to be on the other end of a victory.

 The Seahawks outscored the Cardinals 24-0 in the second half behind a stellar performance from Jaxon Smith-Njigba . The wide receiver had nine catches for 155 yards and three touchdowns. He has scored Seattle's first four touchdowns of the season, becoming only the second player in NFL history to record each of his team's first four-plus touchdowns of the season, according to Elias Sports Bureau.

 And like the Seahawks have done during their win streak dating to last season, they made sure to troll their opponent. They first shared a comic of their mascot posing in front of a buried Big Red, the Cardinals' mascot. Seattle then posted an image of a burnt tortilla with a "W" grilled on it and the caption: "That's a wrap."

 

 

 Cleveland Browns 23, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 19 

 The Browns are in the win column following a late defensive stand against the Buccaneers.

 Lightning delayed the game by 2 hours, 12 minutes, resuming while Tampa Bay held possession at the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter. The Buccaneers had a chance to take the lead on fourth-and-11 with 22 seconds left. But quarterback Baker Mayfield threw an interception and Cleveland came up with a clutch victory.

 The Browns poked fun at the Buccaneers' classic "Bucco Bruce" logo postgame, sharing a meme that pointed at Bruce and asked: "What does he even do?"

title: NFL Week 2's best arrivals, led by Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes
summary: Rounding up the top pregame and tunnel arrivals from around the league.
full_text:
There are no rules for the best NFL gameday arrival fits, but there is certainly an unspoken competition, and the judges are often a player's football peers.

 An animated discussion among Cincinnati Bengals  defenders in the locker room after a win illustrated this.

 The source was cornerback DJ Turner II 's custom bold double-breasted suit by fashion designer Pharoah Kirk -- the unofficial fit of the day. Respect was given to Turner's fit, with one player promising to top his arrival the following week.

 "I'm always about that action," Turner said. I gotta put it on."

title: Jackson, Ravens face questions after frustrating loss to Saints
summary: Here are the major questions facing the Ravens' offense from Sunday's loss.
full_text:
BALTIMORE -- Trailing by a touchdown in the final minute Sunday, Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson threw the ball deep downfield toward wide receiver Rashod Bateman in an attempt to keep a comeback drive alive. 
 
 But Jackson's final pass of the game sailed 5 yards past Bateman and got picked off by Saints safety Julian Blackmon . Bateman pounded the ground with both fists, which summed up Baltimore's frustrating 24-17 loss to New Orleans. 
 
 A week after everything seemed to go right for the Baltimore offense in the season opener, Jackson and the Ravens have to figure out how it all went wrong. There seemed to be a disconnect, from a quizzical playcall to a head-scratching turnover to a lot of self-inflicted mistakes. 
 
 "We are going to stick together," Ravens running back Derrick Henry said. "Obviously, we didn't get the result we wanted; [it left a] bad taste in our mouth. It is just a little adversity. It is all about how we respond, and I know the guys are going to respond the right way [by] watching the film, correcting things and moving on to Dallas and being ready for Rio." 
 
 There is uncertainty about which players will be lining up for the Ravens offense Sunday in Rio de Janeiro. Wide receiver Zay Flowers didn't play because of a hamstring injury, and left tackle Ronnie Stanley couldn't finish the game because of a toe injury. 
 
 Here are the other major questions facing the Ravens' offense from Sunday's loss: 
 
 

 Why did the Ravens throw deep on third-and-1 instead of giving the ball to Henry? 
 
 The most debated playcall came with the game tied at 17 in the middle of the fourth quarter. On a third-and-1 at the Baltimore 37-yard line, Jackson launched the ball 50 yards to Chris Moore , who had the pass batted away from him. 
 
 
 It seemed like a risky decision for first-year playcaller Declan Doyle to call a pass to Moore, who was just elevated off the practice squad. The straightforward choice would have been to hand the ball to the 6-foot-3, 252-pound Henry, who got less than 2 yards on just three of his 16 carries (and one was a 1-yard touchdown run). 
 
 "It's a play that we liked," coach Jesse Minter said. "Thought we had a shot there for an explosive. Obviously, it didn't work out, so it is always going to be [everyone] looking at it after the fact." 
 
 Since Henry joined the Ravens in 2024, Baltimore had a 75% success rate on third-and-1 situations entering Sunday, third best in the NFL over that span. But Henry said he wasn't disappointed that he didn't get a chance to convert that third down himself. 
 
 "We are going to ride with 'Dec,' man," Henry said. "He called a [play], [he] wanted to take a shot and it didn't work out this time." 
 
 After Baltimore punted, New Orleans put together a 16-play, 68-yard winning drive. 
 
 
 
 
 What was Jackson thinking on that game-ending interception? 
 
 Jackson's interception with 13 seconds remaining was a rare one. It was only the second time in his nine-year career that he has been picked off in the final two minutes of regulation. 
 
 The fact that Jackson's pass was nowhere near Bateman caused many to wonder who was at fault. Did Jackson wildly overthrow Bateman? Or did Bateman give up running his route? 
 
 "We were just trying to make something happen," said Jackson, who was pressured from the right side after guard Olaivavega Ioane missed a block. "It was just the same group of guys out there. I feel like they were a little fatigued, and how I played it, it was a timing thing. I feel like I want that pass back, though." 
 
 With Flowers inactive, Bateman led Baltimore with a career-tying seven catches for 88 yards, including a 22-yard touchdown. Asked about Jackson's interception, Bateman said there was no miscommunication. 
 
 "I ran the right route, looked up [and] the ball was what it was," Bateman said. "That is really what it is. It is just one of those plays that you look at it and you can't get it back. Lamar played well. I think we all played well. [There] is just a lot of cleanup to do." 
 
  
 
 
 When will the Ravens stop committing so many penalties? 
 
 When the offensive line drew a number of penalty flags last week, Minter chalked it up to the linemen's aggressiveness. When the offense continued to commit penalties Sunday, it started to look this is one of the biggest issues facing the Ravens. 
 
 Over the first two weeks, the Baltimore offense has been flagged for 12 penalties for 120 yards. Only the Carolina Panthers (15) and Los Angeles Chargers (13) have committed more offensive penalties this season. 
 
 "Last week, we were able to overcome them, but this week we weren't," Jackson said. "So, that is why we have to clean things like that up. It starts in practice, though." 
 
 In the first two games, Baltimore has totaled four false starts and four holding penalties. The costliest penalty came in the third quarter, when holding on Moore negated a 12-yard scramble. 
 
 "For any situation it is tough to deal with when you know you are beating yourself, but we live to fight another day," Bateman said. "It is only Week 2. None of us in here [is] fixing to sit here and stress out and cry about it. We're all grown men. We know what we have got to go do to fix it. Everybody is on that accord right now."
